Khatinans, that Aminuddin transferred 3¼ decimals of land to Siddique Mia and made gift in respect of some of the land of Plot No. 188, that Aminuddin died leaving son Gedu Miah and daughter Kachchama, that Gedu Miah sold 7½  decimals of land to defendant Nos. 42-45 and Gedu Miah also sold 3½ decimals of land from plot No. 188 and further 3½ decimals of land to Champa Bibi. In total Gedu Miah sold 18¼ decimals of land and thus exhausted his entire share, that Yasin died leaving 3 sons, Abdul Motalib, Abdul Hamid and Abdul Karim and one daugher Tahera and they possessed the land left by Yasin in ejmali and they purchased 2 decimals of land from Shukur Mahmud, that Abdul Motalib died leaving defendant Nos. 2-10, that Abdul Karim, plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 2-10, used to live in the homestead of Yasin, that in Yasin's portions plaintiffs, defendant Nos. 2-10 and defendant No.1 have huts of different size, that in Khoaj's part his heirs are living.

4. The trial Court dismissed the suit with the finding that plaintiff failed to establish any case for declaring the deed illegal, that in the land in suit Siddique Miah and the father of defendant Nos. 42-45 have title, that plaintiffs failed to establish their right, title and interest and exclusive possession in the land in suit, that the suit is not barred by limitation and the suit as framed is maintainable.

5. The plaintiffs went on appeal and the appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that plaintiffs have established their claim of title in respect of 7½ decimals of land in suit and have failed to establish their claim of 1⁄2 decimal of land and as such would not get possession thereof, that plaintiffs would not get any relief as sought in prayer 'ga', that the document described in the 4th schedule would not affect plaintiffs' title, that defendants' kabala dated April 20, 1967 bearing No. 3495 is not legal. On the aforesaid findings the appellate Court decreed the suit in part and thereby declared title of the plaintiffs in respect of the land of plot No. 187/986 measuring 20½  decimals and also declared the deed described in schedule 4 void and illegal.

<u>6. As against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court the contesting defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that by the kabala Ext. 3 Abdul Motalib and Rahima Khatun did not acquire any title in the land of S.A. Khatian No. 170, that although Ext. l (C.S. khatian) was prepared in the name of Aminuddin predecessor of the plaintiffs but the presumption of the correctness thereof rebutted from the defendants' side, that plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the land in suit, that plaintiffs by competent and reliable witness have not been able to prove their basic document on the basis whereof they are claiming the land in suit, that from the plaintiffs' side no reliable evidence was brought on record to show that C.S. khatian was correctly prepared in the name of Aminuddin upon exclusion of his other brothers, that defendants have proved by reliable evidence that they are in possession of the land in suit.</u>

7. We have heard the learned Advocate-on-record and perused the materials in the petition for leave to appeal. The learned Advocate-on-record for the petitioner failed to point out error in the judgment of the High Court Division of the kind calling for interference by this Division.

8. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 2505 of 2013
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Naser Uddin Chowdhury, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners. 
Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No 1. Respondent Nos. 2-3 Not represented.
parties:
Most. Amena Khatun and others
Vs.
Shuja Nagar Shashan Committee, represented by its secretary Sri Kumaresh Kumar Odhikari and others
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J: This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.06.2013 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3583 of 2005 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No 13 of 1984 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna, for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession of the Suit property measuring .20 acre of land under plot No. 633 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 4, S.A. Khatian No. 275 of Mouja Sufanagar, stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to ex-landlord Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and others and they possessed the same as it was under their khas possession. Being approached by the Hindu Community for using the suit property as cremation ground, the ex-landlords approved their proposal and consequently allowed them to create a cremation ground thereon and, thereafter, the suit property has been used as cremation ground by the local Hindu Community and for the aforesaid reason an Ekrarnama dated 22.03.1947 was executed by the ex-landlords in respect of the suit property and its possession was delivered to the plaintiff committee and since then the plaintiff committee has been using the suit property as cremation ground for more than 12 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants. The ex-landlords never settled the suit property to anybody. The cremations on file suit property has been managed by the local Hindu Community through a committee and the plaintiff being Secretary of the committee instituted the above suit. S.A. record was wrongly prepared in the name of defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 1 being purchaser from defendant No. 2 claimed his title over the suit property in the month of Baishakh, 1983 and denied the title of the plaintiff. The plaintiff was not aware of the wrong S.A. record and deed of purchase of defendant No. 1. During S.A. survey, the Survey Officer told the plaintiff that the suit land would be recorded as Government khan land showing possession of the Committee with remarks for public use. Subsequently, defendant No. 3 son of defendant No. 1 in the year 1982 dispossessed the plaintiff and an allegation was filed before the S.D.O. Sadar, Pabna. Hence, the plaintiff Committee represented by its Secretary filed the suit.

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury, Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and Tarak Gobinda Chowdhury. Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury settled the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh (defendant No.2), who on settlement got possession of the same on payment of rents to the ex-landlord. During S.A. operation, the suit property was recorded in the mime of the, ex-landlord Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury and Dukhu Sheikh filed Objection Case No. 26 of 1960 and got S.A. record in his name and, thereafter, Dukhu Sheikh transferred the suit property by registered deed dated 03.10.1962 in favour of defendant No. 1 and delivered possession in his favour. Defendant No. 1 mutated the suit property in his name and paid rent to the government. The plaintiff never acquired any title and possession to the suit land. During liberation war the patni papers of Dukhu Sheikh were lost and thus those could not be delivered in favour of defendant No. 1.

4. Defendant No. 3 appeared and filed additional written statement and denied the claim of the plaintiff that he dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property on behalf of the defendant No. 1 and that the plaintiff filed an allegation to the local S.D.O. to that effect.

5. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna by his judgment and decree dated 11.04.2002 decreed the suit.

6. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the trial Court the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 93 of 2002 and upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record the learned Special District Judge, Pabna allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the appellate Court the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 3583 of 2005 before the High Court Division, and obtained Rule. By the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Hence, the defendants as petitioners have tiled the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

8. Mr. Md. Naser Uddin Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that Dukhu Sheikh defendant No. 2, the vendor of the predecessor of the defendants-petitioners, got the land from the jaminder Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury by way of settlement and accordingly S.A. Khatian was prepared in his name. Thereafter, defendant No. 2 sold the suit land to defendant No. 1, who mutated the land in his name and paid all taxes to the Government. The present petitioners are in possession of the suit land and are using part of it as their homestead. He submitted that the evidence of the Advocate Commissioner shows that the land was never used as a cremation ground and the ekrarnama of the Jaminder for this purpose was not acted upon and for that reason the land was returned to the original landlord, who then settled the suit land in favour of defendant No. 2 Dukhu Sheikh. He submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that the plaintiff was unable to prove his right title, possession and dispossession of the suit land by producing legally acceptable documentary and oral evidence. He finally submitted that Dukhu Sheikh, having sold the land in 1962, lost his title and possession and, hence the solenama, nadabinama and deposition of Dukhu Sheikh in Court are of no value.

9. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondents made submission in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and other connected papers on record.

<u>11. A perusal of the judgment of the appellate Court discloses that the evidence of the witnesses was not discussed whereas the trial Court observed that P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 consistently deposed that the suit land has been used as cremation ground. The trial Court further observed that defendant No. 2, who deposed as P.W.1, filed a solenama stating inter alia, that the suit land was never settled in his favour and that he did not execute any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 on 03.10.1962, but defendant No. 1 did not cross-examine hint to controvert his statement and deposition. The lower appellate Court, on the other hand, reversed the decree of the trial Court, upon relying on the deed of sale, executed by defendant No. 2 in the year 1962 and the consequent record of rights in favour of defendant No. 1. The appellate Court also relied upon the fact that the plaintiff committee neither took any step to record its name in the S.A. record nor paid any tax in respect of the suit land, nor produced any papers in respect of the use of the land as a cremation ground and thereby allowed the appeal.</u>

12. The High Court Division discussed the evidence of the witnesses and observed that among the P.Ws, P.W. 5 is a member of the Muslim community, who deposed corroborating the plaintiffs claim that the property was used as cremation ground. The High Court Division noted that D.W.4, the Deed Writer, deposed in support of the registration of the deed of 1962, but since the executant (defendant No. 2) did not admit the execution of the deed, the evidence of D.W. 4 did not help the defendants. The High Court Division also observed that there were no papers produced in support of the alleged settlement of the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh (defendant No. 2). The High Court Division concluded that mere mutation and payment of rent does not confer title to the defendants.

13. The defendants did not produce any evidence with regard to the alleged settlement of the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh by the Jamindar giving an explanation that the papers were lost during the liberation war. In the absence of such papers and in view of the positive evidence of defendant No. 2 Dukhu Sheikh that he did not get settlement of the suit property from the Jamindar, nor executed any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 in 1962, the High Court Division rightly excluded the evidence of D.W. 4; the Deed Writer. Moreover, the High Court Division observed that D.W. I himself, although alive at the time of trial and present in the Court did not depose in support of the defendants' case. The son of defendant No. 1, who deposed in Court merely stated that his father (defendant No. 1) was present in the Court, but unwell. However he did not produce any medical certificate in support. In this regard the High Court Division accepted the claim of the plaintiff that D. W. 1 did not depose because he would not wish to depose falsely. In our view the High Court Division correctly concluded that since the settlement in favour of Dukhu Sheikh does not stand, the S.A. record in his favour has no basis.

14. We find that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and does not call for any interference. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: Both these Rules were taken op for hearing together as both the Rules arose from the judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 (decree signed on 11.01.2012) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.619 of 1999 reversing those dated 31.8.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. These Rules were issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 passed in Title Appeal No.619 and 709 of 1999 by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka reversing those dated 31.8.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Facts of the ease, in brief, are that Md. Abu Patch Bhuiyan the predecessor of the petitioners herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.653 of 1980 in the Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Court, Dhaka against the defendant-opposite party for declaration of title. The said suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer as Title Suit No.360 of 1985 again the suit was renumbered on transfer before the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka as Title Suit No.77 of 1993.

4. Plaintiff's case, in-short, is that:

That the property fully described in the schedule hereinafter called the suit property originally, belonged to one Syed Ahmed Hashmi son of Hazi Ahmed of 71, Circuit House, Daily Road, Dhaka, the defendant No. 1 who became the owner of the same by way of allotment from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust by Allotment Letter No.2444 dated 26.3.1962 for a valuable consideration of Tk.I0,219/- only and accordingly he had been owning and possessing the suit property peacefully and exclusively without any hindrance from the quarter.

5. That the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi while owner in possession of the suit property in the manner aforesaid by exercising all rights of ownership and on payment of rent to the ex-land-lord in his name, the plaintiff went in to possessions of the suit property in the middle of May, 1962 and since then the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit property adversely against the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi and all other and constructed structures in some portion of the suit property and constructed boundary wall by his owls money and for his own interest and has been living thereon with all the members of his family and letting out some portion of the house to monthly eject able tenants without any hindrance or disturbance from any quarter.

6. That the plaintiff during his long peaceful and undisturbed possession since 1962 developed the suit property by spending huge amount of money and also paid rents of the suit property in his name enjoyed the profits and dealt wills the suit property openly and adversely against all others including the defendants and the plaintiff also installed the Electric and Sewerage connection in the suit property.

7. That while owning and possessing in the manner aforesaid the S.A. operation started in the area, the settlement staff surveyed the suit premises and assigned the new S.A. plot and recorded the same in the name of the plaintiff finding him in actual physical possession and on examination of his papers, but after final publication of S.A. record the plaintiff found to his utter surprise that the suit premises was wrongly recorded in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi, the plaintiff tried his best to corrects the S.A. record in his name but could not do so as all the stages of correction of S.A. record was then over. But the plaintiff has been paying rents and taxes to the Government in respect of the suit premises in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi as marfatder and had not been facing any disturbance in reaped of his peaceful possession of the suit property.

8. That in the recent R.S. operation the settlement Amin Sureveyed the suit premises and assigned the new R.S. plot and recorded the same in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi the defendant No.1 wrongly and through mistake. An objection under Rule 30 was filed by the plaintiff in the settlement department for correction of the R.S. record in his name.

9. That the plaintiff has been paying rent and taxes of the suit premises to the Government and living therein with all the members of his family without any hindrance from any quarter, the plaintiff as such acquired good title over the suit premises by adverse possession having been in peaceful and undisturbed possession for more than 12 (twelve) years.

10. That the defendant No.2 who has got no right, title, interest and possession of the suit property, with a view to grab the suit property has been giving out in the locality that he has purchased the suit property from the defendant No. 1 and with this end and view lie will enter into the suit property on a good opportunity moment by force and take possession of the same and the defendant No.2 is very dangerous and notorious type of man in the society and is also bad reported man in the area and none will dare to protest against the malafide activities of the defendant No.2 out of fear of life.

11. That the defendant No.2 on 25.6.1980 at about 11 A.M. accompanied by other bad type of men in the locality attempted to enter into the suit property by force and gave out in the locality that he purchased the suit property from the defendant No.1, but due to timely intervention of the plaintiff and his men, the defendant No. 2 could not succeed in his nefarious activities an due to this a cloud has been cast upon the indefeasible right, title and interest to the plaintiff in respect of the suit property and to remove the cloud so cast a declaration of plaintiffs title from the Court in respect of the suit property is essential and as such the plaintiff has filed this suit.

12. Defendant, Syed Ahmed Hashmi contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that:

13. That the addresses of the plaintiff mentio0ned in the plaint are wrong and the plaintiff has no right and ownership in the suit property. The said plaintiff is the tenant of the defendant in the suit property at Tk.400/-.

14. That the suit property previously owned and possessed by the RAJUK and thereafter the RAJUK allotted the said suit property to the defendant paid all dues to the RAJUK.

15. That the defendant has been possessing and residing in the suit property building house therein and the suit property was recorded in the name of the defendant in the S.A. and R.S. Khatain and the defendant has been possessing the same by paying rent and khazna of the suit property.

16. That the defendant ranted the suit property to the plaintiff and made an agreement in this respect. The plaintiff was not paying the rent regularly.

17. Defendant No.3, RAJUK contested the suit by filing written statements, stating, inter-alia,

18. That the land measuring 13 katha 8 chatak situated in Gulshan Model Town. The said Syed Ahmed Hashmi got allotment of the said land on 26.3.1962 and also got building plan on 21.10.1962 but the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi did not construct any building in the suit property according to mid building plan. Thereafter RAJUK got the possession of the suit property by canceling the said building plan.

19. That the defendant No.1 had no citizenship of Bangladesh after 1972. The defendant No.1 had been possessing the said suit property illegally and there was no adverse possession in the suit property.

20. At the trial plaintiff side examined as many as 5 witnesses while one witness namely, defendant No.2 was examined as DW-2 and one witness was examined for and on behalf of defendant RAJUK as DW-1 and both the parties also exhibited some documents to prove their respective cases.

21. After hearing the argument of both the sides an on considering the evidence and materials on record the learned trial Judge, however, decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31.8.1999 (decree signed on 6.9.1999).

22. On appeal being Title Appeal No.619 of 1999 and Tide Appeal No.709 of 1999 the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka by the impugned judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 31.8.1999 passed in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 on the finding that there is no cause of action for filing the suit, the suit is barred by law, the suit is defective, inconsistent and the plaintiff side miserably failed to prove his case.

23. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. No.619 of 1999 and Title Appeal No.709 of 1999 the present petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

24. In this case before entering into the merit of the case, I feel it necessary to mention that Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners obtained both these Rules and while the matter was taken up for hearing Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed retired from the case and thereafter, Mr. Moudud Ahmed along with Mr. Syed Md. Tajrul Hossain filed a fresh power and took adjournment again and again and thereafter, on 02.7.2015 filed an application for call for the records of Title Appeal No.6I9 of 1999 and accordingly after hearing the said application was allowed by order dated 63.2015 and thereafter again the case was made ready for hearing on 5.8.2015 and thereafter on 20.8.2015 on the prayer of Mr. Moudud Ahmed again took adjournment till 26,8,2015 for the last time and on that date Mr. Moudud Ahmed again took adjournment and thereafter on 30.8.2015 Mr. Moudud Ahmed again upon referring an application for calling the record filed on 26.8.2015 submits that to proper adjudication of the matter record from the RAJUK may kindly be called for and after hearing both the sides the said application was kept with the record, as prayed for and on the prayer of Mr. Moudud Ahmed again the matter was adjourned till 6.9.2015 and on 6.9.2015 the matter was again adjourned for two days and thereafter on 8.9.2015 Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam appearing on behalf of the petitioners filed a fresh power and says that Mr. Moudud Ahmed retired from the case and Mr. Tajul Islam, however, most empathically prays for short adjoumment to do the case and thereafter finally on 13.9.2015 Mr. A. J. Mohammad All along with Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam appearing on behalf of the petitioners prays for adjournment the case till re-opening of the forthcoming vacation and after hearing both the sides the further prayer for adjournment is rejected and thereafter Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali or Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam did not turn to make their submission.

25. In this case Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed and Mr. Moudud Ahmed time to time make the submission although finally without concluding the submission they retired from the case.

26. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in both the Rules after placing the material portion from the judgments of two Courts below and other materials on record submits that the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Dhaka erred in law in setting aside the well founded judgment of the trial Court without properly considering the facts and circumstance of the case and the case made out by the petitioners that the defendant-opposite party No.2, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake party and the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land over a period of 35 years by paying all rents to the Government and as such they are entitled to get adverse possession.

27. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners at one stage, however, submits that the Court of appeal below ought to have considered that fraud vitiates everything as the appellant, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake person, who is not entitled to get any relief whatsoever and thereby fail into an error of law resulting in the error in the, decision occasioning failure of justice.

28. Mr. Mahbubey Alum, the learned Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party-Rajuk in support the Civil Revisions submits that the properly in question owned and possessed by RAJUK and according to law the plaintiff must prove more than 60 years continuous possession in the suit land in order to get adverse decree against the Government but in this case the plaintiff in the plaint taken a plea of getting possession in May, 1962, that is, admittedly below 60 years. Mr. Mahbubey Alam further submits that from a plain reading of the plaint together with the evidence of PW- 1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4 and PW-5 it is apparent that the plaintiff's suit is incompetent, baseless and frivolous in nature. Mr. Mahbubey Alam in support of his submission has relied on the decision reported in 61 DLR 430.

29. Mr. Bhobesh Chandra Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party, RAJUK in the course of his argument after placing the plaint of the case submits that the instant suit is incompetent and vexatious in nature and the plaintiff filed the suit with intent to grab the land. Finally, the learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the Court of appeal below rightly arrived at a finding that the plaintiff side neither prove any case of title nor prove their any ownership and possession in the suit land.

30. Mr. Md. Mokhlesur Rahman (Zahid), the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-opposite party No.1, Syed Ahmed Hashmi proved his ownership in the suit land by adducing evidence both oral and documentary that he got the suit land from RAJUK through lease allotment letter dated 26.3.1962 (Ext.Ta) and subsequently it was registered on 20.8.1962 being deed No.7789 dated 20.8.1962 (Ext.Neo) and tire Court of appeal below as last Court of fact factually found that the defendant Syed Ahmed Hashmi is the real owner of the suit land on getting lease from RAJUK in accordance with law. He further submits that the plea as taken by the plaintiff in the trial Court below that the instant defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake person false to the ground pursuant to order No.149 dated 19.7.98 passed by the teamed Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman further submits that the plaintiff neither made out a case of adverse possession nor in their evidence although the trial Court below abruptly decreed the suit on the ground of adverse possession and the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact rightly on assigning sound reason arrived at a clear finding that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove their any title in the suit land whatsoever. Finally, Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman submits that the plaintiff's suit is in fact incompetent, baseless, misconceived and the same is not legally tenable in law which is liable to be buried without any further delay for the ends of justice.

31. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and the learned Attorney General and Deputy Attorney General and perused the judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses and other connected papers as filed thereto.

32. Now, to deal with the contention raised by the learned Advocates for the respective parties, I feel it necessary to decide first whether the suit itself was maintainable.

33. To resolve this dispute, I feel it necessary to quote hereunder the prayer portion of the plaint in full extent. Prayer portion of the plaint roads as follows:

34. A decree declaring plaintiff's title over 16 annas share of the suit property.

35. All costs of the suit.

36. Any other ancillary relief of reliefs to which the plaintiff is legally and equitably entitled to.

37. From the above, it transpires that the plaintiff did not make any prayer for a decree of adverse possession.

<u>38. Reading the plaint as a whole, it appears that they entered into the suit land as tenant of defendant No.1, Syed Abased Hashmi and subsequently, they entered into the suit land in the middle part of May, 1962 and since then the plaintiff side owning and possessing the suit land as adversely against their landlord, Syed Ahmed Hashmi.</u>

<u>39. On scrutiny of the record, I do not find any valid ground to suggest that the plaintiff entered into the suit land as tenant under defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi in the middle part of May, 1962.</u>

40. The Court of appeal below as last Court of fact after a detailed discussion of the materials on record came to the conclusion that there was no cause of action to file the suit, the plaintiff's case is not maintainable against RAJUK according to law.

41. In coining to this finding that the said Court observed us follows:-

“বাদীপক্ষ আর্জির কোথায় ৬০ (ষাট) বছরের উর্দ্ধকাল নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে ৩নং বিবাদী ডিআইটি তথা রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের জ্ঞাতসারে বিরুদ্ধ দখলকার রহিয়াছে তাহা উল্লেখ করেন নাই। ……………বাদীর আর্জি পর্যালোচনা করিলে দেখা যায় যে, বাদী রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ বা সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমী অর্থাত যথাক্রমে ১ ও ৩ নং বিবাদী এর বিরুদ্ধে বিরুদ্ধ দখলজনিত স্বত্বের স্বপক্ষে কোন ই্তিহাস বা ঘটনা বা কোন নালিশের কারন বর্ণনা করেন নাই। বাদী যাহার বিরুদ্ধে নালিশের কারন উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন অর্থাত ২নং বিবাদী তিনি এই মোকদ্দমার বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির লীজদাতা বা লীজগ্রহিতা কেহই নহেন। বাদী ৩য় ব্যক্তি ২ নং বিবাদী এর বিরুদ্ধে নালিশের কারন উদ্ভব দেখাইয়া ১, ২ ও ৩ নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে বিরুদ্ধ দখলজনিত স্বত্বের দাবী করিয়াছেন।…………….. যেহেতু ল অব এ্যাডভার্স পজেশন এর বিধান মোতাবেক কোন ঘচনা আর্জিতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই্, কোন ঘটনার ভিত্তিতে, কিভাবে, কখন, কোথায় এই প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমীর সম্পত্তি জবরদখল করিয়াছিলেন এবং উক্তরূপ জবর দখল প্রকৃত হাশমীর জ্ঞাত ছিল তথাপিও প্রকৃত হাশমী বাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দীর্ঘ ১২ বছরে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহন করেন নাই, বাদী জোরপূর্বক হাশমীর জ্ঞাতসারে নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে ভোগ দখলকার রহিয়াছে তদ্রুপ কোন ইতিহাস বা ঘটনা আর্জিতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই, সেহেতু আর্জিতে মূল মোকদ্দমা উদ্ভবের যে কারন উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন তাহা প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমী বা রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের কোন স্বার্থ ক্ষুন্ন হয় নাই। এই মোকদ্দমা দায়েরে বাদীপক্ষের কোন নালিশের কারন উদ্ভবন হয় নাই। এই মোকদ্দমার ঘটনা ও বর্ণনা মোতাবেক রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক অচল। এই মোকদ্দমার প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমীর বিরুদ্ধে কোন নালিশের কারন বিদ্যমান নাই।”

42. These are being purely findings of fact based on proper appreciation of fact and law.

43. I find no flaw in the reasonings of the Court of appeal below. The learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka appears to have considered all the legal aspects of the case and justly set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

44. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstance of the case, it appears that the plaintiff's suit is incompetent, frivolous, misconceived and barred by law as well.

45. However, in view of the papers, lease deeds, exhibits, city survey and admitted facts it is desirable that the defendant-opposite party, RAJUK will do the needful in favour of the defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi.

46. I want to address the question raised by the plaintiff side that the present Syed Ahmed Hashmi is not a genuine Syed Ahmed Hashmi.

47. In this connection, I like to quote hereunder the material portion of the order No.149 dated 19.7.1998 which reads as follows:

“১নং বিবাদী সৈয়দ আহম্মদ হাসমি তাহা প্রমানের নিমিত্তে ১নং বিবাদির বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী ফিরিস্তি যোগে ১ নং বিবাদীর ফটো সম্বলিত যুগ্ন সচিব, মন্ত্রি পরিষদ বিভাগ কর্তৃক ১৪/৬/৯৮ ইং তারিখের জাতীয়তা সনদপত্র প্রথম শ্রেনীর ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট কর্তৃক ২/৯/৮৯ ও ৩০/৯/৭৩ ইং তারিখের হলফনামার ফটোবপি দাখিল করে বিধায় আপাতঃ দৃষ্টিতে আদালতের নিকট প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, আদালতে স্বয়ং উপস্থিত সৈয়দ আহম্মদ হাসমি-ই ১নং বিবাদী হিসাবে মোকদ্দমায় প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করিতেছে।”

48. In view of my discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant Rules must fail.

49. In the result, both the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

50. Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

case_source:
(From the Judgment and Order dated 10.05.2005 passed by the High Court Division in writ Petition Nos. 1186 and 6591 of 2004)
WITH
(From the Judgment and Order dated 12.08.2005 passed by the High Court Division in writ Petition No.6073 of 2005)
full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Fisheries and livestock and 4 other writ respondents seek leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 10.05.2005 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in writ Petition No. 1186 of 2004 (heard analogously with Writ petition No.6591 of 2004) making the rules absolute.

2. Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 989 of 2005 has been Preferred against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1186 of 2004, in making the rule absolute.

3. Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 990 of 2005 arises out of the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in making the rule absolute in Writ petition No. 6591 of 2004.

<u>4. Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 58 of 2005 at the instance of Government of Bangladesh and six others arises out of order of the High Court Division in disposing of Writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 directing the writ respondent-petitioners to pay the arrear salaries and other benefits of the writ petitioner-respondents in the national pay scale with effect from 17 March 2003.</u>

5. Civil Petitioner for leave to Appeal Nos. 989 and 990 of 2005 arising out of the same order passed by the High Court Division and Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 58 of 2005 also arising out of similar matters the three petitions are disposed of by this single order.

6. The writ petitioner-respondents moved the High Court Division in writ petition No. 1186 of 2004 challenging order dated 22.11.2003 (annexure-G to the writ petition) and for a direction to include the writ petitioners in the revenue budget with continuity of service and other attended benefits.

7. The writ petitioner-respondents of writ Petition No.6591 of 2004 moved the High Court Division challenging the legality of order dated 14.05.2003 (annexure-J to the writ petition) and for a direction to absorb them in revenue set up with continuity of service and other attended benefits.

8. In writ petition No.6073 of 2005 leading rise to Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 58 of 2005 the writ petitioners filed an application for direction upon the writ respondents to pay arrear salaries and other benefits to them and in all the writ petitions the High Court Division granted interim orders giving the directions as prayed for.

9. Hence are these petitions.

<u>10. There is delay of eight days in filing Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 58 of 2005 which is condoned.</u>

11. The respondents in Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 989 of 2005 in their application under article 102 of the Constitution stated that they were in the service of the Government in the 1st and 2nd livestock development projects since 1977 and were guided by recruitment rules approved by Chief Martial law Administrator through memo dated 16.10.1986 which is materially identical with the provision of Non-Gazetted Employees (Dept. to livestock Service) Recruitment Rules, 1985 and that in the project proforma of the project in question it was clearly shown that out of 1552 recruited employees, 1487 officers and staffs would be transferred to the revenue budget on completion of the project and that the Establishment Division sent recommendation of absorbing 854 posts including its incumbents with a condition that 170 employees would be directly transferred to the revenue budget and remaining 684 personnel would be transferred to the revenue budget by surrendering same number of vacant post from the revenue budget of Ministry of fisheries and in the meantime some of them already have been transferred to different revenue posts by the ministry of fishery and now 815 officers and staff are serving in the revenue set up while the petitioners have been waiting for regularization in revenue budget and that the ministry of finance issued circular for transferring 544 out of 815 posts in the revenue budget on certain per-conditions and being aggrieved by the said circular the writ petitioners preferred the above writ petitions and obtained rule.

12. In Civil petition for leave to appeal No.990 of 2005 the respondents stated in the writ petition that they were appointed by the Department of Bureau of Manpower, Employment Training, in short, BMET in 1st phase of a development project in the year 1988 and then transferred to 2nd phase of the same project in 1995 and that the project proforma of the project assured the employees of the project that on completion of the project the officers and staff of the project would be automatically transferred to revenue budget and will be regularized and the ministry of establishment made recommendation to transfer the officers and staff to revenue budget and agreed to absorb the petitioners on condition of surrendering 187 vacant posts of the BMET and the review committee of the ministry of finance recommended the petitioners to be absorbed in the revenue set up and that while the petitioners were waiting for regularization in the revenue set up, the secretary committee expressed their inability to absorb the petitioners in the revenue budget through memo dated 03.04.2003 in pursuance of which the petitioners services have been terminated by the BMET with effect from 03.04.2003 and hence they felt constrained to file the writ petition.

13. Both the writ petitions were contested by the Government stating, inter-alia, that although the ministry of Finance decided to transfer the post to revenue budget surrendering same number of vacant post and although such post was abolished by the ministry of manpower yet the sachib committee in the meeting held on 17.03.2003 did not find any reason to transfer those posts to the revenue budget and accordingly refused to accept the proposal of the Administrative ministry to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue budget and that the Sachib committee is entitled to formulate any policy for the requirement of manpower and the leave petitions having no substance the rules are required to be discharged.

14. Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 58 of 2005 the writ petitioners alleged that they entered into the Service of the republic in a development project in 1988 and 1995 under the department of the Bureau of manpower, employment and training and in the project proforma it was provided that after completion in the project they would be transferred to revenue budget and that to facilitate absorption of the petitioners, the Administrative ministry of the petitioners, ministry of planning, Ministry of Establishment and standing Committee on Finance Ministry gave their full consent to absorb the services of the petitioners in the revenue set up and that while all steps were taken and hurdles were overcome to finally transfer them in the revenue set up Sachib committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary expressed inability to transfer the services of 187 posts to revenue set up without assigning any reason and as such they felt constrained to institute the writ petition.

<u>15. In the aforesaid writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 the writ petitioners filed an application before the High Court Division praying for direction upon the respondents to pay their arrear salaries and other benefits. The High Court Division by order dated 21.08.2005 allowed the prayer directing the writ respondents i. e. the petitioners herein to pay their salaries as prayed for.</u>

16. In support of the petitions Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney General appeared for the petitioners.

17. Mr. Abdur Rob Chowdhury, learned Counsel represented the respondent Nos.1-8 in Civil petition for leave to appeal Nos. 989 of 2005 and 990 of 2005 and respondent Nos.3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 20 and 21 in Civil petition for leave to appeal No.58 of 2005 and submits that the writ petitioners are legally entitled to be absorbed in the revenue set up as in the project proforma it was provided that after completion of the project they would automatically be absorbed in the revenue set up and mores the Ministries of establishment and finance duly recommended their absorption in the revenue budget and as such the High Court Division made the rule absolutes in writ petition Nos.1186 of 2004 and 6591 of 2004.

18. He further submits that considering the facts and circumstances and the judgment passed by the High Court Division in the aforesaid two writ petitions, the learned Judges of the High Court Division passed the impugned order on 21.08.2005 in Writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 giving the directions as prayed for and the aforesaid judgments and orders of the High Court Division do not call for any interference.

<u>19. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney General on the other hand submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider the fact that as the writ petitioners appointment was time bound under the appointment letter, any alleged internal consideration about the regularization cannot make any legitimate expectation in the mind of the petitioners that their regularization in the revenue budget is guaranteed, and unless by any instrument of correspondence the government manifest its promise, on supposed violation of the same can be imposed upon the government.</u>

20. He further submits that the regard being had to the fact that as the Government has no lack of authority in imposing pre-condition for the purpose of regularization in the revenue budget and so far as the creation of post in the revenue budget the Government has the discretion either to create of not to create post, which Government exercises on the basis of requirement and the court has no jurisdiction to compel the Government to create post in the revenue budget by applying the legitimate expectation of the writ petitioners and the principle of promissory estopple.

21. He thereafter submits that sometimes infrastructures along with manpower of Development project are transferred to revenue budget after completion of the project. This is done purely on the necessity of potentiality and fund availability of the Government and in this case the project was taken afresh in the 2nd phase.

<u>22. Lastly he submits that the writ petitioners were purely employees of the said development project for the fixed period of the project and with the completion of the 1st phase of the project the services of the petitioners were terminated as per terms and conditions of their appointment in the project and as such the petitioners are on longer regular employees of the Government.</u>

23. The submissions made on behalf of the petitioners in all the three petitions merit consideration.

24. Leave is, therefore, granted in all the petitions to consider the same.

25. The petitioners are permitted to prepare paper book out of court in accordance with rules.

26. Parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of appointment till disposal of the appeals.

27. The petitioners are directed to make the appeals ready for expeditious hearing within 6 (six) months.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 16-11-94 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No 765 of 1990)
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.:- This appeal by leave by defendant Nos. 1 and 3-appellants is from the judgment and order dated 16-11-93 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 765 of 1990, making the Rule absolute, thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 31-1-90 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Feni in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1986 dismissing the plaintiff respondent's Suit and reversing those dated 30-1-86 passed by the learned Munsif, Dagan Bhuiyan, District Feni in Title Suit No. 153 of 1984, decreeing the suit.

2. The plaintiff respondent filed the suit for declaration of title to. 1¼ acres of land (Schedule-ka) out of a total of .7 acres of land in khatian No. 5, plot No. 202 of Mouza 171 Dagan Bhuiyan (Schedule-kha) and for recovery of possession thereof. It is the case of the plaintiff that Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali, two brothers, by an amicable family partition arranged that Hamid Ali will get .7 acres of land in plot No. 202, khatian No. 5 (Schedule-kha) and other lands and that Azhar Ali will get .7 acres of land in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 both of Mouza Dagan Bhuiyan. Accordingly Azhar Ali while in exclusive ownership and possession of his allotted share sold his entire share in khatian No. 3 to Sirajul Haque and divested himself of all interests therein. Hamid Ali sold the entire .7 acres of land in plot No. 202 to his son Bashirullah by a registered deed dated 23-3-53. Bashirullah in his turn sold. 3½ acres out of .7 acres of land to his brother Hafizullah by a registered deed dated 26-10-60. Thereafter both bashirullah and Hafizullah sold the entire .7 acres of land to the plaintiff and his mother Hashmater Nessa by a registered deed dated 15-2-65. After the death of the plaintiff's mother the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the Schedule Kha land as her only heir. The Schedule kha land was originally anal land which the plaintiff converted into a bhiti land. He has constructed a kitchen in the bhiti and has stored some bricks and other house building materials. One Azizul Haque is occupying a portion thereof as a tenant under the plaintiff, the remaining land being in the khas possession of the plaintiff. On 16-12-78 defendant No. 1, a son of Azhar Ali, in the absence of the plaintiff, dispossessed him from the kutcha room in the north eastern portion of Schedule kha land measuring 1¼ acres which is the suit land the M. R. O. R. khatian has been prepared in the name of the plaintiff's vendor Bashirullah. The plaintiff has mutated his name and has been paying rent. The defendants have no right, title and interest in .7 acres of land of khatian No. 5. Hence the suit.

3. Defendant No. 1 alone and defendant Nos. 2 and 5-7 together filed separate written statements and denied the plaintiff's case. They admitted that there was an amicable partition between the two brothers Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali and that Azhar Ali got in his share .7 acres of land in plot No. 197 in khatian No. 3, but it is their common case that Hamid Ali was given .7 acres of land in plot No. 192 of khatian No. 46 of the same Mouza and Hamid Ali subsequently transferred his entire share of .7 acres in khatian No. 46 to one Abdul Gani who made a structure on that land and let out to the Sub-Registrar's office of Dagan Bhuiyan. Defendant No. 1 stated in his written statement that his father Azahar Ali had. 3½ acres of share in plot No. 202 which he transferred to defendant No. 1 and his 5 brothers by two deeds of Hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 14-11-60 and 17-11-60. The six brothers raised the land, constructed a kutcha house and have been conducting therein the business of selling pan and firewood's since long. The plaintiff has not constructed any kutcha house on the north eastern corner of the plot. He has not stored any bricks there. No person called Azizul Huq has any construction there. There has been a fraudulent and wrong recording of rights in the recent khatinas. It is stated by defendant Nos. 2 and 5-7 in their written statement that .7 acres of land of plot No. 202 of khatian No. 5 (schedule kha) remained in the ejmali of Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali. Hamid Ali has no saleable interest in the land of khatian No. 5, plot No. 202 beyond his 8 annas interest i.e. 3½ acres. The plaintiff or his vendors Bashirullah and Hafizullah were never owners and possessors of more than 3½ acres of land in plot No. 202. The plaintiff is not entitled to any decree in the present suit. His remedy lies in a suit for partition seeking separate saham of his own portion of plot No. 202. The present suit is a test case to dislodge the defendants right, title and interest by way of making a foray into 1¼ acres out of .7 acres of land of plot No. 202.

4. The plaintiff examined 8 witnesses and the defendants examined 7 witnesses and both sides exhibited various documents.

The trial Court found title in favour of the plaintiff on consideration of Hamid Ali's document of sale to his son Bashirullah (Ext. 2(a) Bashirullahs's transfer of 3½ acres of land to his brother Hafizullah (Ext.2) and Bashirullah and Hafizullah's transfer of .7 acres of land to the plaintiff and his mother Ext. 2(B). The trial Court also found that the S.A. khatian (Ext.B) stands in the name of the plaintiff's vendor Bashirullah. It also found that the plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government by rent receipts (Ext. 3 series). Series of kabalas Ext. 5A to 5E show that Azhar Ali and his heirs sold away all the .7 acres of land which Azhar Ali obtained by way of partition in plot No. 197 of khatian No. 3. The trial Court also considered the case of the plaintiff's possession and subsequent dispossession and found that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case.

5. The appellant Court below found that there was no dispute between the parties that Azhar Ali got in his share .7 acres in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3. The dispute is whether Hamid Ali got .7 acres in plot No. 202, khatian No. 5, as claimed by the plaintiff or .7 acres of land in plot No. 192 No. 46, as claimed by the defendants Khatian No. 46 was exhibited by the plaintiff. The appellate Court below found that the plaintiff could not give any personal knowledge of the amicable partition and P.W. 3 Hafizullah and P.W. 8 Bashirullah also could not give proper relevant answers relating to partition in their cross-examination. The appellate Court below found that in khatian No. 46 there are 2.58 acres of land and Azhar Ali is the owner by purchase in respect of .83 acres of land therein. In this khatian Hamid Ali had no ownership. The appellant Court below noted the case of the defendants that Hamid Ali obtained .7 acres of land from khatian No. 46, plot No. 192. P.W. 8 Bashirullah, son of Hamid Ali admitted in his cross-examination that his father Hamid Ali used to possess .7 acres of land of khatian No. 46, plot No. 192 and that the said land is now being possessed by Abdul Gani. That is precisely the case of the defendants and the appellate Court below found that this admission by P.W. 8 weakened the case of the plaintiff The appellate Court below then considered Ext. 5 series, which were earlier considered by the trial Court and found that by Ext. 5 series the sons of Azhar Ali sold the land of plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and also other lands of khatian No. 46 to various persons. In view of the fact that the defendants admit Azhar Ali's share in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and in view of the fact that Azhar Ali had independent title to .83 acres of land in khatian No. 46 the appellate Court below, contrary to the finding of the trial Court, found that Ext. 5 series do not support the plaintiff's case at all. The appellant Court below also held that since there was no partition by metes and bounds the recording of the land of khatian No. 5 in the name of Bashirullah and the mutation of it in favour of the plaintiff does not create any presumption. The defendants title thereto have not been injured thereby.

6. The appellant Court below also discussed the plaintiff's evidence on possession and dispossession and found that the plaintiff has not been able to prove his case in this respect as well. As such the trial Court's decree was interfered with and the suit was dismissed.

7. In revision the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division disposed of the judgment of the lower appellate Court in the following terms:-

The learned appellate Court as it appears from his judgment without considering the evidence either the documentary evidence or the oral evidence abruptly came to the conclusion that the plaintiff failed to prove his title. The learned Judge also failed to consider the evidence as to possession and dispossession. The suit being a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession, the learned Judge ought to have considered the evidence relating to title as well as possession and further the act of dispossession so as to pass a finding as to pass a decree or dismissing the suit. Non consideration of vital evidence relating to possession and dispossession affected the decision of the learned Judge materially and this error has occasioned a failure of justice. The finding arrived at by the trial Court having not been adverted, the judgment complained of is not a proper judgment for reversal as such is liable to be set aside.

8. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the High Court Division interfered with the findings of fact of the Court of appeal below, the last Court of fact, without considering the evidence on record and erroneously held that the Court of appeal below abruptly came to the conclusion that the plaintiff failed to prove his title.

9. Mr. Moksudur Rahman, learned Advocate for the appellants, has taken us through the judgment of the lower appellate Court and submitted that the court of appeal below has exhaustively considered both the oral and documentary evidence. The lower appellate Court's conclusion that the plaintiff failed to prove his title was not abrupt at all rather it is the finding of the High Court Division which is abrupt. He also pointed out that the appellate Court below fully considered the evidence as to possession and dispossession.

10. Mr. Khandkher Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondents has taken us through both the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate Court below. He could not show from the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate court below. He could not show from the judgment of the trial Court that the finding of title in favour of the plaintiff has been arrived at after considering the plaintiff's case on khatian No. 5 and the defendants case on khatian No. 46. Also he could not show that the trial Court at all adverted to the bone of contention between the parties, namely, whether Hamid Ali obtained in his share land from khatian No. 5 or from khatian No. 46. The trial Court seems to have decided the plaintiff's title in khatian No. 5 by finding that Azhar Ali and his heirs exhausted by sale his share in plot No. 197 which does not establish that Hamid Ali received in his share land of khatian No. 5. The trial Court has not considered the state of khatian No. 46 at al although it was exhibited by the plaintiff and has not dealt with the admission of P.W. 8 Bashirullah that his father used to possess .7 acres of land in khatian No. 46 and that the said land is now being possessed by Abdul Gani which is the defendants case. Mr. Ahmed also could not show that the lower appellate Court did not consider the oral and documentary evidence and that its conclusion about the plaintiff's title was arrived at abruptly. Nor he could show that the appellate Court below failed to consider the evidence as to possession and dispossession.

11. Mr. khandker Mahbubddin Ahmed then submits ultimately that if the High Court Division was not correct in its criticism of the judgment of the Court of appeal below then the matter should be remanded to the High Court Division for hearing of the civil revision afresh.

<u>12. We would have done so, had it not been for the fact that the trial Court completely missed the bone of contention between the parties and that the court of appeal below applied its mind to the real controversy between the parties and has written out an exhaustive judgment discussing both the oral and documentary evidence in details leaving no room for further improvement. It will therefore be a futile exercise to send the case back on remand to the High Court Division, particularly when Mr. Khankder Mahbubddin Ahmed could not point out any illegality occasioning failure of justice in the judgment of the lower appellate court which merits a re-consideration.</u>

13. We therefore find that the defendant appellants are rightly aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

14. The appeal is allowed with costs. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division are set aside and the judgment and decree dated 31-1-90 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Feni in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1986 are affirmed.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J : This appeal at the instance of 44 plaintiffs directed against judgment and decree dated 23.07.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong allowing application under Order VII Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure thereby rejecting the plaint of Other Suit No. 65 of 2004 as barred under section 23 of Artha rin Adalat Ain 2003, Act 8 of 2003.

2. Plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit praying for decree as,-

“(ক) তপশীল সম্পত্তি এবং উহাতে স্থিত সকল গ্রহাদি বাদীগনের স্বত্বীয় ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দিতে।

(খ) তপশীল সম্পত্তিতে ১নং বিবাদীর কোন স্বত্ব সামিত নাই ছিল না মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

(গ) তপশীল সম্পত্তি সম্পর্কে ৩নং বিবাদী বরাবরে ১নং বিবাদীর ০৬/০১/৯৬ ইংরেজী তারিখে সম্পাদিত কথিত এবং উক্ত তারিখে রেজিস্ট্রীকৃত ৩২ নম্বর যু্ক্ত বন্ধকী দলিল জাল, জালিয়াতি, ফেরবীও তঞ্চক এবং বাতিল ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

(ঘ) তপশীল সম্পত্তি সম্পর্কে ৩নং বিবাদীর বরাবরে ১নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক গত ০৬/০১/১৯৯৬ ইংরেজী তারিখে সম্পাদিত কথিত এবং উক্ত তারিখে রেজিষ্ট্রীকৃত ৩২নং বন্ধকী দলিল প্রদানের ১নং বিবাদীর কোন স্বত্ব সামিত্ব এবং অধীকার নাই মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

<u>9. Learned Judge took view that the suit is barred as per provision of section 23 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and plaintiffs could challenge the decree under section 32 of the said Ad. In rejecting the plaint, learned Judge relied on the decision of 44 DLR (AD) (1992) 260 wherein the Appellate Division held that, if any remedy is ordinarily available under both general law and special law, the remedy prescribed by the special law Must be sought in exclusion of the one available under the general law."</u>

10. Now, let us proceed with our judgment.

<u>11. This appeal the question calls for determination as to whether provision of Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable or not Learned Judge took view that the suit is clearly barred by special law, as such, the suit cannot proceed as special law provide remedy. It is to be mentioned that the application filed by defendant Nos. 2-3 did not specify under which provision/sub rule of rule 11 of Order VII the suit is barred but on a reading of the judgment it appears that learned Judge took the view that suit is barred under provision of sub rule (d) of rule 11 of Order VII wherein in the law is that plaint if barred by any law, it shall be rejected. It is settled by different decisions of the Appellate Division that if application does not specify under what provision of law, the application is made court is not bound to tress out the clause, fit the application with that clause and reject the plaint on taking into consideration of the facts of the case.</u>

<u>12. On a reading of the relief claimed in the suit, we have seen that plaintiffs did not challenge the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 03 of 2002. If we consider the case of defendant in its true perspective then best case for defendant No. 3 and 4 is that suit is barred by law. The plaintiffs are 3rd party as they are not in any manner or in any form before the Artha Rin Adalat. Let us tee what are the remedies available to a 3rd party who is stranger to the proceeding or whether any remedy provide to a stranger or 3rd party of a suit of Artha Rin Adalat. As per section 6(5) of the Act, the presence of 3rd party can be seen as mortgagor or guarantor i.e. they in this and that forum are within the frame of the suit i.e. these two categories of 3rd party in framing of the suit in any forum be before the Adalat  as such these two categories of 3rd  party are not stranger to the suit or proceeding. Section 32(1) provides for filing objection by 1st  party, without specifying whether mortgagor or guarantor against execution proceeding without going for further litigation against debtor. Section 32(2) if read with Section 6(5) then it only fix either mortgagor or guarantor, not any stranger as they are not involve in the matter in any capacity. Section 36(1) of the Act relating to a stranger 3rd party where this 3rd party stranger has given relief for realising money from the debtor through the execution proceeding. In the instant case- 44 plaintiffs have filed the suit primarily for a decree of title as their properties were given mortgage by a single person and according to the plaintiffs, this single person has no title over the mortgage property. Artha Rin Adalat no where provide for deciding title which is the jurisdiction of civil court alone. It is the settled principle of law that plaint is to be rejected only on reference to the plaint or on reading of the plaint if it is found that plaint has come within any of the sub-rule of rule 11 of order VII of the Code then the plaint 'shall' be rejected. It may be said that on a meaningful, not formal, reading of the plaint if it is manifestly vexations and meritless, not disclosing a clear right to sue, then in exercise of Rule 11 of Order VII of the Code , taking care of the ground mentioned therein is fulfilled, plaint can be rejected. In the instant suit plaint does not disclose any such defect to be throttled before born.</u>

13. Learned Judge took the view that suit is barred as per section 20 of the Act.

14. From the discussion made herein above we are of the view that this provision of law has been misapplied by the learned Judge because Artha Rin Adalat is vested with pleanary jurisdiction for realising money of the financial institutions, it has no jurisdiction to decide title of the land involved in the suit. It is special law for limited purpose. Section 20 of the Act relates to parties to the suit, section 32 relates to stranger, who has a claim over the money, nothing more, nothing less. It is seen from the Commissioner's report that plaintiffs possessing the suit land. It is also seen that plaintiffs constructed even 5 storied buildings over the suit land before mortgage given by defendant No. 1. It also appears that plaintiffs mortgaged the schedule property to different financial institutions and repay the loan. It appears that some documents have been produced by hand from Bank relating to the suit land, clause 10 of the mortgage deed empower the Bank official to inspect the mortgage property, which from the foregoing fact, has not been done as if the Bank official inspect the mortgaged land then they would certainly found that defendant No.1 did not possess the mortgaged land, rather as per Advocate Commissioner's report, plaintiffs' possession would be found. Section 20 of the Act cannot be invoked by a stranger, it only relates to the parties to the suit.

15. Learned Judge was of the opinion that plaintiffs can get remedy under section 32 of the Act. Section 32 of the Act is as follows:-

“অর্থঋন আদালতের ডিক্রী বা আদেশ হইতে উদ্ভুত জারী মামলায় কোন তৃতীয় পক্ষ দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির আইনের বিধানমতে দাবী পেশ করিলে, আদালত প্রাথমিক বিবেচনায় উক্ত দাবী সরাসরি খারিজ না করিলে, ডিক্রীদার অনুর্ধ ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে উহার বিরুদ্ধে লিখিত আপত্তি দায়ের করিয়া শুনানী দাবী করিতে পারিবেন।”

(২)উপধারা মতে দাবী পেশ করিবার ক্ষেত্রে, দরখাস্তকারী, ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের অথবা ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের আংশিক ইতিমধ্যে আদায় হইয়া থাকিলে অনাদায়ী অংশের, ১০এর সমপরিমান জামানত বা বন্ড দাখিল করিবে এবং অনুরুপ জামানত বা বন্ড দাখিল না করিলে উক্ত দাবী অগ্রাহ্য হইবে।

16. It is true that stranger 3rd party could came before the court under this Act but it appears that 10% of decreetal amount ought to be deposited but this provision is not applicable to the plaintiffs as the suit was filed for declaration of title. Even though, why plaintiffs would pay such huge amount of money as plaintiffs case is that they did not mortgaged the property and when 44 plaintiffs are owner of the property, how a single person could mortgage the entire property. As such, the facts of the instant suit requires evidence as per Order X of the Code to settle the dispute. When evidence is required then trial is to commence and when trial is required, plaint can not be rejected.

<u>17. The learned Judge rejected the plaint taking view that there is complete ouster of jurisdiction of Civil Court. We have also seen that plaintiffs are neither loanee nor mortgagor but their property was given mortgage by defendant No. 1 of which defendant No. 1 has no title. Plaintiffs chosen their forum as they cannot invoke the jurisdiction of Artha  Rin Adalat as plaintiffs do not fall any of the category of the parties who can invoke jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat. On the question of jurisdiction one must refer to the substance of the matter and not to the forum of the suit. But to find out the jurisdiction of the court it is to be looked in to as to whether relief claimed by the plaintiffs can be awarded by the court. If plaintiffs can established the facts then plaintiffs can get relief from forum chose otherwise the suit would be dismissed. Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowered civil court to entertain suit of civil nature. The fact of each of the suit, speaks whether civil court has jurisdiction or not. Artha Rin Adalat Ain as special statute provided special measure to the parties who can invoke provision of the Act. Under Artha Rin Adalat Ain only financial institutions can institute a suit against loanee and guarantor or mortgagor not anyone for realizing money and not to decide any other claim. It has been established that civil courts have jurisdiction to see if the statutory authority has acted in conformity with the provisions of the statute. Civil courts have always the jurisdiction to determine whether a court of special jurisdiction is acting in accordance with law or within the limits prescribed by law or in conformity with the fundamental principles of judicial procedure as such determination in. effect amounts to determining the extent to which the jurisdiction of the civil court is ousted. It is well settled that ouster of jurisdiction is of no avail in case of coram non judice or without jurisdiction or where the provisions of the Act containing the ouster clause have not been complied with, In the case of I3angladesh Shilpa Rin Sangshtha-Vs-Rahman Textile Mills Ltd and others, 51 DLR (AD) 221 majority view is that suit having been filed before civil court cannot proceed but the minority view which according to me took correct view held as,-</u>

<u>"Plaints and the prayers of both the suits show that the plaintiffs have disowned liability of loan alleging re-payment of the same by the BTMC on their behalf and asserted that the properties concerned were not mortgaged or hypothecated with the Sangstha and that the action taken by the Sangstha was malafide. It has to be noticed that there has been no provision for appeal or no forum provided in the Order for redress of genuine grievances of anybody or person when injustice is perpetrated on them. It cannot be imagined that such a body or person should be precluded from receiving assistance from a Court of law, Civil Court is a Court of ultimate jurisdiction, and in cases where no other remedy is provided for, the door of the civil court should not be closed and hermetically sealed against one who has been subjected to injustice. In the view I have taken of the legal position I am constrained to find hat in the instant case the civil Court has jurisdiction to entertain the plaints. The correctness of the allegations can be resolved only at the trial."</u>

18. Similar view as taken by the minority that majority view also get support from the case of Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha-Vs-Azir Uddin Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 96 and also from the case of Delwar Coil Foam Industries Ltd vs. Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Shangstha and others, 1991 BLD 317. In the case of blur Mohammed vs. M. Ahmed 39 DLR (AD) 1 it is held that "This is a well-known proposition of law which this court has yet no occasion to depart from or express any disagreement with it. The point, however, it whether any bar of suit imposed by the legislature can be disregarded to make such suit, which is so barred, maintainable in order to try an issue on malafide alleged M the plaint, it may, at least in some cases, be seen that hardship, or even injustice, may result if, in spite of evident truth in the allegation of male fide, the suit is held to be not maintainable because there is a bar against such suit in the statute concerned, But, seeker of justice in a court of law should become aware, if not already so, that justice is done according to law. A Judge may have sympathy for a litigant's suffering due to technicalities of law made by the legislature still in view of the express legislative intention, he must follow the hands-off doctrine. Otherwise chaos and anarchy would prevail leading to all sorts of complexities and confusion. Whatever the legislature says unless it is contrary to Constitution, its mandate, either express or implied, has been beyond by Court."

19. So far, we have seen the financial institutions disbursing huge loans against mortgage without any spot verification and loosing huge public money. If it is found that loan against mortgage has been disburse to a wrong title less person then the money shall be realised from the persons who involved in disbursing the money.

20. We find merit in the appeal.

21. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

22. Judgment complained is set aside. Other Class Suit No. 65 of 2004 is to be proceeded legally.

23. Send down the lower court records.

24. Communicate this order at ones.

End.
