case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 26.07.2004 passed by the High Court Division in E. A. No. 54 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Md. Mulammel Hossain J.:- This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.07.2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in F.A. No. 54 of 1999 affirming those dated 28.10.1998 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 102 of 1992 decreeing the suit. 

2. Facts involved in this case, in short, are that the plaintiffs-respondents instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 102 of 1992 in the Court of Sub-Ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka praying for declaration that the "Ka" schedule property as Debutter Property and the registered deed dated 3.01.1977 as described in the "Kha" schedule is illegal, collusive, null and void impleading the appellants as principal defendants. 

3. The case of the plaintiff-appellants, in short, are that the suit property measuring .71 acres of land appertaining to three plots in C.S. Khatian Nos. 456 and 458 of Mouza Gopar, Police Station Keranigonj, District-Dhaka as morefully described in the schedule to the plaint was correctly recorded in the name of the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi was its shebait and accordingly the impugned C.S. Khatians were prepared and finally published in the name of Deity. Hari Priya Baisnabi alias Dukhi Baisnabi as the Shebait of the deity constructed homestead in the suit land to perform the religious rites of the Bigraha. On the death of Hari Priya Baisnabi the religious minded persons requested the predecessors of the respondents Khapa Chan& Bairagi to perform the religious rites of the deity. Accordingly Khapa Chand Bairagi performed the religious rites of the Deity residing right in the suit property. The S.A. Khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant-appellant and finally published; that the local people were not aware about the wrong recording of S.A. Khatian. So they could not file any objection; that in 1970 the local people filed a Miscellaneous Case under Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for correction of the S.A. Khatian in the Court of the Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka (now Assistant Judge) against Khepa Chand Bairagi which was subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution; that after the death of Khepa Chand Bairagi his two sons did not create any hindrance in the performance of the religious rites of the Deity that the local people came to know that the sons of Khepa Chand Bairagi are trying to dispose of the suit property and as such on 03.05.1985 local religious minded people formed a committee to run the religious rites of the Deity; that in 1987 one Kebel Chandra Sarker, General Secretary of the Committee filed a petition before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Keraniganj for correcting the S.A. Khatian in the name of the Deity and on that petition Mutation Case No. 1002/87-88 dated 28.10.1987 was started and the S.A. record was corrected by mutating the suit property in the name of the Deity. But the defendant-appellants raised an objection for cancellation of the said mutation case before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Keraniganj claiming their title in the suit property and that Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 was restored; that subsequently all the mutation cases were disposed of in favour of the defendant-appellants.

4. The defendant-appellants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made by the plaintiffs-respondents contending, interalia, that the suit property measuring 35 decimals of land was recorded in the name of the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha as a rent receiver and one Hari Priya Baisnabi as its Shebait, possessed the same as rent free tenant and .35 acres of land in plot Nos. 151 and 153 under C.S. Khatian No. 458 was recorded in the name of Kunju Bihari. Mondal; that Hari Priya Baisnabi used to reside in the suit land; As she became old and was unable to move she brought Khepa Chand Bairagi to reside in the suit property who used to deal with harbal medicine and that in 1948 Hari Priya Bisnabi died and after her death her only heir Khepa Chand Bairagi inherited the suit property and possessed the same along with the members of his family running harbal medicine business there-in; that prior to that there was no Deity in the suit property and the C.S. recorded bargader also did not possess the same; that after whole sale acquisition the suit property vested in the Government and thereafter in 1951 Khepa Chand Bairagi took pattan of the suit land in his name correctly and possessed the same as his own property; that he never performed any religious rites of the Deity; that on 31.01.1977 Khepa Chand Bairagi transferred the suit property by deed of gift in favour of his two sons and wife-defendant-appellants and mutated their names vide Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 dated 26.11.1984 and paid rent to the Government; that on 03.01.1990 these defendant-appellants came to know that their mutation case has been cancelled and the Khatian has been restored; that the plaintiff-respondents filed Review Case No. 76/90-91 against which the defendant-appellants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 1992 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and the mutation cases were restored; that the plaintiff-respondents preferred appeal which was disallowed on 04.04.1993; that the plaintiff-respondents in collusion with some local notorious persons forcibly dis-possessed the defendant-appellants from 5'X6' yards of land of the suit property and that they installed a Deity there but in fact in the suit property there was never any Deity; that the suit property is the paternal property of the defendant-appellants. 

5. The suit was decreed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka on 28.10.1998. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and degree dated 28.10.1998 (Decree signed on 08.11.1998) passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka the defendant-appellant preferred First Appeal No. 54 of 1999 before the High Court Division and a Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned Judgment and decree dated 26.07.2004 dismissed the first appeal and affirmed those passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka. 

6. The defendant-appellants as petitioners being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 26.07.2004 passed by the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 1476 of 2004 before the Appellate Division. 

7. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the right to a decree to a plaintiff in a suit for declaration arises  Only when he is within limitation pre-scribed for the purpose in the Limitation Act and that the instant suit being for a declaration of title on cancellation of the document for transfer of the property in the suit and in the circumstances of the case the provision of Article 92 of the Limitation Act is applicable in the case and the cause of action arose from the date of definite knowledge of the plaintiff in respect of the impugned document being available to him in 1962 and he filed the case for correction of the record of right already being prepared in the name of the transferee defendant petitioner but the suit filed on 20.06.1992 is obviously barred by limitation. The learned Counsel further submitted that the gift by Shabait to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 being to persons in line of succession to the office of Shebait being valid in law, the Courts below committed illegality iii declaring the said gift Ext. Cha, executed on 13.01.1977 to be void holding the same to be a Kabala and the instant suit having been filed on 20.06.1992 which on its face is barred by law of limitation. 

8. Mr. Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate with Mr. N.K. Saha, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record appearing for the appellants submits that the High Court Division most illegally passed the impugned judgment and decree dismissing the appeal without considering that the suit is barred by limitation. He then submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division without any valid reason opined that the alleged registered deed of gift was not a valid deed of gift admitting that the defendant-appellants have been possessing the suit land as their own property for more than 12 years. He then submits that the S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian were recorded in the name of the appellant's father and Khepa Chand Bairagi by a registered deed of gift transferred the suit property on 13.01.1977 in favour of his widow and two sons. He finally submits that present appellants have been possessing the suit land on payment of rent to the Government Sheresta and as such the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

9. Mr. Herandra Nath Nandi, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-On-Record, appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the suit property being a Debuttar Property and the appellants being not owners, Shebaits or next friend of the Deity have got no locustandi to contest the suit and prefer the appeal as they have no right, title and interest and possession in the suit land. He then submits that having regard to the facts that the C.S. Khatians were correctly prepared and published in the name of deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew I3igraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi as the Shebait and the said property belonged to Niskar Brahmmatra and completely dedicated to the plaintiff deity; that wrong recording of S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian in the name of the defendant-appellants should not cover any title to the suit property upon them and admittedly the defendant-appellant failed to show any papers showing that the suit property was vested in Government and the Government gave pattan to Khepa Chand Bairagi. He then submits that the High Court Division as a Court of Appeal rightly found that once the Debuttar Property is vested to the alter of Deity it cannot be divested and the suit property in the present case was rightly recorded and dedicated in the name of Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha. Mr. Nandi, the learned Advocate for the respondent finally submits that the 'Ka' schedule property is Debuttar Property as Vested upon the Deity and transfer of the said property by the alleged registered deed in favour of the appellants are collusive, illegal and null and void and as such the question of limitation does not arise and the suit was filed very much within the period of limitation. 

10. From the careful perusal of the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division it appears that the High Court Division found that C.S. Khatian No. 456 was rightly recorded in the name of Hari Priya Baisnabi as Shebait and the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha was the raiyat. So we cannot agree that the plaintiff Deity had rent receiving interest in the suit property. The High Court Division also rightly found that the suit land of C.S. Khatian No.458 comprising plot Nos. 151 and 153 has been recorded as Brahmatra under C.S. Khatian No. 456 and as a Shebait Hari Priya Baisnabi was in possession. It also appears that the High Court Division also found that there is no people showing that Khepa Chand Bairagi took jot pattan of the suit property in the year of 1951 but there is no paper that the property was vested in the Government and the Government gave pattan to Khepa Chand Bairagi. Once the suit property is vested in the Deity it cannot be divested and the Debutter Property under Section 415 of the Hindu Law is inalienable. The Shebait can reside for the purpose of performing religious rites and for the benefit and preservation for the Debutter Property. The learned Judge of the High Court Division rightly found that the deed of gift created by Khepa Chand Bairagi in favour of the defendants is void ability. It is well established by the Supreme Court that as a general rule of Hindu Law property given for the maintenance of religious worship is inalienable. In the case of Hunooman Persaud Vs. Mst. Babooee reported in 1856-6-MIA 393 it has been held that Shebayet has no power to alienate the Debater Property except in a case of need or for the benefit of the estate. He is not entitled to sell the property for investing the price of it to bring in an income larger than that derived from the property itself. 

11. In the case of Bishnath and another v. Sri Thakur Radha Ballabhji and others reported in AIR 1967 (S.C.) 1045 it has been held that a suit filed by an idol for declaration of its title and possession of property from a person who is in possession thereof under a void alienation, being only in the nature of enforcement of a private right by the idol and not being for any one of the reliefs found in Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, falls outside its purview and is not barred. It has further been held that when such an alienation has been effected by the she bait acting adversely to the interests of the idol, even a worshipper can file the suit, the reason being that the idol is in the position of a minor and when the person representing it leaves it in a lurch, a person interested in the worship of the idol can certainly be clothed with an hoc power .of representation to protect its interest. 

12. In the case of Pradip Kumar Chakraborty Vs. Jamila Khatun Bibi & ors reported in 51 DLR (AD) 156 the Appellate Division while referring to the decision of the case of Kishore Joo Vs. Guman Behari Joo Deo AIR 1978 All 1 wherein -it has been held that- "in exceptional circumstances persons other than a Shebait can institute a suit on behalf of an idol." has quoted with approval the following except of BK Mukherjea's book on "The Hindu Law of Religious and Charitable Trust": 
"The deity as a juristic person has undoubtedly the right to institute a suit for the protection of its interest. So long as there is a shebait in office, functioning properly, the right of the deity, as stated above, practically lie dormant and it is the shebait alone who can file suits in the interest of the deity. When, however, the shebait is negligent or is himself the guilty party against whom the deity needs relief, it is open to worshipper or other persons interested in the endowment to file suits for the protection of the debutter. It is open to the deity also to file a suit through some person as the next friend for recovery of or for other relief. Such a next friend may not unoften be a person who as a prospective she bait or a worshipper is person-ally interested in the endowment". 

13. Accordingly the Appellate Division in the aforesaid decision held that a pujari and a worshipper of the deity who has offered himself to act as next friend of the Deity can by no means be precluded from representing the Deity. 

14. In the case of Abdul Hafez and another v. Lal Meah reported in 8 BLD (HCD) 497 it has been held that if there is an entry adverse to the plaintiff he is not bound to institute suit for declaration that the entry is wrong. Such a suit will be in time if brought within 6 years of the threatened invasion. In the instant case it appears that the appellant Khepa Chand Bairagi when transferred the property the plaintiff-respondents filed the suit seeking appropriate relief as stated above. In the case of Chunnu Mia Vs. Manindra Lal Roy and others reported in 39 DLR (AD) 42 it has been held that a permanent lease or absolute alienation of debater property is beyond ordinary powers of management whether in the case of the head of a math, the shebait of a family idol or the dharma Karta of a temple, such alienation can be justified only by proof of necessity for the preservation of the endowment or institution. 

15. In the instant case admittedly the suit property was recorded in the C.S. Khatian as Debutter Property in the name of Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi. After the death of Hari Priya Baisnabi, Khepa Chand Bairagi was inducted in the suit property as Shebait and residing for the purpose of performing religious rites. Both the Courts below made concurrent findings that the defendant failed to show any document that the suit property was vested in the Government and then the Government gave pattan of the suit property in favour of Khepa Chand Bairagi in 1951. Rather it has been proved by the plaintiff-respondent that Khepa chand Bairagi was inducted in the suit property as shebait to perform religious rites of the Deity. A shebait does not acquire any title to the Debutter Property. The Debutter Property can not be alienated by him except in case of unavoidable necessity. There is no denying the fact that the shebait can reside in the suit property for the purpose for performing religious rites. It does not create any title in his favour so Khepa Chand Bairagi was not legally entitled to transfer the suit property by a deed of gift in favour Of the defendants-appellants: Accordingly both the Courts below rightly found that the said deed of gift is illegal and void abilities. We are of the view that mere recording of some ones name in the S.A. or R.S. Khatian does not create any title to the property. In the instant case the General Secretary of the Committee on behalf of the Deity has filed the suit in respect of the Debuttar Property which is very much supported by the decision of the Indian Supreme Court reported in AIR-1967(SC) 1044 and the decisions of this Appex Court reported in 39 DLR (AD) 42 and .51 DLR (AD)156. 

16. It appears that the High Court Division while dismissing the appeal found that the trial Court rightly held that the suit property having been vested in the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha became debutter property and Khepa Chan Bairagi having been inducted in the suit property as Shebait cannot alienate the said debutter property to the defendants-appellants; that the defendants-appellants being the heirs of the Shebait, Khepa Chan Bairagi, have the right of performing the religious rites of the Deity as Shebait and are entitled to retain their possession by performing the duties of the Shebait but they are not entitled to transfer the said debutter property. 

17. In the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the discussions made above we are of the view that the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and decree rightly affirmed those passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge and there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division which does not call for any interference by this Court. 

18. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 26.07.2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in F.A. No. 54 of 1999 is hereby affirmed. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 1st day of December, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.158 of 2001 with Transfer Appeal No.648 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. These two leave petitions have arisen out of the same judgment and decree dated the 1st day of December, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 158 of 2001 heard analogously with Transfer. Appeal No. 658 of 2001 allowing both appeals in part.

2. Facts giving rise to the leave petitions are as follows:

3. Respondent No. 1, Nek Parvin Islam, as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka (now Joint District Judge) for declaration of title in 2½ kathas of land described in schedule-'Ka' to the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit land) and for recovery of khas possession of the flat described in schedule-'Gha' to the plaint out of 3(three) storied building from added defendant Nos. 9-11 and for cancellation of kabala No. 11689 dated 24.09.1977 of Dhaka Sadar Sub-Registrar's Office as described in schedule-'Kha' to the plaint allegedly executed by her in favour of her father, A.K.M. Abdullah (since deceased) and her step mother, Begum Sufia Abdullah who were impleaded in the suit as defendant Nos. 1 and 3 respectively as void, illegal, collusive and inoperative.

4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that her father-AKM Abdullah purchased the suit land with his own money in the benami of her mother-Amena Khatoon, defendant No. 2 by two registered kabalas being Nos. 3660 and 3661 both dated 07.08.1967. The plaintiff was born on 01.01.1965 and the marriage of her mother with her father was dissolved mutually in 1971 and prior to that the suit land was orally gifted to her by her mother and the witnesses (names of the witnesses have been mentioned in the plaint) present at the time of making the gift took formal delivery of possession of the gifted land on her behalf; the said gift was confirmed by her mother swearing an affidavit before the Notary Public on 18.04.1971. The gift was made in presence of plaintiff’s father with his consent who is also an attesting witness in the affidavit confirming the gift. Subsequently, the plaintiffs father created a registered sale deed bearing No. 11689 dated 29.04.1977 showing transfer of the suit land along with another 2½ kathas of land belonging to one Jahanara Khatoon, defendant No. 4, i.e. in total 5(five) kathas of land, in his favour and in favour of her step mother-Sufia Khatun, defendant No. 3. The plaintiffs father got her signature in some stamp papers telling her that a power of attorney would be made for taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation for making construction on the suit land. The construction on the suit land was made by taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation; the plaintiff herself constructed the incomplete 3rd floor with her husband's money and she is living therein with her family members and her name has been duly mutated in the record of right. The plaintiff is also in possession of the northem part of the ground floor of the building. After attaining majority, the plaintiff requested her father to hand over the documents relating to her property, but on this plea and that plea, her father avoided the same. The plaintiff's mother- Amena Khatun filed Title Suit No. 420 of 1981 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which, on transfer to the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, was renumbered as Title Suit No. 181 of 1992 for declaration of her title in respect of the suit land (earlier gifted to her) without impleading her in the said suit. The suit was dismissed on the finding, inter alia, that Amena Khatun was the benamder of AKM Abdullah (the plaintiffs father) in respect of the suit land. The plaintiff came to know that her father and her step mother executed and registered 3(three) sale deeds bearing Nos. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 showing transfer of 3¼ kathas of land (each deed showing transfer of 1¼ kathas of land) in favour of defendant Nos. 6-8 and delivered possession of 3(three) rooms of the second floor and 2(two) rooms of the northern portion of the ground floor to them through tenant-defendant Nos. 9-11 who are now in illegal possession thereof without having any valid, right, title and interest therein. The defendants denied the title of the plaintiff on 15.05.1992; hence she was compelled to file the suit for the aforementioned reliefs.

5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 3, defendant No. 2 and defendant Nos. 6-8 filed separate written statements in the suit. Subsequently, defendant Nos. 6-8 along with defendant Nos. 9-11 also filed additional written statement. During the pendency of the suit, defendant No. 1 died and in his place his son-Mostaque Ahmed was substituted as defendant No. 1 (k), but defendant No.  1(a) and defendant No. 3 did not contest the suit.

6. In the written statement of defendant 1 Nos. 6-8, it was contended, inter alia, that defendant No. 1, father of the plaintiff purchased the suit land in the benami of his wife-Amena Khatun, mother of the plaintiff by kabala dated 07.08.1967 and defendant No. 4-Jahanara Khatun purchased contiguous western 02½ kathas of land by two registered kabalas of the same date from the same vendor. Defendant No. 2-Amena Khatun, mother of the plaintiff, eloped from custody of defendant No. 1 to marry one Tajul Islam leaving her in the custody of defendant No. 1 who brought up the minor plaintiff and gave marriage with one Shafiqul Islam in 1976. Defendant No. 1 married defendant No. 3, Begum Sufia Abdullah. To avoid future threat to his title in the suit land from defendant No. 2, the plaintiff, was made the owner of the suit land showing a colourable transfer by way of oral gift by defendant No. 2 and on receipt of proper consideration, the plaintiff voluntarily agreed to make a sale deed in respect of the suit land in favour of her father and step mother and accordingly, she joined her name as one of the vendors along with defendant No. 4-Jahanara Begum and transferred the suit land along with contiguous western 2½ kathas of land by a common sale deed being No. 11689 dated 20.04.1977. After the said kabala, defendant Nos. 1 and 3 obtained a revised plan from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) for construction of a building on 3¾ kathas of land out of said 5(five) kathas of land and when they proceeded for obtaining loan from defendant No. 5, House Building Finance Corporation, upon the objection raised by defendant No. 2, sanctioned loan was withheld. In the circumstances, defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 156 of 1979 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and got a decree in his favour. Then after getting loan of taka 1,76,000.00 from defendant No. 5, defendant No. 1 extended construction of the 1st floor and completed two units of the 1st floor and one unit of the 6. 2nd floor and possessed major portions of  the building through monthly tenants and allowed his daughter, the plaintiff to live in a room of the 2nd floor as a licensee and thus, while defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 3 were in possession of the building on 3¾ kathas of land, they in order to repay the loan amount sold vacant land measuring 4¼ kathas outside the building area to defendant Nos. 9 and 10 and one 1 Mohammad Yakub Ali by registered E kabala No. 4639 dated 23.12.1985 in which purchasers are in separate exclusive possession by opening separate holding number and thereafter, defendant Nos. 1 and 3 sold the remaining undivided 33/4 kathas of land and building to the defendants by three registered kabalas being Nos. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 and handed over possession of the land and building with the licensee, that is, the plaintiff to them. The defendants are the bonafide purchasers of the suit land for value without any notice of fraud committed by defendant Nos. 1 or 3 alleged by the plaintiff. The plaintiff saying no right, title and interest in the suit and being in possession in a portion of the suit land as a licensee was not entitled; to get any relief in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed.

7. The petitioners who were defendant Nos. 6-8 in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992, filed a separate suit being Tide Suit No. 255 of 1993 in the Fourth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka which on transfer to the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 28 of 1995 for declaration of title in 3¾ kathas of land and for eviction of Nek Parvin Islam, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 making the same averments as made in the written statement filed in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992. Nek Parvin Islam, plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 who was impleaded in Title Suit No. 25 of 1992 as defendant No. 1 filed written statement therein stating same facts as stated in the plaint of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992.

8. Defendant No. 2 in her written statement contended, inter alia, that the suit land was purchased in her own name by the money given by her parents by kabala dated 07.08.1967. After purchase, she developed the land by filling earth and after obtaining plan from the then DIT constructed building thereon by the money paid by her parents and brothers. The suit land was never purchased by defendant No. 1 in her benami and he never paid money for purchasing the same. The Plaintiff deposed in Title Suit No. 420 of 1991 supporting her. The plaintiff was born in 1959. As defendant No. 1 was not a man of good moral character, quarrel used to take place oft and often between herself and defendant No. 1 for which she was compelled to go for separation and subsequently married one Tajul Islam. The plaintiff was brought up in the suit land under the care of the defendant and was married to one Shafiqul Islam and they were living in the suit property as her caretaker and also as her licensee. The defendant never gifted the suit land to the plaintiff and there was no reason as well for such gift, had she any intention to transfer the suit land she would have done so by executing a registered deed. Defendant No. 1 having failed to grab the suit property of the defendant by adopting various tactics one after another, lastly created a fraudulent deed and obtained loan from defendant No. 5 illegally this was not binding upon her. The defendant had been exercising her right of possession in the suit land through her daughter and son-in-law. The plaintiff f by revising the plan of DIT constructed the first floor. The defendant never mortgaged the suit land with the House Building Finance Corporation. The plaintiff inducted one Kabirul Islam as a tenant of defendant No. 2 and he paid rents to the plaintiff as a tenant of the defendant. The sale deed dated 20.04.1977 being deed No. 11689 from the plaintiff was illegal, void and without any effect and the same was liable to be declared void and by the said kabala, defendant No. 1 did not acquire any right and title in the suit land.

9. Both suits were heard analogously and the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 (two separate decrees were drawn up and signed) dismissed Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 and decreed Title Suit No. 28 of 1995.

10. Value of Title Suit No. 28 of 1995 being taka 60,000.00 only, defendant No. 1 (Nek Parvin Islam) filed appeal: before the District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 767 of 2000 against the judgment and decree passed therein. Nek Parvin Islam being the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 158 of 2001 before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree passed therein Subsequently, Title Appeal No. 767 of 2000 was transferred to the High Court Division from the Court of the District; Judge, Dhaka and was renumbered as Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001. A Division Bench of the High Court 1 Division after hearing the appeal from original decree and the transfer appeal analogously by the impugned judgment and decree allowed both appeals in part in the following terms:

"Accordingly the First Appeal No. 158 of 2001 and the Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001 are allowed in part with cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 passed in T.S. No. 88/92 and T.S. No. 28/95 are set aside and both T.S. No. 88/92 and T.S. No. 28/95 are decreed in part. The right, title and interest of Nek Parvin Islam, plaintiff in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 and defendant No. 1(sic) Title Suit No. 28 of 1995, in respect of 2½ kathas of land corresponding to 0.0410 acres of land out of 0.0825 acres in plot No. 117(old plot No. 41/42) acquired through gift made by Amena Khatoon "in presence and with consent" of A.K.M. Ahdullah is declared to be Valid and the alleged sale of said 2½ kathas of land belonged to Nek Parvin Islam vide registered sale deed No. 3660 dated 27.4.67 and registered sale deed No. 3661 dated 7.8.67 P.S. Ramna Sadar Sub-Registrar, Dhaka each for 1¼ kathas, vide Sale Deed No. 11689 dated 29.4.77 as well as vide Sale Deed No. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 3.5.92 is declared to be illegal and void. The said Nek Parvin Islam however will have no right and title on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land but shall have possessory right because of her ownership on 2½ kathas of land. Messrs Siddiqur Rahman, Md. Sirajul Islam and Farida Yeasmin do have joint possession on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land with ownership only on the balance 1¼ kathas of land with joint possession. The respective shares in the joint possession may be determined mutually or through a proper suit in accordance with law and till then the said Nek Parvin Islam, Siddiqur Rahman Md. Sirajul Islam and Mrs. Farida Yeasmin shall continue to possess and enjoy the suit property jointly."

11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No. 158 of 2001 and Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001 defendant Nos. 6-8 have filed Civil Petitions for Leave Appeal Nos. 663 of 2009 and 664 of 2009 respectively before this Division.

12. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the leave petitioners in both leave petitions, has submitted that the High Court Division committed grave error of law in allowing the appeals in part declaring the right, title and interest of Nek Parvin Islam (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992) in respect of 2½ kathas of land (the suit land) on the basis of alleged oral gift made by defendant No. 2 of the suit and the sale deed dated 29.04.1977 being deed No. 11689 so far as , it relates to 2½ kathas of land, that is, the suit land and the sale deed Nos. 1245, 1246 1 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 3 in favour of defendant Nos. 6-8 as illegal and void inasmuch as it did not reverse the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff failed to prove her case of acquisition of title in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by her mother, defendant No. 2, who was a benamder of defendant No. 1 only; defendant No. 2 being the benamder of defendant No. 1 she was not legally entitled to make the alleged gift in favour of the defendant. He has further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in declaring the deed dated 29.04.1977 void inasmuch as the plaintiff failed to prove the allegation of fraud in executing and registering the deed by her particularly when she did not deny the fact of execution of the same. He has further submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider the admitted fact that it is the plaintiffs father who constructed the building on the suit land along with other land by obtaining loan from the House Building Finance Corporation and the plaintiff is in possession in a portion thereof as a licensee of her father in their proper perspective and thus, erred in law in decreeing the suit in part. He has further submitted that the finding of the learned Judges of the High Court Division as to the minority of the plaintiff at the time of execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977 accepting her date of birth as 01.01.1965 is not based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record particularly in the face of the evidence DW4, the mother of the plaintiff and thus fell into an error in holding that the said kabala transferring the suit land as void being hit by section 11 of the Contract Act and also the deeds of defendant Nos. 6-8 executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 3 as void.

13. On the above submissions, Mr. Mahbubey Alam prays for granting leave to appeal to the petitioners from the impugned judgment and decree to examine the points.

14. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of respondent No. 1 in both leave petitions, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division by submitting that the learned Judges approached the case from correct stand point and correctly sifted the evidence on record in holding that at the time of execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977, the plaintiff being minor, the same was void within the meaning of section 11 of the Contract Act and that the plaintiff acquired title to the suit land on the basis of the oral gift made by her mother, the ostensible owner in presence and with the consent of defendant No. 1, her father, the real owner.

15. From the impugned judgment and decree, it appears that the High Court Division formulated two points for its decision (i) whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992, who is defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 28 of 1995, is the real owner of the suit land measuring 21/2 kathas of land gifted by her mother with the consent of her father as described in schedule-'Ka' to the plaint and is in possession therein with others; (ii) whether the sale deed bearing No. 1168 dated 29.04.1977 showing Nek Parvin Islam and Jahanara Begum as the vendors in favour of AKM Abdullah and Begum Sufia Abdullah as the purchasers is valid, so far as it relates to the sale by Nek Parvin Islam in respect of 2½ kathas of land, she being minor at the relevant time.

16. In view of the pleadings of the respective parties and the findings of the trial Court, it appears to us that the High Court Division correctly formulated the points for its decision in disposing of the appeals. The High Court Division decided both points in favour of the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam. Let us see whether the High Court Division was correct in deciding the points in favour of Nek Parvin Islam in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record.

17. Admittedly, the suit land measuring an area of 2½ kathas was purchased by plaintiffs (Nek Parvin Islam) father in the benami of her mother-Amena Khatun (since divorced) by kabala dated 07.08.1967. The case of the plaintiff is that while she was minor her mother being the ostensible owner of the suit land gifted the same to her in presence of her father, defendant No. 1 and with his consent and the gift was accepted on her behalf by the witnesses present at the time of making the gift; subsequently, defendant No. 2 in support of the oral gift had sworn an affidavit before a notary public on 18.04.1977 wherein her father figured as an attesting witness. The High Court Division believed the case of the plaintiff of acquisition of title by her to the suit land on the basis of the oral gift made by her mother, the ostensible owner and also found her possession in the suit land on the basis of her own title. In coming to the said findings, the High Court Division considered 4(four) facts (a) Amena Khatun, the plaintiffs mother was the ostensible owner (b) the oral gift was made by defendant No. 2 in favour of Nek Parvin Islam with the consent of the real owner, defendant No. 1 and in his presence (c) defendant No. 1 became an attesting witness in the affidavit sworn by Amena Khatun in support of oral gift made in favour of Nek Parvin Islam and (d) in the Kabala dated 29.04.1977 allegedly executed and registered by Nek Parvin Islam, defendant No. 1, the real owner, admitted the said fact of oral gift by defendant No. 2 in favour of the plaintiff and accepting her as the owner of the suit land purchased the same from her. We find nothing wrong with the High Court' Division in taking into account the said facts in finding title of the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by Amena Khatun. Because at the time of oral gift admittedly defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 were the husband and the wife respectively and defendant No. 1, the real owner by those open overt acts gave up his right, title and interest in the suit land. In this regard, we like to put emphasis on the legal phraseology that 'one cannot approbate and reprobate.' It further appears that the plaintiff as PW1 deposed in support of her case of acquisition of title in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by Amena Khatun. PW2 Monir Hossain, a man of aged about 70 years clearly corroborated the plaintiff’s case of oral gift by her mother, defendant No. 2 by deposing that he was present at the time of making the gift. Although during pendency of the suit, plaintiffs father, AKM Abdullah died, the fact that he became an attesting witness in the affidavit sworn by Amena Khatun confirming the oral gift made by her in favour of her daughter, Nek Parvin Islam, in respect of the suit land was not denied by his legal heir, defendant No. 1(a) and defendant No. 3. Further, there being clear recitals in the kabala dated 29.04.1977 as to the fact of transfer of the suit land in favour of plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam by way of oral gift by defendant No. 2, the High Court Division rightly found that the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam acquired title therein on the basis of oral gift made by defendant No. 2. But the trial Court did not consider these facts in giving finding that the plaintiff failed to prove her case of oral gift by defendant No. 2 in respect of the suit land and thus fell into an error in dismissing the suit of Nek Parvin Islam.

18. The High Court Division in holding that at the time of alleged execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977 by the plaintiff, she was minor accepted the case of the plaintiff that she was born on 01.01.1965. In accepting the plaintiffs date of birth as on 01.01.1965 the High Court Division relied upon the birth certificate issued by the Headmistress of Siddheswari Girls High School and her testimony as PW3 (when. she deposed, she retired as the Headmistress of the School). PW3, Rahima Khatun deposed that in the School admission Register, the date of birth of the plaintiff was recorded as 01.01.1965 and she proved the birth certificate issued by her as exhibit-1(Ka). The High Court Division also relied upon an affidavit sworn by the plaintiffs mother-Amena Khatun on 02.07.1991 (exhibit-1) to the effect that she was born on 01.01.1965. Monir Hossain, PW2 aged about 70 years specifically stated in his cross-examination that in 1971 the age of Nek Parvin Islam was around 6/7 years and this clearly corroborated the birth certificate exhibit-1(Ka) and the declaration made by Amena Khatun on 02.07.1991 that the plaintiff was born on 01.01.1965. Whereas, the trial Court simply relied upon the deposition of DW4, (Amena Khatoon) mother of the plaintiff who deposed that Nek Parvin Islam was born in 1959 without considering that Monir Hossain (PW2) and Rahima Khatun (PW3) were independent witnesses and they had no reason to be partisan for the plaintiff. The trial Court also failed to consider that after Amena Khatun (DW 4) married one Tajul Islam, she filed Title Suit No. 420 of 1981 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka (on being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 181 of 1992) against defendant No. 1, AKM Abdullah for declaration of her title in the suit without impleading the plaintiff. Therefore, defendant No. 2 having set up her own title to the suit land in denial of plaintiffs title became a partisan and interested person, her evidence could not be accepted on the question of the date of birth of the plaintiff particularly when her testimony clearly contradicted the affidavits sworn by her, one giving declaration that she gifted the suit land to the plaintiff (exhibit-3) and the other declaring   the plaintiffs date of birth as 01.01.1965 (exhibit-1) and other evidence which belied the testimony of DW4 as discussed hereinbefore. The trial Court also failed to consider that the date of birth of plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam as recorded in the admission register of the School was given when no dispute as to the right to the suit land arose, so that would get preference over the assertion of the contesting party, defendant No. 2.

19. The trial Court was absolutely in error in taking the view that since in the deed, dated 24.09.1977 the age of the plaintiff was not mentioned, she was major and that had she not been major, the Sub-registrar would not have registered the kabala ignoring the evidence as discussed hereinbefore which were considered by the High Court Division. It further appears that the High Court Division in holding that the plaintiff being minor, the kabala allegedly executed and registered by her was void, relied upon a decision of the Privy Council given in the case of Ma Hnit and others-vs-Hashim Ebrahim Meter and another reported in AIR1919 (PC), 129.

20. From the above, it is clear that in holding that the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam was minor, at the time of execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977, her date of birth being 1 01.01.1965, the High Court Division clearly reversed the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff was born in 1959 and thus she was major at the time of execution and registration of the kabala. The High Court Division clearly reversed the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff failed to prove her case of oral gift of the suit land by defendant No. 2. In view of the finding of the High Court Division that the plaintiff was minor at the time of the alleged transfer of her 2½ kathas of land in the name of her father and step mother along with other 2½ kathas of land of one Jahanara Begum by the kabala dated 29.04.1977 and therefore, she could not enter into any contract for sale in view of the provision of section 11 of the Contract Act, it was not at all necessary to prove any other fact, may the fraud as submitted by Mr. Mahbubey Alam.

21. Mr. Mahbubey Alam could not show that the findings of the High Court Division, the last Court of fact as noted down hereinbefore are the result of misreading of the evidence on record or non-consideration of any material evidence or based on misconception of law.

<u>22. It being a fact that after purchase of 5(five) kathas of land by kabala dated 29.04.1977 (2½ kathas from the plaintiff and 2½ kathas from Jahanara Khatoon) the plaintiffs father made construction on the 3¾ kathas of land which included 2½ kathas of land of the plaintiff by  taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation, the High Court Division rightly declared plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam's right, title and interest in respect of 2½ kathas of land (the sui land), but she will have no right and title on the building constructer thereon except "possessory right because of her owner ship on 2½ kathas of land." The High Court Division also rightly protected the possession of the contesting defendants by observing that they "do have joint possession on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land with ownership V only on the balance 1¼ kathas of land with joint possession." We fully endorse the observations of the High Court Division that "The respective shares in the joint possession may be determined mute ally or through a proper suit in accordance with law and till then the said Nek Parvin Islam, Siddiqur Rahman, Md. Sirajul Islam and Mrs. Farida yeasmin shall continue to possess and enjoy the suit property jointly." And we further observe that if any sui for partition is filed as observed by the, High Court Division, the trial Court would consider the case of the contesting defendants that they purchased 3¾ kathas of land along with the 3(three) storied building, standing thereon, but in no case, they shall have any claim over the suit land that is, 2½ kathas of land as described in scheduled-Ka to the plaint.</u>

23. With the above observations, the petitions are dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 30 of 2005
lawyer:
Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-record ----- For the Petitioners 
Respondents ----- Not represented
parties:
Yusuf Ali and another ----- Petitioners
VS
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the D.C. Sylhet and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated January 17, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 402 of 1981)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: Delay is condoned.

2. This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment dated January 17, 2004 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 402 of 1981 disposing of the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated September 24, 1980 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1978 allowing the same upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated April 25, 1978 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 125 of 1976 dismissing the same.

<u>3. The suit was filed seeking declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for a decree of permanent injunction. It was averred in the plaint that the land in suit since petty settlement is known as Bhut Bhuti Nala and Jur Beel and was recorded in C.S. patta No. 89, that during R.S. operation the said land was recorded in the name of Loke Patni and Others as Mahal Shamil Jalkar in patta No 5, that plaintiff Nos. 1-6's predecessor Syed Alim purchased 14 annas share of the land in suit in 1955 and the rest 2 annas share was purchased by plaintiff No. 7, that although at the initial stage of survey the khatian was prepared in the name of Loke Patni and others but in the finally published khatian names of some other persons were also recorded along with the name of Loke Patni and others, that the land in suit gradually silted up and lost its original character i.e. nala and beel and thereby became fit for boro cultivation, that Loke Patni excavated a 'Khal' over the suit land for irrigation purpose and same has been recorded in Dag No. 18, that the land in suit is partly boro land and there is Government khas land by the side of the land in suit and the same has been settled with the cultivators for boro cultivation, that defendant Nos. 1-4 have been contemplating to settle the land in suit to defendant No.5, hence the Suit seeking the relief for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction.</u>

4. The suit was contested by the Government by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the land in suit is a fishery and as such on the acquisition of rent receiving interest vested in the Government and thereupon the Government is possessing the land in suit treating the same as fisheries and is leasing out the fisheries to different persons, that fringes of the fisheries are leased out for boro cultivation, that the plaintiffs' deeds are fraudulent and ante-dated, that Loke Patni and others had no saleable interest in the land in suit.

5. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record held that Ext.5 khatian shows that Loke Patni and others possessed the land in suit for use on behalf of their co-villagers and the same is Jalkar, that Ext.2 patta and Ext.5 khatian shows that only Jalkar was leased out and Exts.6 and 6(a) show that the land in suit is marshy land and thus from the said documents it is seen that the land in suit is beel land and in all probability in the fringe of the Jalkar fishery boro is cultivated, that the land in suit is not the boro land but Jalkar, that Loke Patni and others did not acquire any saleable interest in the land in suit and they had only jalker right in suit, as evidenced by Ext. c, record has been prepared in the name of the Government, that no material has been brought on record to show that after purchase in 1955 plaintiffs paid rent, that no explanation has been offered for not producing the original kabalas on the basis whereof plaintiffs are claiming the land in suit, that there is no averment in the plaint as to why the plaintiffs are not in possession of the kabalas by which they have purchased the land in suit, that at the time of trial attempt was made through the deposition of P.W.2 that the kabalas were stolen but as there was no such case in the pleading the said deposition can not be taken into consideration, that averments made as to cause of action are not true, that in the totality of the facts it appear that Ext.4 by which plaintiffs said to have purchased the land in suit is not genuine, that from Exts. (a) and (b) it is seen that the land in suit is fishery and the Government auctioned the same and thus it is seen that the land in suit is not boro land, that plaintiffs have not acquired any right, title and interest in the land in suit on the basis of their allege purchases since the land is fishery vested with the Government on the acquisition of rent receiving interest. On the aforesaid findings the trial Court dismissed the suit. The appellate Court upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit on the findings that from the Government's side no paper was produced to show that the land in suit was fishery and on the acquisition of rent receiving interest the same vested in the Government and as regard the land in suit no C.A. Roll was prepared and as such interest in the land in suit remains with the tenant and consequent thereupon the plaintiffs by their purchase from the recorded tenants acquired right, title and interest in the land in suit, that S.A. record Ext.5 was prepared without any basis.

<u>6. The Government moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record, particularly Memo No. SA/IMA-373/73/1219(38) dated 1.8.1973 and the Memo No. SA/IMA-52/72/215- JM dated 7.12.1973 arrived at the finding that the land in suit in fact is a fishery and known as Mohal. Shamil Fisheries, that record shows that Loke Patni and others were given settlement of the Mohal Shamil Fisheries on taking ground rent as they were representing the villagers, that plaintiffs' vendor had no title in the land in suit and they had representative character as regard the land in suit, that plaintiffs by their alleged purchase did not acquire any title in the land in suit. The High Court Division also observed that since the plaintiffs are in possession and they are representing the villagers as such their prayer for permanent injunction from leasing out the land in suit which is fishery to outsider is maintainable. In our view this observation of the High Court Division is unwarranted since the admitted position is that fishery is non-retainable after the acquisition of rent receiving interest and on the acquisition of rent receiving interest fishery vested in the Government and as such it is for the Government to deal with the fishery in question in the way it considers will secure the interest of the State or in other words the Government is quite competent to lease out the fisheries through auction or through negotiation if thereby interest of the Government is best served.</u>

7. The learned Advocate-on-record has taken exception to the following observation of the High Court Division:

"But claim of title of the Loke Patny as passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, is set aside."

8. From the consideration of the materials on record as it is seen that the land in suit is fisheries and consequent thereupon on the acquisition of rent receiving interest as per the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the fishery has vested in the Government and as such plaintiffs by purchase from the Loke Patni and others who were representing villagers and who had no saleable interest in the land in suit, did not acquire any title.

9. In that view of the matter High Court Division did not commit any error in making the aforesaid observation.

10. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2489 of 2009
lawyer:
Garib-E-Newaz, Advocate instructed by A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
Respondents ------ Not represented
parties:
Kadbanu Bibi and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Wazed Ali Sikder and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 25.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3610 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J. Instant applications filed under Article 103 of the Constitution seeking leave to appeal against the common judgment and order dated 04/11/2009 passed by the High Court Division dismissing the First Appeal No. 238 of 2005 and First Appeal No.242 of 2005 thereby judgment and decree dated 28/07/2005 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court Dhaka decreeing title suit No.5 of 2000. 

2. The Respondent No. 1 of both applications as plaintiff filed title Suit No.5 of 2000 praying for declaration title and of the suit property should to the plaint contending amongst other that the defendant No.3 Abdul Aziz Khan owning and possessing the suit property 9 decimals of land who purchases vide registered of sale deed No.651 dated 21/01/1966 (4.5 decimals) and vide registered sale deed No.5126 charging the rule issued in Civil 0,Revision No.3610 of 1995 thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 18/06/1995 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal, dismissing the Title Appeal No.30 of 1992 affirming the judgment and decree dated 28/01/1992 passed by the teamed Assistant Judge, Mehendigonj, Barisal, decreeing the Title Suit No.26 of 1990 declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.76 of 1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mehendigonj, Barisal, as illegal, collusive and void. 

3. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the instant petition are that the respondent No.1 hereof as plaintiff filed the suit against the petitioner, as principal Defendant, and others contending, amongst others, that the schedule property in the suit belonged to petitioner No.1 hereof, who entered into an agreement for sale of the same to the plaintiff respondent hereof on 20.03.1989 on receipt of Tk.1200/- as advance out of the consideration money and the possession was also delivered and thereafter on receipt of the balance of the consideration amount on 14.04.1985 required sale deed was duly executed and registered and accordingly the plaintiff got his name mutated in the records of right and have been paying the land revenue to the Government and that on or about 08.04.1990 the plaintiff came to know that the defendant petitioner No.1 hereof filed Title Suit No.76 of 1989 without adding the plaintiff-respondent No.1 hereof as a party in the suit and accordingly the plaintiff filed an application for adding him as a defendant in the suit, which was rejected on 09.04.1990 upon hearing the parties, and that on the same day a sole-decree was passed in Title Suit No.76 of 1989 on the basis of a compromise petition. The defendant No.1-petitioner hereof claimed that he got the suit land by way of gift vide a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 10.12.1981 from his minor son but the said minor son transferred the suit property along with other properties to the plaintiff prior to execution of the said heba deed and thus the heba deed was fraudulent, collusive and void document also being made without consideration and therefore the said son could not subsequently inherit the suit property from his mother the defendant No.1, after her death, and that the decree in Title Suit No.76 of 1989 was obtained on the basis of a solenama and that too by practicing fraud upon the Court and therefore the impugned decree is void, illegal, without jurisdiction and liable to be cancelled. 

4. The defendant No. 1 petitioner hereof contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Azid Ali Bepari and that the defendant No.1 was the wife of Azid Ali Bepari and that the said Azid Ali Bepari gifted the suit land in favour of the defendant No.2, son of defendant No.1 on 10.12.1981, who at the relevant time was a minor and delivery of possession was received by the defendant No.1 on behalf of her minor son, the defendant No.2, and accordingly they were enjoying usufructs from the suit land on payment land revenue and that Me gift was genuine and that there was no act of fraud in the transfer through the heba deed and that the defendant No.2 filed Title Suit No.547 of 1983 for setting aside the heba deed and that by suppressing the service of summons of the case and playing fraud upon the Court obtained an exparte decree against the defendant No.1 on 09.06.1986 and that thereafter for setting aside the said exparte decree the defendant No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.76 of 1989 and that the defendant No.1 though entered into a 2nd marriage yet used to visit her first husband's house regularly and she I possessed the suit property along with other properties through her brothers. Azid Ali Bepari being defendant No.1 in the said suit (Title Suit No.76 of 1989) filed a solenama and accordingly the Title Suit No.76 of 1989 was decreed on the basis of said solenama setting aside the decree passed in Title Suit No.547 of 1983 and that the plaintiff was not made a party in. said Title Suit No.76 of 1989 and that the defendant No.2 denied to have entered into any agreement with the plaintiff or executed any bainapatra in respect of the said property and that the possession of suit property was never handed over to the plaintiff and that the sale deed dated; 14.04.1985 is a collusive, void, anti dated and illegal one and that the bainapatra dated 20.03.1980 was a created document I to undo the heba deed dated 10.12.1981.

5. On consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the respective parties, the learned Assistant Judge, decreed the suit on contest against the defendant-petitioner No.1 hereof and exparte against the rest setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.76 of 1989 declaring the same to be void, illegal, collusive, without jurisdiction and nullity. 

6. Being aggrieved, the defendant-petitioner No.1 hereof filed Title Appeal No.30 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Barisal, and the said appeal, mil. transfer, was heard and dismissed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal, and that in the appeal the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 were added as appellant Nos.2 and 3 claiming to have become owners in some part of the suit property by purchase from the defendant-petitioner No.1 hereof and that being aggrieved by such dismissal the defendant-appellant-petitioners hereof moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3610 of 1995 and upon hearing, the Rule, issued therein, has been discharged by the High Court Division by the judgment and order impugned in the instant civil petition. 

7. We have perused the leave petition and the judgments of the Courts below as annexed to the petition as well as the pro-visions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate. 

8. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the suit being a suit for declaration simpliciter is not maintainable as per provisions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act inasmuch as in the prayer portion of the plaint there was no prayer for declaration of title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and that the Appellate Division in several cases has held that a suit in which title of the plaintiff has been disputed by the defendant, a declaration of title and possession is necessary and in the absence of I a prayer for such declaration such suit is not maintainable in view of the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and hence the decree as passed is illegal and not maintainable. 

9. It appears from the judgment of the trial Court that specific issue was framed being issue No.4 "বাদীর নালিশী জমিতে স্বত্ত্ব দখল আছে কি?" and that the contesting parties in the suit have contested the said issue with evidence and that the trial Court on consideration of the  materials and evidence on record as well as the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the contesting parties found the title and possession of the plaintiff on the suit land and further it appears that though in the prayer portion such specific prayer for declaration title and possession was not made but in the body of the plaint the title and possession of the plaintiff was claimed and that since the question of title and possession was made an issue in deciding the suit and contesting the parties without raising any objection contested the same being issue No.4 quoted above and the trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record found the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit, the defect as alleged was cured, more so when no objection was raised against such defect in the suit and when no objection was raised against the framing of said issue No.4. It seems that the trial Court on its wisdom to adjudicate the case properly, on consideration of the pleadings of the parties, framed the said issue No.4 in accordance with law. 

10. We are of the view that the decisions of the Appellate Division on the point of maintainability referring to Section-42 of the Specific Relief Act, as submitted by the learned Advocate, are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case and that in fact the contesting parties were given due opportunity to contest the issue framed to decide the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. It further appears that the appellate Court below also considered the issue of title and possession of the plaintiff respondent No.1 hereof on the suit land and found that the impugned gift deed to be a void document since the recipient was minor at the relevant time and had no occasion to purchase any `jainamaz' and deliver the same as consideration for the gift, as alleged, and that the Appellate Court below in detail discussed the case as well as the evidence available on record and dismissed the appeal with cost affirming the judgment of the trial Court. It also appears that the High Court Division has considered all aspects of the cases, including the issue No.4 framed and decided by the trial Court, in the following manner: 
"On appeal, it appears, the learned Appellate Court also considering the evidence and materials on record came to the finding that the plaintiff acquired title in the suit land by registered kabala dated 24.04.1985 executed and registered by Azid Ali and that the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land since then and that Kadbanu or Kadam Ali did not acquire any title in the suit land by heba-bil-ewaj dated 10.12.1981 and that Kadam Ali being minor at the relevant   time had no capacity to give `Jainamaj and Tasbih' in exchange of the gift and that no possession was handed over to Kadbanu Bibi or Kadam Ali and that the defendant did not produce the original heba-bil-ewaj deed in the Court, but produced the certified copy of the same and  that Azid Ali knew to give his signature but he has executed the heba-bil-ewaj deed by putting thump impression and that the heba-bil-ewaj deed was not acted upon. On these findings the learned appellate Court dismissed the appeal. It appears, the present suit is a suit for declaration that the decree dated 09.04.1990 passed in Title Suit No.76 of 1989 is void, fraudulent and not binding on the plaintiff as he was not made party in the said suit though he claims to be the owner of the suit land by registered deed dated 14.04.1985. Both the Courts found that the present plaintiff was a necessary party in the said suit, but he was not made party and that his application for addition of party was rejected by the trial Court. The case of the defendant is that the suit as framed is not maintainable. According to the learned Advocate for the petitioner the defendants having challenged the right, title and possession of the plaintiff in the present suit, the plaintiff ought to have prayed for declaration of his title in the suit land along with the prayer for declaration that the decree dated 09.04.1990 is void. According to the learned Advocate in the present suit no prayer for declaration of title having been made, the present suit for declaration j that the decree dated 09.04.1990 is void is not maintainable. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the decision of Ratan Chandra Dey and others Vs. Jinnator Nahar and others reported in 13 MLR (AD)168 and the decision of Md. Jashimuddin (Kanchan) Vs. Md. Ali Ashraf reported in 11 13LD (AD)101 wherein there lordships of the Appellate Division held that when the defendant in his written statement claim title and possession in the suit land, a simple suit for declaration that a decree or a deed is void is not maintainable without first establishing his title to the suit land. The proposition of law as has been decided in the said 2 decisions are not disputed, but in the present case both the Courts correctly found that the plain-tiff was able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. It may be noted that the trial Court framed issue No.4 to the effect that whether the plaintiff has got right, title and possession in the suit land and the trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record specifically found that the plaintiff has got title and pos-session in the suit land. Since in the present suit an issue has been framed as to the title and possession of the plaintiff and both the Courts found that he got right, title and possession in the suit land, in my opinion, further declaration regarding title of the plaintiff is not essential in the present suit and as such in the absence of such prayer for declaration of title, the present suit as framed is also maintainable. Thus it shows that the facts of the present case is distinguishable from the facts of the above reported cases and as such, in my opinion those decisions are not applicable in the present case." 

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and as the contesting parties contested the issue No. 4 as to the title and possession on the suit land, having had all opportunities, we do agree with the findings and decision of the High Court Division and further we are of the view that the objection as raised by the learned Advocate referring to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act at this stage do not merit any consideration in the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed hereinabove.

12. Accordingly no interference with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is called for.

13. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 422 of 2010
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Principal and Secretary, Nawabgonj Government College, Nawabgonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahabuba Khatun (Dolly) and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. <u>This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 05.02.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 dismissing the suit. The plaintiff-respondent herein filed the above mentioned Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 for declaration of title and partition. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that 4.02 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint originally belonged to 3 brothers, namely, Ashutosh Chatyapadhya, Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya and Monimdra Chatyapadhya in equal share and the C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. That after partition of Pakistan and India Sharat Chandra Migrated to India and arranged an exchange of his share i.e. .95 acre out of schedule 'Ka' land with Indian land of one Ishahaque Mia-the father of the plaintiffs. That for effecting the exchange Sharat Chandra executed a power of attorney in favour of one Harun-ar-Rashid. Harun-ar-Rashid having obtained necessary permission from the then District Collector, Rajshahi, executed and registered a deed of exchange dated 13.10.1952 in favour of Ishahaque Mia. Thus Ishahaque Mia having acquired title and possession in the suit land had been in possession and enjoyment of the same for long 20 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants, Nawabgonj Government College and others. That Ishahaque Mia while in possession of the suit land executed a power of attorney in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid who being so empowered executed and registered two hiba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 09.10.1974 transferring the said .94 acre of land of Ishahaque Mia in favour of his daughters, the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4. Thus the plaintiffs acquired the suit land and since acquisition they have been in possession of the same by paying rent to the government to the knowledge of all including the defendants. That the defendant college subsequently purchased 2/3rd share of 'Ka' schedule land from Ashutosh and Monindra and has been in ejamali possession of that land with Ishahaque Mia and thereafter with the plaintiffs. That the 'Ka' schedule land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds among these co-sharers. That only in the month of October, 1985 when an employee of the plaintiffs went to pay rent in the local Tahsil Office the Tahsildar disclosed that the land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 College in R.S. Khatian and was finally published. That this R.S. record of the land in the name of the college in 16 annas share is wrong and collusive. That on the basis of this wrong recording the defendant college claimed title in the entire 'Ka' schedule land and thus the title of the plaintiffs in the suit has been clouded and hence the suit.</u>

2. The defendant college and the government contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants admit the title of 3 C.S. recorded tenants and subsequently also of Ishahaque Mia in the 'Ka' schedule land. But their case is that the defendant college being established in the then newly created Nawabgonj Sub-Division purchased 95 1/2 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule from Ashutosh Chattapadhya by a registered sale deed dated 23.02.1957 and also purchased the other 95 1/2 decimals of land from Monindra Chatyapadhya Chandra by registered sale deed dated 12.04.1957. That the share of Sharat Chandra was transferred to Ishahaque Mia by way of exchange and the said Ishahaque Mia transferred his 95 1/2 decimals of land to the college by an oral gift in presence of many and the college authority accepted it with gratitude. These defendants stated also that out of 4.02 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint 2.86 acres of land only finally stood as rest 1.16 acres fell into road and ditches. That the college authority thus, is in possession of 2.86 acres of land of the 'Ka' schedule to the knowledge of all including the plaintiffs. This land has been duly recorded in the name of the college in R.S. khatian. The college authority has erected wall on the west and northern side of the R.S. plot few years ago. The college authority is in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years and as such they have acquired title by adverse possession also. That the plaintiffs have filed this suit on false claim suppressing the real facts.

3. Before the trial court the plaintiffs examined 7 witnesses and the defendant examined 3 witnesses. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties, dismissed the suit holding, inter-alia, that the suit land is admittedly in possession of the college and that there is no allegation of forcible dispossession by the college and that the plaintiffs created the hiba-bil-ewaj and sale deeds from a person having no title to the suit land and that too after the same had been in possession by the college for more than twelve years.

4. On appeal the High Court Division set aside the findings and decision of the trial court and decreed the suit making observations and findings to the effect that the plaintiffs being daughters of the admitted co-sharers have succeeded in proving their title to the extent of 1/3rd share in the land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint and that the defendants could not prove their claim that the father, of the plaintiffs transferred his 1/3rd share in the 'Ka' schedule land in favour of the defendant college by oral gift and that the defendant college could not prove also its claim that the college has acquired title in this land by adverse possession also and that the recording of the 'Ka' schedule land in the name of the defendant college in 16 annas in R.S. Khatian has been wrong.

5. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on-Record for the leave-petitioner-defendant Nawabgonj Government College though has made some submissions in support of the leave-petition, but he could not assail the above findings and decision of the High Court Division.

6. We have gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division, that of the trial court and also the evidence on record.

7. We find that the High Court Division, on meticulous examination of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the contesting defendants could not prove at all their case that Ishahaque Mia the admitted co-sharer of the 'Ka' schedule land-gifted his 1/3rd share in favour of the defendant college orally. The High Court Division, on consideration of evidence and facts and circumstances and making elaborate discussion found also that the contesting defendants' claim that the defendant college has acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession also-has not been proved at all.

<u>8. We have gone through the evidence on record. We find nothing to disagree with the above findings and decision of the High Court Division. It is admitted that Ishahaque Mia became the owner of the 1/3rd share of C.S. recorded tenant Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya by way of exchange and he was also in possession of these 1/3rd share of the schedule 'Ka' land. The plaintiffs are the four daughters of this Ishahaque Mia. The trial court though made some observations that the plaintiffs could not prove their case that they acquired these 1/3rd share of their father by two registered hiba-bil-ewaj deeds, but the High Court Division found that the plaintiffs have proved their title in these 1/3rd share of Ishahaque Mia. The High Court Division rightly made observations to the effect that the plaintiffs though could not produce the original copy of their title deeds, namely, heba-bilewaj deeds and also the power of attorney executed by their father Ishahaque Mia in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid and gave explanations of failure to file those original deeds, but in consideration of the fact that the plaintiffs, being natural heirs of the vendor Ishahaque Mia, had no reason to create those documents in respect of their heritable property for maintaining a partition suit against co-sharer in joint possession. We find these observations of the High Court Division also reasonable. It is in evidence that Ishahaque Mia had four daughters the plaintiffs only, he had no son.
