A. F. Hasan Arif; Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants 
Goutom Kumar; D.A.G instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Md. Abdul Matin Kazi and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh ----- Respondent
case_source: (From the Judgment and decree dated 17.05.2001 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 116 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J.:- This appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs by leave to consider the legality of the judgment and decree dated 17.05.2001 passed by the third Judge of the High Court Division allowing' the First Appeal No.116 of 1996 and dismissing the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.11.1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 255 of 1993. Earlier a Division Bench of the High Court Division delivered dissenting judgment on 01.08.2000 in the said appeal.

<u>2. The relevant facts for the disposal of the appeal, in short, are that the appellants instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title in the suit covering an area of 1.20 acres of C.S. Plot No. 1 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 53 of Mouza Kakrail., Police Station Ramna, (former Keranigonj) Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands measuring 48.90 acres of said Plot and Khatian corresponding to S.A. Plot No.64 and S.A. Khatian No. 26 originally belonged to Bhawal Zaminder Rajkumer Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury who settled the suit land to Ashraf Ali Kazi, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs executing a pattannama on 05.02.1905. Said Ashraf Ali Kazi took over possession of the suit land and paid rent to the Zaminder. In C.S. operation, the suit land along with other lands of the disputed jam, was recorded in the name of Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Against the said record of right Ashraf Ali Kazi filed objection to get the same corrected and got an order on 24.05.1925. In S.A. operation the same was again recorded in the name of Public Works Department. On 12.01.1992, the plaintiffs discovered the pattannama, rent receipts and mutated C.S. Khatian in an old box in their house. On 08.03.1992, they collected the certified copies of the S.A. and C.S. Khatians and confirmed about the erroneous preparation of S.A. record of right. Thereafter, they filed this suit.</u>

3. The defendant-respondents contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the that the suit land along with other lands covering 48.90 acres originally belonged to Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Accordingly, the same was recorded in C.S. Plot No. 1 and khatian No. 53. Subsequently the Deputy. Commissioner, Dhaka took over possession of the suit land. The story of settlement of the plaintiffs from Bhawal Rajkumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury is false and the document produced by the plaintiffs are forged and fabricated. The C.S. Khatian had not been corrected at the instance of the plaintiffs' predecessor. The corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs is forged. The Government has been possessing the suit land. The Government started to construct buildings in the suit land for residential purpose of higher Government Officials. The S.A. record of right was duly prepared in the name of the Government. The suit should be dismissed.

4. The trial Court by his judgment and decree dated 11.09.1995 decreed the suit. The defendant- respondents preferred First Appeal No. 116 of 1996 in the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division comprised by Mr. Justice Md. Mozammel Haque and Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid heard the said appeal. Mr. Justice Md. Mozammel Haque by his judgment dismissed the appeal. On the other hand, Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Then the said appeal was heard by Mr. Justice Md. Tafazzal Islam as third Judge who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 16th and 17th May, 2001 allowed the appeal on setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Against the judgment and decree passed by Mr. Justice Md. Tafazzal Islam, the plaintiff-appellants preferred this appeal getting leave.

5. Leave was granted to consider the sub-missions of the appellants that the plaintiffs having proved their permanent settlement of the year 1905 producing pattanama (Ext.1) and the rent receipts of the years 1907, 1912, 1928, 1932, 1938, 1940, 1945 and 1948 (Exhibit-2 series proved their title in the suit land as well as their uninterrupted possession in the same over 87 years, the third Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in dismissing the suit. The Second submission was that the pattannama (exhibit-1) written in the year 1905 on stamp paper of more than 30 years old and the value of the land was shown at 11.15/- only and in such view of the matter, the same was not required to be registered under Section 17 of the Registration Act. The next point was that the plaintiffs' predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi paid rents to the landlord vide exhibit-2 series are the best piece of evidence of possession of the plaintiffs in .the suit land. It was further pointed out that the C.S. record of right stand corrected on the basis of the objection filed by Ashraf Ali Kazi (exhibit-3 series). It was further pointed out that the documents produced by the plaintiffs were old documents of more than 30 years so as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act those documents should be accepted as legal evidence.

6. Mr. A.F. Hasan Arif, the senior Counsel 'appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff-appellants got the suit land by way of settlement in the year 1905 and produced more than 30 years old pattannama (exhibit-1) . The plaintiffs paid rents to the Zaminder vide Exhibit-2 series and they got the C.S. Khatian corrected vide exhibit-3 series and had been possessing the suit land more than 87 years. The third Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in disbelieving the pattannama, corrected C.S. Khatian and rent receipts. He submits that the findings of the third Judge of the High Court Division regarding authenticity of exhibit-1 made in an old British Indian Stamp of 1905, and the rent receipts (exhib-it-2 series), the corrected C.S. Khatian (exhibit 3 series) and exhibit-4, the volume book of Government containing C.S. Khatian are erroneous. He further submits that since price of the land was Tk. 15/- only as it appears in the pattannama, the same was not required to he registered under section 17 of the Registration Act.

7. Mr. Goutom Kumar, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the High Court Division on vivid discussions on the materials on record came to the conclusion that the pattannama, rent receipts of the Zamindar and corrected C.S. Khatian are forged and fabricated documents. He submits that Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid rightly directed to prosecute the plaintiff-appellants initiating proceeding under Section 476 read with 195 (1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on allegation of forging those documents. He submits that the plaintiffs had no title-and possession in the suit land. The Government, constructing the buildings in the suit land; has been possessing the same. The instant suit was not at all maintainable without the prayer for recovery of khas possession.

8. We have heard the learned Advocate for the appellants and the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent perused the judgment of the courts below and other materials on record.

9. The case of the plaintiffs is that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi took settlement of the suit land on the basis of pattannama dated 05.02.1995 (exhibit-i). P.W.1 Abdul Matin Kazi, who was about 67 years old at the time of adducing his evidence on 19.08.1994 (that is, he was born after 22 years of alleged execution of the said pattannama) in his evidence, inter alia, said, এই সেই পত্তন নামার মূল কপি প্রঃ- ১ হিসাবে চিহ্নিত। কোর্ট দাখিল করিলাম। বিবাদীপক্ষে এই মর্মে আপত্তি যে, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। নোটারি পাবলিক কর্তৃক প্রত্তন নামার সত্যায়িত টাইপ কপি দাখিল করিলাম। প্রঃ ১(ক) আপত্তি সহকারে”। The is, exhibit-1 and 1(Ka) had been admitted in evidence with objection. The plaintiffs examined P.W.2 Sailendra Nath Sarker, a man of 78 years old, to prove the pattannama. In his cross-examination he said " ১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারব না।" From his evidence it appears that this witness was horn sometime in 1916, that is, after 11 years of the alleged execution of the pattannama. In order to substantiate the contents of the pattannama, the plaintiffs produced a notarized copy of the said pattannama exhibit-1(ka) P.W. 2 admitted that contents of the exhibit-1 are not readable. The plaintiffs did not examine the writer of the duplicated pattannama nor they examined the notary public, who notarized the same. In such view of the matter, Ext.1(Ka) could not be relied on. In the case of Harihar Prashad Vs. Desnarain reported in AIR 1956 SC 305 it was observed that the presumption enacted in Section 90 of the Evidence Act can be raised only with reference to original documents not to copies thereof. Furthermore, it appears that from Ext.1(Ka) that Ext.1 had been executed by Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. The P.W. 2, who claimed to be the Tahsilder of Bhawal Estate and joined in the said Estate in 1346 B.S., did not say in his evidence that Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the Manager of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, the Zaminder of Bhawal Estate. The plaintiffs failed to produce any other evidence to prove that Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the manager of the Estate.

<u>10. Submission of Mr. Arif is that since the Ext. 1 Pattannama is an old document of more than 30 years and had been produced from proper custody, the court would presume that the signature and every other part of Ext.1 is that person's hand writing and, the same had been duly executed by the person by whom it purports to be executed as per provision of Section 90 of the Evidence Act. The spirit of section 90 of the Evidence Act is that if private documents not less than thirty years old are produced from proper custody and are on their face free from suspicion, the court may presume at they w have been signed or written by the persons whose signatures they bear or in whose hand writing they purport to he, that they have been duly attested and executed, if they purport so to he Section 90 only lays down that the court may presume that document purporting to be 30 years old are genuine. That it must not presume them to be so. Supreme Court of India in the case of Sri Lakhi Baruah Vs. Sri Padma Kanta Kalita reported in AIR 1996 SC 1253 observed that Section 90 of the Evidence Act is founded on necessity and convenience because it is extremely difficult and sometimes not possible to lead evidence to prove handwriting, signature or execution of old documents after lapse of 30 years. In order to obviate such difficulties or improbabilities to prove execution of an old documents section 30 has been incorporated in the Evidence Act, which does away with the strict rule of proof of private documents. Presumption of genuineness may he raised if the document in question is produced from proper custody. It is, however, the discretion of the Court to accept the presumption flowing from Section. The presumption is permissive and accordance no the circumstances of each case the court may or may not raise it. That is, such presumption discretionary and so where a document is suspicious on the face of it or mutilated, the court may refuse to make presumption. It is not obligatory on a court to raise the presumption. The language being "may" when the person who has been examined as P.W.2 to prove the Ext.1 himself has said “১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারবো না"; then why the court will rely upon such document .At the time of making exhibit the defendant raised objection saving, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। In such circumstances, the provision of section 90 ought to be applied with more care and great caution because nothing can he more easy than, for an unscrupulous ours person, who is wrongfully in possession and wants to make out a title to it to forge such document in his favour more than 30 years old and produce it as the proper custodian relieving himself of the necessity of proving its execution. The Ext. 1 patina must not be presumed to he genuine merely from its being ancient. Some other evidence were required to be given of the early existence and publicity of Ext. 1 . Neither C. S. khatian nor S. A. khatian had been prepared on the basis of Ext. 1.</u>

11. In order to show the existence and publicity of Ext.1 or in other words to prove the story of their settlement dated 11.02.1905 and rebut the presumption under Section 103. B of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which is available in favour of the Government since C.S. record of right was prepared in favour of the Government ( Ext. A), the plaintiffs produced Ext .2 series, the Zamindari dakhilas and alleged corrected khatian Ext. 3 series. It is the claim of the plaintiffs that against C.S. Khatian their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi filed Objection Case No. 327H/1932 and got his name corrected in the Zamindery Sherista and obtained certified copies of the corrected Khatian from Zamindery sherist- Correction of the entry in Khatian filing objection in the Zamindery Sherista is totally illegal. As per provision of Section 108A of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which was transferred as section 115B, by the Bengal Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1928, only the Revenue Officer specially empowered by the Government on application or of his own motion, within two years (earlier time limit was for 12 months) from the date of certificate of the final publication of the record of right under sub-section (2) of Section 103A, correct any entry in such record of rights which he was satisfied had been made owing to a bonafide mistake. That is, Revenue Officer was legally authorized to correct the Khatian nobody else. The concerned volume regarding P.S. Khatian was called for to ascertain the authenticity of Ext. 3 series which was marked as Ext. 4 . T. Islam, J examined Ext. 3 series, the corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs and relevant volume book of C.S. khatian Ext. 4 thoroughly. Such examination, as it appears from his observation that the same was made most carefully which is praise-worthy.

<u>12. The observation in that regard are as follows:</u>

<u>"I have gone through Ext. 4, which is the volume of Mouza 282 Kakrail produced before the trial court. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13, 24, 53 and 55 as contained in Ext. 4, on the top of the front page at the left hand side under the heading  উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words "ভারত সম্রাট" have been printed and out of the above Khatian at the right hand side of the Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13-24 under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে বিস্তারিত দখল the names of different persons were printed and in the remaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 53 and 57, under this very heading at right hands side, public works Department and District Board respectively, both on behalf of Bharat Samrat were printed. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6 and 17 as contained in Ext. 4 similarly under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the word পত্তন রাজেন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় ৩নং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and out of the above khatian under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল of C.S. Khatian Nos.  4,5 and 6 the names of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3 and 7 only, and this heading " কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস’"Were printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian Nos. 31-32, 33Ka, 34-35, 39-40, 43, 46-47 and 47Ka as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্তস্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words পত্তনী কালীন নারায়ন রায় ৩০নং দখল কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian No. 8, as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্থ স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words মিরস জামাল, ৭নং রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Sheikh Abdul was printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian Nos. 30, 51Ka and 51 Kha as contained in Ext. 4, under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words সিকিম তালুক রামকৃষ্ণ দত্ত were printed and out of the above Khatians, in C.S. Khatian No. 30 under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and in Khatian No. 51 Ka and 51 Kha under the above heading of অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the names of other persons were printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian No. 25-27 and 51 as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিসত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words and also the names of 13 co-sharers of the Zamindari were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed.</u>

<u>Thus in the Khatians mentioned above on the front page on the top at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/ পরিচয়ে the names of Zamindars were printed and at the right hand side under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of tenants/riots were printed and at the over leafs of some of the above Khatians, the names of the possessors were printed.</u>

<u>Regarding C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contains in Ext. 4, as it appears at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words ভারত সম্রাট were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/ অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Public Works Department on behalf of Bharat Samrat, have been printed and it is only at the over leaf, Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was shown as mere possessors of 48.90 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 1 as stated earlier, in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3-7, 8, 30, 31, 32, 32 Ka 33, 34, 39; 40, 43,47, 51Ka and 51 Kha of Ext. 4 in most of the cases the Court of words of the heirs of Kumar Rabindra Narayan have been shown as Zamindars and in few cases the above court of words have been shown ryot under the heading" অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল and is none of the above Khatians Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was not shown as Zamindar or tenant. It thus appears that on 23.04.1917, when the above C.S. Khatian were finally published, Kumar Rabindra Narayan ceased hold any interest in any of the above Khatians and instead the court of wards of his heirs were shown as Zamindar and tenants.</u>

<u>Accordingly how in C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contained in Ext. 4 Kumar Rabindra Narayan could be shown as possessor and like wise how in Ext. 3 also Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself could be shown as Zamindar."</u>

13. It was further observed that the claim of the plaintiffs that Kumar Rabindra Narayan got Zamindari of C.S. plot No. 1 containing 48.90 acres of land has also no basis at all.

<u>14. Mr. Arif failed to satisfy this court making any submission to discard aforesaid findings referring any material on record. The aforesaid findings arrived at by the last court of facts are based evidence. Since Kumer Rabindra Narayon was neither landlord nor tenant in the land recorded in Khatian No. 53 and plot No. 1 no one, claiming himself as manager of Kumer Rabindra Narayon Chowdhury, had any authority to settle the same on his behalf. He was not a person immediately under whom the tenant holds and no tenancy had been established pursuant to Ext. 1 in re sport of the suit land.</u>

15. The C.S. record of right was prepared in the name Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Such record of right is evidence of the matter referred to in the entry and should be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. Since such presumption being a statutory one could not be taken away mere by allegation that the same is incorrect. The burden of proving that such entry in the record of right is incorrect is on the party who alleges it. In this case the plaintiffs failed to rebut the presumption by adducing evidence. The documentary evidence produced by the plaintiffs are found to be forged and fraudulent one by the Court of facts.

16. The plaintiffs stated that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi died sometime in 1948. It has also been stated in the plaint that in 1992 the plaintiffs allegedly got the papers produced in the Court in an old box. The plaintiffs did not produce any materials in support of their claim to deal with the property, at least, from 1948 to 1992. They did not take any step to record their names in the khatian and to pay rent to the Government. It is totally unacceptable proposition' that one, who is allegedly in possession in the land and structure thereon within Dhaka City Corporation, would not take any step to record/ mutate his name in the khatian, pay rent, municipal taxes, WASA, Gas bills etc.

17. A controversy has arisen as to whether the instant permanent tenancy can be created otherwise by a registered instrument. The last court of facts held that the suit land is non- agriculture land to be used for non-agricultural purpose. The Contents of pattanipatta or amalnama as reproduced in duplicatted copy (Ext 1Ka) were as follows:

<u>“শ্রী আশ্রাব আলী কাজী, পিতা সোমাকাজী, জাতী মুসলমান, পেশা গৃহস্থী, সাং-হাতীর রাস্তা, থানা কেরানীগঞ্জ, জেলা-ঢাকা। -----পাট্রা গ্রহিতা।</u>

<u>লিখিতং কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় চৌধুরী পিতা মৃত- শ্রীযুক্ত রাজা রাজেন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী, জাতী ব্রাক্ষণ, পেশা- জমিদারী, পক্ষে নিযুক্তীয় ম্যানেজার-শ্রী কামিনী কুমার বন্দোপাধ্যায়, সাং- জয়দেবপুর, থানা- কেরানীগঞ্জ, জেলা-ঢাকা ------- পাট্রা দাতা। কস্য খাস দখলীয় জমির পত্তনী পাট্রা বা আমল নামা পত্র মিদং কার্য্যংগে যেহেতু আমি ভাওয়ালের জমিদার শ্রীযুক্ত কুমার রবীন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় চৌধুরী স্টেটের নিযুক্তির ম্যানেজার। আপনি পাট্রা গ্রহিতা আমার সেরেস্তায় নিম্ন তপসিল বর্ণিত খাস জমি চিরস্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত নেয়ার জন্য প্রার্থনা করিলে আমি তাহা আমার সেরেস্তার কর্মচারী দ্বারা যাচাই করিয়া আপনার প্রার্থনা মঞ্জুর করত আপনার নিকট হইতে চিরস্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত বাবদ মং ১৫/-(পনের টাকা) নহর সেলামী গ্রহণ করিয়া নিম্ন তফসিল বর্ণিত খাসজমি আপনার নিকট পত্তন করিলাম। অদ্য হইতে ভূমি পাট্রা গ্রহিতা লিখিত খাস জমি নিজ দখলে নিয়া বাগ-বাগিচা বাড়ী ঘর তৈয়ার করিয়া পৌত্র পৌত্রদিময় ওয়ারিশগণ ক্রমে ভোগদখল ও বসবাস করিতে রয়। হইতে কোন প্রকার ওজন আপত্তি করিতে পারিব না। করিলে তাহা আইনতঃ সর্বাদালতে বাতিল বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।</u>

<u>প্রকাশ থাকে যে, পত্তনি জমির বার্ষিক খাজনা কপি গ্রহণ করত নিজ নাম জারী করিয়া নিতে পারিবেন। এবং ভর্বিষতে কোন করআদী বৃদ্ধি করিলে তাহাও দিতে বাধ্য থাকিবে। এতদ্বার্থে স্বেচ্ছায় অত্র পাট্রানামা সম্পাদন করিয়া দিলাম-ই সন ১৯০৫/১১ ফেব্রুয়ারী।</u>

<u>(তফসিল বা চৌহদ্দী)</u>

<u>জিলা-ঢাকা, থানা-কেরানীগঞ্জ, কালেকটরীর তৌজিভুক্ত কাকরাইল মৌজাস্থিত ১নং খাস খতিয়ানভুক্ত মোট জমি ৪৮.৯০ শং কাতে পত্তনী জমি ১.২০ শতাংশ যাহার উত্তরে অন্য মৌজা দক্ষিণে, পূর্বে ও পশ্চিমে রাস্তা।</u>

<u>লিখক-</u>

<u>শ্রী ফনিন্দ্র চন্দ্র রায়</u>

<u>সাং- জয়দেবপুর।”</u>

<u>18. From the contents of Ext. 1(Ka), intention of the parties as gathered from those contents; surrounding circumstances and the claim of the plaintiffs it appears to us that the plaintiffs tried to establish that the Ext. 1 is a lease deed which is unregistered and unilateral one in respect of the property described therein and which is to be used for orchard and homestead and the same is a lease in perpetuity. In the case of Safar Ali Master Vs. Abdul Mazid reported in 47 CLJ Page 27 it was observed that homestead land within a municipality even, though recorded as "bagan" land in the record of rights is not governed by the Bengol Tenancy Act but by the Transfer of Property Act. In the case of Ramdas Vs. Bipradas reported in 19 C.W.N. page 35 it was held that tenancies for residential purposes are outside the scope of the Bengol Tenancy Act. We are of the view that the alleged iv lease was to be regulated under the provision of Transfer of Property Act not by the Bengol Tenancy Act. Lease as defined in section 105 of the transfer of Property Act is a transfer of right to enjoy immovable property made for a certain time express or implied, or in perpetuity. In the case of Abdus Satter Vs. Suresh Chandra Das reported in 32 DLR (AD) page 170 it has been observed that the essential elements constituting lease are the following: a) the right must be one as to immovable property, (b) the right must be that enjoyment of immovable property; (c) these must be a transfer of much right; (d) the right of transfer must be made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity; (f) the consideration must be of the particular kind namely, premium or rent as defined by the section either or both of them. In the case of M.H. Khondker, Advocate Vs. Bangladesh reported in 30 DLR (SC)1 it has been held that (i) by a lease a subordinate interest is created by a person in favour of another person in respect of some immovable property on condition of premium or rent (ii) the right which is created a lease is the right of tenancy 'Lease" and tenancy are cognate terms, implying the same kind of jural relationship. In the case of Bastacolla Colliery Co. Ltd. Vs. Bandhu Beldar reported AIR 1960 Pat 344 it has been observed by the Full Bench of Patna High Court that before amendment of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act by Act 20 of 1929 a valid lease could be created by a patta executed by the lessor but all leases coming within the first paragraph of Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act can only be made by registered instrument. Since the instant transaction is a transfer of interest of non- agricultural land and to be used for nonagricultural purpose entitling the leasee the enjoyment of such immovable property which includes the right to possession thereof in perpetuity such tenancy can only be created by registered instrument. An unregistered documents of lease which was required to be registered conveyed no title and created no right of the plaintiffs. Ext. 1 is inoperative under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and could not create a tenancy; could not create the inception of tenancy and could not be considered to find out tenancy. A document which was compulsorily registrable but was not registered is void as regards immovable property which is non agriculture in nature and to be used for non-agricultural purposes.</u>

19. So far possession is concerned the defendants claimed that the Government constructed or started to construct building in the property in question. The evidence as to possession of the plaintiffs are insufficient. In the plaint the plaintiffs, inter alia, stated, বাদীগণ ও নালিশী সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত দলিল দস্তাবেস ছাড়া নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বড় ধরনের নির্মাণ করার জন্য মনের জোর পায় নাই। বাদীগনের পিতা কর্তৃক নালিশী সম্পত্তির চারিদিকে সীমানা নির্ধারণ দেওয়াল ছাড়া অন্য কোন নির্মাণ করে নাই।” In evidence the plaintiff No.1 as P.W.1 deviating the plaint case said “আমার আব্বা অংশ বিশেষ বসবাস করতেন গৃহনির্মান করিয়া বক্রি বংশের সবজীর চাষাবাদ ক্রমে ভোগ দখল করতেন, তাহার জীবনকাল পর্যন্ত।" The plaintiffs failed to produce any paper regarding utility services i.e. DESA, WASA, GAS etc. in support of their claim of possession. On 14th May, 2013 the plaintiff appellants submitted a supplementary paper books producing some papers including information slip in support of their case. The contents of information supplied, inter alia, were: "সরজমিনে তদন্তে দেখা যায় প্রার্থীর জমি গণপূর্ত বিভাগের বাউন্ডারী দেওয়াল দ্বারা বেষ্টিত।” That is, from their papers it appears that the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land. On due consideration of the evidence on record, the last court of facts rightly found the possession of the defendants in the suit land. The said finding is based on evidence.

<u>20. Since the plaintiff appellants are out of possession, the suit for simple declaration without the prayer for recovery of khas possession was not maintainable.</u>

21. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we are constrained to hold that it was an ill attempt of the plaintiffs to grab the government property by creating some documents. In such view of the matter Md. Abdur Rashid, J. rightly directed the trial Court to take steps against the plaintiffs drawing proceeding under section 476 read with Section 195(1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

22. In view of the facts and circumstances recorded above, we do not find any sub-stance in the appeal.

23. In the result the appeal is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 3rd day of June, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.3229 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. Added respondent No. 6 has filed this petition for leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated the 3rd day of June, 2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3229 of 2004 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of this leave petition are as follows:

3. Respondent Nos. 1-3 herein as petitioners (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners) filed Writ Petition No. 3229 of 2004 before the High Court Division challenging the order dated the 9th December, 2003 passed by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board (writ- respondent No.1) in Case No. 3-108/95 (Review) Dhaka, the order dated the 29th August, 1995 passed by Mr. Mohammad Enamel Haque, Chairman, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka in Case No. 3- 85/94 (Appeal)-Dhaka and the order dated 08.10.1989 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.19 of 1987 to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and also for a direction upon writ-respondent Nos. 3-5 to Mutate their names in Case No. 19 of 1987 according to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in respect of 7 S.A. plots measuring 5.17 acres of land. The Rule was issued in the terms prayed for.

4. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that Moqbul Ahmed, predecessor-in-interest of writ-petitioner No.1 filed an application before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon. Circle, (writ-respondent No.5) for mutating his name in respect of 5.17 acres of land of S.A. plot Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358, and 1365 of Mouza Tejkunipara within Police Station-Tejgaon, Dhaka on the basis of decree obtained in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 of the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka; the application was allowed, but instead of 5.17 acres; 8.70 acres of land of S.A. khatian No.605 was mutated including the land of plot Nos.1370, 1377, 1383, 1384 and 1385 in respect of which Moqbul Ahmed had no claim. Writ-respondent No.6 (there are two respondent No.6, so, in order to clear the confusion they are described by name as well), Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, filed an appeal against the said order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon, before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka, (writ-respondent No.4), being Miscellaneous Appeal No.11 of 1990, who by his order dated 08.03.1994 allowed the appeal and sent Case No.19 of 1987 back on remand to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka for reconsideration and decision. The predecessor-in-interest of petitioner No.1, late Moqbul Ahmed, moved the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, Dhaka against the said order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vide Miscellaneous Appeal No.62 of 1994 in which the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) dated 08.03.1994 was confirmed by order dated 05.11.1994. Writ-respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, filed Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968 in the First Court of Munsif, Dhaka under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (the Act) impleading Peerzada Abul Quashem. Md. Hasnain Siddiqui and Satinath Bandapaddhaya as opposite parties for correction of record in respect of the same plots of land as mentioned hereinbefore. This was a fraudulent Endeavour behind the back of said Moqbul Ahmed and others. The miscellaneous case was twice rejected, but somehow Abdus Sattar Chowdhury managed to have the case decided in his favour beyond the knowledge of Moqbul Ahmed and others. Moqbul Ahmed filed an appeal before the Land Appeal Board against the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka, being No. 3-85/94(Appeal)- Dhaka; on hearing the appeal, the Chairman of the Land Appeal Board, Mr. Md. Enamul Huq, by order dated the 29th day of August, 1995 allowed the same and restored the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 08.10.1989. Against the said order of the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, writ-respondent No. 6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, filed a review application before the Land Appeal Board which was registered as Case No. 3-108/95(Review)-Dhaka. The case was disposed of by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board (hereinafter referred to as the Full Board) comprising of the Chairman and two other members by order dated the 9th day of December, 2003; the Full Board set aside the order dated 08.10.19879 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) in Case No.19 of 1987 and at the same time, maintained the mutation of 7 S.A. plots being Nos. 1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358 and 1365 measuring an area of 5.17 acres in the name of Moqbul Ahmed (the father of writ-petitioner No.1) and also maintained the mutation of 12 S.A. plots being Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358, 1365, 1370, 1377, 1383, 1384 and 1385 in the name of Abdus Sattar. And thus, the Full Board modified the order dated 29.08.1995 passed by the: Chairman, Land Appeal Board in Case No.3-85/94(Appeal)-Dhaka; hence the writ-petitioners filed the writ petition.

5. Md. Mintu Chowdhury, leave petitioner, got himself added in the writ petition as respondent No.6 (as stated in the leave petition as well as in the impugned judgment and order) and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that it was not correct that Moqbul Ahmed, predecessor-in-interest of writ-petitioner No.1 filed application  before the Assistant Commissioner(Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka for mutating his name in respect of 5.17 acres of land of S.A. plot Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 11356, 1357, 1358 and 1365 of Mouza Tejkunipara on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970. The aforesaid application was filed by Moqbul Ahmed for mutation of his name in respect of the concerned R.S. record of the said moan on the basis of the decree passed in the said title suit. the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka allowed the mutation illegally in respect of S.A. record which is contrary to decree of Title Suit No. 280 of 1970. On the basis of the decree in respect of R. S. khatians and R.S. plots, there cannot be mutation in respect of S.A. khatian and S.A. plots unless and until the concerned decree in respect of R.S. record was amended according to law. Moreso, the writ-petitioners did not claim that the said R.S. plots arc the corresponding S.A. plots. So the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) was set aside by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka vide Order dated 08.03.1994 in Miscellaneous Appeal No.11 of 1990 which was subsequently affirmed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner by order dated 05.11.1994 and then, by the Full Board in Review Case No.3-85/94 vide Order dated 09.12.2003. The disputed and the important question of fact cannot be resolved in writ jurisdiction. It is not correct that filing of Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968 by writ-respondent No. 6, Abdus Sattar, was a fraudulent endeavor behind the back of Moqbul. Ahmed and others and he managed to have the case decided in his favour. Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968 was filed in the then First Court of Munsif, Dhaka under section 143(sic, it should be 143A) of the Act for correction of record. After due service of notices of the miscellaneous case on the opposite parties, the same was decided in favour of Abdus Sattar. There was nothing for Moqbul Ahmed "to be constrained" with the result of Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 as he instituted Title Suit 280 of 1970 for correction of R.S. record and not S.A. record and obtained the decree in his favour in respect of 7 R.S. plots being Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358 I and 1365 measuring 5.17 acres. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) rightly decided Miscellaneous Appeal No.64 of 1994 which was confirmed   by the Additional Divisional: Commissioner by Order dated 05.11.1994 and the Full Board as mentioned hereinbefore. The Land Appeal Board, on an erroneous view of the facts and law, affirmed the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 05.10.1989 and as such, the Full Board, on review, rectified the mistake in Review Case No.3-108/95(Review-Dhaka) by order dated 09.12.2003. Since the decree passed in Title Suit No.280 of 1970 is on the basis of A.S. record, as prayed for in the plaint of the suit, the Full Board had to sustain mutation of the aforesaid 7 R.S. plots measuring 5.17 acres in the name of Moqbul Ahmed. Simultaneously the Full Board had no other alternative but to sustain mutation in the name of Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in respect of 12 S.A. plots measuring 8.70 acres of land on the basis of the "judgment and decree" passed by the learned Munsif, First Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 filed by him and that position was ultimately upheld by the Full Board in the review case. Unless and until the decree of Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 is amended by the proper Court in proper forum, no other Court or authority would be able to change it or give contrary decision in that respect. The Full Board rightly sustained mutation in the name of Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in respect of 12 S.A. plots as mentioned earlier as well as the mutation in respect of R.S. plots measuring 5.17 acres of land in the name of Moqbul Ahmed on the basis of decree of the civil Court. The order of the Full Board dated 09.12.2003 is not inconsistent and contradictory as alleged. The sustenance of mutation in the name of writ-respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar, in respect of 12 S.A. plots measuring 8.17 acres of land is correct and that has nothing to do with the mutation of 7 R.S. plots measuring 5.17 acres of land in the name of Moqbul Ahmed. The writ-petitioners never claimed that these are corresponding plots and as such, they are not entitled to get any relief in the writ petition on such controversial and disputed facts. It is not correct that the Full Board "has suffered from confusion in respect of R.S. plots, and S.A. plots." The order of the Full Board in Review Case No. 3-108/95(Review-Dhaka) being perfect and legal, does not warrant any interference. The writ-petitioners are to the satisfied with the decree of the civil Court passed in Title Suit No.280 of 1970 and therefore, they had nothing to be aggrieved unless and until the said decree is amended and corrected in an appropriate forum.

7. Two supplementary affidavits were filed on behalf of added respondent No.6, Md. Mintu Chowdhury (leave petitioner): the first one in November, 2009 (date is not available from the record) and the second one on the 18th day of May, 2010.

In the first supplementary affidavit, it was stated, inter alia, that his father being the legal owner and in possession of the property in question filed Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968 (name of the Court not mentioned) during his life time against Peerzada Abul Kashem and Mahmood Hossain Siddique for correction of the record of rights wrongly prepared in their names, but on the basis of a misleading and wrong report, the miscellaneous case was dismissed ex-parte by order dated 01.08.2007. On another application filed by the father of the respondent under Order XLVII, rule 1 read with section 114 of the Code for reviewing the order dated 01.08.1970, the miscellaneous case was restored vacating the said order of dismissal by order dated 22.08.1970 (correct dated is 29.8.1970) fixing 02.09.1970 for hearing the case on which date after examining the father of the respondent (Abdus Sattar Chowdhury) and considering the exhibits filed on his behalf the names of the opposite parties of the said miscellaneous case were deleted from the case khatian and name of writ-respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar, was incorporated' which is apparent from annexure-'F-I' to- the affidavit-in-reply. 10. A Division Bench of the High Court Division hearing the writ petition by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute declaring the impugned order dated 09.12.2003 passed by the Full Board to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and directed respondent No.1 (the land Appeal Board) to cancel the same and writ-respondent No.5, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka to restore the S.A. records in the name of the writ-petitioners to the extent of 5.17 acres as it originally stood; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

11. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners, has tried to assail the impugned judgment and order on the submission that the High Court Division instead of considering the propriety and legality of the order passed by the Full Board in the review case, misdirected itself in observing "we have already seen that the predecessors of the petitioners acquired title in the case property on the basis of the decree dated 29.12.1970 passed in Title Suit No.280 of 1970 against respondent No.6 and others" without considering that the judgment and decree was passed in the said suit on the basis of R.S. record and that runs counter to the claim of the writ-petitioners. Mr. Mahbubey Alam has further submitted that the Full Board having found error on the face of the record to the effect that in the order dated 29.08.1995 passed by the Chairman in Appeal No. 3-85/94(Appeal)-Dhaka, it was observed “২৬। এই মামলার বাদী ২৮০/৭০ নং মামলা দায়ের করিয়া পূর্ববর্তী ডিক্রি রদের ডিক্রী লাভ করেন।” which is contrary to record inasmuch as the plaintiffs of that suit did not seek any such relief in the suit and as such, the Full Board rightly allowed the review application, the High Court Division erred in law in interfering with the order of the Full Board. He has lastly submitted that the High Court Division misdirected itself in making the Rule absolute on new grounds without considering that all 3(three) grounds taken in the writ petition, in fact, run counter to the claim of the writ-petitioners and thus exceeded its jurisdiction in passing the impugned judgment and order interfering with the order passed by the Full Board and as such, the same calls for interference by this Division.

12. Mr. Mahmudul Islam learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of writ-petitioner-respondent Nos. 1-3, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

13. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute relying on the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 wherein it was declared that the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit land. From the plaint of Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 which was annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the added respondent as annexure-'I', it appears that the predecessors of the writ-petitioners filed the suit for declaration that they are the exclusive owners in possession of the suit land and that none of the defendants has any right, title or interest therein; in the suit, respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, father of the leave petitioner was impleaded as defendant No.1 , but he did not contest the suit. The High Court Division came to the finding that on the basis of the decree passed in the said suit, the predecessors of the writ-petitioners got their names mutated by filing Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1977-78 and S.A. khatian No.605/1 was prepared in their names and they had been paying rents regularly to the Government and after 17 years there from writ-respondent No.6 filed Miscellaneous Case No.19 of 1987 for mutating his name and correction of the S.A. record on the basis of the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 and on such application, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle by order dated 09.01.1988 cancelled the mutated S.A. khatian in the name of the predecessor of petitioner No.1 and several others in respect of plot Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358 and 1385 covering an area of 5.17 acres of land on the finding that he acquired title on the basis of the order passed in the said miscellaneous case (355 of 1968), though Maqbul Ahmed and others, the predecessors of the writ-petitioners, were not made parties in the miscellaneous case.

14. The star document of added respondent No. 6 relying on which the Assistant Commissioner (Land) cancelled the mutated khatian in the name of the predecessor of writ-petitioner No. 1 and others and the Full Board allowed the review application is the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968. The High Court Division did not put any reliance upon the order passed in the said miscellaneous case on the view that the same was allowed ex-parte without serving   any notice upon the opposite parties though the same was earlier dismissed ex-parte on 01.08.1970. The High Court Division further noticed that the said miscellaneous case was restored on 29.08.1970 on the basis of an application filed on 27.08.1970 under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code, that is, just after two days of the filing of the application without serving any notice upon the opposite parties after an application filed under section 151 of the Code for vacating the order dated 01.08.1970 was rejected on 27.08.1970. In this regard, the High Court Division considered sub-section 13 of section 143A of the Act (since repealed) which provided that for the purpose of review, the relevant provisions of the Code, that is, Order XLVII thereof shall be made applicable for the purpose of filing an application for review and rule 4(2) of Order XLVII provides that no application for review shall be granted unless notice of the application has been served upon the opposite party. The High Court Division observed that the miscellaneous case was allowed ex-parte on 02.09.1970 without serving any notice upon the opposite parties and that again just after 3(three) days of the date of restoration of the case where order was passed to delete the names of the opposite parties from S.A. khatian and to incorporate the name of writ-respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury. In this regard, the High Court Division further noticed that in the said miscellaneous case, Moqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Most. Khurshid Jahan Akhter, the predecessors-in-interest of the writ-petitioners, were not made parties and the same was filed against Peerzada Abul Kashem and Mohammad Hasnain Siddiqui; Maqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Most. Khurshid Jahan Akhter filed an application in the miscellaneous case on 02.08.1969 under Order, rule 10 of the Code for adding them as opposite parties, the application was kept with the record. The High Court Division further found that 7(seven) plots in question were ROR plot being Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1365, 1384 and 1385 and those related to S.A. record and not R.S. record. The High Court Division further observed that in 1969, there was no existence of R.S. record and the Assistant Commissioner (Land) committed a bonafide mistake stating R.S. plots in place of S.A. plots inasmuch as R.S. khatian was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the District of Dhaka in Of 1985 or thereabout. The High Court Division further noticed that from annexure-G to the affidavit-in-reply, it was evident that the names of predecessors of the petitioners, Maqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Most. Khurshid Jahan Akhter, wife of Maqbul Ahmed, were mutated in Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1977-78 and accordingly, mutated S.A. khatian No. 605/1 in respect of plot Nos.1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1357, 1358 was recorded correctly in their names in respect of an area of 5.17 acres only and from annexure-'G-1' to the affidavit-in-reply, it appeared that subsequently, R.S. khatian No.76 of mouza Tejgaon Shilpa elaka, previously Tejkunipara, P.S.-Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj was finally published under section 144(7) of the Act in the names of the aforesaid persons correctly and till date respondent No.6 did not take any step in respect of the said finally published R.S. khatian in the name of the petitioners' predecessors; since the later record of right, i.e. R.S. record was finally published in the names of the predecessors of the writ-petitioners, such entry in the record of rights shall be presumed to be correct unless it is proved by evidence to be incorrect and the R.S. record of rights shall prevail over the S.A. record.

15. From the order passed by the Full Board impugned in the writ petition, it does not appear that it considered the facts noticed by the High Court Division as noted hereinbefore. Mr. Mahbubey Alam could not also point out with reference to any provision of law and the document that the findings given and the observations made by the High Court Division in the impugned judgment and order are the result of non consideration or misconstruction of the documents annexed to the writ petition, the affidavit-in-reply as well as the affidavit-in-opposition and the supplementary affidavits filed by added writ-respondent No.6 or based on no evidence or are against law.

16. The High Court Division further held that the Full Board exceeded its jurisdiction in allowing the review application inasmuch as it failed to point out discovery of new and important matter or evidence which after the exercise of due diligence was not within the knowledge of respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury or could not be adduced by him at the time when the order was passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, without strict proof of such allegations as provided in Order XLVII, rule 4(2) of the Code. Mr. Mahbubey Alam found it difficult to assail this view of the High Court Division with reference to the Rules, 1990 or the Code. Mr. Mahbubey Alam could not also assail the finding of the High Court Division that the R.S. record was finally published under section 144(7) of the Act in the District of Dhaka in 1985 and thereabout and in 1969, there was no existence of R.S. record, so it is of no use to argue that since the predecessor of the writ-petitioners filed Title Suit No.280 of 1970 in respect of R.S. khatian and R.S. plots, the High Court Division was not justified in deciding the propriety of the order of the Full Board relying on the decree passed in the said title suit. In this regard, we like to observe that in a proceeding under section 143A of the Act (since repealed), title is not decided and the decree passed in a suit for title shall always prevail upon the order passed in such a proceeding, so the High Court Division committed no illegality in relying upon the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in preference to the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.355 of 1968 in interfering with the order passed by the Full Board.

17. The scope, the manner and the forum of review are circumscribed by the provisions of the Statute. The power of review of the Land Appeal Board has been provided in section 6 of the Land Appeal Board Ain, 1989 as amended on the 14th day of June, 1990. And in rules 3(3), (5), 4(1) (3) and 5 of the Land Appeal Board Rules, 1990 (the Rules, 1990) the procedure for filing a review application to the Land Appeal Board and its disposal have been laid down. In the context, we consider it relevant and pertinent to consider the above provisions of the Ordinance and the Rules, 1990 which are as follows:

৬। পুনর্বিবেচনা।–(১) বোর্ডের কোন আদেশের দ্বারা কোন ব্যক্তি সংক্ষুব্ধ হইলে তিনি আদেশটি প্রদানের ষাট দিনের মধ্যে উহা পুনর্বিবেচনার জন্য বোর্ডের নিকট বিধি দ্বারা নির্ধারিত পদ্ধতিতে আবেদন করিতে পারিবেন।

(২) বোর্ডের বিবেচনায় সংগত মনে হইলে আবেদনকারীর প্রার্থনার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে বোর্ড উহার সিদ্ধান্তের বাস্তবায়ন উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন পেশকৃত আবেদনটি নিষ্পত্তি না হওয়া পযন্ত স্থগিত রাখিতে পারিবে।

‘৩(৩) বোর্ড কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশের পুনর্বিবেচনা, মামলায় আইনানুগ জটিলতা বা আইনের ব্যাখ্যার প্রয়োজন দেখা দিলে চেয়ারম্যান বিষয়টি ফুলবোর্ডে (চেয়ারম্যান ও সদস্যগণ সমন্বয়ে গঠিত বোর্ড) বিবেচনার জন্য উপস্থাপনের আদেশ প্রদান করিতে পারিবেন এবং সচিব উক্তরূপে আদেশের জন্য চেয়ারম্যানের নিকট বিষয়টি উপস্থাপন করিবেন। চেয়ারম্যান বিষয়টির উপর ফুলবোর্ডের সিদ্ধান্তের প্রয়োজন মনে করিলে তিনি ফুলবোর্ডে বিষয়টি পেশ করিবেন এবং ফুলবোর্ড শুনানীর মাধ্যমে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিবেন।

(৫) পক্ষগণ স্বয়ং (নি��ুক্ত) আইনজীবীর মাধ্যমে আপীল/রিভিশন ও পুনর্বিচার (রিভিউ) আবেদন দায়ের করিবেন।

৪(১) বোর্ডের সমীপে আদেশ প্রদানের পূর্বে বোর্ড পক্ষগণকে নোটিশ প্রদান এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট সমুদয় রেকর্ড তলব ও পর্যালোচনা করিতে পারিবে।

(৩) পুনর্বিবেচনার আবেদনের পক্ষগণকে নোটিশ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

৫। পুনর্বিবেচনার আবেদনঃ (১) পুনর্বিবেচনার আবেদনে তর্কিত আদেশে যে আইনগত ও তথ্যগত বিষয়াবলী বিবেচিত হয় নাই সম্পূর্ণভাবে তা উল্লেখপূর্বক পুনর্বিবেচনার বিষয়সমূহ নির্দিষ্ট করে আবেদনকারী পুনর্বিবেচনার আবেদন করিতে পারিবে।

(২) বোর্ড কর্তৃক পুনর্বিবেচনার আবেদনের উপর প্রদত্ত আদেশ এবং উপ-বিধি (১) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে আপীল/রিভিশন মামলায় প্রদত্ত আদেশ চূড়ান্ত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।”

18. A reading of section 6 of the Ordinance shows that by this section the Land Appeal Board has been vested with the power of review of its order if an application is filed for such review within the time prescribed therein. Of the Rules as quoted hereinbefore, rule 5 shows that in the application for review, the applicant shall have to state the law and the facts which were not considered in the order sought to be reviewed and shall also have to pin point the subjects of review (বিষয়সমূহ) of the order of the Land Appeal Board. From rule 5, it further appears that while considering the application foe review the Full Board must see that the applicant fulfilled the conditions as mandated therein and if not the application would deserve no consideration on merit. The application for review was not annexed either to the writ petition or to the affidavit-in-opposition and the supplementary affidavits-in-opposition, so we could not see the contents thereof. But from the order of the Full Board, it is apparent that neither any fact nor any law was stated or pointed out which was not considered by the Land Appeal Board while passing the order sought to be reviewed nor the subject matter for review was formulated or specified. Rule 5 of the Rules, 1990 is quite in conformity   with Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code. As per rule of Order XLVII of the Code, review of a decree or an order can be allowed only when the person who seeks review of such decree or order can make out a case of discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made or on account of some mistake or error apparent   on the face of the record, or for any other sufficient reasons. But in the instant case, respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, failed to make any such case. And the Full Board also did not give or any such finding.

19. From the order of the Full Board, it appears that it reviewed the order of the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, in a casual manner without pointing out or giving any finding as to any law or fact which was not considered by him in passing the order dated 29.08.1995 or error apparent on the face of the record committed by the Chairman of the Board in passing the said order sought to be reviewed as provided in Order XLVII, rule 1(1) of the 7 Code. As pointed out by the learned Judges; respondent No.6, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, failed to make out any case of discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the order was passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board and the Full Board did not also give any finding to that effect.

<u>20. A reading of the order of the Full Board further shows that in fact, they re-opened the matter and re-heard the same and has written out a fresh judgment on the same materials considering which the Chairman of the Land Appeal. Board passed the order on 29.08.1995. It also appears to us that the Full Board proceeded in a manner as if they were hearing an appeal from the order of the Chairman of the Land Appeal Board and corrected the mistake committed by him which was not within the scope and extent of the exercise of the power of review. The Full Board also failed to appreciate that the object of review is neither to enable the reviewing authority to re-hear the matter nor to write a second judgment. And in the context, the High Court Division rightly held that the Full Board travelled beyond its jurisdiction in deciding matters not within its jurisdiction as contemplated under the Rules, 1990.</u>

21. For the discussions made above, we do not find any factual and legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and order and consequently, no merit in the leave petition.

22. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

Vs.
The Administrator and the Chairman of the Allotment Committee, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 27.7.1999 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 471 of 1989)
full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J.:-This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated 27th July, 1999 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 471 of 1989 discharging the Rule Nisi. 

2. The appellant instituted Writ Petition No. 471 of 1989 challenging the allotment of 47 shop rooms in the ground floor and 6 rooms in the 1st floor of Ahasanullah (Nawabbari) Super Market, Ahasan Manzi!, Dhaka by the respondents. According to the appellant there were 300 shop rooms in C.S. Plot Nos. 725-726 at the premises of Ahasan Manzil, Ahasanullah Road, Dhaka. The appellant and others shop owners had been carrying on their business in those shop rooms for a long time and earned their livelihood. The appellant took lease of a shop room from the Dhaka Nowab Court of Wards Estate in 1980. In 1985 the Government decided to acquire the historic Ahasan Manzil along with the lands of C.S. Plot No. 725-726 with a view to preserve and protect the said Ahasan Manzil as monument making necessary renovation thereof and to establish a museum thereon. After such acquisition the appellant along with 300 victim shop keepers became seriously affected. The affected shop keepers made a representation to various authorities including the President of the Republic and the then Chief Martial Law Administrator for saving them from total ruination with a suggestion that a Super Market should be constructed adjacent to the Ahasan Manzil monument where the shops were located on C.S. Plot No. 725- 726. The Government having found the proposal meaningful accepted the same and decided to construct a Super Market on the said plots adjacent to the Ahasan Manzil monument. 

3. In the premises, the government by letter dated 18th January, 1986, directed the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to take over and deliver the possession of the lands to the Dhaka City Corporation for construction of a Super Market thereon. In order to ensure that the shops in the said Super Market are made available to the affected shop keepers at the first instance by way of allotment on priority basis, the Government by letter dated 28th January, 1986, constituted a field survey committee. The said committee conducted a survey and prepared a list of affected shop keepers by physical verification and submitted its report to the Government on 15th February, 1986, and issued certificates to each of the affected shop keepers. Thereupon the Dhaka City Corporation took up construction work of the Super Market and with a view to meet the construction costs asked the affected shop keepers to pay salami of Tk. 25,000/- each in advance. The appellant and other shop keepers paid the salanii against receipts. Thereafter the City Corporation fixed the salami for a shop room at Tk. 1,50,000/- and asked the shop keepers to pay the balance amount by 5 equal installments of Tk. 25,000/-each. The appellant and other affected shop keepers duly paid the salami. 

4. After completion of the construction works, the City Corporation did not allot the shop rooms as per list prepared by the field survey committee on priority basis and allotted 18 shop rooms out of 140 shop rooms in the ground floor and 6 of rooms in the 1st floor to outsiders who are not affected shop keepers by illegal and corrupt consideration. As a result, the appellant and other affected shop keepers have been deprived of their legitimate right and entitlement of a shop room in the ground floor. 

5. Respondents contested the rule nisi by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations made in the writ petition. They claimed that there was no commitment by the City Corporation to allot shop rooms in the ground floor to the affected shop keepers. After the completion of the construction works, they have allotted shop rooms of the Super Market on the basis of open lottery and some of them have gotten shop rooms in the 1st floor, some of them in the 2nd floor and some in the 3rd floor. They took over possession from the City Corporation of their respective shop rooms and thereafter, they could not complain against the allotment after accepting the process of allotment. 

6. Their further case is that the affected shop keepers did not file appeal under section 155 of the Dhaka Municipal Corporation Ordinance, 1983, if they were at all aggrieved against the said allotment and therefore, the writ petition is not maintainable. Their further case is that all the allotees of the shop rooms in the ground floor having not been impleaded in the writ petitions, the appellant and other writ petitioners are not entitled to the relief, inasmuch as, if the said allotments were interfered with the said allotees would be adversely affected. 

7. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the impugned judgment discharged the rule nisi observing that 317 shop keepers were affected by the acquisition of the lands and out of them 5 were land owners, 81 were tenants under the Dhaka Nowab Court of Wards Estate and remaining 231 were sub-tenants under the tenants of the said Estate. The learned Judges further  observed that there are 143 shop rooms in the basement, 140 in the ground floor, 141 in the 1st floor and 151 .in the 2nd floor, that the appellant or other affected shop keepers failed to prove that the City Corporation gave them any assurance to allot shop rooms in the ground floor of the Super Market and that the affected shop keepers including the appellant were given allotment of shop rooms either in the 1st floor or in the 2nd floor and they got possession of their respective shop rooms in February, 1988. 

8. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Judges of the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering that the appellant and other affected shop keepers having been listed as the affected shop keepers as per report prepared and the certificates issued by the field survey committee -and having paid salami to the City Corporation, they had acquired a vested right to have allotments of shop rooms at the first instance on priority basis in the ground floor to the exclusion of the outsider. 

9. Mr. Md. Abdul Zabbar, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant failed to show any material on record that the Dhaka City Corporation assured the affected shop keepers to allot shop rooms in the ground floor of the Super Market. The learned Counsel, however, contends that the City Corporation having allotted 48 shop rooms to outsiders including Barrister Rabeya Bhuiyan and the relations of the Administrator of the Dhaka City Corporation, who are not affected shop keepers, it is apparent that the alldtments have not been made fairly, and in an arbitrary manner and thus, those arbitrary allotments should have been declared to have been made or given to them without lawful authority. The learned counsel further contended that the appellant being an affected shop keeper and in view of the certificate issued of the field survey committee, he had acquired a vested right to get the allotment on priority basis in the ground floor but the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to consider the said aspect of the matter and illegally dis-charged the rule nisi. 

10. Annexue-D to the writ petition is a deed of undertaking given by Md. Abul Hossain, General Secretary, Nawab Bari Bastra Samity being counter signed by the President of the said Samity on 13th January, 1988 on behalf of the affected shop keepers. In pursuance of the said undertaking, the shops were allotted in presence of the Administrator Dhaka City Corporation on the basis of lottery on 10th January, 1988. The said lottery was held as per decision of the shop allotment committee providing that nobody would be entitled to raise any objection or institute any case against such allotments. Accordingly, the shops were allotted to the affected per-sons including the appellant by lottery. Annexure-B(3) showed that the appellant took possession of his shop room in the 2nd floor on 12th May, 1988 and after taking over possession, he instituted a writ petition in April 1989. There is also nothing on record to show that the City Corporation assured the appellant and other affected shop keepers to allot shop room in the ground floor of the Super Market. 

11. Though out of total 567 shop rooms in the Super Market, there are only 317 shop keepers who arc affected by the acquisition of the lands. It is on record that total number of shops in the ground floor is only 140, whereas, actual total number of affected persons were 307 and out of those rooms, in the ground floor only 36 rooms were allotted to outsiders in order to meet the construction costs by increasing the amount of salami. Admittedly the allotments of the shop rooms have been made by lottery. On the basis of lottery, the appellant- was also given allotment of a shop room and he got delivery of possession. He did not raise any objection at the time of issuance of the allotment letter and delivery of possession. In that view of the matter find no substance in the first contention of the learned Counsel for the appellants. 

12. The field survey committee issued certificate to the appellant and other affected persons for ascertaining the persons who were real affected persons by the acquisition of the lands with a view to allot shop rooms to them. This survey 'report does not accrue any vested right upon the affected shop keepers to have an allotment in the ground floor of the Super Market. Over and above, the appellant has not impleaded all the allottees who have got-ten shop rooms in the ground floor. These allottees have paid the premium and gotten possession of their respective rooms. The writ petition without impleading them as respondents is not legally maintainable, inasmuch as, the court can not give any declaration as prayed for in favour of the appellant without affording them an opportunity on being heard. Further, the appellant has not preferred any appeal as provided under section 155 of the Dhaka Municipal Corporation Ordinance, 1983. Section 154 of the Dhaka City Corporation Ordinance, 1983 provides that any person aggrieved by an order passed by the corroboration or any officer in pursuance of the said ordinance or rules or by laws may prefer an appeal to the pre-scribed authority within the period of limitation and any order passed in the appeal shall be final. If the appellant has got any grievance against the allotment, he could have preferred an appeal but without seeking redress to the proper authority in accordance with law moved the writ petition challenging the allotment. Without resorting to the alternative remedy available, the writ petition is not legally maintainable. 

13. In view of the above, I find that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have committed no error of law in discharging the rule nisi. I find that the writ petition is not legally maintainable. There is no merit in the contentions of the learned counsel. The appeal is therefore, dismissed without any order as to costs. 

End.

Vs.
