VS
Mahbuba Sarwar and others ------ Respondents (in both the cases)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 14th day of December, 2010 passed by the High. Court Division in First Appeal No.89 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and decree dated the 14th day of December, 2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.89 of 2007 allowing the appeal.

2. Facts essential for disposal of this petition are that the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.46 of 1991 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Narayangonj for specific performance of contract impleading respondent Nos.1-3 herein as defendant Nos.1-3, RAJUK (formerly DIT) represented by its Chairman and its Deputy Director (Estates) as defendant Nos.4 and 5. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 05.11.1991 with the direction upon defendant Nos.13 to execute and register the kabala in respect of the suit land within 60(sixty) days failing which the plaintiff would get the kabala through Court. As the defendants did not execute the kabala as per the decree, the plaintiff levied Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 and eventually, the kabala was executed and registered through Court. It further appears that the plaintiff (of Title Suit No. 46 of 1991) also took possession of the suit land through Court vide the said execution case.

3. Respondent Nos.1-3 herein who were defendant Nos.1-3 in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 filed Title Suit No.146 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj for declaration that the ex-parte judgment dated 05.11.1991 and the decree dated 13.11.1991 passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 were illegal, collusive, inoperative and not binding upon them; for cancellation of the kabala dated 21.07.1992 being No.2386 executed and registered by the Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in favour of the plaintiff in Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 as shown in schedule-'Kha' to the plaint and also for recovery of khan possession of the land as described in schedule-'Ka' to the plaint. Eventually, the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No.1 of 2005 (hereinafter referred to as the instant suit).

4. The main allegations made in the plaint of the instant suit were that plain-tiff No.1 was not aware of filing the suit; the ex-parte decree passed therein, filing of Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 and execution of the decree through the execution case before 06.04.2003. She came to know about the ex-parte decree, the registration of the kabala through Court in the said execution case on 07.04.2003. Plaintiff No.1 did not file any family suit being No.6 of 1985 for her appointment as guardian of plaintiff Nos.2 and 3. Plaintiff No.1 was not at the address at which the summons of the suit was sent, but defendant No.1 in collusion with the process server managed to obtain service returns and obtained the ex-parte decree by practicing fraud upon the Court sand also managed to execute and register the impugned kabala through Court in respect of the suit land. Plaintiff No.1 also denied the fact of entering into any contract with defendant No.1 to sell the suit land.

5. The suit was contested by the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners who was impleaded as defendant No.1(hereinafter referred to as the defendant) by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that plaintiff No.1with intent to transfer the suit property filed an application before the 4th Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) and Family Court, Narayangonj being Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1985 for appointing her as guardian of plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 and she was appointed as guardian and then obtained permission to sell the suit property vide Permission Case No. 5 of 1986. Plaintiff No. 1 in person   and on behalf of plaintiff Nos.2 and 3 agreed to sell the suit property to the defendant for a consideration of taka 4,00,000 (four lac) and received a sum of taka 10,000 (ten thousand) against a written acknowledgement under her hand on 25.04.1985 for herself and on behalf of plaintiff Nos.2 and 3 as earnest money and thereafter, she received taka 20,000 (twenty thousand) on 12.02.1989 and taka 500 (five hundred) on 04.05.1989 and taka 10,000 (ten thousand) on 05.07.1989 as additional earnest money against separate acknowledgement receipts. There was art understanding between the defendant and plaintiff No.1 that on obtaining permission of the Court to sell the suit property, she would execute and register a saf-kabala in favour of the defendant in respect of the suit land by taking the balance consideration from him. A legal notice was also published in the daily 'Banglar Bani on 07.11.1989 through Mr. Kazi Ahmed Ali, Advocate, drawing attention of the interested persons, if any, relating to the suit property for communicating with the said learned Advocate with "requisite documents" in support of their claim, but none turned up. Thereafter, the defendant requested plaintiff No.1 time and again to receive the balance consideration money of taka 3,55,000.00 and execute and register the saf-kabala in his favour, but she did not pay any heed to the request and as such, a legal notice was served upon her by the defendant through his said learned Advocate under registered post with a copy to the Deputy Director (Estates), DIT, Dhaka. But the notice was returned unserved upon plaintiff No.1 with the endorsement "Refused" on 28.07.1990. In the above circumstances, the defendant was constrained to institute the suit (Title Suit No.46 of 1991) in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj against the plaintiffs for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property and the suit was decreed ex-parte on 13.11.1991. The summonses of the suit were served upon the defendants (of Title Suit No.46 of 1991) and accordingly, the suit was decreed ex-parte as per the procedure. No fraud was practiced by the plaintiff of that suit (the defendant of the instant suit) in obtaining the decree for specific performance of contract; the decree passed in the suit was valid and binding upon the plaintiffs (of the instant suit). As the plaintiffs of the instant suit (the defendants of Title Suit No.46 of 1991) did not comply with the terms of the operative portion of the decree, the defendant levied Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj for execution of the decree. The defendant deposited the balance consideration of taka 3,55,000.00 and then the saf-kabala being No. 2386 was executed and registered in his favour on 19.07.1992 in respect of the suit property and the delivery of possession was made on 07.04.2003 with the help of police force in presence of a Magistrate and since then the defendant has been possessing the suit property. Shafiuddin Sarwar, brother-in-law of plaintiff No.1 instituted Title Suit No.106 of 1993 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj for setting aside the ex-parte decree of Title Suit No.46 of 1991 against the defendant impleading the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 2-4 and others as defendants which was dismissed for default on 20.07.1999 at the stage of further hearing. The plaintiffs filed the instant suit on some false pleas and pretext so the suit was liable to be dismissed.

6. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 22.03.2006 dismissed the suit.

<u>7. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No. 89 of 2007 before the High Court Division and a Division Bench by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the appeal with a cost of taka 1,00,000.00 (one lac) against the defendant, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit. The High Court Division also set aside the ex-parte decree dated 05.11.1991 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 and declared the same as collusive, illegal, inoperative, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The High Court Division also declared the kabala dated 21.07.1992 being No.2386 executed and registered by the Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 vide Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 cancelled and at the same time rejected the plaint of Title Suit No.46 of 1991 as being frivolous, void, ab-initio and "based upon concocted story of agreement and being barred by law" and directed the defendant to hand over the vacant possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs within 60 (sixty) days failing which the possession would be delivered by the trial Court by evicting the defendant. The High Court Division also declared the proceedings of Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 as void; hence this petition for leave to appeal.</u>

8. Heard Mr. Khizir Ahmed, learned Advocate for the petitioners and Mr. Qamrul Hoque Siddique, learned Advocate who entered caveat on behalf of the respondents, perused the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaint, the evidence on record, the other materials on record and the impugned judgment and decree.

9. In the instant suit, the following prayers were made:

“(ক) অত্রাদালতের দেঃ ৪৬/৯১ নং মোকাদ্দমায়  প্রচারিত বিগত ৫/১১/৯১ইং তারিখের একতরফা রায় ও ১৩/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখের ডিক্রি বে-আইনী, যোগসাজাসিক, তঞ্চকতাপূর্ণ, অবৈধ, অকার্যকর ও বাদাগন প্রতি প্রযোজ্য নহে মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রি দিতে।

(খ) দেঃ ৪৬/৯১ নং মোকাদ্দমার রায় ও ডিক্রি হইতে উদ্ভত ১/৯২ নং ডিক্রি জারী মোকদ্দমা অনুকুলে হাছিলকৃত ১নং বিবাদী বরাবরে সম্পাদিত ও রেজিষ্ট্রীকৃত আরজীর খ তপছিল বর্ণিত সাবকবলা দলিল বাতিল ও ক্যানসেলেশন ক্রমে উহা সংশ্লিষ্ট সাব-রেজিষ্ট্রী বালাম বহিতে নোট করার নিমিত্ত বোরকারীর আদেশ দিতে,

(গ) আরজীর ক তপছিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে বাদীগনের অনুকূল মূল বিবাদীর প্রতিকূলে খাস দখল পাওয়ার ডিক্রি দিতে,

(ঘ) মূল বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ক্ষতিপূরণ বাবদ ১০,০০,০০০/- (দশ লক্ষ) টাকা আদায়ের ডিক্রী দিতে এবং মোকাদ্দমার উদ্ভবের সর্বশেষ দিন হইতে উক্ত ক্ষতিপূরণ এর টাকা আদায়ের দিন পর্যন্ত উক্ত টাকার উপর শতকরা ২০% হারে টাকা আদায়ের ডিক্রি দিতে,

(ঙ) দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধি আইনের ২৪(৩) ধারার বিধান মতে মামলা খরচ এবং খরচের উপর শতকরা ৬% টাকা হারে মামলা খরচাসহ ডিক্রি দিতে, এবং

(চ) আইন ও ইকুইটি মতে আদালতের ন্যায় বিচারের বাদীগন অন্যান্য ফলপ্রন্ত কোন প্রতিকারের ভাজন হইলে তাহাও ডিক্রি দানে সুচিবার করিতে আজ্ঞা হয়।”

10. The trial Court considering the pleading of the parties framed the following issues:

“১। আত্রাকারে ও প্রকারে অত্র মোকাদ্দমা চলিতে পারে না?

২। অত্র মোকাদ্দমা তামাদিতে দুষ্ট কিনা?

৩। অত্র মোকাদ্দমা পক্ষ দোষ দুষ্ট কি না?

৪। দেওয়ানী ৪৬/৯১ নং মোকাদ্দমার ৫/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখের রায় এবং ১৩/১১/৯১ইং তারিখের একতরফা ডিক্রি তঞ্চকী কিনা?

৫। বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থীত মতে ১০,০০,০০০/- টাকার ক্ষতিপূরণ পাইতে হকদার কিনা?

৬। আর্জির খ তপসিল বর্ণিত কবলা দলিল তঞ্চকী ও অকার্যকর কিনা?

৭। বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার ছাড়া কি কি প্রদিকার পাইতে পারে?

৮। বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার কিনা?

11. The trial Court dismissed the suit answering issue No. 2 in the affirmative, issue Nos. 4 and 5 in the negative, i.e. against the plaintiffs; issue No. 3 in the negative, i.e. in favour of the plaintiffs and issue Nos. 6-8 in the negative, i.e. against the plaintiffs.

12. The High Court Division reframed the issues as under:

"(a) Whether the ex parte judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was valid in law on account of non appointing any guardian ad litem as required under Order 32 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure?

(b) Whether the ex parte judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was passed in normal course of business or hastily and abnormally?

(c) Whether the plaintiff No.1 was appointed as guardian of person and property for plaintiff Nos.2 and 3 and got a permission for transforming (sic, it would be transferring) the suit land as claimed by the defendant No.1?

(d) Whether the plaintiff No.1 was entitled to enter into any contract on behalf of minor daughters and that was enforceable in law?

(e) Whether the Title Suit No.1 of 2005 was barred by limitation as held by the trial court?

(f) Whether the defendant could produce   any paper in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 or in the instant suit to prove the fact of existence of any agreement for transfer of the suit land by the plaintiff No.1 for herself and on behalf of her minor daughters and in absence of any such evidence what would be the consequence of Title Suit No.46 of 1991?

(g) Whether the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 were enforceable in law?

(h) As per the submission made by Mr. Quayum, the learned Advocate for the defendant, whether the title Suit No.46 of 1991 is liable to be sent back on remand?

(i) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief as prayed for?

(j) What more relief the plaintiffs are entitled to get?"

13. From the issues framed by the High Court Division, it appears to us that the High Court Division travelled beyond the scope of the suit and it went even beyond the relief prayed by the plaintiffs in the suit. Be that as it may, of the 10(ten) issues: issues (h), (i) and (j) appear to us relevant to decide the questions involved in the instant suit. And we do not consider it at all necessary to discuss the propriety of the issues other than these issues (issues (h), (i) and (j)) decided by the High Court Division.

<u>14. So far as issue (h) is concerned, the learned Judges refused to send the suit back to the trial Court on the view that "(a) there was no existence of any contract as alleged by the defendant No.1 (b) The plaintiff No.1 being a defacto guardian had no authority to enter into any contract (c) If existence of any contract is accepted that is void and not enforceable in law as per decisions referred to above."</u>

<u>15. In taking the above view, the Teamed Judges totally failed to consider that the moment the ex-parte decree was set aside, the suit stood restored in its original position and the only legal consequence of such restoration was that the suit had to be proceeded with and disposed of in accordance with law.</u>

16. We also failed to understand how the questions as raised by the learned Judges quoted hereinbefore were relevant in deciding the question as to whether the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was liable to be set aside or not. Whether there was existence of any contract, whether plaintiff No.1 had any authority to enter into any contract and whether the contract, if any, would be "void and not enforceable in law" are the matters to be decided in Title Suit No.46 of 1991. In the context, it is necessary to state that in the suit, no relief was sought against the contract for the performance of which Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was filed.

<u>17. The learned Judges made another fundamental mistake in rejecting the plaint of Title Suit No.46 of 1991 on the finding that "defendant No.1 instituted Title Suit No.46 of 1991 upon 100% false statements and without having a valid agreement, consequently the Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was liable to dismissed. We are of the view that Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was not liable to be decreed and that suit was barred by law and the plaint was liable to be rejected", though the learned Judges themselves found that "upon eventual success in the appeal, the Title Suit No.46 of 1991 although are liable to be restored to its file and number." It is also necessary to keep on record that though the learned Judges found Title Suit No.46 of 1991 barred by law, they did not point out or mention under what provision of law it was barred. We ourselves have tried to lay our hand on any provisions of the Statute to see whether the suit (Title Suit No.46 of 1991) was barred by law, but we failed. When Title Suit No.46 of 1991 was decreed ex-parte and the instant suit was filed for setting aside the said ex-parte decree, the question of rejection of the plaint of the suit did not arise at all. More so, when the defendants of the suit (Title Suit No.46 of 1991) did not get any chance to file written statement (as the suit was heard ex-parte) stating their own case, how it could be said that the suit was filed upon 100% false statements and such a finding is absolutely based on wild assumptions and presumptions. And no plaint can be rejected on the assumptions or presumptions that the facts stated in the plaint are false. Whether the statements made in the plaint are false or not, are purely questions of fact and are to be decided at the trial. In rejecting the plaint, the learned Judges invoked section 151 of the Code, but the inherent power under the section cannot be exercised on assumptions and presumptions of facts and or on suspicion. In other words, the truth or falsity of the statements made in the plaint cannot at all be a ground to reject a plaint either be it under Order VII, rule 11 or under section 151 of the Code. And if that legal proposition of the High Court Division is accepted, it will create havoc in the dispensation of justice delivery system in civil litigations. We conclude that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned Judges erred in law in deciding the issue in the negative. Therefore, that portion of the order of the High Court Division cannot be sustained.</u>

<u>18. Be that as it may, considering the evidence and the other materials on record, it appears to us that the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.46 of 1991 cannot be sustained and the High Court Division rightly set aside the same. Consequently, the kabala executed and registered by the Court in favour of the defendant being kabala No.2386 dated 21.07.1992 in Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 pursuant to the said ex-parte decree cannot also be maintained and the High Court Division rightly cancelled the same. Since the exparte decree is set aside and the defendant got delivery of possession of the suit land in execution of the ex-parte decree, he cannot get the benefit of the ex-parte decree and therefore, he cannot be allowed to enjoy the fruit of the decree continuing his possession therein and the plaintiffs must be restored back with their possession of the suit property. Therefore, the decree of the High Court Division directing the defendant to deliver possession of the suit property is to be maintained and the findings and the decisions of the learned Judges in respect of issues (i) and (j) appear to us correct subject to the findings and the observations made hereinbefore.</u>

<u>19. For the discussions made above, the judgment and decree of the High Court Division cannot be maintained in its entirety and it needs modification. Since we have heard the learned Counsel of both the parties and from the institution of the suit (Title Suit No.46 of 1991), 14 (fourteen) years have elapsed, we are of the view that justice would be best served if the petition is disposed of finally without giving leave. Accordingly, the petition is disposed in the following terms:</u>

<u>The impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division so far as it relates to setting aside the ex-parte decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 and cancelling the kabala dated 21.07.1992 being No. 2386 executed and registered by the same Court in Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 is maintained. The order rejecting the plaint is set aside. Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj (now Joint District Judge) is restored to its file and number and shall proceed and be disposed of in accordance with law. The direction of the High Court Division upon defendant No.1 (now it will be the petitioners herein, being the heirs of the deceased defendant) to hand over the vacant possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs is maintained. The direction of the High Court Division to allow defendant No.1 (now it will be the petitioners herein) to withdraw taka 3,55,000.00 deposited by him in Title Execution Case No.1 of 1992 is maintained. The awarding of cost of taka 1,00,000.00 against defendant No.1 is set aside.</u>

20. The judgment and decree of the High Court Division stands modified in the above terms.

21. Contempt Petition No. 13 of 2011 is disposed of accordingly.

End.

full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. The vires of sub rules (3) and (4) of rule 4 of  উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করন ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, 1995 published by SRO No. 65-Ain/95/SM/ Bidhi-1/5-6/94 dated 2nd May, 1995 so far as it relates to counting the seniority from the date of regularization and in respect of cadre posts from the date of encadrement has been challenged by the respondents in the High Court Division, who were appointed in the development projects in The Bangladesh Agriculture Resource Institute under the Ministry of Agriculture. The High Court Division made the rule absolute declaring the notification dated 12th March, 2003, to be ultra the constitution.

2. Short facts are as under:

3. With petitioner No. 1 after obtaining the postgraduate degree in soil, science from the University of Dhaka entered into the service of the soil Resources Development Institute on 5th May, 1986 as scientific officer and the writ petitioner Nos. 2-4 after obtaining Bachelor's Degree in Agriculture joined the service as scientific officers with similar scales. Thereafter the writ petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 obtained, the post graduation degrees in soil science. They were initially appointed in a development project with a clear assurance that on completion of the initial project period they would be included and absorbed in the revenue set up. In due course they were included in the revenue set up on 5th June, 1993, The writ respondent Nos. 6-17 were originally appointed under the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI) in the Analytical Service Division as scientific officers with the identical scales. They were junior to the writ petitioners and were doing the same nature of job and thy had entered into the service of the autonomous institute of the BARI long after the writ petitioners entry in the service. But writ respondent Nos. 11-17 entered in the service of the BARI after the writ petitioners were included in the revenue set up the government. Thus the writ petitioners are senior in service at the entry point as scientific officers and also in the revenue set up. The writ respondent Nos.6-17 were included in the government service on 20th May 1993 and they had joined the government service with effect from 1st October, 1993. The writ petitioners were brought under the project effective from 1st July, 1992 and the writ respondent Nos. 6-12 were brought into government service effective from 1st January, 1993, By circular No.7053/1/Civ-11 dated 3rd March, 1985, the government promulgated the Recruitment Rules for those who were appointed in development projects prior to the transfer of the officers and staff from the development projects prior to the transfer of the officers and staff from the development project to revenue budge. Subsequently the Ministry of Establishment now public Administration had issued circular dated 11th January, 1992 specifically providing a time frame of not exceeding six months for regularization of the service of the persons brought into revenue set up from the Development projects.

4. In the case of Gazetted officers their regularization required consultation with the PSC and it was made obligatory to finalize as per recruitment Rules and sent requisition to the PSC for regularization. The PSC was also required by the afore-said circular to complete all formalities for regularization within a minimum period of five months. The Ministry of Agriculture sat over the matter of regularization of the service of the writ petitioners till 10th May, 1999, on which date, they were regularized. The writ respondent Nos. 6-17 who entered in the government service from the autonomous body of BARI were neither regularized, nor their appointment in class-1 government posts were approved by the president though their services were confirmed by the competent authority. Thus the writ respondent Nos. 6-17 though doing the same job as scientific officer junior in service to the writ petitioners, the Ministry of Agriculture issued a notification under SRO No. 10/Law/2003 dated 12th January, 2003, purporting to be an amendment to the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No. XXII of 1976) providing that the officers who were transferred from BARI to government service had been granted seniority from the date of their original appointment in the BARI. It was a colorable legislation which is in conflict with articles 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution and the provisions of the services (Re-organization and conditions) Act, 1975 and the Amendment to the soil Resources Development Institute (Officers and staff) service Regulations, 1998.

5. Admittedly, the writ petitioners were appointed on a development project on different dates. Some of them were appointed in 1986, some of them were appointed later on but they did not give the exact date in their appointments. Their services were regularized by a notification under memo dated 5th June, 1993, with effect from 1st July, 1992 on temporary basis for a period of six months and then they were permanently absorbed in the revenue set up by notification dated 10th May, 1999, on the recommendation of the public service commission. It has been mentioned therein that their seniority will be decided in accordance with rule 3 of Rules of 1995. Their claim is that writ respondent Nos. 6-17 entered in the service on 1st October, 1993, and therefore, they are junior to them. They claimed that the Ministry of public Administration in violation of the Rules regularized their service in the revenue set up much latter than they were legally entitled to be absorbed.

<u>6. The High court was of the view that the service of the writ petitioners were regularized with effect from 10th May, 1999, although as per public Administration's circular under memo dated 11th January, 1992, their regularization should have been made within six months from the date of their absorption on temporary basis on 1st July, 1992,. It further observed that they had acquired a right of regularization within six months from the date of ad-hoc appointment but for the neglect or lathes on the part of the government, they were made junior to some of the writ respondents, and therefore, the notification dated 12th January, 2003 ultra vires articles 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution. By this notification the president in exercise of powers under article 142 of the constitution amended rule 6 of Soil Resources Development Institute officers and Employees Appointment Rules, 1998. The amendment is reproduced below:</u>

<u>কৃষি মন্ত্রণালয়ের ৬-২-১৪০০ বাং মোতাবেক ২০-০৫-১৯৯৩ ইং তারিখে জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপন নং কৃষি-৩/বিবিধ-২/৯৩/২৮৫ দ্বারা Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute Ordinance, 1976 (LXII of 1976) এর অধীন স্থাপিত Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute, অতঃপর উক্ত ইনস্টিটিউট বলিয়া উল্লিখিত, এর নিম্নলিখিত এর নিম্নবর্ণিত কর্মকতা ও কর্মচারীগণকে মৃত্তিকা সম্পদ উন্নয়ন ইনস্টির্টিউটে হস্তাম্ভরের কারণে তাহাদের চাকুরী মৃত্তিকা সম্পদ উন্নয়ন ইঁনস্টিটিউটে হস্তান্তরিত বান্যস্ত হইয়াছে বলিয়া গণ্য করা হইবে, এবং উক্ত কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীগণের চাকুরী পৃথক পৃথকভাবে তাহাদের চাকুরীতে প্রথম যোগদানের তারিখ হইতে সরকারি চাকুরী হিসাবে গণ্য করতঃ অবসরতাতা ও অবসরজনিত সুবিধাদিসহ জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণের জন্য এই বিধিমালার আওতাধীন কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী হিসাবে গণ্য করা হইবে, যথাঃ-</u>

<u>(ক) Directorate of Agriculture (Research and Education) এর কর্মকর্তা কর্মচারীগণ যাহারা Ordinance LXII of 1976 এর section 16 (c) এর অধীন উক্ত ইনস্টিটিউটে হস্তান্তরিত বা ন্যস্ত (stand transferred) হইয়া উহার অধীনস্থ এনালাইটিক্যাল সার্ভিসেস ডিভিশনে কর্মরত ছিলেন; এবং</u>

<u>(খ) উক্ত ইনস্টিটিউটের এনালাইটিক্যাল সার্ভিসেস ডিভিশনের কুমিল্লা, রাজশাহী, খুলনা ও জয়দেবপুর আঞ্চলিক গবেষণাগারে কর্মরত কর্মকতা ও কর্মচারীগণ ৷</u>

7. The Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institutes employees and officers having been transferred to the soil Resources Development Institute, those employees and officers would be deemed to have been appointed from the date of joining in the government service and that they will get seniority, pension benefits etc. from , the date of joining.

8. It is on record that there was no law or rules or regulations prescribing the procedure to be followed for regularization of the officers and employees appointed in development projects in the revenue set up. It is only by SRO 65 under memo dated 2nd May, 1995, the government formulated the Rules. The procedure to be following for regularization has been mentioned in rule 3 thereon. This rule provides inter alia that-

a) in a revenue budget post if an officer or employee is appointed on temporary basis in a project and if his appointment is made after following the appointment procedures of the government, the service of such officer or employee will be regularised.

b) there should be continuity of service till the date of regularization.

c) prior to the date of regularization the service of the employee must be satisfactory.

d) if an officer or employee of the revenue budget is on leave preparatory retirement or is retired from the service, his service be treated with retrospective effect from the date of leave preparatory retirement or the retirement, as the case may be, but his service must be satisfactory till the date of leave preparatory retirement.

e) The posts which require the recommendation of the public service commission, regularization will be made on the recommendation of PSC and in respect of other posts, the recommendation of the departmental promotion committee will be necessary.

9. As regards seniority rule 4 provides:

জ্যৈষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ - (১) এই বিধিমালার আওতায় নিয়মিতকৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যেষ্ঠতা নিয়মিত করণের তারিখ হইতে গণনা করা হইবে; তবে একই প্রকল্পে পূর্বে নিয়োজিত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী চাকুরীর প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের অভাবে (পদধারীর ত্রুটির কারণে নহে) পরে নিয়োজিত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর পূর্বে যা একই সংগে নিয়মিত না হইয়া পরবর্তীতে নিয়মিত হইলেও পরে নিয়োজিত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর উপরে তাহার জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে ৷

(২) একই তারিখে কোন প্রকল্পে নিযুক্ত কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীগণের জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে নিম্নরূপ-

(ক) উক্তরূপে নিয়োগের সময় সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক প্রস্তুতকৃত মেধা তালিকা ও প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং (যদি থাকে) এর ভিত্তিতে; এবং

(খ) ঊক্তরূপে তালিকা যা প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং না থাকিলে ন্যূনতম শিক্ষাগত যোগ্যতা অর্জনের বৎসরের এবং উক্ত বৎসর একই হইলে বয়সের ভিত্তিতে।

(৩) নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর নিয়োগের তারিখ এবং রাজস্ব বাজেটের পদে নিয়মিত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর নিয়মিতকরণের তারিখ একই হইলে নিয়মিতভাবে নিযুক্ত কর্মকর্তাগণ বা ক্ষেত্রমতে কর্মচারীগণ রাজস্ব বাজেটের পদে নিয়মিত ত কর্মকর্তা বা ক্ষেত্রমতে কর্মচারীগণের উপর জ্যেষ্ঠতা পাইবেন।

8) এই বিধিমালার আওতায় নিযমিতকৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী পরবর্তীকালে বাংলাদেশ সিভিল সার্ভিসের কোন ক্যাডারে অন্তর্ভুক্ত হইলে ক্যাডার ভুক্তির তারিখ হইতে সংশ্লিষ্ট ক্যাডারে তাহার জ্যেষ্ঠতা গণণা করা হইবে ৷

(a) the seniority will be counted from the date of regularization of an officer or employee but if an officer or employee is appointed whose service has been regularised after regularization   of an officer or employee" appointed later on due to shortage of relevant service record, who has been working in the same project, the officer or employee who has been appointed earlier will get seniority.

(b) in case of appointment of an officer or employee appointed on the same day, the seniority will be decided in the following manner:

(i) according to the gradation list prepared by the authority and the grading, if any;

(ii) in the absence of the above, on the basis of the year of acquiring the basic qualification and if the year is the same, on the basis of age

(c) if the date of appointment in the project of an officer or employee is the same with an officer or employee of the revenue budget, the officer or employee appointed in the revenue budget shall gel seniority.

(d) if an officer or employee is encadered by the public service com-mission later on, their seniority will be decided from the date of encadrement.

10. On consideration of almost similar Rules in, respect of officers and employees of development projects, who have been regularised in the revenue set up, this court in LGED v. Mizanur Rahman 17 BLC (AD) 91, held as under:

(i) Whenever any vacancy in LGED is created in the revenue set up, it shall consider for absorption of employees or officers of the development projects within the meaning of section 2 (ga) of the Rule, 2005, If the project in which s/he is working is completed subject to the condition that such employee or officer has requisite qualifications for the said post.

(ii) whenever a vacant post is created in the revenue budget, the WED shall absorb/transfer an employee or officer from the development project mentioned in clause (1) to fill up that post in accordance with Rules of 1985 and the ECNEC's decision dated 10th January, 2008.

(iii) An officer or employee shall be absorbed if s/he was appointed in the development project within the meaning or rule 2 (ka) of Rules, 2005 in accordance with the procedures prescribed for appointment in public employment.

(iv) An officer or employee must have requisite qualifications for the post in which he is seeking absorption.

(v) An officer or employee must have continuity in service in the project in which he is working.

(vi) An officer or employee must have satisfactory service record before his case is considered for regularization in the revenue budget.

(vii) If an officer and employee whose rank and status does not relate to the posts advertised by the impugned notifications on the day of its publications, such officer or employee would not be eligible for consideration for absorption.

(viii) The employees and officers who have been working in the development projects mentioned in clause (1) on monthly pay basis would only be eligible for consideration for absorption in the revenue budget.

(ix) Unless and until vacancies in the revenue budget in the LGED are created, the employees and officers of the development project mentioned in clause (1) cannot claim as of right to be absorbed in the revenue budget;

(x) While considering and selecting an employee or officer of the development project for absorption in the revenue budget, the appointing authority shall maintain strictly the prevailing quota system for employment in the public employment being following by the Government.

(xi) The LGED shall consider the cases of those working on master roll basis for absorption in the revenue budget by phases if they have requisite qualifications subject to availability of vacancies according to their seniority.

11. The present Rules prescribes the procedure in deciding the seniority in the similar manner.

<u>12. Now taking these Rules as it stand, whether the writ petitioners can claim seniority over the write respondents. Admittedly the writ petitioners have been transferred in the revenue budget temporarily on 1st July, 1992, on which date, three was no rules regulating their seniority. They could claim seniority. They could claim seniority in pursuance of rule 4 of the Rules circulated by SRO NO. 65 dated 2nd May, 1995. There is no denial of the fact that they had been regularized by order dated 9th November, 2003 with retrospective from 10th May, 1999 as per Rules of 1995. They have accepted their regularization and did not take any exception because of rule 4 of Rules of 1995. The writ respondents have been appointed on regular basis. They were not appointed on any project, and therefore, the writ petitioners cannot claim seniority over the regular employee. It is true that as per Ministry of public Administration's Circular under memo dated 11th January, 1998, there was a direction for regularization within six months from the date of creation of post in the revenue set up but the authority did not act as per direction. This circular may be taken as pious desire of the authority and directory in nature. It has no force of law. More so, this circular will not prevail over. Rules of 1995, which have force of law within meaning of article 152 of the constitution.</u>

13. Under rule 4 of Rules 1995, the criteria for determining the seniority has been spelt out. In presence of these Rules, the writ petitioners cannot claim any right on the basis of the circular of the Ministry of জনপ্রশাসান, dated 11th January, 1992. The High court Division without declaring the rule 4 of the regularization and Determination of Seniority of the employee transferred from the development projects declared the writ petitioners as senior to the writ respondents mainly on the reasoning that had they been regularized within six months they would not have opposed rule 4. How fallacy the opinion is? A rule which has force of law cannot be ignored or impeded its enforceability only because it is in conflict with the circular. It failed to notice that the circular which has been circulated by a Ministry which has no force of law. It is issued for the purpose of internal departmental officials to follow the guidelines and the violation of any of the provision does not confer a right upon an officer or employee, which can be enforceable by law. Secondly, the Rules have been promulgated by the government in accordance with the provisions of the constitution, which will prevail upon the circular.

14. Rule 6 ka in the soil Resources Development institute (officers and staff) Recruitment Rules, 1998 has been added by the president in exercise of powers under article 140 (2) of the constitution in prior consultation with PSC providing that by reason of transfer of the officers and employees of Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute to soil Resources Development Institute, their services shall be deemed to be employee of the latter institute from the date of joining in the service and that their benefits and seniority will be determined accordingly. The substance of the amendment of the Rules by means of addition of a rule is that the officers and employee who have been appointed in Bangladesh Agricultural Research institute shall get their seniority with retrospective effect from the date of joining in the service by reason of their transfer to the Soil Resources Development Institute.

15. The writ petitioners cannot claim any infringement and /or infraction of their existing right by reason of this amendment on simple reason that they have not been anointed on regular basis in accordance with soil Resources Development Institute Recruitment Rules, 1998 and therefore, by these Rules their purported rights of seniority,   if any, have not been taken away. A statute, is to be deemed to be retrospective (Allen V. Gold Reefs of W. Africa (1990) 1 Ch 656). which takes away or impairs any vested right acquired under existing laws, or creates a new obligation or imposes a new obligation or imposes a new duty, or attaches a new disability in respect to transactions already past. Lord Hatherley in Pardo V. Bingham, (1870). L.R. 4 Ch. App. 735 said:

'whether on general principles the statute ought in this particular section to be held to operate retrospectively, the general rule of law undoubtly being, that there be a clear indication either from the subject matter or from the wording of a statute, the statute is not to receive a retrospective construction……….

16. Craies on Statute Law, Seventh Edn. it is said, 'Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive' it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement; as statutes of oblivion or of pardon. They are certainly retrospective, and literally both concerning and after the facts committed.' As a general rule of law that statutes are not to operate retrospectively but sometimes it is expressly enacted that an enactment shall be retrospective. Craies in the same edition at page 392 said that if it is a necessary implication from the language employed that the legislature intended a particular section to have a retrospective operation, the courts will give it such an operation.

17. In the chapter of 'Statutes virtually retrospective' craies at page 396 said, sometimes a statute, although not intended to be retrospective, will in fact have a retrospective operation. For instance, if two persons enter into a contract, and afterwards a statute is passed, which, as Cockburn, C.J. said in Duke of Devonshire V. Barrow (1877) 2QBD 286 'engrafts an enactment Rayon existing contracts' and thus operates so as to produce a result which is something   quite different from the original intention of the contracting parties, such a statute has, in effect, a retrospective operation.' As observed above, the writ petitioners existing rights under the Rules  have not been taken away. More so, the language used in the amendment has no ambiguity and in clear terms it is said that it will have retrospective operation under such situation the court cannot give it prospective operative.

<u>18. The views expressed by of the High Court Division that the writ petitioners' were appointed in the development project and ultimately they were included in the revenue set up in 1983 with effect from 01.07.1992 and it was duty of the government to make them regularized and having not done so, obviously made the writ petitioners junior are not inconformity with law. It must assign reason why the amendment of the Rules should not be given retrospective operation. This court in Bangladesh Rtd. Govt. Employees welfare Association v. Bangladesh, 51 DLR (AD) 121 observed that a legislative enactment or a government action cannot be knocked down as unconstitutional even if it results in equality or is even shocking to the conscience unless such enactment or such action is violative of any provision of the constitution or law and that inequity or unconscionable effect cannot be rectified by the court applying article 27. If a diffential treatment satisfies the twin test of logical classification and reasonableness, it cannot be shocking to conscience. There will always be difference between a man and another man or a pensioner and another pensioner, but the question is whether such difference has any relevance in search of nexus between the object of the legislation and the classification made observed in Air-way Electric Appliance Corp. V. Day (1924) 266 US 71.</u>

19. The writ petitioners did not make sufficient pleadings in support of inconsistency of the Rules with articles 27 and 29. The basis of their claim of ultraviresness has been stated in paragraph 12 and onwards. They stated that their regularization was deliberately delayed by seven years, but the writ respondents were given ante-dated seniority. They further stated that rule 4 of 1995 Rules is in conflict with the BCS seniority Rules 1983. To declare a law to be ultra vires the constitution on the basis of an application by an employee in the service of the Republic, he must have acquired a right. The writ petitioners right have been recognized only on 2nd May, 1995 and as per provisions of these Rules they cannot claim seniority over the writ respondents. More so, if one claims inconsistency of any law with any of the provisions of the constitutions, article 26 of the constitution provides that all existing law inconsistent with provision in part III of the constitution shall to the extent of consistency become void, The writ petitioner did not make any statement that how rule 4 of the Rules 1995 is inconsistent with Articles 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution.

20. Assuming that rule 4 is inconsistent with article 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution, the High Court Division did not declare it as such. It has declared the notification dated 12th January, 2003 of the Ministry of Agriculture without making any observation as to whether this notification ultra vires rule 4 of Rules 1995. What is surprising to note here is that neither the writ petitioners made sufficient pleadings in support of their claim that rule 6ka of Soil Resources Development Institute Recruitment Rules, 1998 ultra vires rule 4 of the Rules of 1985, they made any statement nor did the High Court Division make any findings or observations in this regard and abruptly declared rule 6 ultra vires articles 27 and 29 (1).

<u>21. We would, however, like to observe here that we have been noticing in good number of cases that despite there are provisions for regularization of the service of employees or officers in the revenue set up either within six months or within such time as soon as the posts in the revenue budget are lying vacant, the government or the PSC intentionally delays in the process of regularizing their service and sometimes, it recommends some junior employees or officers to the PSC for regularization and then recommend the senior employees to the PSC for regularization, who have been appointed on ad-hoc basis earlier with the result that the junior employees or officers get seniority and status over the senior employees and officers. This has created anomaly in the service of different departments. This discriminatory treatment should be avoided. Henceforth, it is directed that if any post in the revenue budget lies vacant, the employee or officer who is eligible for appointment to the said post should be regularized and if such appointment requires recommendation of the PSC his name should be recommended in due time so that he should not be deprived of his right of seniority than the junior employee of officer.</u>

22. This appeal is allowed with the above observations. Civil Petition No. 691 of 2007 will be guided by the judgment of this appeal.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 12th June, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4791 of 1995).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 12th day of June, 2005 passed by a learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4791 of 1995 making the Rule absolute in part.

<u>2. Facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.1(a)-1(c) herein as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 03 of 1986 in the Court of the then Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Sadar, Gopalgonj for declaration of title to the suit land along with some other declarations stating, inter alia, that 'ka' and 'kha' scheduled land to the plaint belonged to Bireswar Dhali, Malin Chandra Dhali, the plaintiff and Alok Chandra Dhali. Alok Chandra Dhali sold 26½  decimals land from schedules la and 'kha to the plaint by a registered kabala dated 20.02.1954 in favour of the plaintiff. Bireswar Dhali transferred 19½ decimals land from 'ka' scheduled land by a deed of gift dated 03.09.1984 in favour of the plaintiff. The S.A record was wrongly recorded in the name of Laxmimoni, the mother of Bireswar along with others. The said entry of Laxmimoni in the S.A. record was wrong. Alok Chandra by his transfer vide the sale, deed dated 20.02.1954 exhausted his share in the suit land. The S.A record was also prepared in the name of Alok Chandra wrongly. Defendant No.1 created two kabalas from the sons of Alok Chandra Dhali and demanded title in the suit land for the first time on 06.11.1985, on the basis of the said kabala; hence the suit.</u>

3. The trial Court dismissed the suit (the date of the decree is not available from the record). Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No.15 of 1991 before the District Judge, Gopalgonj. The Appellate Court allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial Court with observation that the plaintiff ought to have filed the suit for declaration of title and partition by impleading the necessary parties in the, suit. After remand the plaintiff amended the plaint and added the prayer for confirmation of possession and for partition.

4. The suit was contested by defendant No.1 by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that Alok Chandra and Bireswar did not transfer any land to the plaintiff by the kabalas dated 20.02.1984 and 03.09.1984 respectively. Alok Chandra Dhali and Bireswar Dhali had migrated to India 25/30 years before and they died there but the plaintiff created the false deeds of transfer in their names. The defendant purchased the suit land from the heirs of Alok Dhali and Bireswar by the three kabalas and he has been in possession thereof by mutating his name and paying rents to the government. The plaintiff had no title and possession in the suit, so they had no cause of action to file the suit and the suit was liable to be dismissed.

5. After amendment P.W 1 was recalled and he was examined. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.06.2002 decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in respect of 06½ 2 decimal land in Plot No.2469 of R.S Khatian No. 606 and also giving saham for the said area of the land. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 69 of 1995 before the District Judge, Gopalgonj. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gopalgonj by his judgment and decree dated 28.09.1995 dismissed the appeal and at the same time dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 47 of 1985 before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and decreed the suit in part confirming plaintiff's title and possession in 59 decimals land in schedule 'ka' and 13 decimals land in schedule 'kha' to the plaint, but dismissed the prayer for partition for "non joinder of parties and property." The learned Judge further observed that "However, the plaintiff may file a fresh suit for partition impleading the Roads and High Way and on bringing the entire land of schedule 'ka ' and Kha to the plaint in the 'said suit."

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant-appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1160 of 2005 before this Court and leave was granted giving rise to this appeal to consider the submissions made on his behalf to the following effect:

"Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in reversing the concurrent finding of facts made by the Courts below that the plaintiff has failed to prove his right, title, interest and possession over suit land, particularly the land described in 'ka' schedule of the plaint without controverting the above finding with reference to evidence on record, confirming the title and possession of the plaintiff over 59 decimal of land from 'ka' schedule that is in Plot No. 2469 of R.S Khatian No. 603 of the aforesaid Mauza. Although the plaintiff filed the instant suit for .20 decimals of land of 'ka' schedule of the plaint and 6½ decimals from 'kha' schedule land of the plaint and the above finding of the High Court is beyond the pleading.".

7. Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Counsel for the appellant, has firstly pointed out that in the suit, the plaintiff did not examine himself and on his behalf his son was examined as P.W1 without having any authority from him (the plaintiff). Therefore, in the absence of any evidence of the plaintiff, there was only pleading and pleading could not be basis for decreeing a suit. He has further contended that the High Court Division itself found that the suit for partition was not maintainable because the necessary party, namely, Roads and Highway, in whose favour a portion of suit plot was acquired, was not impleaded as a defendant and that the entire properties of the khatian were not brought in hotchpotch, it erred in law in decreeing the suit confirming title and possession in favour of the plaintiff in respect of 59+13 decimals land from the two schedules. He has also contended that suit land was vague as the same was not described as per the mandate of Order VII, ride 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the plaintiff was not entitled to the declaration of title and confirmation of possession. He has lastly contended that both the Courts below on discussion of the evidence, found possession of the defendant in the suit land. The proper suit which ought to have been filed by the plaintiff was the suit for partition, but the High Court Division having found the suit for partition non maintainable due to non impleading of the necessary parties and for non inclusion of the entire properties of the khatain in hotchpotch committed a serious error of law in giving declaration of title of the plaintiff to the extent of 59+13 decimals land from the two schedules and as such, the impugned judgment and order be set aside and the appeal be allowed.

8. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondent, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He has submitted that the defendant failed to prove his title in the suit land on the basis of his purchase from the son of Bireswar and Alok Dhali. He has further submitted that the plaintiffs kabala is of the year 1964, whereas, those of the defendant were of the year 1966. Therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in decreeing the suit finding title of the plaintiff in 59+13 decimals land and there being no merit in the appeal, the same be dismissed.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Counsel as well as the learned Advocate-on-Record of the respective party and we have gone through the materials on record. Admittedly initially the suit was filed only for declaration of title along with the other declarations that the kabalas dated 03.06.1985 being Nos. 498 and 4199 of the Office of Sub-Registrar, Gopalgonj in favour of defendant No.1 showing Modhusudan as its executor were fraudulent, collusive, illegal, null and void, inoperative; and was not binding' upon the plaintiff and the S.A khatians being Nos. 260 and 72 in the name of Alek Dhaki as described in the schedule to the plaint was fraudulent, collusive; illegal, null and void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The suit was dismissed and on appeal, the Appellate Court sent the suit on remand to the trial Court with the following observations;

"উক্তরূপে উচিৎ এবং যথাযথ ব্যক্তিদেরকে পক্ষ করতঃ স্বত্ব সাব্যস্ত পূর্বক বাটোয়ারার প্রার্থনাসহ আনুষাঙ্গিক প্রতিকারের মোকদ্দমায় পক্ষদ্বয়ের বিবাদমান বিষয়ে নিষ্পত্তি উপযুক্ত মোকদ্দমা বলিয়া মনে করি। সুতরাং তর্কিত পর্যালোচনা ও তন্মুরে উপনীত সিদ্ধান্ত তথা রায় ও ডিক্রী আইন ও ঘটনাগত দিক হইতে সঠিক ও যুক্তিযুক্ত না  হওয়ায় তাহা বহালযোগ্য নহে রদরহিতযোগ্য হইতেছে এবং মূল মোকদ্দমাটি উপরোক্ত পর্যালোচনার আলোকে পুনঃ বিচারের নিমিত্তে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতে প্রেরণের যোগ্য হইতেছে। অত্র বিবেচ্য বিষয়ের সিন্ধান্ত অত্ররুপে নিস্পত্তি হয়। ফলতঃ অত্র আপীল মোকদ্দমাটি কৃতকার্য্য হইয়াছে। "

10. From the above quoted observation made by the Appellate Court, it is clear that though the plaintiff amended the plaint adding the prayer for partition and also made amendment in the schedule to the plaint, he did not implead the necessary parties and also did not bring all the properties in hotchpotch. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division itself gave finding in clear language that in view of the fact that necessary parties were not impleaded in the suit and all the properties were not brought in hotchpotch, the suit for partition was not maintainable, yet decreed the suit only in respect the prayer for title of the plaintiff. From the evidence, it appears that some of the P.Ws admitted the possession of defendant No. 1 in the suit land. The High Court Division did not reverse the finding of possession given by the Courts below with reference to the evidence on record. It further appears that the High Court Division gave abrupt finding that the plaintiff was in possession in the suit and that the defendant was not in possession thereof.

11. We have not been able to lay our hand on any provision of law either in the Code of Civil Procedure or any other law that when the plaintiff(s) makes the prayer for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for partition, the Court can suo moto split up the prayers and give the relief to the plaintiff(s) for declaration in respect of the property which was subsequently included in the schedule to the plaint for partition. It is a fact that the plaintiff is in possession in the homestead property of plot No. 2469 and it is also in evidence that the defendant is in possession in a portion of the suit land.

<u>12. In view of the above, we are of the view that justice would be best served to both the parties if the appeal is remanded to the Appellate Court for hearing afresh giving chance to the plaintiff to amend the plaint by impleading the necessary party, namely, Roads and Highway and the other necessary parties, if there be any and also bringing in hotchpotch the entire property of the khatian. In the context, we would observe that under section 107, of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Appellate Court is clothed with all the powers of a trial Court. The plaintiff is directed to make the necessary amendment in the plaint within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of this judgment, failing which the suit shall stand dismissed.</u>

13. In view of the fact that we are sending the appeal back to the Appellate Court for hearing it afresh, we refrain ourselves from making any comment about the first point raised by Mr. Nurul Amin as noted hereinbefore. However, the Appellate Court will decide the point along with the other issues. The parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the position and the possession of the suit land till disposal of the appeal.

14. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order is set aside. The appeal is sent back to the Appellate Court for hearing it afresh and for disposal in accordance with law in the, light of the observation made and the finding given hereinbefore.

15. With above observation, finding, and the direction, this appeal is disposed of.

End.
