Kamal-ul Alam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants (in both the cases) 
Nurul Islam Sujan, Advocate instructed by Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents (in both the cases)
parties:
Most. Ajimon Bewa and others. ------ Appellants (in both the cases)
VS
Md. Mosiruddin Fakir and others ------- Respondents (in both the cases)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 5th day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4692 of 2005 with Civil Revision No.4688 of 2005)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. These two appeals, by leave, are from the judgment and order dated 5th day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4692 of 2005 heard analogously with Civil Revision No. 4688 of 2005 making the Rules absolute issued in both the revisions.

2. Respondent Nos. 1-9 as the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 458 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Shibgonj Bogra for declaration of title. From the facts as stated in the leave petition, it appears that during the pendency of the aforesaid suit, the plaintiffs filed another suit being Other Suit No. 110 of 1985 in the same Court for recovery of possession.

3. The case of the plaintiffs in both the suits, in short, was that Moshor Fakir, lit their predecessor, acquired the suit land from landlord-Rafatullah Mondal and had been in possession thereof since 1338 BS as korfa tenant and C.S. Khatian No. 93 in respect of suit land was correctly prepared I in the name of Moshor Fakir. Moshor Fakir while possessing the suit land died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his legal heirs and since his death, the plaintiffs had been possessing the same. The defendants had no right, title and possession in the suit land. On 01.11.1984, defendant No. 2 disclosed to plaintiff No.1 that defendant No.1 executed and registered a kabala in his favour in respect of the suit land and MRR Khatian in respect of the suit land was prepared in the name of defendant No.1, Defendant No. 2 further disclosed that he would build a pucca house therein, Thereafter, plaintiff No.1 went to the local Tashil office and came to know for the first time that the name of defendant No.1 was included in the MRR Khatian along with the name of the plaintiffs father; hence the suit.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Rafatullah Mondal was the landlord and Moshor Fakir was a korfa tenant under him in the suit land. Moshor Fakir 3rd Falgun, 1338 BS executed an 'istafapatra' in respect of the suit land in favour of the landlord and transferred his right, title and interest in his favour and he (landlord) took khas possession of the suit land. Thereafter, Rafatullah Mondal on 19.11.1942 transferred 91 decimals land including the suit land by a kabala in favour of his son, Tasiruddin Mondal and thereafter.

<u>5. Tasiruddin Mondal transferred the same to defendant No.1 by a kabala dated 18.02.1948. Defendant No.1 on 02.08.1960 transferred 9¾ decimals land from Plot No. 381 to Monsur Ali Mondal and he had been possessing the same. Defendant No.1 transferred 8 decimals land to defendant No.2 by a registered kabala. Said Monsur Ali Mondal transferred 93/4 decimals land to defendant No. 2 and thus defendant No. 2 acquired 173/4 decimals land and he had been possessing the same. Defendant No. 2 built a pucca house long before filing the suit, The defendants had been running business in a portion of the house. The plaintiffs had no right, title in the suit land and the defendants did not dispossess them there from on 18.11.1948. The suit land was not properly valued and sufficiently stamped, so, the suit was liable to be dismissed.</u>

6. Both the suits were heard analogously and the learned Assistant Judge by a common judgment dated 24.07.1989 (separate decrees were drawn and signed) decreed the suits, Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants preferred Other Appeal Nos.142 of 1989 and 147 of 1989 respectively before the District Judge, Bogra. The Appellate Court by a common judgment dated 30.06.1992(separate decrees were drawn and signed) remanded the suits to the trial Court for fresh trial. After remand, the suits were heard afresh and the learned Assistant Judge by the judgment dated 13.05.2004 (separate decrees were drawn and signed) decreed both the suits. Against the judgment   and decree of the trial Court, the predecessor of appellant Nos. 1-4 and 5 preferred Other Appeal Nos.68 and 72 of 2004 respectively before the District Judge, Bogra. The learned Joint District Judge 2nd Court, Bogra by a common judgment dated 05.10.2005(separate decrees were drawn and signed) allowed both the appeals and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed   the suit, Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs  filed Civil Revision Nos.4688 of 2005 and 4692 of 2005 before the High Court Division and a learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rules absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1807 and 1808 of 2008 and leave was granted by this Court to consider the submissions made on their behalf by their learned Advocate-on-Record which are as follows:

"Mr. Md. Mazibar Rahman, learned Advocate-on-Record„ appearing for the petitioners submitted that the defendants have proved their case and on the other hand the plaintiffs failed to prove the case of possession inasmuch as for non-impleading the necessary parties the suit flied by the said plaintiffs is not maintainable, as it has been clearly found by the learned District Judge while disposing of the Appeals; being Other Appeal No. 68 of 2004 and Other Appeal No. 72 of 2004 heard analogously and passed the judgment and decree reversing the judgment and decree passed analogously on 13.05.2004 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Shibgonj, Bogra in Other Suit No. 45 8 of 1994 and Other Suit No. 110 of 1985 and the High Court Division without reversing the findings of the Appellate Court arrived at a wrong and erroneous decision on a total misconception and non-consideration of the case; that the learned joint District judge being the last Court of findings of fact arrived at a clear finding in reversing the judgments and decrees of the trial Court and on the other hand the High Court Division reversing all the findings of the Appellate Court arrived a wrong and erroneous decision which is also perverse. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that the plaintiffs having been failed to prove the case and on the other hand the defendants proved the case including the Estofapatra given by Moshor Fakir in favour Rafatullah and thereafter, the Rafatullah transferred the suit land on 19.11.1942 in favour of his son Tasimuddin and since then there is the continuation of possession of the defendants and the High Court Division having failed to consider the same the impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2008 is liable to be set aside, The learned Advocate-on-Record finally submitted that in view of the facts that the plaintiffs did not file the suit in time and it is the clear findings of the appellate Court that ‘‘ নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, বাদীগণ সময়মত মামলা দায়ের করেন নাই। তাই বাদীদের মামলাটি তামাদী দোষে অচল।" and the said findings having not been reversed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, the finding that " বিবাদীগণ বাদীকে নালিশী জমি হইতে বেদখল করে নাই।" have also not been reversed and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside,"

7. Mr. Kamal-ul Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the 'appellants, has reiterated the submissions on which leave was granted and in support of his submissions, he has referred to the materials on record including the plaint, the written statement and the deposition of the witnesses.

8. Mr. Nurul Islam Sujan, learned Counsel, for the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

9. The judgment and decree impugned before the High Court Division was the judgment and decree of reversal, so it was its incumbent duty to see whether the Appellate Court being the last Court of fact adverted to the findings of the trial Court in reversing its judgment and decree. Let us see whether the High Court Division did the said job in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restoring those of the trial Court.

10. From the judgment of the Appellate Court, it appears that the main question to be decided in the suit was whether Moshor Fakir surrendered the suit land to Rafatullah Mondal and whether after surrender Rafatullah Mondal got possession thereof, The Appellate Court considering the evidence on record came to the clear finding that PW1-Masiruddin Fakir admit-ted in his cross-examination that there were homestead of the defendants in the suit land and presently, he lives at Sadullahpur and one of his brothers lives 1/2 miles away. The Appellate Court further found that from the plaint, it appeared that out of the three sons of Moshor Fakir, plaintiff No.1 was Masir Fakir, plaintiff No. 2 was Abdul Fakir and plaintiff No. 3 was Dilbar Fakir and their addresses were shown at Sadullahpur and the addresses of their two sisters, Maziran and Sutki, were shown at their husband's addresses, so at the time of filing Title Suit No.458 of 1984 for declaration of title, the plaintiffs did not reside in the suit land.

<u>11. The Appellate Court further found that in the plaint, the plaintiff did not say as to how they exercised their right of possession in the suit land. Though the plaintiff claimed that the defendants dispossessed them from the suit land on 18.11.1984. from the testimonies of the plaintiffs' witnesses, it was clearly proved that long before the said date of alleged dispossession, the plaintiffs were not in possession of the suit land. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the PWs proved that the defendants had been in possession of the suit land long before the filing of the suit, the defendants' witnesses also said that defendant No. 1 had been in possession of the suit land since 30/35 years, PW1 in his cross-examination stated that Refatullah used to possess the suit land, The Appellate Court further observed to the effect that " উভয় পরে সাক্ষীদের সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় ইহা স্পষ্ট বুঝা যায় যে, ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখের বহু পূর্ব হইতে নালিশী জমিতে ১নং বিবাদী গেন্দালা দখলকার আছে। অর্থাৎ ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখে বাদীকে বেদখলের আর্জি বর্ণিত বক্তব্য সঠিক আছে। The Appellate Court further found that the plaintiff claimed that Moshor Fakir did not give ‘ইস্তফা’ of the suit land to Rafatullah and although the defendants spoke about the ‘ইস্তফা’ they did not file the same, yet PW1 admitted in his cross-examination that the suit land used to be possessed by Rafatullah. The Appellate Court also found that from the evidence of PW1 it was clearly proved that Rafatullah transferred the suit land in favour of his son, Tasiruddin on 19.11.1942 and had he not been in possession of the suit land, he would not have transferred the same in the name of his son and that it was not a believable story that in 1942, Rafatullah would create an ineffective deed in favour of his son thinking about the present suit and that no body would create a fake deed in favour of his son. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that since it was proved from the testimonies of the PWs that the plaintiffs had not been in possession of the suit land for a long time and they had left the suit property long before it could be clearly understood that Moshor Fakir gave 'Estafa' of the suit land in favour of Rafatullah. Therefore, Rafatullah had the right to transfer the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that from the documentary evidence, it appeared that except the C.S. and the MIRR khatian, the plaintiffs filed only one rent receipt and that also after the filing of the suit, on the other hand, on behalf of the defendants, besides the deeds dated 19.11.1942 in favour of Tasiruddin by Rafatullah, dated 18.02.1948 in favour of Gendala by Moshor and the deed dated 02.08.1960 in favour of Shahjalal, mutation khatian, DCR, 15 rent receipts and the other khatians were filed which also proved the defendants' possession in the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that the witnesses might tell lie or wrong, but the circumstances do not, the circumstances of case proved that the suit land reverted back to Rafatullah and he transferred the same in favour of his son who in turn sold the same in favour of Gendela, defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 and Mansur purchased the same land from Gendela.</u>

12. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the plaintiffs first filed the suit for declaration of title and then filed the second suit for eviction of the defendants from the suit land which proved that the defendants did not dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land, so the plaintiffs had no reasonable cause to file the suit for eviction and basically the plaintiffs were required to file a suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession, the plaintiffs' suits were not maintainable in law, The Appellate Court further found that the deeds being dated it 19.11.1942, 18.02.1948 and 02.08.1960 were very old documents and there was no reason to say that those were ineffective deeds, The Appellate Court also found that from the evidence of PW 1, it was clear that the plaintiffs transferred a portion of the suit land and from the two plaints, it appeared that the transferees from them were not made parties in the suit, so the plaintiffs had no right to pray for declaration of title in respect of the entire suit property and the suit was also bad for defect of party. The Appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs had no title and possession in the suit land and accordingly reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit.

13. The High Court Division in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court did not at all advert any findings of the Appellate Court as noted down hereinbefore. It further appears that in coming to the above noted findings, the Appellate Court discussed the evidence both oral and documentary, but the High Court Division failed to consider these findings of the Appellate Court with reference to the evidence on record and also failed to pin point how and why the Appellate Court committed the error in reversing those of the trial Court and it, in a very slip shod manner, just restored those of the trial Court. Thus, the High Court Division failed to exercise the jurisdiction vested in it under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We have gone through the pleading of the respective party and the evidence, we found the findings and the observation of the Appellate Court based on correct appreciation of the evidence.

14. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained and accordingly, the same is set aside, the appeals are allowed. There will no order as to cost.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 4th day of August, 2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1299 of 2003)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated the 4th day of August 2003 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division Writ Petition No. 1299 of 2003 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts giving rise to this appeal are as follows:

3. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as petitioners   (hereinafter referred to as the petitioners) filed the said writ petition before the High Court Division impugning the notification issued by respondent No. 1, the Secretary, Ministry of Land, under the signature of respondent No. 2, a Senior Assistant Secretary of the Ministry vide her office Memo: No.  ভূঃমঃ/শা-২মৌঃ নাঃ পঃ-৫/৯৯/৪৩৭ dated 27.08.2000 (annexure-11 to the writ petition) to have been "passed without   lawful authority."

4. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that on 23.06.1997 the petitioners along with five others filed an application before respondent No. 9, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Jagannathpur, against respondent No. 10 and 9 (nine) others for reviewing an ex-parte order of mutation dated 04.06.1995 passed in Mutation Miscellaneous Case No. 70 of 1994-95 stating, inter alia, that they have been owning and possessing the land described in the schedule to the application in ejmali from their predecessor-in-interest and S.A. khatian was prepared correctly in their respective names. The petitioners have been cultivating Aman and Boro paddy in the scheduled land. On 23.06.1997 when the petitioners approached to pay rent, they were informed that respondent No. 10, Jamshed Mia and 9(nine) others had collusively mutated the land in their names, "by purposely manufactured papers and documents" without serving any notice upon them. The application gave rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 196-97(Review). Pursuant to the notice issued its the review application, respondent No. 10 appeared and prayed for adjournment and the case was fixed on 31.07.1997 for hearing, but before that date on 29.07.1997, respondent No. 10 filed Miscellaneous Case (Revision) No. 07 of 1997 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sunamaganj (respondent No. 6) against the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 53/96-97(Review) and managed to get an order calling for the records from the office of respondent No. 9, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Jagannathpur and an order of stay of further proceedings of the said review miscellaneous case. Respondent No. 10 tried to kill time on this or that plea and ultimately, the case was fixed for hearing on 23.11.1998. Meanwhile, respondent No. 10 filed another application on 27.08.1997 before respondent No. 5, the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj with the prayer for adding 9 (nine) acres of land or 48 plots of Patleechak mouza and 26 acres of land of 106 plots of Moizpur mouza, in total 35 acres of land, to Darikhanjanpur mouza. On 18.11.1997, the petitioners filed a written objection before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sunamganj, respondent No. 6 opposing the prayer and stated in detail of the attempts of respondent No. 10 on different time for addition of certain plots from 2(two) different mouzas to be merged with Darikhanjanpur mouza. In the written objection, it was further stated that respondent No. 10 managed to serve notices upon the opposite parties of the case by forging their signatures in collusion with the process server, he managed to serve notice on Tara Mia who died in 1982, on Miajan and Kurpan Utah who died 40 years and 42 years respectively before filing the case and managed to obtain an ex-parte order on 04.06.1995 without serving any notice upon the petitioners and others. The office of respondent No. 5 rejected the said application for  addition of the said lands to Darikhanjanpur mouza by order dated 14.06.1998 considering the facts and circumstances of the case and all possible complicacies in respect of addition of the said two mouzas with Darikhanjanpur mouza. Respondent No. 10 again filed an application before respondent No. 5 for reviewing the said order dated 14.06.1998 which was also rejected by and under the signature of respondent No. 6 and communicated vide Office Memo SA 98/2352(2)1(3) dated 02.12.1998 in the said order, the respondent also discussed all possible complicacies of law8 and the reasons stated in the written objection filed by the petitioners and other as to the proposal of addition of the plots from two different mouzas with Darikhanjanpur. Against the said rejection, respondent No took an appeal before the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet being Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal No. 288 of 1998 who by order dated 14.12.1998 stayed operation of the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sunamganj and in addition opined that "proposal shall go to survey, and Settlement Dept for final decision." Accordingly, respondent No. 4 by his order dated 25.07.1999 sent the case records to the Director General of Land Records and Surveys Directorate, Tejgaon, for taking necessary action. The clever respondent, in the meantime, managed to obtain an order from the office of respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Land under the signature of respondent No. 2 vide her office Memo No.  ভূঃমঃ/শ-২ (মৌঃ নাঃ পঃ)-৫/৯৯/৪৩৭ dated 27.08.2000 of the administrative approval for addition of said 9 acres of land of 48 plots of Patleechak mouza and 26 acres of land of 106 plots of Moizpur mouza with Darikhanjanpur mouza; hence, the petitioners filed the writ petition impugning the said memo.

5. It was further contended by way of submission that the office of respondent No. 1 "Passed administrative approval Notification" under the signature of respondent No. 2 vide her office Memo No.  ভূঃমঃ/শ-২ (মৌঃ নাঃ পঃ)-৫/৯৯/৪৩৭ dated 27.08.2000 without serving any notice upon the petitioners and was beyond jurisdiction as he was not empowered under rules 321 and 322 of the Bengal Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935(hereinafter referred to as the manual, 1935). The procedure laid down in rules 321 and 322 of the Manual, 1935 were also not complied with by respondent Nos. 1 and 2 before issuing the impugned notification. The application of respondent No. 10 for addition of some plots from two different mouzas with Darikhanjanpur mouza was rejected twice by the office of respondent No. 5 under the signature of respondent No. 6 after considering the facts and circumstances of the case against which respondent No. 10 did not approach the immediate higher authority, but taking the advantage of political influence managed to obtain an administrative approval in this regard from respondent Nos. 1 and 2 who approved the some beyond jurisdiction. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 passed the order of approval without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners and others. Moreover, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were not the proper authorities under rules 321 and 322 of the manual, 1935 to give the administrative approval. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 passed the order of approval without taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the ease and the possible complicacy of laws where the Government will not be benefited, in any way, and will not cause any loss or injury to respondent No. 10, rather maps of three mouzas must be amended and the people of those three mouzas will suffer irreparable loss and injury about their record-of-rights, mutations, rents. In the present survey, the lands of those curtailed plots have been recorded under the previous Patleechak and Moizpur mouzas in the names of the petitioners and others by the survey authority and the attestation khatian has been prepared in their names, but respondent No. 10 did not raise any objection anywhere against such survey or attestation till today. The impugned order of approval was passed by the respondents for addition of certain plots from two different mouzas with Darikhanjanpur mouza on some unfounded, vague, illegal and arbitrary cause. The impugned notification was void, illegal, beyond jurisdiction and was the result of colourable exercise of power and as such, was liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and was of no legal effect.

Rules were framed under Part- IV called the State Acquisition Rule, 1951. Chapter-IV of the said Rules consisting rules 17-38 has provided for preparation and publication of record-of-rights. Sections 32 to 46 in Chapter-V of the Act, 1950 have provided fine preparation of compensation assessment roll and acquisition of rent receiving interests. Section 46 of the Act, 1950 has provided for modification of the record-of-rights prepared under Chapter-IV by eliminating the entire chain of interest of rent receivers and then for reprint and distribution of the record-of-rights. Part II Chapter II, Part III Chapter III, Part IV, Chapters VA, VI to X1 of the Act, 1950 are with regard to acquisition of rent receiving interests and for payment, of compensation for such acquisition. Sections 81 to 143 of the Act have dealt with class, status, right and liabilities of tenants, enhancement and reduction of rents, collection and realisation of rent, subdivision and amalgamation holdings and maintenance of Record of rights. Section 144 of the Act and subsequently added section 144A (inserted by amendment, 1967) are in Part- V. Chapter-XVII in Part-V of the Act has provided for maintenance and revision of the record-of-rights and a presumption of correctness has been attached to the revised record-o rights. Section 152 has empowered the: Government to make rules for Part-V and in exercise of the said power the Rules, 1954 was framed. It is also pertinent to mention that Chapters l-IV of the Rules, 1954 were published in the Dacca Gazette on 7th April, 1955 and Chapters V-IX of the Rules were published in the Dacca Gazette on 14th August, 1955.

29. Rules 26-35 of the Rules, 1954 have provided detailed procedure for revision of record-of-rights. Rules 27 and 27A thereof have laid down almost the same procedure as was made by rule 49 of the Rules, made under the B. T. Act. Rule 28 of the Rules, 1954 has directed that the work up to the stage of attestation, as mentioned in rule 27 thereof, shall be completed in accordance with the Technical Rules and Instructions of the Settlement Department, as modified, from time to time, by the Director of Land Records and Surveys and under such other instructions as may be issued in this behalf by the Director of Land Records and Surveys or by the Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of Settlement Officer in any district or part of a district or local area. It is also a fact that record-of-rights prepared under Part-IV of the Act, 1950 for the entire present Bangladesh was finally published by 1962/1963, (In Sylhet District, it was published in 1963). It is also a fact that in 1967, by way of amendment, section 143A was inserted in the Act, 1950 giving scope for correction of the record-of-rights, if prepared wrongly through the intervention of the Court, but that section did not vest the Court with the power to correct/alter the exterior boundary of a mouza map; the section was repealed in 1975. Thus, it is obvious that once a record-of-rights is finally published, it goes out of the administrative executive domain of the Government to alter it and only a pronouncement by a civil Court can say whether it was correct or wrong. From section 80 in Part-V of the Act, 1950, it is also clear that from the date of coming into force of Part-V, the enactment specified in the schedule shall be repealed and the schedule clearly shows that both B. T. Act and Sylhet Tenancy Act, 1936 along with several other statutes have been repealed. It is also a fact that the Sylhet Tenancy Act was enacted in 1936 where provisions were made for survey and preparation of record-of-rights, but no survey was made and no record-of-rights was prepared therein before the Act, 1950 came into operation, mouza map was prepared in the greater Sylhet district in course of preparation of record rights under section 17 of the Act, 1950 and became final with the final publication of the record-of-rights (S.A. Khatian) in 1963. So the executive branch of the Government in Sylhet lost all its administrative power to alter/correct and modify the map and record-of-rights finally published in 1963. Part-V of the Art, 1950 having already come into effect, the Government, in exercise of its power under section 144 thereof, may, in any case f it thinks fit, make an order directing that a record-of-rights in respect of any district, part of a district or a local area be prepared or revised and if such an order is made, then and then, only Settlement Officer can start a proceeding under rule 27A of the Rules, 1954 for alteration /correaction of the exterior boundary of a mouza strictly following the requirements of that rule and a successful completion on the process would permit preparation of new mouza map including or excluding any land which was not therein in the S.A. map of that mouza.

30. Rules 1 and 2 of the Manual, 1935 have clearly stated that it is a compilation of the principal rules of procedure relating to surveys and settlements. Survey and settlement operations or survey operations alone are/week conducted under different Regulations and Acts. But the rules of procedure and the technical rules relate primarily to surveys and settlements under the Settlement Laws, the B.T. Act and the Bengal Survey Act. Thus, it is clear that the rules of the Manual, 1935 cannot over-ride   or supersede the laws, namely: the Act, 1950 and the Rules, 1954(55). Consequently, rules 321 and 322 or any other rule(s) of the said Manual does not authorize the Government to alter the exterior boundaries of any mouza shown in the S.A. map after final publication of the S.A. khatian in 1962-63. And if an order is made under section 144 of the Act, 1950, to prepare or revise the record-of-rights for any area, then and then, only Settlement Officer can start a proceeding under rule 27A of the Rules, 1954(55) for alteration of the exterior boundary of a mouza strictly following the requirements of that Rules and a successful completion of the process would permit preparation of a new mouza map including or excluding only land which was not there in S.A. map of that mouza. Any other action to change the exterior boundary limits of any mouza shall be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect as rightly submitted by Mr. Siddique.

31. Keeping in view, the state of law as discussed hereinbefore, let us see whether the administrative approval for correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map of the finally published S.A. record of two mouzas, that is, 62 Patleechak and 88 Moizpur by severing 9.00 acres of land of 48 plots and 26 acres of land of 101 plots there from and then adding those with Darikhanjanpur mouza vide the impugned notification was given in accordance with law.

32. Admittedly, in the instant case, the Government did not make any order under section 144(1) of the Act, 1950 directing that the record-of-rights in respect of the 3(three) mouzas, namely: Patleechak, Moizpur and Darikhanjanpur, under police station-Jaganthapur, district-Sunamganj be prepared or revised by the concerned Revenue Officer in accordance with the Rules, 1954. No application was also filed by not less than one-half of the total number of tenants of any of the said 3(three) mouzas to the Government to make an order directing that the record-of-rights in respect of the said 3(three) mouzas be prepared or revised as provided in sub-section (2)(a) of section 144 of the Act nor there were situations as contemplated in clauses (b) and (c) of the said sub-section under which the Government could make such an order for correction/ change of the maps of the said mouzas by a Revenue Officer in accordance with Rules, 1954. No proposal was also submitted by the Assistant Settlement Officer, after ascertaining the opinions of the local people for the determination of the area to be adopted as a unit of survey and record because of the fact that the area contained within the boundaries of the 3(three) mouzas maps, in the S.A. khatian is unsuitable as a unit of survey and as stipulated in rule 27A(2) of the Rule's, 1954.

33. The proceeding to correct the mouza map/change of the mouza map of the 3(three) mouzas in question was, in that, initiated in the office of the Director General, Land Records and Surveys Directorate, Tejgaon on the basis of the applications filed by the sole respondent, that is, Jamshed Miah who claimed to be a man of village-Darikhanjanpur. We are a hit surprised to see that when the law, namely: section 144 of the Act, 1950 has made it clear that it is the Government only which can make an order directing that a record-of-rights in respect of any district, part of a district or local area he prepared or revised by a Revenue Officer in accordance with such rule as may be made by it and rule 27A(2) of the Rules, 1954 having clearly provided that when the area contained within boundaries of a village map of any previous survey is unsuitable as a unit of survey and record Ilk the Revenue Officer having the additional designation of Settlement Officer only who after ascertaining, as far as possible the opinions of the local people shall submit his proposal through the Officer to whom he is subordinate, for the determination of the area to be adopted as a unit of survey and record to the Government through the Ministry of Land for approval of such proposal (up to 1972 proposal had to be submitted to the Board of Revenue) how the Director General of Land Records and Surveys could entertain the applications of an individual straightaway, that is, the respondent and how report could be submitted on such application by the Assistant Settlement Officer and how the other Government functionaries, namely the Assistant Commissioner (Land), the Thana Nirbahi Officer and the Deputy Commissioner, could concur with such report for correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map of the finally published S.A. khatian.

34. Be that as it may, let us have a look at the applications filed by the respondent before the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, the reports submitted by the various authorities on the prayer The law of the respondent for correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map of the 3(three) mouzas in question and the inter see correspondences amongst them relying on which the Director General wrote to the Government for giving administrative approval for the correction/change of mouza map. But before that it must he kept on record that the applications filed by the respondent before the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, the application filed by the Chairman, Patleechak Union Parishad to the Thank Nirbahi Officer, Jagannathpur in support of the prayer of the respondent and the reports and the inter se correspondences as referred to and mentioned in the affidavit in-opposition by the respondent were not filed by way of annexure duly certified to be true by his learned Advocate and all reports and applications filed before the Director General of Land Records and Surveys and before the Thana Nirbahi Officer were quoted in the body of the affidavit-in-opposition. However, from the impugned judgment and order it does not appear that any objection was taken by the writ-petitioners before the High Court Division in not filing those documents, as annexure being duly certified as true copy by the concerned learned Advocate and the High Court Division did not also take any exception to that as well, we found no other way but to consider those as they are. But we deprecate this kind of practice.

36. From this letter of the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, it is clear that without starting any proceeding of as provided in rule 321 of the Manual, 1935 and submission of any proposal by the Assistant Settlement Officer to the Zonal Settlement Officer for correction of the mouza map/change of mould map as mandated in rule 27(2) of the Rules, 1954, report was given by the Assistant Settlement Officer for correction of the mouza map of the said 3(three) mouzas. A so-called "attending sheet" showing that 100 villagers were present on 29.05.1997 in an apparently inquiry held by the Chairman of No. 2 Patlecchak Union Parishad regarding the correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map of the mouzas in question has been quilted in the body of the affidavit-in-opposition. In the so-called "attending sheet" quoted in the body of the affidavit-in-opposition except the name and father's name of 100 people, no other particulars, such as, village or mouza has been mentioned. It further appears from a notice quoted in the body of the affidavit-in-opposition that the Chairman of the said Union Parishad issued the same on 01.06.1997 asking the people of Moizpur and Patleechak (not Darikhanjanpur) to remain present at Rasulganj Bazar on 03.06.1997 at 12 O'clock with their respective papers for Molding a meeting to decide "about the correction of mouza map/change of mouza map." At the bottom of the notice, names of 3(three) persons each of Patleechak mouza and Moizpur mouza without disclosing their full identities, such as, father's name, have been mentioned. The notice further shows that the same was issued at the instance of the Assistant Settlement Officer, Jagannathpur who earlier gave his report in favour of correction of the mouza wap/change of mouza map. No fact was "stated in the affidavit-in-opposition and no other particular was furnished as to how the said notice was served upon the inhabitants/residents of the said two villages/mouzas. It is also very significant to note that prior to the issuance of the said notice for holding enquiry on the subject, the Chairman had allegedly enquired into the matter on 29.05.1997 as sought to be proved by the "attending sheet" as stated hereinbefore. So the notice, even if issued on 01.06.1997, does not, at all, show that Amy enquiry was held to ascertain the opinions of the local people within the meaning of rule 27A(2) of the Rules, 1954 read with rule 321 of the Manual, 1935. In this regard, it is to the noted that law does not recognize any such exercise by the Chairman of any Union Parishad.

37. In his report, he mentioned that during the spot enquiry on 03.10.1997, the Thana Nirbahi Officer, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) and the Thana Agriculture Officer, the Thana Project Officer (Education) and the local elites were present, but he did not mention the names of the local elites who were present at the spot inquiry and in turn, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) just Mr. warded the report of the Kanangu to the Thana Nirbahi Officer and then, the Thana Nirbahi Officer by his letter under Memo No. 97/1206 dated 07.10.1997 sent the report of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) along with the report of the Kanangu and those of the Chairman, local Union Parishad to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj for taking next necessary action. It further appears from the said memo that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) asked the Assistant Commissioner': (Land) to give the report through the Thana Nirbahi Officer after holding inquiry into the matter by himself. মৌজা একত্রিকরনের বা বিভক্তি করণের নিয়ম মোতাবেক প্রাক্তন সহকারী সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার বর্ণিত প্রত্যেক সংস্থাকে নিয়া শুনানী সমাপ্ত করেছেন কিনা তাহা অত্র নথি পর্যালোচনায় প্রতিয়মান হয় না। তবে প্রত্যেক সংস্থা মতামতের পত্র সংযুক্তি অনুসারে প্রতিয়মান হয় যে, জনসাধারন সহ সকলের মৌজা একত্রি করনের মত বা সম্মতি আছে বা ছিল এবং বর্তমানেও হয়ত আছে হেতু দরখাস্তকারীর তদবিরের তাড়নায় পুনঃশুনানীর প্রয়োজন মনে করি নাই।

এমতাবস্থায় মৌজা একত্রি করনের স্বপক্ষে আবেদনকারীর নিম্ন বর্ণিত শর্তগুলি নাই। যেমন দড়িখঞ্জনপুর জরীপ আরম্ভ ১০/১২/৯৫ এবং পাটলীচক ৩১/৩/৯৬ ইং তারিখ কিন্তু দরখাস্তকারী মৌজা একত্রি করনের আবেদন করেছে ১৫/১/৯৬ ইং।

জরীপ নেটিফিকেশন পাওয়া পূর্বে মৌজা একত্রিকরনের আবেদন করা উচিত ছিল। দ্বিতীয় এই ২টি মৌজা দড়িখঞ্জনপুর মৌজার সহিত একত্রি করনের কোন প্রাকৃতিক সীমা রেখা নাই, শুধু দড়িখঞ্জনপুর নামী এই প্রস্তাবিত মৌজার ২টি অংশ রেকর্ড আছে এবং দখল করে।

এতদ্ব্যতীত এই ৩টি মৌজার মাঠ রেকর্ড তসদিক রেকর্ড ও ডিপি ইত্যাদি ধারা সমাপ্ত হয়েছে। এমতাবস্থায় এই ৩টি মৌজার একত্রি করনের প্রয়োজন হলে মৌজা ৩টির সিট ও রেকর্ডের ব্যাপক পরিবর্তন ও পরিবর্ধন করার প্রয়োজন হবে বলে মনে হয় এবং এই ক্ষেত্রে প্রজাস্বত্ব বিধির ৪২ নম্বর বিধি প্রয়োজনের নিমিত্তে জোনাল সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার মহোদয়কে মহা-পরিচালক মহোদয়কে লিখতে হবে।

এই মৌজা ৩টির পরবর্তী ধারাগুলি অত্র মিস কেস আরম্ভের কারনে বন্ধ রাখা হলো।

কর্তৃপক্ষের সদয় অবগতি ও কাযকরী ব্যবস্থার জন্য অত্র মিস কেসের প্রতিবেদন প্রেরণ করা হইল।

40. From this order of the Assistant Settlement Officer, Jagannathpur, it is clear that the conditions as mentioned in rules 321 and 322 of the Manual, 1935 and in rule 27(2) of the Rules, 1954(55) to start a proceeding for correction of a mouza map/change of mouza map were absent. In the affidavit-in-opposition, the respondent tried to show that there were papers such as application filed by the Chairman of Patleechak Union Parishad vide his Memo No. 21/97 dated 18.06.1997 giving his opinion in favour of correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map, the report of the Assistant Settlement Officer, Jagannathpur, vide his letter dated 25.08.1996 (Memo number not available) to the Zonal Settlement Officer, Sylhet Zone, pursuant to his Memo No. ৩৩/২৯/পিঃ৫৯২ dated 04.08.1996 in favour of the prayer of the respondent, the letter written by the Zonal Settlement Officer, Sylhet Zone to the Director (Land Records) Land Records and Surveys Directorate asking him to take necessary action on the report of the Assistant Settlement Officer, report by the Thana Land Officer (Kanangu) dated 03.10.1997, report by the Assistant Commissioner(Land), Jagannathpur to the Thana Nirbahi Officer vide his Memo No. 1183 dated 07.10.1997, the opinion of the Thana Nirbahi Officer which was seen to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj vide his Memo No. 97/1206 dated 07.10.1997, report by the Assistant Commissioner(Land), Jagannathpur vide his Memo No. ভূমিঃজরিপ৬-৪/৯৭/২৭১ dated 25.03.1998, another letter written by the Thana Nirbahi Officer to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj under Memo No. 98/362 dated 29.03.1998 expressing their opinions in favour of amalgamation of the mouzas in question as discussed above, but there was no letter from the police administration and the local people. And all those were tiled and given in connection with an application tiled by the respondent on 15.01.1994, though in the affidavit-in-opposition, he claimed that he filed two applications before the Director General, Land Records and Surveys Directorate on 15.01.1996 with the prayer for severing the lands of 106 plots of Moizpur mouza and the lands of 48 plots of Patleeckak mouza and add those with Darikhanjanpur mouza. The Assistant Settlement Officer in his said order further stated that it did not appear from the record that the former Assistant Settlement Officer completed the hearing of each of those persons (প্রত্যেক সংস্থাকে). He further stated that “তবে প্রত্যেক সংস্থা মতামতের পত্র সংযুক্তি অনুসারে প্রতিয়মান হয় যে, জন সাধারণসহ, সকলের মৌজা একত্রি করনের মত বা সম্মতি আছে বা ছিল এবং বর্তমানেও হয়ত আছে হেতু দরখাস্তকারীর তদবিরের তাড়নায় পুনঃশুনানীর প্রয়োজন মনে করি নাই।

41. In this regard, it is also necessary to state that in the writ petition the petitioners   categorically stated that in the present survey, the lands containing "those curtailed plots" have been recorded under the previous Patleechak and Moizpur mouzas in the names of the petitioners and others by the survey authority and the attestation khatian has been prepared in their names, but the respondent did not raise any objection   any where against such survey or attestation till the filing of the writ petition. These assertions of the petitioners are clearly substantiated by the order of the Assistant Settlement Officer dated 25.04.1999.

42. It is very pertinent to state that the opinions mentioned by the Assistant Settlement Officer in his order dated 25.04.1999 and as mentioned while stating the case of the respondent, were given by the concerned persons at a time when no proceeding by way of starting a miscellaneous   case as required by rule 321 of the Manual, 1935 was, at all, started. This fact is also evident from the letter written by Director General, and Records and Surveys Directorate to the Zonal Settlement Officer on 16.03.1997 vide his Memo No. 66/90/510 and the letter written by the Zonal Settlement Officer, Sylhet Zone to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj vide Memo No.  ৩৩/২৯/পিঃ ৮৩৪ dated 15.06.1999. From the said letter of the Zonal Settlement Officer written to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj and his subsequent letter dated 05.08.1999 vide Memo No. 33/29/P:/1098 written to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, it is apparent that the miscellaneous case was started only in 1999. From the Memo of the Zonal Settlement Officer, it further appears that a fresh application was filed by the respondent on 22.02.1999 allegedly on behalf of the local people (এলাকাবাসীর পক্ষে) for severing 9.00 acres Of lands of 48 plots of Patleechak mouza and 26:00 acres of lands of Moizpur Monza and to add those with Darikhanjanpur mouza, but in law as discussed above, there was no scope of filing such application. The said Memo of the Zonal Settlement Officer further reveals that the miscellaneous case was initiated on the basis of the so-called reports of the local administration which were obtained or given much prior to the starting of the same and that too without completing the hearing of the concerned persons and the people of the locality as stated in order dated 25.04.1999 of the Assistant Settlement Officer. And it is also a tact that no formal proposal on the subject in compliance with the provisions of rule 27A (2) of the Rules, 1954 was submitted by the Assistant Settlement Officer. In this regard, it is also necessary to keep on record that only after the starting of the said miscellaneous case opinion was sought for from the Superintendent of Police, Sunamganj by the Zonal  Settlement Officer by his Memo No. 33/29/P:/1097 dated 05.08.1999 who gave his report on 03.10.1999 (after the letter to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys was sent by the Zonal Settlement Officer on (15.08.1999) in a casual manner without giving his own independent opinion just' saying that necessary action might be taken on the basis of the report of the Thana Nirbahi Officer, the Assistant Commissioner(Land) and the Chairman of the Union Parishad. That the Zonal Settlement Officer acted on the application of an individual, the respondent in clear defiance of law as discussed above is clear from his letter dated 15.06.1999 written to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj vide his Memo No. 33/29/P:/834 as quoted herein below.

49. And then the impugned administrative approval of the change of mouza/mouza map of the said 3(three) mouzas were given vide annexure-H to the writ petition.

50. The proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1999 was not produced before the High Court Division and no date is also available from the record as to its initiation, but obviously the case was not initiated before 1999. It is also apparent from the order of the Assistant Settlement Officer dated 25.04.1999 that after the miscellaneous case was started, no attempt was made to lake the opinions of the people of the 3(three) mouzas who would be the most affected persons in case the mouza map is changed/corrected. From the said order, it is also apparent that there was heavy tadbir from the respondent to get the job done any how and this further shows that the concerned functionaries did not give their opinions on the application of the respondent independently in accordance with rule 321 of the Manual, 1935 and rule 27A (2) of the Rules, 1954(55). It is also pertinent to state at the risk of repetition that in the meantime, the respondent's application filed to the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj on 27.08.1997 for addition of 9.00 acres and 26.00 acres of lands of Patleechak and Moizpur mouza respectively with Darikhanjanpur mouza was rejected on 14.06.1998; application filed by the respondent for reviewing the said order was also rejected on (12.12.1998 against which he filed Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal No. 288 of 1998 before the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet who without disposing of the said revenue miscellaneous appeal on merit sent the records to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys for final decision relying on the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent that the issue had been pending for final decision by the Survey and Settlement Department, but from the correspondences of the Assistant Settlement Officer, the Zonal Settlement Officer and the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, it does not appear that the fact of rejection of the prayer of the respondent adding 9.00 acres of lands of Patleechak mouza and 26.00 acres of lands of Moizpur mouza with Darikhanjanpur mouza by the Deputy Commissioner was, at all, noticed. The High Court Division, in deciding the merit of the Rule, took notice of this fact of rejection of respondent's prayer twice by the highest local authority. The High Court Division further noticed that only the Chairman of Patleechak Union Parishad informed the Thana Nirbahi Officer that the people had no objection if the said lands were added with Darikhanjanpur mouza and on such report the Zonal Settlement Officer, the Thana Nirbahi Officer, the Additional Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police acted. From the various reports and the inter sc correspondences amongst the concerned functionaries as discussed above, we also find substances in the finding of the High Court Division that “There is no dispute that in the process the opinion of the people of village ‘Moizpur’ or ‘Darkhanjanpur’ (sic) was never sought for.”

51. On receipt of the proposal from the Director General, Land Records and Surveys to give administrative approval to include 9.00 acres and 26.00 acres of lands of Patleechak mouza and Moizpur mouza respectively with Darikhanjanpur mouza the Ministry of Land, by its letter dated 17.04.2000 asked him to state clearly as to the necessity of such inclusion of the lands of the said two mouzas as in his letter there was nothing in that respect, but instead of the Director General, the Director (Survey) replied to the said letter saying that on behalf of Darikhanjanpur mouza, the respondent, Jamshed Mia filed an application for inclusion of the lands of the said two mouzas with Darikhanjanpur mouza and that the local people, the Thana Nirbahi Officer, the Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police, had no objection if the lands of the said two mouzas were included in Darikhanjanpur mouza. But merely no objection from the local people and the local administration to change the mouza map could not be a ground to substitute the statutory requirements under rule 27A (2) of the Rules, 1954(55) that proposal for determination of the area to be adopted as a unit of survey and record has to be submitted by the Assistant Settlement Officer, after ascertaining, as far as possible, the opinions of the local people through the Officer to whom he is subordinate, i.e. the Zonal Settlement Officer to the Government and that too only when the area contained within the boundaries of a village map of a previous survey is unsuitable as a unit of survey and record (here map of the concerned mouzas was prepared during the S.A. khatian). But in the instant case as is revealed from the order of the Settlement Officer dated 25.04.1999 that the opinions of the people of mouzas in question were not ascertained; in none of the reports and inter se correspondences of the local administration as sought to be relied upon by the respondent in his affidavit-in-opposition, there is anything to show that the area contained within the boundaries of the map of the 3(three) mouzas in question was found to be unsuitable and required to be changed. Not only that all the authorities acted at the instance of an individual the respondent. We like to further observe that in the applications filed by the respondent as quoted in the body of the affidavit in-opposition, he failed to make out an case nor in the reports submitted by the Chairman of Patleechak Union Parishad and the other Government functionaries any case to correct the mouza map/change of mouza map of the three mouzas as contemplated in section 144 of the Act, 1955 and in rule 27A (2) of the Rules, 1954(55) could be made out. It appears to us that the Director General, Land Records and Surveys, the Settlement officers and the other functionaries were either totally ignorant of the provisions of law as discussed above or were bent upon to act at the behest of an individual by flouting the law. In the context, the High Court Division rightly found that

"In the case before us, neither new village nor any separate settlement unit was required to be constituted or formed so none of the Rules is at all applicable in the circumstances. Whole proceeding was initiated at the instance of a villager .. ."

52. Of course the High Court Division was not correct in holding that no concurrence of the "Board of Land Revenue" was taken before the conclusion of the proceeding as in view of the change of law in 1972 there was no necessity to submit the proposal and the record to the Board of Revenue as correctly stated in the concise statement filed by the writ-respondent-appellant.

53. In this case, in fact, the cart was put before the horse inasmuch as after acting on the application filed by the sole respondent for correction of the mouza map/change of mouza map of 3(three) mouzas, namely; Patlecehak, Moizpur and Darikhanjanpur which were finally published in the S.A. Khatian as evidenced from the application filed by the Chairman of Patleechak Union Parishad to the Thana Nirbahi Officer, Jagannathpur, the reports of the Assistant Settlement Officer, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) and the concurrence by the other local administration, the Director General, Land Records and Surveys gave tagged to the Zonal Settlement Officer to send his opinion by starting a miscellaneous case who in turn by a letter dated 15.06.1999 under Memo No. 33/29/P:/834 requested the Deputy Commissioner to give his opinion on the subject. And from the letter written by the Zonal Settlement Officer to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys Directorate on 05.08.1999 it appears that a miscellaneous case being No. 1 was started in the office of the Assistant Settlement Officer, Jagannathpur only in 1999. Although as per own admission of the respondent long before of the said letter reports were given by the local administration including the Thana Kanangu and the Assistant Settlement Officer in favour of correction of the mouza map/change of the mouza map of the mouzas in question as discussed hereinbefore. In this regard, it is also relevant to state that the Assistant Settlement Officer himself did not start any case as per provisions of rule, 27(2) of the Rules, 1954 and rule 321 of the Manual, 1935, rather he started the case being directed by the Zonal Settlement Officer at the instance of the Director General, Land Records and Surveys.

54. We like to further observe that if at the instance of an individual as it happened in the instant ease, the mouza map is allowed to be corrected/changed, it will create havoc in the administration of the land management of the country and in the process, the law on the subject as discussed shall be made nugatory.

<u>55. From the discussions made above, it is abundantly clear that the conditions for correction of mouza map/change of mouza map of the 3(three) mouzas, namely Patleechak, Moizpur and Darikhanjanpur as articulated by the legislature in section 144 of the Act and rule 27A(2) of the Rules, 1954 being absent, the whole exercise made in that behalf by the Assistant Settlement Officer, the Zonal Settlement Officer, the Director General of Land Records and Surveys, the opinion given by the local administration including the Deputy Commissioner and the approval given by respondent No. 1 vide annexure-'H' to the writ petition on such exercise could by no term be said to be with jurisdiction but without jurisdiction. Therefore, the High Court Division acted within its jurisdiction of exercising its power of judicial review in declaring the impugned administrative approval given by the Government to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.</u>

56. For the reasons stated hereinbefore, we find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
