full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 9.11.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 51h Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.825 of 1999 affirming those dated 17.10.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, I' Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.16 of 1998 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside. 

2. Material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the petitioners as plaintiffs brought the aforesaid suit being Title Suit No.16 of 1998 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Court, Dhaka for declaration of title of the suit as described in schedule to the plaint comprising of .62 acres under Mouza-Uttarkhan C.S Khatian No.145 Dag No.1481. The plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land was originally belonged to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate who granted pattan in favour of the plaintiffs on payment of Tk.26/- as salami; that the plaintiffs thereafter, on the basis of the said pattan mutated their name, paid rents to the Government regularly and during last S.A. operation their names were rightly recorded in the S.A. Khatian No.13; that when the pattan was granted in favour of the plaintiffs, the nature of the suit land was a pond and after taking pattan the plaintiffs filled up half portion of the suit land by earth-filling and build dueling house thereon and the rest being cultivable land under their possession; that during last R.S. operation the suit land was wrongly recorded as khas land of the Government as a result of which Settlement Case being No.54/86-87 was started with Chandpara Shahi Moshjid and thereupon, notice were served upon the plaintiffs infringing their right and title, hence the suit. 

3. The defendant contested the suit by filling written statement denying most of the averments of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was originally belonged to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate and subsequently, the same was recorded as khas land of the Government; that the suit is barred by limitation and during last R.S. operation the record of right was rightly prepared and published in the name of the Government and later on, the Government leased out the property in favour of the Chandrapara Shahi Moshjid Committee through Settlement Case No.54/86-87. The suit land was never gave pattan by the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate in favour of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest of the suit land and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The trial Court on the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues for determination namely : 
(I) whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner? 
(II) whether the case is barred by limitation? 
(III) whether the plaintiffs have right, title and possession in the suit land? 
(IV) whether the settlement case in question was void, illegal and beyond jurisdiction? 
(V) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree, as prayed for? 

5. During trial plaintiffs examined 3 (three) witnesses and exhibited a series of documents and defendant side examined I (one) witness to prove their respective cases. 

6. The trial Court below on consideration of the materials on record dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 17.10.1999 (decree singed 27.10.1999) on the finding, inter alia, that the plaintiffs neither proved their right, title and possession in the suit land nor proved their pattan (Ext. l) by adducing evidence. 

7. The unsuccessful plaintiffs then preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.825 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court Dhaka, who by his judgment and decree dated 9.11.2008 affirmed the decision of the trial Court below holding that the plaintiffs could not prove that the pattan (Ext. I) was granted by the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate in favour of the plaintiffs. 

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated. 9.11.2008, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners have come before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below, disposition of witnesses, exhibits and other relevant materials on record submits that judgments of both the Courts below are not in fact based on correct evaluation of facts and materials of the case and as such the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside. He next submits that the plaintiff-petitioners in support of their claim proved as many as 4 (four) vital documents namely; (i) Pattan dated 4.4.1939 (Ext.1), (ii) 5(five) rent receipts (Ext.2-2Gha), (iii) S.A. Khatian (Ext.3) and (iv) rent receipt under S.A. Khatian (Ext.4) but both the courts below mere on surmise and conjecture mechanically held that the plaintiffs could not prove their pattan as well as right, title and possession in the suit land by educing evidence. 

10. Referring to the deposition of sole D.W I, Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman contends that it is apparent from the evidence of sole D.W1 that this witness in his deposition admitted that the S.A. Khatian of the suit land was prepared in the name of the plaintiff-petitioners and there is nothing on record to suggest that the Government leased out the suit property in favour of Chandapara Shahi Mosjid Committee and as such the judgment of both the Courts below are based on gross misreading and misinterpretation of material evidence on record. He also submits that both the Courts below ought to have decreed the suit inasmuch as the plaintiffs examined as many as 3 (three) witnesses and all of tem in their respective testimony categorically testified that the plaintiffs got the suit the land by way of pattan dated 4.4.1939 granted by Bhawal Court of Wards Estate (Ext.1), mutated their name and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent regularly to the Government as direct tenant of the Government. Mr. Rahman, finally submits that taking rent from the plaintiff-petitioners it does not lie in the mouth of the defendant opposite party No.1 that the suits property was vested in the Government and the plaintiffs are not in possession over the suit property.

11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Abdus Salam Mondal the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the Government by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. He submits that both the Courts below on due consideration of the entire materials on record rightly arrived at a finding that the plaintiff-petitioner could not prove their right, title and possession on the basis of their so-called unregistered pattan. He further submits that both the Courts below rightly arrived at a concurrent finding that Pattan (Ext.1) was forged, collusive and illegal document which has never been acted upon and as such question of interference does not arise at all. 

12. I have heard the learned Advocate and the learned Deputy Attorney General at length and perused the judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses and other materials on record. To appreciate the contentions of the learned Advocate and the learned Deputy Attorney General, it is necessary to scrutinized the materials evidence on record to arrive at a correct decision whether both the Courts below committed any illegality in holding that the plaintiff-petitioners having failed to prove their right, title and possession on the basis of Ext.1 (pattan).

13. Plaintiff No.1 Alauddin Kazi himself was examined as PW-1 who in his deposition stated that: “নালিশী সম্পত্তি ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস এর খাস সম্পত্তি ছিল। আমি ৪/৪/১৯৩৯ তারিখে ২৬/-(ছাব্বিশ)টাকা সেলামী দিয়ে নালিশী সম্পত্তি পত্তন নেই। আমি আমার নাম জারী করি। খাজনা দেই। পত্তন নামীয় খাজনার রশিদ ৪টি দাখিল করিলাম। বিগত এস,এ জরিপের সময় এস,এ খতিয়ানের আমার নাম শুদ্ধভাবে রেকর্ড হয়। এস,এ পার্চার সহি মহুরী নকল দাখিল করিলাম। ১৯৯২ইং সন পর্যন্ত খাজনা দিয়েছি। খাজনার রশিদ সমূহ দাখিল করেছি। নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে আমি দখলে আছি।”
This witness in his deposition also stated that earlier the suit land was a pond, who by filing earth thereon started cultivating and fishing. This witness in his cross examination denied that the suit property has been leased out in favour of the Chandpara Shahi Mosjid. PW-2 Abdur Rahman Kazi stated in his deposition that the plaintiffs got .the suit property by the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate by way of pattan and the suit property was mutated in their name and S.A. record was also prepared in the name of the plaintiffs. PW-3 Kazi Lehazuddin, stated in his deposition that :  “নালিশী সম্পত্তি আমার বাড়ি থেকে অনেক দূরে। আমি বাদীকে চিনি। বাদীগন নালিশী সম্পত্তি ভোগ দখল করে। নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে পুকুর করে ও কিছু জমিতে ফসল চাষ করে বাদীগন, নালিশী সম্পত্তি মসজিদ কমিটি ভোগ দখল করে না।” This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion that Chandpara Shahi Mosjid Committee has been possessing the suit property. 

14. DW-1, Md, Zulfiqur Ali stated in his deposition that the suit property has been leased out in favour of Chandpara Shahi Mosjid Committee through Settlement Case No.54/86-87. This witness also stated that pattan of the plaintiffs was forged; collusive, and Bhawal Court of Wards Estate never granted pattan in favour of the plaintiffs. This witness in his cross-examination admitted that S.A. khatian of the suit property was prepared in the name of Alauddin Kazi and Shamsuddin Kazi (plaintiffs) being Dag No.1481. This witness in his cross-examination also stated that:  “নালিশী জমি সরকারী খাস জমি হওয়ায় এটা চাঁনপাড়া শাহী মসজিদকে বন্দোবস্ত দেওয়া হয়েছে। উক্তরুপে এস,এ রেকর্ড বাতিল হয়েছে। ঐ বন্দোবস্তের কোন কাগজ দাখিল করিনি। ইংরেজী ১৯৮৮ সনের বন্যায় নথি নষ্ট হয়। ইংরেজী ১৯৮৮ সনের বন্যায় নথি নষ্ট হবার সমর্থনে কোন কাগজ দাখিল করেছি কি না তা মনে পড়ছে না।”

15. On a close perusal of the evidence of PW-1, PW2, PW3 and DW-1 together with the Exhibits namely, (i) Pattan dated 4.4.1939 (Ext.1), (ii) 5(five) rent receipts (Ext.2-2Gha), (iii) S.A. Khatian (Ext.3) and (iv) rent receipt under S.A. Khatian (Ext.4), it appears that the plaintiff-petitioners in support of their right, title and possession over the suit property adduced sufficient corroborative evidence both oral and documentary. It also appears that the defendant-opposite parties could not make the case shaky of the plaintiff-petitioners by way of cross-examination. 

16. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman at the end of the day in support of his lengthy argument has referred to some decisions reported in 2 BLC (AD) 134, 30 DLR (SC) 84, 48 DLR (AD) 160, 48 DLR (AD) 154, 43 DLR (AD) 130, Calcutta Weekly Notes (Volume25) 165 and 35 DLR (AD) 216. 

17. Now in order to appreciate the legal aspects involved in this case, it would be useful if I consider the cited decisions. 

18. It the case of Abul Bakar Siddique Vs. A. D. C. Kurigram and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 154, it has been held that:
The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division having independently assessed the evidence and having found a case of non-consideration of material evidence on record and consequently non-reversal of material findings interfered with the finding of fact. To our mind, the revisional Court is competent to interfere in a case of non-consideration of material evidence which is specifically material for the determination of the material issue, namely, the issue of shifting of the school to the new mouza. 

19. In the case of Abdul Mazid Howlader and another Vs. Lahajjudin Howlader and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 160, it has been held that: 
There being a total non-consideration of all the witnesses of the pre-emptees, the learned Single Judge acted wrongly in refusing to exercise his revisonal jurisdiction in a case where due to non-consideration of the material evidence on record an erroneous decision has been arrived occasioning a grave failure of justice. 

20. In the case of Rajkumari Baishnabi vs. Shyama Bibi reported in Calcutta Weekly Notes (Volume 25) 165, it has been observed that: 
Their Lordships passed the following judgment:- We are of the opinion that this appeal must be allowed. The learned District Judge has decided one question and one question only, namely, that the unregistered deed produced in the case was not admissible in evidence. On this ground he has held that the tenancy alleged to have been held by Shyama under Rajkumari has not been established. The District Judge, however, has overlooked that in this country it is possible to establish a tenancy without the production of a lease by proof of payment of rent by the tenant and acceptance of rent by the land lord. 

21. In the case of Bangladesh Vs. Tabarak Ali Mia and others reported in 43 DLR (AD) 130, it has observed that: 
Patni taluk had its origin on the estates of the Raja of Burdwan but has since been extended to other Zaminderis. The character of this tenure is that it is a taluk (etymologically, `taluk' stands for some intermediate interest being derived from `alak' to suspend from) created by the Zaminder, to be held at a rent fixed in perpetuity by the lessee and his heirs forever. Zaminder is the land lord, patnidar is his tenant. A patni although in form a lease, is not a mere lease-hold property. A patnider may let out the lands in any manner conducive to his interest, provided his interest was subsisting. 

22. In the case of Akrab All and others Vs. Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81, it has been held that: 
According to section 103(B)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be, correct until it is proved to be incorrect. The learned Judges of the High Court appear to have started with the view that the court of appeal below was palpably wrong in presuming title in favour of the defendants from a mere entry in the records of right and that the defence having admitted title of the predecessor of the plaintiff, the plaintiff was relived of the burden of providing the title of Aftabuddin Sarker. Their Lordships were not correct in their view as to the effect of the entries in a finally published record of right and in relieving the plaintiff, in the face of the said entries of the burden of proving the title of Aftabuddin Sarker. The entries in the Khatian Ext.A that Faizuddin Haji was in the occupation of the holding appertaining to the jote of Aftabuddin Sarker on the basis of purchase for a consideration of Rs.50/- and that the land was fit for assessment of rent but there was no payment Were not beyond the scope of the survey, held under Chapter X part1,thepengal Tenancy Act, 1885.

 23. In. the case of Erfan A i. ;Vs. loyrial Anedin Mia rep9Tted. in 35.:PLR '(AD):.216, it has been held that:
The rent receipt were excluded from consideration by the lower' Appellate Court taking the that these are provisional receipts and that they carry little weigh that any Person interested in a land may pay rent to the Government Acquired Estate". This view is erroneous, for rent receipts, though documents of title, are important, items, of  evidence: of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title. Again, plaintiffs name has also been recorded in the S.A. Khatian prepared in the period immediately following the whole-sale state-acquisition in 1956 and all objections raised by defendant Wo.,1 were overruled by the Revenue-officer and then by the appellate authority.

24. Thus, from all the decisions, it is clear that a patindar may let out the lands in any manner conducive to his interest, provided his interest was subsisting. Rent receipts and S.A. Khatian are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title and a finding, of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower Court is binding on this Court;' 'as' a Revisional Court except in certain well defined exceptional circumstances such as non Consideration or misreading a Material evidence oh record affecting the merit of the case. 

25. I have already noticed that in this case, the plaintiff-petitioners in order to prove  their right, title and possession in the suit property produced so many important documents namely, pattan dated 4.4.1939 (Ext.1), .5(five) rent receipts(Ext:-2.-.2 Gha), SA -Kahtian (EXt.3) and . rent receipt under S AKhatian (Ext. 4) . The Court  of appeal below by the impugned judgment' affirmed the decision Of the trail Court with the observation that  “পুর্বোক্ত আলোচনা ও সাক্ষ প্রমান পর্যালোচনান্তে আদালত এই অভিমতে আসে যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদ বাদী ভাওয়াল কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ডস স্টেট হইতে পত্তন গ্রহন করা এবং উক্ত পত্তনের আলোকে স্বত্ত্ব প্রতিষ্ঠিত হওয়া এবং উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে স্বত্ত্ববান ও দখলকার থাকার বিষয়টি বাদীপক্ষ প্রমানে সমর্থন হন নাই। সেই দিন থেকে বাদী তাহার স্বত্ত্বের ঘোষনামূলক ডিক্রী পাইতে পারেন না। বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত তদ্রুপ সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করায় আদালতের হস্তক্ষেপ করার কোন কারন নাই। নালিশী সম্পত্তি সম্পূর্ন অংশে বাদী পক্ষের নিরংকুশ দখল না থাকায় সুনির্দিষ্ট প্রতিকার আইনের ৪২ ধারা মতে স্বত্ত্ব ঘোষনার মোকদ্দমা চলিতে পারে না মর্মে বিজ্ঞ আদালত যে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করিয়াছেন তাহার সহিত অত্রাদালত একমত পোষন করেন।

 In the given facts and circumstances of the case and the uniform decisions of the highest Court as cited above, I have no hesitation to hold that the above quoted finding of the Court of appeal below is product of misreading and non considering the material evidence on record inasmuch as in this case the plaintiffs had produced their kabala, S. A. Khatian and rent receipt in the trial Court to show their continuous possession but the Courts below did not consider the same. 
By the way, it may be mentioned that in this case the learned Deputy Attorney General took time again and again lastly on 8.12.2011 by filling an application took time till one week after the vacation for collecting the record of Settlement Case No.54/86-87 though, he failed to collect the same. 

26. There is another aspect of the case should also be looked into. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners while elaborating his submission inviting my attention to Annexure and D' series of the supplementary affidavit dated 29.11.2011 and submits that city survey khatian No.16259 dag No.8219 & 8222 respectively in respect of the suit property have been prepare in the name of the petitioners and the Appeal Case being No.69700 of 2002 filed by the defendant-opposite parties under section 31 of the Bengal Tenancy Act before the settlement officer was rejected with the observation that: “ নালিশী জমি আর,এস, রেকর্ড তদন্তকালীন সময়ে কিভাবে অথবা কোন কাগজের ভিত্তিতে সরকারের ১নং খতিয়ানের রেকর্ড হইয়াছে এই মর্মে প্রশ্ন করে জানতে চাওয়া হইলে আপীলকারী পক্ষ জানান যে, আর, এস রেকর্ড কিভাবে নালিশী জমি রেকর্ড হইয়াছে তাহা তিনি জানেন না। এই মর্মে কোন কাগজপত্র দেখাইতে তিনি অপারগতা জানান। তিনি বলেন যে, যেহেতু আর,এস, রেকর্ড চুড়ান্ত ভাবে প্রকাশিত ও গেজেট বিজ্ঞপ্তির মাধ্যমে সরকারের নিকট হস্তান্তর করা হইয়াছে, সেহেতু ইহা সরকারী খাস জমি হিসাবে গন্য হইবে। তিনি নালিশী জমি সরকারের ১নং খতিয়ানে রেকর্ড করার দাবী জানান।------ আপীলকারী পক্ষে দাবী যৌক্তিক ভিত্তি না থাকায় তাহাদের নামে রেকর্ড করার দাবী বিবেচনা করা গেল না।” And, as such at any rate judgments of both the courts below do not deserve to be sustained. 

To this the learned Deputy Attorney General finds it difficult to repel the contention of Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners. 

27. For the reasons stated above, I am inclined to hold that both the Courts below erred .in law in passing the judgments under challenge without following the correct principle relating to the appreciation of the evidence and materials on record and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice. 

28. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 9.11.2008 (decree singed on 9.11.2008) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.825 of 1999 affirming those dated 17.10.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate. Judge, 1' Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.16 of 1998 dismissing the suit is set aside and thus, the suit is decreed. 

29. Let a copy of the judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Abdul Hakim, J. :- These three Rules were issued in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004, Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 at the instance of defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Sun No.69 of 1993) and defendant Nos.1-6 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993) and defendant Nos.l4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 respectively, directed against one and same judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.55 of 1997 (heard analogously with Title Appeal Nos.64 and 65 of 1997) dismissing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.01.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and Title Suit No.85 of 1993. 

2. All these Rules have been arisen out of the judgment and have been taken up together for hearing and therefore disposed of by this common judgment.

3. The opposite party Nos.1-6 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.284 of 1986 in the 
Court of Sadar Munsif, First Court, Sylhet on 20.09.1986 for partition of the suit property claiming an area of 0.11 acres land impleading the present petitioners as defendant Nos.2-10 and other defendants. Subsequently, the said suit transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No.85 of 1993. 

4. The defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.284 of 1986 as plaintiffs instituted Title 
Suit No.261 of 1986 on 21.12.1986 for partition in respect of 0.15 acres of and against the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.284 of 1986 in the Second Court of Sub-Judge, Sylhet. The suit was renumbered as Title Suit No.69 of 1993 of the same Court. 

5. Plaintiffs case of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in short, are that suit land measuring 1 
Kedar, I Powa, 4 Jashti, 6 Pon equivalent to 0.34 acres described in the schedule I to the 
plaint originally belonged to Morium Nessa Chowdhurani, the predecessors of the defendant Nos.16 and 17. She settled 1 Powa, 4 Jashti equivalent to 0.1177 acres out of schedule I land to Bosai Mia predecessor of the plaintiffs and Swab Mia, the predecessor of the defendant Nos.18 and 19 by Hukumnama dated 1 Srabon, 1320 B.S.; that Bosai Mia died leaving the plaintiffs and Swab Mia who subsequently died leaving defendant Nos. 18 and 19; that Bosai Mia during his life time and after his death his heirs have been possessing the schedule-3 of the suit property on payment of rents to Monirunnessa Chowdhurani: who died subsequently leaving two daughters (1) Mahebbadon Chowdhurani, defendant No.16 and (2) Helalbadon Chowdhirani, Vs. Marad 
defendant No.17. 

6. During settlement operation schedule I land wrongly recorded in the name of Bosai 
Mia, predecessor of the plaintiffs, Suratunnessa, Abul and Amor Chand; that Monirunessa Chowdhurani filed Objection Case No.990 of 1961 before the Settlement Officer under Section 19(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (shortly, the SAT Act), the said case was allowed and 0.17 acres of schedule I land was recorded in her name and remaining 0.17 acres recorded in the name of Bosai Mia, Suratunnessa, Abul and Amu Chand, plaintiffs claim that although 0.11 acres of land was not recorded in their name, but they are in possession of said 0.11 acres as 
heirs of Bosai Mia; that defendant Nos.l-6 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993) in their written statement stated that Abul and Amar Chand filed Objection Case No.1860 of 1961 under Section 19(1) of the SAT Act which was dismissed. The plaintiffs are in ejamli possession, since they are possessing less share they claimed partition of their share of 
0.11 acres in the schedule 3 of the suit land requested the defendants to partition of their share in the schedule land but they refused to do so. Thus the plaintiffs were compelled to file the present suit for partition. The defendant Nos.2-10 and the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 have no right, title and interest in the suit land. 

7. Defendant Nos.2- 10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 contested the said suit by filing joint 
written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the schedule I land belonged to Monirunnessa Chowdhurani. She settled 0.30 acres of land out of schedule I by a registered Kabuliyat dated 4' Magh, 1328 B.S. to (I) Sk. Abdul and (2) Rahim Box; that Abdul died leaving three sons namely, Lal Mia, Reaz Mia and Siraj Mia. Lal Mia died leaving three sons defendant Nos.3-5, four daughters defendant Nos.6-9 and wife defendant No.10; that Siraj Mia died unmarried, so, his shares devolved upon the defendant Nos.2-10. These defendants claimed that the alleged Hukumnama of the plaintiff dated 1 Srabon, 1320 B.S. is fictitious and the predecessor of the defendants had no knowledge about the Objection Case No.990 of 1961 under Section 19(1) of the SAT Act. Accordingly, the defendant Nos.2-10 claimed separate saham 0.15 acres of land out of schedule I. During last settlement operation part of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendant's predecessor and since there is no partition between the plaintiffs and defendants, now they are claiming partition by filing Title Suit No.69 of 1993. 

8. Defendant Nos.16 and 17 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.I2 and 13 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 are same. Their positive case is that their mother -Monirunnessa settled the schedule 3 land to predecessor of plaintiffs Bosai Mia. These defendants denied right, title and interest of the defendant Nos.2-I5. Defendant Nos.2-I5 were given yearly lease by Monirunnessa Chowdhurani and since they failed to pay rents accordingly they were evicted and possession taken by the lessor Monirunnessa Chowdhurani. These defendants are claiming saham of 0.17 acres in the suit land. 

9. Heirs of Suratunnessa defendant Nos.I2 and 15 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and also defendant Nos.9 and 10 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in their written statement stated that the Monirunnessa Chowdhurani settled 0.0425 acres of land out of schedule I in favour of Suratunnessa mother of the defendant Nos.11-15 in the latter part of 1948 and they have been possessing the same by constructing huts. Their further case is that the predecessor of the defendant Nos.2-10 were evicted from their land as they failed to pay rent. So, the defendants are entitled to get separate saham for an area of 0.0425 acres of land in the suit land. Defendant Nos.I4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 contested the suit by filing joint written statements claiming that their predecessor Rahim Box and the predecessor of the plaintiffs jointly look settlement of 0.30 acres of land by erecting their habitual huts thereon and they also claimed separate saham for an area of 0.15 acres of land in the suit land. 

10. In the suit the trial Court framed the following issues:
“১। দেং ৮৫/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমা বর্তমান আকারে ও  প্রকারে চলিতে পারে কিনা?
২। দেং ৬৯/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দ্মা বতমান আকারে ও প্রকারে চলিতে পারে কিনা?
৩। দেং ৮৫/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমা এবং দেং ৬৯/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমার পক্ষ দোষ আছে কিনা?

৫। দেং ৬৯/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমায় নালীশী তপশীলভূক্ত ভূমি অন্দরে .১৫ শতাংশ জমিতে উক্ত মোকদ্দমার বাদীদের স্বত্ব স্বার্থ ও দখল আছে কিনা?
৬। নালিশী ২২৩৪ দাগের সম্যক জমি সম্পকিত ২৮৮৪ ও ১৫৩৯ নং খতিয়ান নম্বর সঠিক কিনা?
৭। দেং ৮৫/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদীগণ ডিক্রি পাবে কিনা এবং দেং ৬৯/৯৩ ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদীগণ ডিক্রি পাবে কি?

11. In the suit, plaintiffs examined 3 PWs. and exhibited their documents as exhibit Nos.l-3(Umo) and unregistered Hukumnama dated 14 Srabon, 1320 B.S. which was marked as "X" by the trial Court. On the other hand, defendant Nos.2-10 examined 2 witnesses namely Reaz Mia defendant No.2 and their documents were marked as exhibit Nos.A-D(4). Defendant Nos.I 4, 15 and 17 examined 2 witnesses namely Safina Khatun, defendant No.15 as DW.I and Nur Mia as DW.2. Defendant Nos. 16(Ka) and I 6(Kha) examined one Dewan Ferdous Ahmed Chowdhury as defendant No.1 on their behalf and examined one document which was marked as exhibit-Ja. In the suit, Advocate Commissioner, Mr. Abdus Sabur Chowdhury was examined in the suit as DW.1. 

12. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record decreed the Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in part and also decreed the Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in part by a single judgment dated 30.01.1997 allotting saham to Murad Mia and other plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.l-6 of Title Suit No.69 of -1993 share of 0.0425 acres out of 0.11 acres and decreed the Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in part allotting a saham of 0.0850 to plaintiff of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993. Further allotted 0.0425 acres to the heirs of Suratunnessa, defendant Nos.11-15 in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 defendant Nos.9 and 10 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and also allotted saham 0.17 acres to Jamindar, Monirunnessa Chowdhurani, predecessor of defendant Nos. 16(Ka) and 1 6(Kha) in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.I2(Ka) and 12(Kha) in Title Suit No.69 of 1993. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree Vs. Mend Mia & Ors (A.K.M. Abdul Hakii..11435 of the trial Court defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.64 of 1997, plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.55 of 1997, defendant Nos.I4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.65 of 1997 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. 

13. It may be noted that no appeal was filed by the plaintiffs, Murad Mia and others against the part decree passed in Title Suit No.85 of 1993. Subsequently, all the appeals were transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Additional Court. Sylhet who upon considering the evidence and materials on record, finding and decisions of the trial Court dismissed all the appeals and decree the Title Suit No.85 of 1993 allotting saham of 0.11 acres in favour of the plaintiffs Murad Mia and others by judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004. 

14. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet defendant Nos.2- 10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and defendant Nos-14, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 and obtained the present rules and stay. 

15. It appears that during pendency of the rule opposite party No.19 of the Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004 Afroza Chowdhury died and her heirs was duly substituted as opposite party Nos.19(a)- I9(d) by order of this Court dated 19.03.2006: Subsequently, by order dated 05.04.2007 heirs of Kamal Badan Chowdhury opposite party .No.20 was duly substituted as opposite party Nos. 20(a)-20(h). The opposite party No.27 Motiur Reza Chowdhury died leaving heirs Sadia Chowdhury, who was duly substituted as opposite party No. 27(a) by order dated 09.03.2009, Jamila Khatun opposite party No.36 died and her heirs was duly substituted as opposite party Nos.36(a)- 36(h) by order dated 30.04.2009 and on the death of opposite party No.37 Ahamed Mia @ Omar Chand who died leaving no heirs and same was recorded by order dated 09.03.2009. Opposite party No.9 Safina Khatun died and her heirs was duly substituted as opposite party Nos.9(a)-9(d) by order of this Court dated 09.02.2009. Opposite party No.2 Surat Mia who died leaving his legal heirs opposite party Nos.2(a)-2(e) and same was recorded by order of this Court dated 22.03.2012. 

16. It further appears that the petitioner of the Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 Jamila Khatun died and her heirs were duly substituted by order of this Court dated 30.04.2009 and opposite party No.I 6 died 'and his heirs was duly substituted as apposite party Mos.16(a)-16(e) by order dated 22.03.2012. Opposite party No.24 Noja Begum died leaving her heirs as opposite party Nos.24(a)-24(f) were substituted by order dated 09.03.2009. Ahamed Miah opposite party No.45 died leaving no heirs and same was recorded by order of this Court dated 09.03.2009.

17. Mr. Golam Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing in 4082 of 2004 for defendant petitioners and 4092 of 2004 for the plaintiff petitioners submits that both the Courts below committed gross error of law in not allotting saham in their favour on the basis of the registered Kabuliyat. He further submits that both the Courts below failed to consider the local investigation report which was proved by the Advocate Commissioner and in the report it was found that the suit land is identical with the kabuliyat land and the petitioners predecessor are in physical possession of the said land. He next submits that the trial Court rightly found the unregistered Hukumnama cannot be the document of title and possession and considered the Hukumnama as forged one but the appellate Court erroneously enhanced the share of the opposite party plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 without considering the aforesaid aspect as found by the trial Court. He also submits that the appellate Court erroneously allotted the entire saham of 0.11 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and failed to consider the fact that they did not prefer any appeal against the part decree allotting a saham of 0.0425 acres of land. He finally submits that the judgment of the appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal and accordingly prayed that the rules should be made absolute. In support of his submissions Mr. Golam Ahmed cited the decisions reported in 17 BLD (AD)36, 12 BLD(AD)203 (1992), 47 DLR (AD) 163. 

18. It appears that the Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 was originally filed by the learned Advocate Mr. Osman Gani and subsequently Mr. Golam Ahmed filed fresh power on behalf of the petitioners. At the time of hearing of the revisional application he submits that due to bonafide mistake he filed power on behalf of the petitioners. Subsequently, he issued no objection certificate and Ms. Rani Akhter filed fresh power on 06.04.2015. At the time of hearing, she supported the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004. 

19. Mr. Md. Delwar Hossein, the learned Advocate with Ms. Salma Begum, Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos.I-2(a)-2(e), 3-6 in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004, opposite party Nos.1, 2(a)-2(e), 3-6 in Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and opposite party Nos.I5, 16(a)-10(e), 17-20 in Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 submits that the appellate Court after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record rightly reversed the findings of the trial Court and as such the judgment passed by the appellate Court is a proper judgment of reversal. Learned Advocate by referring paragraph No.7(Kha) of the written statement filed by the defendant Nos.I6 and 17 heirs of Zamindars submits that in their written statement they clearly admitted that their mother Monirunnessa Chowdhurani settled of I Powa, 4 Jashti equivalent to 0.11 acres land to Bosai Mia, predecessor of present plaintiffs to Title Suit No.85 of 1993 by a Hukumnama dated l' Sraban, 1320 B.S. and this fact of possession was also admitted by DW.I Rear. Mia. DW.2 Yusuf for defendant Nos.2-10 and Salina Khatun, DW.I for defendant No.15, Dewan Ferdous Ahmed, DW.I who deposed on behalf of the defendant Nos.16(Ka) and 16(Kha) also admit the same. Since this facts of possession and settlement by the Zamindar in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs are admitted by the Zamindar, the same need not required to be proved tinder Section 58 of the Evidence Act. In this respect learned Advocate refers the case of Nurul Islam Vs Jamila Khatun and others reported in  53 DLR (AD) 45. He further submits that since the predecessor of the defendants Nos.16 and 17 admitted the settlement of 0.11 acres of land to Bosai Mia predecessor of the plaintiffs by Hukumnama and their possession thereon and accordingly the plaintiffs predecessor paid rent to the Zamindar. So, the allegation as raised by the defendants that Hukumnama and rent receipts are forged does not arise at all. In reply to the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners since Hukumnama is a unregistered document and not marked as Exhibit. But the Court considered this as evidence and marked as 'X' but the defendants did not take any step to prove that the same is forged one. In this connection Mr. Delwar cited a decision reported in 2 MLR (AD) 291. The learned Advocate for the petitioners vehemently submits that the trial Court on the basis of S.A. Khatian rightly allotted saharn for 0.0850 acres to the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993. In reply Mr. Delwar for the opposite party submits that the record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. He submits that the S.A. Khatian clearly shows the name of the plaintiffs predecessor Bosai Mia was recorded for 0.0425 acres of land in less share. Thus for non recording entire share claimed by the plaintiffs on the basis of the settlement of 0.1177 acres by Zamindar in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor Bosai Mia and subsequently payment of rent exhibit-2 series does not extinguished their right, title in the suit land. In this connection learned Advocate refers case of Lal Mia being dead his heirs Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Mia and others reported in 28 DLR(AD) 61. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties by referring Order XLI. rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that non filing of appeal by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 against the part decree passed in that suit for an area of 0.0425 acres, yet the appellate Court has jurisdiction to pass proper Order in the appeal filed by the defendants. In this respect the learned Advocate for the opposite parties refers the decision reported in 37 DLR (AD) 63 and 3 BLC 131. He lastly submits that finding of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court is binding upon the High Court Division except in certain well defined circumstances. 

20. Ms. Shirin Akhter Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.I7- 19, 21-26 and 28-33 submits that the predecessor of these defendants, Monirun Nessa settled the schedule suit land to the plaintiffs predecessors, Bosai Mia and these defendants denied right, title and interest of defendant Nos.2-15. She further submits their predecessor gave yearly lease to the predecessor of defendant Nos.2-15 but for non payment of rent they were evicted and possession was taken back by the Zamindar, lessor Monirum Nesa. She finally submits that both the Courts below rightly gave saham of 0.17 acres in the suit land in favour of these defendants. 

21. It appears that regarding settlement of land by Zamindar to the predecessor of the plaintiff Bosai Mia defendant Nos.16-17 in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 they categorically admitted settlement of 0.11 acres of schedule Ill land in paragraph No.7(Kha) of their written statement, which reads as under: উত্তর দায়ক ১৬/১৭ নং বিবাদীগণের মাতা জনাবা মুনীরুননেছা চৌধুরানী নালিশী ভূমিসহ অপরাপর ভূম্যাদি পূর্ববত মৌরসী মালিক সূত্রে ভোগ দখল করিতে থাকাবস্থায় বাদীগণের পূববর্তী বছই মিয়া খাজনাই প্রজা হিসাবে নালিশী ভূমির উত্তর পশ্চিমাংশে বাদীগণের আরজীর ১ম তপশীল মোট মোং ১/৪/এক কেদার এক পোয়া চারি যষ্টি ছয় পন ভূ্ম্যাদির মধ্যে দক্ষিণ পূবাংশে/১ কেদার ভূমি ব্যতিত অবশিষ্ট ভূমি জোত বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত ক্রমে ভোগ দখল করিতে থাকেন।” which clearly proved that these defendants categorically denied the right. title and interest of the defendant Nos.2-10. Although the learned Advocate for the defendant Nos.2-10 tried to submit that this settlement through Hukumnama is unregistered one and challenged the genuineness of the Hukumnama being forged, fraudulent and collusive one. But they failed to prove by producing any reliable evidence that alleged Hukumnama is fraudulent one. Since the allegations of forgery was alleged by the defendant Nos.2- I 0 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993. same should be proved by them. It is settled principle of law that he who alleges fraud must positively proved the fraud. Reliance is placed in this regard on Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Assistant Custodian Vested Property, Dhaka and another Vs. Most. Anju Bibi and others reported in 2 MLR(AD) 291. So. it cannot be said that the learned appellate Court has committed any error of law in allotting 0.11 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs. In this respect plaintiffs examined 3 witnesses to prove their settlement. Murad Mkt, PW.] in his deposition clearly slated that:“নালিশী জমি থেকে ১১ শং জমি আমার বাবা মুনীরুননেছা থেকে ১৯২০ বাং ১লা আষাঢ় তারিখে বিনা রেজিঃ হুকুমনামা মূলে জোত বন্দোবস্ত গ্রহণ করেন। আমি নালিশী দাগে ১১ শং বাবদ পৃথক ছাহাম চাই। নালিশী জমির মধ্যে আমার ঘর ও খালি জায়গা নিয়া মোট ০৭ শং জমিতে বতমানে দখল আছে।” PW.2 Son Mahar in his deposition stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নালিশী দাগে ১ পোযা জমি দখল করে।” PW.3. In his cross-examination he clearly stated that“মুরাদ মিয়া ঘরের জমি অনুমান ১ পোয়া হবে।” 

22. It further appears from the deposition of OW.1 and DW.2 on behalf of the defendant Nos.2-10 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993. defendant No.2 who deposed in the suit as DW.I in his cross-examination categorically admitted that “ বাদরি বাবা বছই মিয়াকে নালিশি দাগে এস এ জরীপের আগে ঘর তুলে বসবাস করতে দেখেছি। বতমানে মুরাদ মিয়া নাঃ দাগের একটি ঘর এ বসবাস করিতেছে।" I DW.2 Yusuf Mia although admitted possession not in the entire 0.11 acres, but admitted the possession in respect of 0.0425. In his cross-examination he stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়ার ঘরের জমির পরিমান ৪ 1/2 শং হতে পারে। DW.I Salina Khatun who deposed in the suit for defendant No.I5 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in her examination-in-chief stated that " বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নালিশী দাগে ১১শং পেতে আমার কোন আপত্তি নাই।” in cross-examination she categorically stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া গং বতমানে ১ পোয়া জমিতে দখলকার।” It further appears that defendant Nos. 16(Ka) and 16(Kha) in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 also admitted the possession of 0.11 decimals of land in the suit schedule 3. Dewan Ferdous Ahmed Chowdhury, DW. I in his cross-examination stated“ আমার মাতা ও খালার দাখিলী W/S টি সত্য হয়। বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নাঃ দাগের পশ্চিমাংশে প্রায় ১ পোয়া জমিতে দখলকার আছে।” 

23. The appellate Court on consideration of oral and documentary evidence, admission made by the Zamindar predecessor of defendant Nos.l6(Ka) and 16(Kha) in -their written statement in respect of-settlement of 0.11 acres by executing Humumnama and considering all the evidence and materials on record rightly found that the plaintiffs predecessor of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 took settlement of 0.11 acres of land from Khatian No.2844 Plot No.2234 out of 0.4 acres of land. Further the trial Court erroneously allotted suborn of 0.850 acres in favour of the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 although they failed to prove their title on the basis of Kabuliyat (Exhibit-A), which was only for one year after expiry of kabuliyat period the contested defendants failed to produce any piece of papers or documents to show that some was extended by the Zamindar. Thus the appellate Court rightly held that the predecessor of defendant Nos.2-10. Abdul and Rahim Box did not extend the period of kabuliyat after one year in respect of the suit land. Thus by recording of S.A. Khatian in the names the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 did not acquire any title in the suit land. Reliance may he placed in this regard on Lal Mia being dead his heirs Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Mia and others reported in 28 DLR(AD) 61. Wherein it has been held that Record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself it is not an evidence of title. 

24. Learned Advocate for the petitioners vehemently submits that the appellate Court should not enhance the share of the plaintiffs-Respondents-opposite parties which was arbitrary and without jurisdiction. This contention overlooks the order XLI, rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure that the appellate Court may pass such order although the plaintiffs-opposite parties might not have filed any appeal against the part decree. In the present case the decree was before the appellate Court no matter whether appeal was preferred by the respondents-opposite party Nos.1-6. The non-obstante clause is directly relevant, for it totally avoids any condition that a party seeking the benefit of the rule should itself have filed an appeal or objection. Therefore, the mere fact of plaintiffs having not filed any appeal would not by itself he sufficient to justify refusal to exercise the Power under order XL', rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This question came up for consideration before the Appellate Division of our Supreme Court in the case of Osman Gani Vs. Mst. Kulsum Bibi and others reported in 37 DLR(AD) 63. The Appellate Division by relying good number of decisions held- "The appellate Court can pass any order as the case may require notwithstanding that the appeal is as to part only of the decree and may be exercised in favour of all or any of the respondents or parties although such respondents or parties may not have filed any appeal or objection." The principle of law enunciated by our apex Court is a complete answer to the submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Thus I find no substance in the argument made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. 

25. In the present case, the judgment of the appellate Court shows that in arriving at its findings the said Court carefully considered all the material facts and the evidence on record both oral and documentary inclusive of Hukumnama, registered Kabuliyat, S.A. Khatian and rent receipts. The learned Advocate for the petitioners failed to point nut any error of law in them. In the premises, I do not find that the appellate Court committed any error of law, which called for interference by this Court. In this respect reliance may be placed in the case of Hazari Bala and another Vs. Niron alias Niranjan Mandal and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) 294. 

26. I have gone through the decisions reported in 17 BLD (AD) 36. 12 BLD (AD) 203, 47 DLR (AD) 163 cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. It transpires that the facts and circumstances of the cited cases are quite distinguishable and got no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of this present case. So. I do not feel the necessity of referring those in detail. 

27. In view of the aforesaid discussion and on consideration of the evidence on record. specially Exhibit-A, points of law involved in the case and the decisions cited above. I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Additional Court. Sylhet in Title Appeal No.55 of 1997. 64 of 1997 and 65 of 1997 dismissing the appeals suffers from no illegality. There being no illegality in the impugned judgment. the same calls for no interference by this Court. 

28. In the result, the Rules having no merit are discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet is affirmed. There will be, however, no order as to costs. 

29. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

30. Let the lower Court's records along with a copy of this judgment he sent down expeditiously.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J.- These two appeals are directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.6.2003 and 29.6.2003 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Pabna and disposed of by a single judgment dismissing the Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003 and decreeing the Other Class Suit No. 9 of 2003. Since these two appeals arises out of a single judgment for same property in between the same parties. Therefore both the appeals were heard together and disposed of by this single judgment.

2. The short facts of the above mentioned Other Class Suits, in short, are that one Syed Jamshed Hussain Choudhury instituted Other Class Suit No.198 of 1996 before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Iswardi Upazila, Pabna for declaration of title over the suit property and also observations were made in L.S. Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1996 are void, illegal and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. On the other hand the Managing Committee of Marami Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha instituted Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1999 before the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna impleading Syed Jamshed Hussain Choudhury and others as defendants for declaration of title over the suit property. Thereafter the learned District Judge, Pabna vide Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 1999 transferred the Other Class Suit No.198 of 1996 to the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna for analogous hearing with Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1999. Eventually on transfer the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna received the suit records and re-numbered the same as Other Class Suit Nos. 8 and 9 of 2003, respectively.

3. The plaint case of Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003, in short, is that Ka Schedule land of Mouza Marami appertaining to D.S. Khatian No. 248 Plot No. 31 measuring 11.02 acres of land, Plot No. 321 measuring 42 decimals of land, Plot No. 337 measuring 18 decimals in total lands are 11.62 acres originally belonged to Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha as lakheraj of which Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur was the Shebat of the Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha. At the time of C.S. operation the record of right finally was published in the name of Joykalimata Thakurani Bighraha showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait of Joykalimata Thakurani.

Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait for the necessity of puja archana and necessary religious functions settled the property in the name of Sree Paresh Narayan Choudhury as tenant in 1943 and issued Amalnama and Dakhila. 26. We have gone through the plaints, written statements, evidence on record and perused the impugned judgment and also anxiously considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties.

27. On perusal of the impugned judgment, materials on record and from the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant it is clearly manifested that the trial Court in deciding said the two Other Suits came to a conclusion that in respect of Kha and Ga schedule lands of Title Suit No. 8 of 2003 none of the defendants neither denied the plaintiff's right, title and possession nor adduced any evidence claiming the aforesaid land, rather the government and other defendants claimed the Ka schedule land but the plaintiff also claimed the title of the same including Kha and Ga schedule land in Title Suit No. 8 of 2003. Therefore, in the impugned judgment the trial Court opined that there are no necessities to discuss about the right and title of the Kha and Ga schedule lands. Accordingly he did not discuss regarding the right and title of the Kha and Ga schedule lands in the impugned judgment as defendants did not denied the same. Therefore, according to Mr. Siddique the trial Court admittedly found the right, title and possession of the plaintiff's in Kha and Ga schedule lands thus dismissing the suit so far it relates to Kha and Ga schedule land not in accordance with law. The Court below ought to have discussed about right and title about these properties. However, we shall discussed the matter later in this judgment.

28. Admittedly the. Emperor of India was original owner who settled the Ka schedule property in favour of Moharaj Birendra Kumar Roy Bhahadur as landlord. It transpires from the materials on record that Moharaj Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur dedicated the same in favour of the deity permanently. D.S. record of right was finally published in the name of deity treating the same as Lakheraj and showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait. Since then Ka schedule property belonged to deity. The plaintiff by producing a Kabuliyat dated 29.11.1943 claimed that the property including Ka schedule and other land had been given Pattan in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury who executed the Kabuliyat. In the recital of Kabuliyat it was clearly inscribed that the property belonged to deity Sree Sree Joykalimata Thakurani and Shebait had given Pattan the same for legal necessity.

29. Now, the 1st legal issue is as to whether a Shebait can transfer any property of deity permanently or give Pattan year to year basis. The plaintiff in his plaint admitted that Ka schedule property was the property of deity Joykalimata Thakurani. He further admitted that D.S. record of right was correctly published in the name of deity showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait. According to him Paresh Narayan Choudhury took Pattan by executing Kabuliyat in favour of Kumark Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur by registered Kabuliyat dated 29:11.1943 which is Ext.3. On perusal of Ext.3 it transpires that it is an unilateral Kabuliyat without supporting any Patta or Dakhila issued by the Shebait as representative of the deity. From the practice and customs at that time without Patta and Dakhila unilateral Kabuliyat is not a acceptable document in the eye of law in respect of settlement of any property by the landlord in favour of Raiyat far away to accept the same from a Shebait of a deity. Moreso, it is pertinent to mention that nothing is found in the recital of the Kabuliyat that the property in question was settled by the Shebait for the legal necessity of the Deity. The plaintiff has claimed the title of the "Ka" schedule suit land in question through his vendor Nesar Hossain who purportedly got the same from Paresh Narayan Chowdhury who also got the same by executing a Kabuliyat in favour of the Shebait of Deity namely Birendra Kumar Nath Roy Bahadur. On perusal of the recital of the Kabuliyat in question, it divulged that the executent of Kabuliyat not only included the property of Deity but also included the land property wherein temple is situated. Accordingly the Poresh Narayan and Nesar Hossain the vendors of the plaintiff also transferred the same property to the plaintiff without any correction or rectification. But it is very interesting that the plaintiff although claimed the property through the aforementioned deed exhibit 16 dated 28.8.1965 and the Kabuliyat in question exhibit-3 but in the plaint and in his testimonies P.W. 1 stand corrected the recital of the Kabuliyat and deed in question stating that 03 decimals land wherein temple is situated never settled in favour of the vendor of the plaintiff. According to the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act landlord can settle any property to Raiyat and Raiyat can settle the property to under Raiyat, but nowhere in the Act there is a provision that Shebait of Deity can settle the Debuttar property to any Raiyat giving right of transper as per provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Moreso, property in question surely belonged to Deity not Shebait, so he is not landlord although has got some responsibility only to look after the property as managerial capacity. Therefore, we are of the view that the claim of settlement in favour of Paresh Narayan Choudhury through unileteral kabuliyat and so on Paresh Narayan Choudhury to Nesar Hossain and to the plaintiff was nothing but a paper transaction without any legal sanction, recognition and basis of title. It is a settled maxim of law that without proving his title deed in accordance with law, by filing some secondary evidence none can claim any title by dint of secondary evidence which are inadmissible in law. The doccuments in question neither produced in original nor proved in accordance with law. Some other private documents were exhibited in violation of provisions of section 63, 64, 65, 66, and 67 of the Evidence Act, a party producing such documents is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution. Even those documents exhibited in trial but the court is to be satisfied as to its execution.

30. The plaintiff by producing some copies of Rent Suit Rent Execution Case and Dakhilas in the name of Nesar Hossain issued by Paresh Narayan Choudhury showing Paresh Narayan Chowdhury as Jotddar and decree-holder, which were obtained on compromise basis by Nesar Hossain and also got the property through Rent Suit all were in pursuance of Kabuliyat dated 29.11.1943, however, those papers were not proved by examining the executant scribe or attesting witnesses. Therefore the legality of those documents is not only questionable but highly doubtful. We have already opined that Kabuliyat exhibit 3 was without any legal sanction, thus, subsequent transaction cannot be treated as proper and genuine and as such, the same cannot be sustained in law. After appreciating the recital of power of attorney and deed in question executed in the favour of the plaintiff it reveals that there is no schedule of land in the power of attorney, not only that on further scrutiny it is portrait from the power of attorney wherein 5 (five) persons including the plaintiff, were the Attornies of Nesar Hossain but deed was executed in the name of plaintiff by one of the attorney, namely, Susil in the name of another Attorney, no reason has been disclosed in the deed in question which not only cast and create cloud but also depict serious doubt about the genuinty and execution of the deed exhibit 16. Moreso, it is clearly found from the materials on record that the property of Kha schedule land was purchased by Sushama, wife of Paresh but the power of attorney exhibit 28 in question was not appointed and executed by Sushama but Poresh. In view of the legal proposition as discussed above the purchase of the plaintiff from the Attorney of Naser Hossain through a power of attorney is of no avail. Therefore, we without any hesitation can conclude that the transfer of the suit land described in schedules in favour of Nesar Hossain and thereafter to the plaintiff without any legal sanction and basis of title deed. In such circumstances, we have failed to discover any materials justifying to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree but to hold that the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in title suit No. 8 of 2003 is not tainted with legal infirmity and perversity.

31. Mr. Siddique very humbly and candidly has submitted that after enactment of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act Paresh Narayan Chowdhury and Nesar Hossain by operation of Law they became tenants under the Government and as such, the plaintiff through his vendors became the tenant under the Government. Now Government cannot deny the title, possession and record of rights which stand in the name of the plaintiff. To examine and consider the above mentioned legal proposition we have meticulously examined the various provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. On scrutiny the provisions of law it appears that most important feature of the suit land must be discussed which comes into effect after insertion of Section 10A in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. For the reference and convenience of discussion we may quote the Section 10A of the said Act, which runs as follows.

"10A. Special provisions regarding certain rent receiving interests held under waqf, waqf-al-al-aulad, debutter or other religious trust- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in clauses (e) and (ff) of sub-section (4) of section 3 or in section 6A, the provisions of this section shall apply to the cases where the interest of a rent-receiver held under any waqf, waqf-al-al-aulad, debutter or other religious trust have been acquired under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of Section 3, but the Government have not exercised the right of possession over such interest till the date of commencement of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) . Ordinance, 1960, by starting collection of rent and reuses from the tenants holding lands immediately under such interests, or by any other means.

(2) On and from the date of acquisition of such interests, the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, as the case may be, holding such interest immediately before such date shall continue, and be deemed to have continued, to manage such interests as the agent of the (Government) till the last day of the agricultural year (in which the) publication of the notification under sub-section (2) of section 43 declaring that a Compensation Assessment-roll in respect of such interests has been finally published (is made) (or till the time the (Government) exercise the right of possession over such interests, whichever is later).

(3) Such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall, as the agent of the (Government), be entitled to collect, at the rates provided in, and subject to the provisions of, sub-section (4), all rents and cesses payable by the tenants to the (Government) in respect of (such interests, and to collect the usufruct of such interests khas land,) for the period from the date of acquisition of such interests till the last day of the agricultural year (or till the exercise of the right of possession, as referred to in sub-section (2), whichever is later,) and to retain the proceeds of such collection (or other income) in lieu of ad interim payments under section 6A (in respect of such interests) and his remuneration, subject to payment to the (Government) annually, in the prescribed manner, of a sum equivalent to the total of the following amounts, namely-

(a) the amounts which were, or are determined by the Collector to have been payable annually for such interests immediately before acquisition on account of revenue or rent and cesses to the (Government) or to the immediate superior landlord, as the case may be, and

(b) the amount that would have been assessable as tax under the Bengal Agricultural Income-Tax Act, 1944, in respect of the income from (such interests), had not the interests been acquired provided that-

(i) no such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to transfer, or to create any encumbrance or charge on, any such interest in any khas land in any manner otherwise than by a temporary lease, but no such temporary lease shall be given for a period exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the agricultural year in which it is created, nor shall any tree be cut down or building demolished, except with the previous permission of the Collector and on such terms as the Collector may prescribe in that behalf; and any transfer or any encumbrance or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision thereof shall be null and void and the full value of any tree cut down or building demolished in such contravention shall be recoverable from the Mutawalli, shebait or trustee as an arrear of rent or land revenue;

(ii) with effect from the Ist Baisakh, 1367 BS, the amount payable under clause (a) shall be reduced by an amount equivalent to the amount which was, or is determined by the Collector to have been payable annually by the tenants, directly under such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, in respect of such interests  immediately before acaquisition on account of the road and public works cesses under the Bengal Cess Act, 1880, or on account of the local rates under the Assam Local Rates Regulation, 1879, as the case may be; and

(iii) in the cases where any such Mutuawalli, Shebait or trustee was entitled to receive, in respect of any interest referred to in sub-section (1), immediately before the acquisition of such interest, any rent or cesses on account of any tenure, holding or tenancy either from the (Government) or from another rent-receiver whose interests in such tenure, holding or tenancy have been acquired and taken possession of by the (Government) under the provisions of this Act, such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to the adjustment, against his annual liability to the (Government) under this section, of a sum equivalent to the amount that was or is determined by the Collector to have been payable to him annually on account of rent and cesses in respect of such tenure, holding or tenancy immediately before such acquisition, but no such adjustment shall be admissible with effect from the 1st Baisakh, 1367 BS, on account of the road and public works cesses under the Bengal Cess Act, 1880, or on account of the local rates under the Assam Local Rates Regulation,1879; and if the total amount available annually for such adjustment exceeds the amount of his total annual liability under this section, he shall be entitled to get the balance from the (Government), after deduction, at the discretion of the (Government), of any other sum due from him to the (Government) under any law or contract.)

Explanation- For the purposes of clause (b), the amount may be calculated at the average rate of lax at which the assessment was made for the last time, before the date of acquisition, under the provisions of the Bengal Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1944.

(4) the tenants referred to in sub- section (3) shall, in respect of the lands held by them subject to the payment of rents immediately before acquisition, be liable to pay rents in respect of such lands at the rates determined in the record of rights finally published under sub-section (3) of section 19, subject to modification under section 53:

Provided that pending such final publication of the record of rights, the tenants shall pay rents for such lands at the rates shown in the preliminary rent rolls prepared under the rules made under Chapter IV and in cases where such preliminary rent rolls also have not been prepared, the tenants shall pay rents at the rate existing immediately before acquisition till such preliminary rent-rolls are prepared:

Provided further that when any such rent is shown either at an enhanced or at reduced rate in the record of rights finally published under sub-section (3) of section 19 or when any such rent is enhanced or reduced under section 53, the tenant shall be liable to pay the balance or entitled to the adjustment of excess payment against future rent payable by him, as the case may be, with retrospective effect.

(5) The arrears of rent and cesses realisable by a Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee from a -tenant under the provision of this section shall be recoverable as a public demand and the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee may apply to the Certificate Officer in the prescribed manner for the recovery of any such arrears under the provisions of the Bengal Public demands Recovery Act, 1913.

(6) The Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall pay to the (Government) any amount on account of excess payment of rent made by a tenant under sub-section (4) remaining outstanding after adjustment under that sub-section against the rent subsequently payable by him during the period of management by such Mutawali, Shebait or trustee.

(7) All sums payable by a Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee to the Government under sub-section (3) or sub-section (6) shall be recoverable as a public demand.

(8) The arrears of rent and cesses recovered by the Certificate Officer under sub-section (5) shall be paid to the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee concerned after deducting therefrom all sums due from him to the (Government ) under sub-section (3) and sub-section (6).

(9) Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force, in computing the period of limitation for the recovery of any arrears of rent and cesses payable by a tenant under sub-section (4), a period of twenty-four months on and from the date of the acquisition of the rent-receiving interest to which such arrears relate shall be excluded.

(10) Every such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall furnish to the Collector, in such form and at such time as may be prescribed, a statement of accounts of collection of rent and cesses made by him under this section during the preceding year and of expenditure incurred by him out of such collection.

(11) No Court shall entertain any suit or application by any person claiming the benefit of this section in respect of any property or for a declaration that he is entitled to any such benefit, unless such person has applied to the Collector and the Collector has passed a final order declaring that he is not entitled to such benefits:

Provided that, if no such final order is passed by the Collector within a period of 3 months from the date of such application, the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, shall be entitled to bring a suit in the Civil Court after the expiry of the said period.

<u>32. According to the provisions of Section 10A of the said Act it is found that all Debuttar property must he managed, controlled and maintained in accordance with the aforementioned provisions of law. Here we must express our view that the 'Ka' schedule suit property of the present case admittedly was/is a Debuttar property since its inception which was correctly recorded in the name of Deity at the time of preparation of D.S. record of rights during the colonial regime of British showing Kumar Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur as Shebait who was the donor of the property. It further appears from the pleadings of the suit, from the recital of exhibit 3 and deposition of P.W.1 herein he admitted that Ka schedule land was /is a Deity's property. It is further admitted facts that there is a temple with Deity and a big pond from which it is apparent that there was/is nothing cultivable and arable land. Ka schedule total land is occupied by the big pond, temple and Pathway of the temple, so how it would be settled for cultivation to a Raiyat which happened in this case. Since from the time of D.S, record of rights the Ka schedule land belonged to Deity as Debuttar property which never comes within the ambit of the settlement as per the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act or thereafter, by operation of law of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.</u>

<u>Moreso, the defendant Government including the period of the erstwhile East Pakistan Government have failed to produce any notification or assessment-roll in respect of the suit land which admittedly a debuttar property, hence, as per provisions of Section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, unless Government take over the possession of the property as provided in the law none but only Deity is the owner and possessor of the Ka schedule land and as such, Shebait will act as representative of the Government.</u>

<u>33. Therefore, we are of the farm view that by executing a Kabuliyat by Shebait of deity in the name of Paresh Narayan Choudhury was never settled as permanent Raiyat Shebait cannot extinguish or alienate permanently the property of Deity in other words Debuttar property and as such, claiming the Deity's property permanently in pursuance of unilateral Kabuliyat Ext.3 cannot be considered as legal instrument. Therefore, including so called record of rights and all further transfer regarding Rent Sale, compromise of Execution Rent Case, settlement of sub-raiyat by Paresh and Naresh and others and thereafter purchase by Nesar Hossein was beyond the provision of law and without lawful authority and jurisdiction. Therefore, in pursuance of such unlawful authority and papers transferred by Nesar Hossein in the name of the plaintiff does not create any legal and lawful authority to have the right, title and possession over Ka schedule land.</u>

<u>34. Now we shall discuss the materials on record in respect of Kha and Ga schedule land of the suit to consider the right title of the plaintiff. It is pertinent to look into exhibit 16, deed No. 7238 dated 28.8.65 which was executed in favour of the plaintiff by the Nesar Hossain Siddique through his constituted attorney Mr. Sushil Kumar Roy, on perusal of exhibit 16 it reveals that the said attorney did not disclose anything in respect his power in the said deed but after the name of Neser Hossain Siddique only inserted his name as attorney.</u>

<u>35. On scrutiny of the power of attorney exhibit 28 it further reveals that one Nesar Hossain executed the same in favour of (a) Faizul Haque (b) Syed Mokarram Hossein (c) Sree Sushil Kumar Roy (d) Mazed Ali (e) Syed Jamshed Hossain Chowdhury. However, from the exhibit 16 deed in question it is crystal clear that out of 5 Attorney’s only Mr. Sushil Kumar executed the alleged deed dated 28.8.65, not only that on scrutiny it further divulged from the power of attorney exhibit 28 that there is no schedule in the power of attorney regarding any land as described in the schedule of the suit as well in exhibit 16. So, we find that although the Court below in its judgment did not discuss on the merit about right and title of the plaintiff in respect of schedule Kha and Ga of the Other Suit No. 8 of 2003 but from the above discussions and considering the plaintiffs title deed exhibit 16 it manifest that the plaintiff has failed to prove his title by producing successive title deed as has been claimed in the plaint which was executed by Sushil Kumar Roy is nothing but a deed without sanction of law as because in the power of attorney there is no schedule of the land as described in exhibit 16, the alleged deed of the plaintiff. So, we can safely hold that the plaintiff has failed to prove his plaint case in respect of not only Ka schedule land but also Kha and Ga schedule land by producing valid documentary evidence. However, from the discussions made above and materials on retard we find no merit in the appeal as well as any cogent reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree so for it relates in respect of Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003.</u>

<u>36. Now, we shall discuss about the Title Suit No. 9 of 2003 which was tiled for declaration of title over the Ka, Kha, and Ga schedules land. From the cause title of the plaint it reveals that the suit was instituted by the Managing Committee of Marami Joykalimata Thakurani Bigrah. On perusal of the plaint it further reveals that although suit filed by the Managing Committee, but in the pleadings there is no statement in respect of legal sanction about the formation of the Managing committee and filing of the suit by the representative nor permission was sought for to the Court to file a representative suit in accordance with law on behalf of the Deity. Gouranga Chandra Ghosh as D.W. 1 deposed before the court who is the plaintiff No. 2 in the suit.</u>

<u>D.W. 1 in his deposition stated that Joykalimata Thakurani is the owner of the suit properties as per D.S. Record of rights where in Mr. Birendra Nath Roy Bahadur was the Shabait but on perusal of the materials on record it transpires that Deity's properties only belongs to schedule Ka of the Suit Nos. 8 and 9 of 2003. The plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 9 of 2003 to prove his case did not adduce any documentary evidence except oral, from which it appears that the plaintiff of Title Sun No. 9 of 2003 has failed to prove their locus standi to file and prosecute the suit. Although it is admitted fact that the schedule No. Ka of Title Suit No. 9 of 2003 is the property of Deity, which also admitted by the P.W. 1 Jamshed Hossain Chowdhury. So, it is apparent that the Deity has had the right, title over the Ka schedule land as per the D.S. Khatian and admission of the plaintiffs of T.S. No. 8 of 2003 unless Government take over the property as per the provision of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. Since we are affirming the judgment and decree so far it relates to other Suit No. 8 of 2003 hence, the right title of the Deity's is affirmed subject to provisions of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. Therefore, the other suit No. 9 of 2003 filed as plaintiff by the defendant Nos. 11 and 12 of other suit No. 8 of 2003 is superbly Hence, the judgment and decree so far it relates to the O.C Suit. No. 9 of 2003 cannot be sustain in law.</u>

<u>37. For the discussions made hereinabove, we are of the view that there is no legal infirmity and perversity justifying the interference so far it relates to the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 8 of 2003 and as such, we find no merit in the instant appeal being First Appeal No. 289 of 2003 thus, the appeal is dismissed and connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 319(F)/ 2004 is disposed of.</u>

<u>38. So far it relates to the judgment and decree of Other Suit No, 9 of 2003 we find it is tainted with legal infirmity and perversity justifying to interfere with the judgment and decree and as such, the same cannot be sustained in law. Hence, the First Appeal No. 290 of 2003 is allowed and judgment and decree so far it relates to Other Suit No. 9 of 2003 is hereby set aside.</u>

39. The order of status quo granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

40. Send down the lower Court records with a copy of this judgment at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. S.H. Md. Nurul Huda Jaigidar, J:-On an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the plaintiff-petitioner, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.06.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.181 of 2006, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of this Rule, are that, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted filed Title Suit No.81 of 1992 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka for restoration of possession in the suit land under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 against the opposite parties as defendants. On being transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka, it was renumbered as Title Suit No.326 of 1997 and thereafter again renumbered as Title Suit No.181 of 2006. The suit was dismissed on contest by th6 impugned judgment and decree dated 24.06.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka and the instant revision has been preferred. 

3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner, in short, is that professor Nurun Nahar Ahmed, on 01.11.1982, by two registered sale deeds sold .1650 decimals of land to the plaintiff petitioner and handed over the possession of the land. After purchase, the petitioner mutated his name in the Revenue Office and paid rents of the purchased land. The plaintiff-petitioner, while was enjoying right, title and interest of his purchased land, cultivated bore paddy through borgadar. He developed the land by earth filing at the cost of 3 lac taka and bounded by bamboo pillar, bamboo fencing and erected one kacha room with bamboo posts, bamboo fencing and tin roof.
