He appointed one care taker who used to this reside therein and look after the land. In this way the plaintiff petitioner had been peacefully possessing his purchased suit land. 

4. On the night following 03.11.1991 at about 03.00 .m.; defendant opposite party Nos.1 and 2 with some other hired gunda armed with deadly weapons by force dispossessed the plaintiff-petitioner 's caretaker and his other 2 friends, who had been staying in the tin shed room and boundary fencing made by the plaintiff-petitioner. The care taker and his two friends went to the residence of the plaintiff-petitioner and informed about the occurrence. In this way, the plaintiff-petitioner was dispossessed from the suit land by the defendant opposite parties with help of hired `gundas'. As such, the plaintiff-petitioner instituted the suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 for recovery of possession in the suit land on 29.04.1992. 

5. The defendant opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement and denied all allegations made in the plaint and thereby denied the alleged possession in and dispossession from the suit land. According to the case of the defendant, the plaintiff was not in possession of the disputed land and that the defendants (opposite parties) have been long and that the question of alleged dispossession by the opposite parties did not arise at all. 

6. Trial Court on consideration of the evidence, oral and documentary arrived at a decision that the plaintiff-petitioner could not prove his case of possession and dispossession and as such, dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment. 

7. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff preferred this revisional application and obtained the Rule. 

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Mr. Ahasanul Quayyum, the learned Advocates have appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner. By filing an affidavit in reply to the counter affidavit of the defendant opposite parties. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan submits that on 04.11.1991 at night the defendants forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit land and since then they have been illegally occupying the suit land. Learned Advocate contends that the plaintiff petitioner has been able to prove his case by adducing substantive evidence and that the defendants could not prove their possession in the suit land prior to the date of dispossession. It is submitted that the defendants also filed Title Suit No.208 of 2006 against the plaintiff-petitioner for permanent injunction in respect of land measuring 1650 out of their 36 decimals purchased from same suit Plot No.203, boundary area of which was given showing defendants, private road in C.S. Plot No.203 on the north, road on the south; defendants under construction buildings on the west in the C.S. Plot No.203, and own land of defendants in C.S. Plot No.203 on the east, where they had garments factory and to the extreme east west built pucca boundary wall with heavy R.C.C. pillars. The said soil for permanent injunction being No.128 of 1992, was ultimately renumbered Title Suit No.208 of 2006 in the Court of Assistant Judge and the suit was decreed in favour of these defendants, but the suit land measuring 161/2 decimals of the present suit of the plaintiff is not identical and same with the suit land of the defendants in the said suit for permanent injunction, rather both are of separate entity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff petitioner Wali Ahmed filed Title Suit No.81 of 1992 renumbered as Title Suit No.181 of 2006 giving a separate schedule in the plaint measuring 16lA decimals out of the same big plot which is butted and bounded on the north road and Md. Dulal Miah, on the south; Ballot, on the east; Abdus Sattar, on the west; formerly Md. Mafizur Rahman, at present Fatema Besunia; and this portion of land is located to the east of the land of Fatema Basunia, and to the further west of Fatema Basunia, claimed land of the defendants is situated, which was made suit land of permanent injunction suit. Accordingly, the suit land of the petitioner is distinct and different showing marked distance from the suit land of Refatul Islam Chowdhury, plaintiff in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 (defendant in the present suit), but with ill motive, defendant Refatul Islam Chowdhury has tried to show plaintiffs suit land is within their 36 - decimals of land, which is not true. That the decree of permanent injunction was obtained by the defendant opposite parties in respect of their purchased land, where the plaintiff has not interest and the defendant opposite parties do not also claim on the plaintiffs earlier purchased 16l/2 decimals land with separate boundary demarcation. The learned Advocate has further pointed that in the judgment passed in defendant's Title Suit No.208 of 2006 for permanent injunction, the trial Court observed as follows: “অত্র মামমলার বাদী পক্ষ জাহের আলী ও আশেয়া বেগম কোন জমি দাবী করেন না। সেই সাথে বিবাদী পক্ষ সাল্লাবী বিবি, রোকেয়া বেগম ও ইছাকের ওয়ারিশ কাজেম আলী গং এর নিকট হইতে কোন সম্পত্তি দাবি করেন না। মালিকানা দাবীর ক্ষেত্রে কোন পক্ষেরই কোন পক্ষের সাথে স্বত্ত্বে কোন দ্বন্দ নাই।” It is also observed by the trial “বাদীর অত্র মামলার আরজিতে বর্ণিত চৌহদ্দি, বিবাদীর দেওয়ানী ১৮১/০৬ নং মামলার আরজিতে বর্ণিত চৌহদ্দির সাথে কোন মিল খুজিয়া পাওয়া যায় না।” PW.I in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 for permanent injunction as referred to by the trial in the impugned judgment, stated in his deposition “বিবাদীর জমির চৌহদ্দি ও আমাদের জমির চৌহদ্দি আলাদা” and in the plaint of title Suit No.208 of 2006 filed by the opposite parties it has been stated clearly that the suit property (.1650 decimals) of their suit is situated in the middle of 36 decimals of land which they purchased by different deed. 

9. With reference to the aforesaid admission about the fact that the plaintiffs suit land and defendants disputed land of their respective suits are not same, the learned Advocate submits that the decree of the 'permanent injunction suit does not in any way affect the plaintiffs claim of possession and subsequent dispossession, which is the subject matter to been seen in Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the plaintiff petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that just after the occurrence of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land he lodged General Diary Entry No.191 dated 04.11.1991 with Mohammadpur Police Station and immediately thereafter, plaintiff also filed a complaint case against the defendant for criminal offences of the defendants for selfsame occurrence of dispossession, which is still pending. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the written statement filed in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 (suit for permanent injunction) which reads as follows: 

"(f) That on 04.11.1991 the plaintiff and another person Manjur Quader along with many `mastan' people forcibly destroyed the surrounding bamboo fencing and liner ghar' of the defendant and trespassed into the defendants land measuring .1650 decimals, the plaintiff and other person Manjur Quader trespassing into the defendans land has been occupying the some illegally and forcibly. They are mere tress passers only. They have no right, title and interest in the said land which is the suit land. 

"(g) That the defendant filed Title Suit No.181 of 1992 under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, in the Court of Sub Judge, Dhaka for recovery of possession of defendants .1650 decimals of land, which is suit land. The said suit is pending for adjudication. The defendant also filed Complaint Case No. 1287a-1/91 under Sections 448/427f380 Penal Code in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for the criminal activity of the plaintiff in the manner stated above, "These facts and circumstances speak volume of the true story of plaintiffs earlier possession and dispossession, he added. He submits that since the defendant did not get decree in respect of the same property of the plaintiff, no appeal was necessary to be preferred. 

10. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court in his judgment, misread misinterpreted the pleadings of the parties and evidence available on record which needs interference by this Court, and since the plaintiff has been able to prove his case, the instant rule may be made absolute by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

11. Mr. Moinuddin with Mosharrof Hossain Sarder, the learned Advocates, have appeared on behalf of the opposite parties and a counter affidavit in reply has also been tiled, Mr. Moinuddin submits that the defendant opposite parties have been owning and possessing the suit property and they have substantial interest in the suit property, whereas the plaintiff petitioner had/has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and that the plaintiff petitioners witnesses made self-contradictory testimony and as such their evidence are not reliable. It is submitted that the trial Court on proper assessment of evidence, oral and documentary arrived at a correct decision and dismissed the suit in the right direction. That the trial Court rightly held that the plaintiff petitioner could not prove his case of possession in and dispossession from the suit property and committed no error of law resulting in an enor in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the suit and as such there is no cogent reason to interfere with the correct, valid and tenable judgment of the trial Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the present opposite party No.2 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.128 of 1992 (subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.208 of 2006) before the Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka against the present petitioner as the sole defendant for same suit land; the present petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement and the Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the present petitioner against plaintiff Title Suit No.208 of 2006 were simultaneously heard one after another and the trial Court dismissed the Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the present petitioner and decreed Title Suit No.208 of 2006 filed by the present opposite party No.2 for permanent injunction as the present petitioner as plaintiff of Title Suit No.181 of 2006 could not prove his case of alleged possession and dispossession. The decree of title Suit No.208 of 2006 (permanent injunction) in respect of the same suit property still valid and the plaintiff petitioner did not even prefer any appeal against the decree of the permanent injunction. Now the plaintiff cannot get any relief in this revisional application. There is no ground in the revisional application calling for interference with the impugned judgment. 

12. The provision of Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 reads as follows: 

"9. Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property -If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit *** recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. 

Nothing in this Section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof. 

No suit under this Section shall be brought against (the government) 

No appeal shall lie from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section, nor shall any review of any such orders or decree be allowed:' 

13. Thus in a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 it is only necessary to prove whether the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land and he was dispossessed by the defendant and to see whether the plaintiff has filed the suit within 6(six) months from the date of dispossession and, if these facts are proved, the plaintiff can get his possession restored. There is no necessity to adjudicate the title of the parties in this nature of suit. 

14. The plaintiffs specific case is that, he was in possession of the schedule land of the plaint on the basis of registered purchase deeds dated 01.12.82 (Exts.5, 5(ka) and erected a but and bamboo fencing there upon. He got his name mutated in the khatian and has been paying rents. But the plaintiff was evicted by the defendants, on 04.11.1991 at 03.00 a.m. illegally by applying force. The onus obviously is upon the plaintiff to prove that he was in possession of the suit land up to 03.11.1991 and on 04.11.1991 at 03.00 am., he was dispossessed by the defendants otherwise than due C011170 of law. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the basis of his finding that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case disbelieving evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses. The learned Advocate for the petitioner persuaded us to go through the evidence of the parties in details and tried to show instances of misreading and non-consideration of the evidence by the trial Court. 

15. The plaintiff examined five witnesses including himself, as PW.I. PW.I Wali Ahmed in his examination in chief stated “আমি নালিশী ভূমিতে পূর্বে দখলে ছিলাম। নালিশী ভূমি থেকে ০৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে ১নং বিবাদী মঞ্জুর কাদের ২নং বিবাদী রেফায়েতুল ইসলাম আমাকে বেদখল করে। ফলে বাধ্য হয়ে আমি মামলা করিয়াছি। আমি দখল পুনরুদ্ধার চাই।” PW. I in his cross examination said “সত্য নহে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে বিবাদীরা আমাকে বেদখল করে নাই। সত্য নহে নালিশী ভূমিতে মাটি ভরাট করি নাই বা টিনের ঘর করি নাই। ৪/১১/৯১ বেদখল হই। এই সময়ে কেয়ারটেকার ছিল।”  PW.2 Md. Hafiz Uddin who was staying in the suit but with caretaker of the plaintiff on the night of dispossession stated in his examination-in-chief “নালিশী সম্পত্তির ১৯৯১ সনের নভেম্বর মাসের ৩ তারিখে বিদাগত রাত্রে আমার নালিশী সম্পত্তির ঞরে ছিলাম। আমি আবুল খায়ের ও নাজিমুদ্দিন ছিলাম। রাত্রি ৩ টার দিকে ঘুমানো থাকাবস্থায় দরজা ধাক্কায় আমাদের ঘুম ভাংগিয়া যায়। আমরা চৌকির উপর বসি আমরা দরজার দিকে যাই। নাজিম উদ্দিন দরজা খুলে, হাবিব নামে এক লোক তাহার সাতে অপর লোক ঘরে ঢুকে ও নাজিম উদ্দিনের সার্টের কলার ধরে ও আমাদেরকে ধাক্কা দিয়া বের করে দেয়। আমরা বের হয়ে দেখি মঞ্জুর কাদের, কেফায়েতুল, তরুণ কুমার এবং এদের পিছনে ৭০/৮০ জন লোক মঞ্জুর কাদেরের হাতে শাবল ছিল। অন্যান্যদের হাতে লাঠি, শাব, দা অন্যান্য জিনিসপত্র ছিল। আমরা পূর্ব দিকে ৫০/৬০ হাত ধুরে আশ্রয় নেই। ওখান থেকে দেখি যে বাউন্ডারী, ঘর সবকিছু ভেঙ্গে নিয়া যায় ও নাঃ জায়গা খালি থাকে।”

PW.3 Nizam Uddin who was caretaker of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land stated in his examination-in-chief 

“নাঃ জমি নীচা ছিল বাদী মাটি ভরাট করেছে ১৯৯১ সনে জানুয়ারী- মার্চ পরযন্ত। বাদী একটা ঘর নির্মাণ বরে। বেড়া মুলি বাশের উপরে টিন। ১০ হাত চওড়া। ১৫ হাত লম্বা। আমি রাত্রে ঐ ঘরের কেয়ারটেকার হিসাবে থাকতাম, আবুল খায়ের, হাফিজ উদ্দিন মাঝে মাঝে এসে থাকতো। ১৯৯১ সনের নভেম্বর মাসের ৩ তারিখ রাত্রি ৩ টায় ঘটনা ঘটে। আমার সাথে আবুল খায়ের ও হাফিজ উদ্দিন ছিল। নালিশী জমির চারিদিকে মুলি বাশের বেড়া, বাশের খুটির বেড়া ছিল, গেট ছিল। রাত্রি তিনটায় দরজায় ধাক্কার শব্দ শুনে ঘুম ভেঙ্গে যায়। হাবিব আমাদেরকে বের হতে বলে আমরা বের হই নাই বাহির থেকে বলে জোর করে বের করে দাও। আমাদেরকে প্রানে মারার হুমকি দিলে আমরা বের হই।” He deposed that the defendants and their men took possession by force removing the structure and fencing of the plaintiff. PW.4 Md. Abut Khair stated in his examination-in-chief “১৯৯১/৩রা নভেম্বর আমি ও হাফিজ উদ্দিন নালিশী জমিতে উপরস্ত ঘরে যাই। আমরা ঐ ঘরে ঘুমাই। রাত্রি ৩টার দিকে জোরে জোরে শব্দ শুনি ও তিনজন যেগে যাই ও চৌকিতে বসি। নাজিম উদ্দিন জিজ্ঞাসা করে কে, বাহির থেকে বলে হাবিব স্যার এসেছে দরজা খুল। নাজিমউদ্দিন সার্ট সায়ে দিয়ে দরজার দিগে যায়। দরজা খুলে হাবিব, দা হাতে ঠান্ডু লাঠি হাতে ঘরে ঢুকে। হাবিব বলে মঞ্জুর সাহেবন স্যার ঘরে তিনজন লোক। মঞ্জুর কাদের বলে যে, পিটাইয়া বের কর। আমরা বের হতে না চাইলে মৃত্যুভয় দেখাইয়া বের করে। বাহির হয়ে দেখি মঞ্জুর কাদের, কেফায়তুল, তরুন, কুবের সহ ৭০/৮০ জন লোক। আমরা পূর্বদিকে যাই। ছাপড়ামত জায়গায় আশ্রয় নেই। মঞ্জুর কাদের শাবল হাতে ঘরে আঘাত করে ও অন্যান্য লোক দরজা বেড়া, টিন ভাঙ্গিয়া লইয়া যায় ও নাঃ জমি খালি পড়িয়া থাকে।” He testified that the men of the defendants ousted them from the house and dismantled and removed the structures of the plaintiff from the suit land. On perusal of the evidence of PWs.2-4 we find that all of them were eye witnesses to the occurrence of dispossession and they, in corroboration with each other, testified as to how and in what manner the defendants evicted the plaintiff from the suit land at night by force. PW.5 Abdus Satter was owner of adjoining land to the suit land and he appears to be a competent and dependable to testify about possession of the suit land. He stated in his evidence “নাঃ জমিতে বাদী ওয়ালী আহমেদ জমি মাটি ভরাট করে। বাদী ওয়ালী মুল বাশের বেড়া দ্বারা একটা ঘর করে। সীমানা চতুর দিকে মুলি বাশের বেড়া করে। বাদীর লোকজন ঐ বাড়ীতে আসত। নাঃ জমি মঞ্জুর কাদের দখল করে এবং টিন সেড ঘর করে জুতার ফ্যাক্টরী করিয়াছে।” he further stated in his examination-in-chief 1991/সনের ৪ঠা নভেম্বর বিবাদী নালিশী জমির দখল নেন। আমি গিয়া দেখি যে, বাদির ঘর দরজা নাই।” Testifying previous possession of the plaintiff, he said that he offered prayer in front of the plaintiffs hit. His evidence along with the testimony of PWs.2-4 has satisfactorily proved the plaintiffs case of possession an dispossession. 

16. DW.I, A.K.M. Hasinul Haque was examined as sole witness of the defendants opposite party, who stated in his examination -in-chief “আমি অত্র মামলায় মঞ্জুর কাদের এর পক্ষে ক্ষমতা পত্র নিয়ে সাক্ষী দিচ্ছি যে, আমার বাসস্থান ধানমন্ডি ১৯ নম্বরে। ০৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে আমি রাত ৩ টার সময় বাসায় ছিলাম। নালিশী জমিতে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে রাত ৩ টায় কি ঘটে তা আমি দেখিনি।”

17. Defendants have no witness to give testimony in proof of their entering into possession of the suit land against the evidence of PWs. 

18. On perusal of pleadings of the patties, exhibits and evidence on record with regard to the acquisition of title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land we find that Professor Nurun Nahar Ahmed on 01.11.1982 by two registered sale deeds No.3821 and 3822 sold suit land measuring .1650 decimals of land to the plaintiff petitioner and handed over the possession therein with specified boundary given in the schedule of the kabals. After purchase in 1982, plaintiff mutated his name in the khatian and paid rent. At the time of purchase, the suit land was low lying area and the purchaser plaintiff cultivated boro paddy through borgadar and developed the land by earth filing spending money; and the plaintiff demarcated boundary of the suit land by bamboo pillar and bamboo fencing, erected one but with bamboo pillar, bamboo fencing and with tin roof and appointed one caretaker PW. Nizamuddin who used to reside therein to look after the suit land. Plaintiff PW.1 stated in his deposition .“নামজারীর খতিয়ানও দিয়াছি (প্রঃ-৩) ন! ৯৪/২, এসএ খতিয়ান ------ উক্ত প্রকারে আমরা ১৬৫০ শতাংশ ভোগ দখলে আছি। নামজারী করেছি। এই সেই নামজারী খতিয়ান নং-৫৪/৩ (প্রঃ-৬)। কতিপয় খাজনার দাখিলা ডিসিআর দিয়েছি (প্রঃ-৭ সিরিজ) আমি নাঃ জমিতে মাটি ভরাট করেছি। ৩ লক্ষ টাকার কাচাঁ স্লিপ দিয়েছি।” Rent receipts and records of right though not documents of title, are important documentary evidence of possession. In support of this contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the case of Erfan Ali Vs. Joynal Abedin Mia (late) represented by his legal heirs Golenur and others, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216. The defendant opposite parties could not controvert the plaintiffs documents Exhibit 3, 6 and 7 series. Defendants purchased land has been mutated in their names separately indicating that their land is not the suit land of this suit. Because two khatians cannot be opened for the same area of land. Moreover, it is evident that the plaintiff purchased the suit land before the purchase by the defendants. It is not acceptable contention that after purchase of the suit land in 1982 and getting name of plaintiff mutated, he would remain silent without taking possession in the suit land. Rather after execution of purchase deed of defendants. Problem cropped up G.D. Entry and complaint case are supporting events in proof of eviction of the plaintiff on 04.11.1991 at 03.00.A.M. 

19. On perusal of the trial Court's judgment, it appears that the trial Court found “বাদী ৯৪/২নং খতিয়ানে তাহার নামে নামজারী পর্চা এবং ডিসিআর ও নালিশী ভূমিতে তাহার দখল সংক্রান্ত তহশীল অফিস কর্তৃক দাখিলী প্রতিবেদন প্রমাণে ব্যবহার করে নাই। But on perusal of the evidence of PW.1, we find it otherwise. All those documents are admitted in evidence as Exhibits 3 and 7 series. These are public documents and need not be proved formally. Again learned Judge found “পিডব্লিউ-১ তাহার জবানবন্দিতে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিথে রাত্রি অনুমান ৩ টার দিকে নালিশী ভূমিতে বাদীর কেয়ার টেকারকে উচ্ছেদ করিয়া তথায় বাশের খুটিসহ টিনের ঘর ভাংগিয়া ফেলে। জবানবন্দির উক্ত বক্তব্য বাদীর আরজীতে কোথাও বর্ণনা করেন নাই।” On perusal of the plaint, we find in the plaint   “বাশের খুটি ও মুলি বাশের বেড়া ও উপরে টিনের ছাউনি দিয়া গৃহ নির্মান করিয়া তাহাতে একজন কেয়ারটেকার বসাইয়া তাহার সম্পত্তি ভোগ দখল ও রক্ষনাবেক্ষণ করিতে থাকে। ------ বিগত ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে বহু লোকজন সহকারে দলবদ্ধ হইয়া বল প্রয়োগে বিবাদীগণ বাদীর দখলীয় উক্ত ১৬৫০ শতাংশ ভূমি চারিদিকের বেড়া ও ঘর ভাংগিয়া সরাইয়া ফেলিয়া তাহা বজর দখল করে।” Again the learned Judge found (PW.2) “তিনি জবানবন্দিতে চারিদিকে বাশের বাউন্ডারী ছিল না বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.2 we find the statement “চারিদিকে বাশের বাউন্ডারী ছিল” The trial Court again found “(পিডব্লিউ-৩) তিনি নালিশী  জমির দক্ষিণে নালা বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন এবং তাহার দক্ষিণে রাস্তা বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন। but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find   “দক্ষিণে নালা, তার দক্ষিনে বিল।” The learned Judge of the trial Court found (PW.3) “তিনি নালিশী জমির পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার বশির উদ্দিন উল্লেখ করেন।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find “পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার” and in cross PW.3 stated “পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার” Again learned Judge found (PW.3) “তিনি কন্ট্রাক্টরের কথা বলিতে বলিতে পারেন নাই।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find “আমার নেতৃত্বে মাটি ভরাট হয়, বয়লামপুর থেকে মাটি এনে ভরাট করি” and in cross examination “ইহা সত্য নয় যে, মাটি ভরাট করি নাই ও কন্ট্রাক্টর দেই নাই।” Again the trial Court found in his judgment PW.4 said “তিনি তাহার জবানবন্দিতে পূর্ব দিকে ছাপড়ায় আশ্রয় নেন মর্মে উল্লেখ করেন যাহা অন্যান্য সাক্ষীদের সাথে বক্তব্যের মিল পাওয়া যায় না।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.4 we find “আমরা পূর্ব দিকে যাই। ছাপড়া মত জায়গায় আশ্রয় নেই। PW.2 stated in his deposition “আমরা পূর্ব দিকে ৫০/৬০ হাত দূরে আশ্রয় নেই। PW.3 also stated in his deposition “আমরা ৫০/৬০ হাত দূরে পূর্ব দিকে আশ্রয় নেই। Again the trial Court found in his judgment “(পিডব্লিউ ৫) তিনি নালিশী জমির বাউন্ডারী হওয়ার কথা বলিতে পারেন নাই।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.5 we find “নালিশী জমিতে বাদী আহম্মদ মাটি ভরাট করে। বাদী ওয়ালী মুলি বাশের বেড়া দ্বারা একটা ঘর করে। সীমানা চুতর্দিতে মুলি বাশের বেড়া করে।” Again he found in his judgment “তিনি মঞ্জুর কাদের নালিশী জমিতে নীচু জমি ভরাট সমান করেন মর্মে উল্লেখ করেন।  but on perusal of the evidence of PW.5 we find “নালিশী জমিতে বাদী ওয়ালী আহম্মদ মাটি ভরাট করে।” On scrutiny of the impugned judgment, we therefore, find the above quoted examples of misreading, non-consideration of the pleadings and evidence on record and the learned trial Judge has committed error of law resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and miscarriage of justice. As such, he said judgment calls for our interference. 

20. From the aforesaid discussion of evidence and other facts and circumstances of this case, we hold the view that the plaintiff-petitioner has successfully proved his prior possession and subsequent dispossession by the defendant on 4/11/191 at 3.00 a.m. and immediately after the dispossession, he lodged General Diary No.191 dated 4.11.1991 with the Mohammadpur Police Station and also filed Complaint Case No.1287a-1/91 and thereafter this suit was filed within 6 months on 29.04.1992. But the learned Judge of the Court below could not adjudicate the whole matters in its true perspective, and arrived at a wrong decision in dismissing the suit occasioning failure of justice. When the defendants had taken force able possession without lawful authority and the suit was filed within 6(six) months, it is incumbent upon the Court to restore possession of the plaintiff in the suit land in accordance with boundary demarcation specified in the schedule of the plaint. The defendants may file proper suit to get their legitimate share partitioned, but they cannot be allowed to take law in their hand. 

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissing the suit is set aside and the suit is decreed with costs. The defendant opposite parties are directed to surrender vacant possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner within 60(sixty) days from this date, failing which, the plaintiff-petitioner shall get possession in the suit land restored through the Court by removing the structures therefrom, if any. 

22. Send down the lower Court's record along with a copy of the judgment to the Courts below immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. S.N. Goswami, Advocate -- For the petitioners 
Mrs. Sucharita Sen Gupta, A.A.G -- For Opposite Party No. 1-3 
Mr. Mohammad Shamsul Alam, Advocate -- For Opposite Party No.4-6
parties:
Abu Taher Mijhi being dead his legal heirs I(a) Mst. Morium Bibi and others ----- Plaintiff-appellant petitioners
Versus
Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion, Bhola and others ----- Defendant-respondent Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 08.09.2010 and 15.09.20 10 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd  Court, Bhola in Title Appeal No. 03 of 2006 affirming those of 'dated 04.09.2005 and 11.09.2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola, in Title Suit No. 01 of 1998 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original Suit being Title Suit No. 01 of 1998 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola for declaration of title and further declaration that the order dated 30.12.1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.92 of 1995-96 described in schedule 'Kha' of the plaint is illegal, collusive and not bindirig upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia, that the suit land measuring 00810 'shahasrangsho' appertaining to plot no.4205/6 of Mouza Char Tofazzal described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint was a khash land under the government. The predecessor of the plaintiffs namely Abdul Mannan Mijhi prayed for settlement of the land from the government and the government being satisfied pursuant to a Group Settlement Case No. 157-17/50-51 granted a settlement for the 'Ga' schedule suit land situated within "Dularhat bazar" in favour of Abdul Mannan Mijhi. Thereafter; the settlement holder Abdul Mannan paid 'selami' to the government and the government accepted the same after granting D.C.R. The predecessor of the plaintiffs erected this shop in the suit land and was continuing his business therein. After the death of Abdul Mannan the plaintiffs inherited the suit property and possessing the same. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that their predecessor on 15.09.1954 and 13.03.1955 paid 'selami and obtained D.C.R. and for the last 50 (fifty) years the plaintiffs are possessing the suit shop. On 25.12.1992 the dacoits put fire to 'Dularhat Bazar in where the plaintiffs shop is situated. Subsequently, for a new khatian in the name of the plaintiffs they filed an application in the office of the defendant No.3 and accordingly a Miscellaneous Case being No.92/95-96 was started. The defendant No.3 asked the defendant No. 1 to inspect the matter and submit a report but the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 in collusion with the defendants No. 1 and 2 managed to submit a false report. The defendant Nos. 4 and 5 while tried to grab the property and the defendant No.3 by his order dated 30.12.1997 being bias in their favour started proceeding of a miscellaneous case to grant re-settlement, the plaintiffs instituted the original suit. 

3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus that the disputed land is situated within 'Dularhat Bazar periphery and in that property the government has 'Chandina' right. No Group Settlement Case was started in respect of the suit land and no settlement was granted in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor Abdul Mannan. There is no existence of group settlement case in the government's custody. The D.C.R. in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor is created and that the order dated 30.12,1997 of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 is correct by which the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 obtained licence to posses the suit land. 

4. The learned trial court after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 04.09.2005. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 03 of 2006 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2"d Court, Bhola and the learned appellate court by the impugned iud2ment and decree dated 08.09.2010 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment of dismissal decree of the trial court. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

5(A). Mr. S.N. Goswami the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mrs. Sucharita Sen Gupta the learned Assistant Attorney General with Mr. Mohammad Shamsul Alam, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan Mijhi in respect of the suit land obtained settlement from the government rightly pursuant to a Group Settlement Case; which is in existence and have been called for but complying the direction of this court in civil revision No. 3800 of 2007 the concerned government official without sending the complete file sent the case record partially with an ill motive and the paper sent clearly go to show that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan in serial. No. 24 obtained settlement of the suit land followed by payment of salami in favour of the government by two D.C.R./Receipts. The learned Advocate also submits that the lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal consulting the said Group Settlement Case and the certified copy marked as Exhibit-I rightly held that, pursuant' to two D.C.R marked as Exhibit-2 and 2(Ka) the government accepted Abdul Mannan as settlement-holder under them. It is in fact proved by Exhibits I, 2 and 2(ka) that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Abdul Mannan applied for settlement of the suit land which was subsequently allowed and thereafter salami was paid by the settlement holder Abdul Mannan. The learned appellate court clearly observed in his findings and decision that the claim of the plaintiffs appears to be correct in view of the exhibited papers but subsequently the Court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in holding the view that the settlement was not completed by opening a separate khatian in the name of plaintiffs predecessor. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below misconstrued the factual aspect of the case inasmuch as it is the specific assertion of the plaintiffs that for opening a separate khatian in their name while they submitted an application before the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) Char Fashion, a miscellaneous case was started. But the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 collusively managed to stop that proceeding only to deprive the plaintiffs and thereby the plaintiffs felt aggrieved and instituted the original suit. The learned Advocate argued that the findings of the lower appellate court itself is self-contradictory and as such perverse in the eye of law. In support of group settlement the learned Advocate referred a decision of this Court reported in 2 D.R. 265 passed in the case of 'The Province of Bengal vs. Nalini Kanto Baraijja Chowdhury and others.

7. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocates on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned courts below concurrently held that the plaintiffs right, title, interest and possession over the suit property is not proved rather disproved. There is no illegality or infirmity in passing the impugned judgment and order. The learned Advocates further submits that the suit property admittedly being 'Chandina Bhiti cannot be settled in favour of any individual pursuant to any settlement case and thereby the alleged settlement in favour of plaintiffs' predecessor is false. Both the courts below in their findings and decision rightly held that the settlement of the plaintiffs' predecessor since not completed by way of executing kabuliat and acceptance of the some, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get relief as prayed for. The learned Advocates also submits that there is no existence of kabuliat in respect of the alleged settlement and the plaintiffs witnesses admitted in their testimony that no kabuliat was executed by the settlement holder. Lastly; there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

8. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that previously in respect of the disputed property there was another Civil Revision being No. 3800 of 2007 in this court invoking the provisions laid down in section 115(1) of, the Code of Civil Procedure and in that Civil Revision the Rule was made absolute with an order of remand to the appellate court for passing a fresh judgment after rectification and compliance of a direction. For proving the genuineness of the plaintiffs claim of settlement from the government and for proper adjudication into the matter of -controversy the group settlement case record was called for as per direction of this Court. After getting partial of that case record; the lower appellate court found the existence of the Group settlement case. Following the direction of this court on an application from the side of the plaintiffs the court of appeal called for the original record/volume from the offices of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion as well as A.D.C. (Rev.), Bhola.' It has come to the notice of this court that after getting the order of the Court partial original papers were sent without sending the case record as a whole and the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion, Bhola sent the Roll of K.M. settlement, wherefrom it is apparent that a Group Settlement Case No. 157-F/1950-51 was started and the page of said settlement-roll go to show that there are four settlement holders whose serial numbers are 23,24,25 and 26. In serial No. 24 there is an inclusion of plaintiffs predecessor's name viz. Abdul Mannan Mijhi, son of Arfan Ali Mijhi. Against the name of that Abdul Mannan it has been clearly mentioned that the disputed land of schedule cka' measuring an area of 00810 `Shahasrangsa' in plot No. 4205/6 under the government khash khatian has been settled by the government in the year 1-957 in favour of Abdul Mannan Mijhi and the amount of Salami was fixed against the suit land. It is to be noted here that the land included within this paper marked as Exhibit-1 and in respect of the land of the government khash khatian 04(four) persons having serial No. 23-26 obtained settlement pursuant to a K.M. settlement roll and therefore it is clear that the said settlement of the government is nothing but a group settlement as contended by the plaintiffs. Apart from this; it is obvious to note that the concerned tahshilder pursuant to that settlement granted receipts in favour of the' plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan after acceptance of selami against the disputed property. In the year 1998 also the concerned official after acceptance of rent granted receipts in favour of plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest vide Exhibits No.2 and 2(ka). 

10. In this context; having gone through the impugned judgment and decree I find that the learned appellate court below scanning the said papers conclusively held that on perusal of the certified copy of K.M. settlement case marked as exhibit- l along with two D.C.Rs. it appears that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan in Group Settlement Case No.157-F/1950-51 in serial No.24 obtained the suit land and accordingly paid selami in favour of the government. It is also held by the lower appellate court that the claim of the plaintiffs appears to be correct. Subsequent to that; the learned court below holding the view that inasmuch as the settlement was not completed and no khatian was opened neither in the name of the settlement holder nor in the names of the plaintiffs; the plaintiffs are not entitled to get the relief as prayed for. It is the observation of the appellate court in the concluding portion of the impugned judgment that:বাদী পক্ষের পূববর্তী আঃ মান্নানের নামে নাঃ ভূমি বাবদ  ১৫৭/৫০-৫১ নং গ্রুপ সেটেলমেন্ট কেস রজু থাকায় উযধশক্ত বন্দোবস্তের বিষয়টি চুড়ান্ত করার নিমিত্তে আবশ্যকীয় প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা যুক্তে বাদী পক্ষের আদালতের স্নরনাপন্ন হওয়া যুক্তিযুক্ত ও সংগত ছিল। From the aforesaid recital of the impugned judgment and decree it is evident that the lower appellate court awarded no decree in favour of the plaintiffs inasmuch as the appropriate relief was not sought for. 

11. From the discussions spelt out earlier it is apparent that the learned lower appellate court is totally misconceived in appreciating the actual position of law and has failed to evaluate the evidence on records in its total approach. The findings suffer from contradiction and proper appreciation of the evidence on records. The fact remains that the government admits that the suit land was settled with the plaintiffs predecessor by group settlement case and accordingly K.M. settlement was done. In the said Settlement Case No.157-F/1950-51 four persons including the predecessor of the plaintiffs obtained settlement and the selami which was fixed including the rents therein has been duly accepted by the government after granting receipts. As such; it cannot be held that the plaintiffs predecessor had any malafide intention or that the plaintiffs case suffers from suppression of facts rather it is evident that it is the bonafide claim of the plaintiffs in respect of the disputed property and they possess the same from the settlement of their predecessor-in-interest since 1957. The subsequent act of filing the miscellaneous case by the defendant No.3 Assistant Commissioner (Land), Charfashion, Bhola cannot be treated as legal. 

12. I have come across from the relevant papers that the suit land is situated within a bazar area commonly known as 'Dularhat' and it is not denied from any corner that in the year 1992 'Dularhat Bazar' was burnt into ashes. It is the pleading's case of the plaintiffs that after the demise of their father they possess the suit shop and subsequently for opening a khatian in their names they filed an application and went to the defendant No.3, A.D.C.(Rev.), Bhola. In the office of the A.D.C. (Rev.) admittedly a Misc. case was started for opening a khatian in the names of the plaintiffs in respect of the disputed property but before disposal of that Miscellaneous case it was filed (" "). It is also within records that the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 tried to obtain a new khatian in their names from the office of the defendant No.3 A.D.C. (Rev.). Challenging the said act of the defendants the plaintiffs instituted the original suit. 
Hence; it cannot be held that in wrong forum or for avoiding appropriate relief the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

13. The witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiffs are two in numbers. The witness No.1 Abu Taher deposed in support of the pleading of the plaintiffs and the witness No.2 states about the possession of the plaintiffs. Vis-a-vis; the only witness adduced from the side of the defendants is a formal witness. This witness states that he cannot say as to whether the group settlement case was started or that Abdul Mannan the predecessor of the plaintiffs was one of the settlement holders. This witness expressed his inability to state that for unholy alliance of the defendants the entire Group settlement case records not sent despite the same was called for by the court. Hence, I find that the act of the government is malafide and on the other hand the onus of proving the case of the plaintiffs as has been discharged properly by adequate credible evidence, the contention as described in their plaint of the plaintiffs is honafide. 

14. Before parting, however, I must observe consulting the connected evidence both oral and documentary that the courts below are wrong during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal as have failed to assess the evidence or records. The pertinent question for disposal of the original suit not at all ascertained or disposed of in its true perspective. Furthermore; the findings and decision arrived at by the lower appellate court is violative to the provisions laid down in Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. There is no discussion of the oral evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties and no compliance of relevant laws. Besides this; the manner of disposal as it appears suffers from gross infirmity and as such it can be easily held that in disposing the original suit as well as subsequent appeal there has been illegality and' non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Be that as it may; I have the reason to draw such inference that the submissions advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners Mr. S.N. Goswami have got much substance. 

Prior to conclusion; I may not be out of place to advert that it is to be remembered that none is above the law of the land and can act arbitrarily. In discharging the official duties the government officials can't act 'hot and cold' and their role must be bonafide. 

15. In the result, the Rule having merit be made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 08.09.2010 and 15.09.2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bhola in Title Appeal No. 03 of 2006 affirming those of dated 04.09.2005 and 11.09.2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola, in Title Suit No. 01 of 1998 is hereby set aside. The original suit be decreed on contest without cost declaring the plaintiffs title to the suit land. 

16. Communicate the judgment and order at once and send down the Lower Court's Record immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abdus Salam Mondal with Mr. Surojit Bhattachargee, Advocates ------ For the appellants
Mr. Fazlul Haque with Mr. M. C. Chowdhury, Advocates ------ For the respondents
parties:
Nazir Ahmed & others ------ Appellants 
-Versus-
Md. Fajal Ahmed & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, J. :  - This appeal at the instance of defendant Nos. 4-6, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.03.2000 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 43 of 1999, decreeing the suit.

2. The respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 43 of 1999 (re-numbered) before the Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet impleading the appellants along with others as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of title and for a further declaration that three kabalas one dated 18.11.1974 executed by Abdul Hashem in favour of Chand Miah the defendant No. 1, registered kabla dated 02.12.1974 executed by Abdul Hashem in favour of defendant No. 2 Raja Miah and registered kabala dated 30.03.1973 executed by Rosomoy Chandra Nath in favour of Abdul Hashem are forged, fabricated, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The plaintiffs brought the suit stating inter alia that some 1.13 acres of land covered by two S.S. plots namely, 2088 and 2007 appertaining to Khatian No. 1220 of Mouza Kumargoan J.L. No. 18 originally belonged to Jogendra Mohantha and Mahananda Mahantha sons of Paramananda Mahantha who having been khas possession of the suit land sold the same in favour of Rosomoy Chandra by a registered kabala dated 16.06.1960; while Rosomoy Chandra was in possession and enjoyment of the suit land the same was put to auction owing to non payment of rent and eventually Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 was initiated and upon conclusion thereof the suit land was sold in auction in due process; Taheruddin purchased the suit land in the said auction held on 29.10.64 and the said sale was made absolute and certificate was issued in favour of Taheruddin on 20.01.1965; thereafter, Taheruddin sold the suit land in favour of Ershad Ali by a registered kabala dated 07.04.1975 who also sold the suit land to Raisa Bibi who got possession; thereafter Raisa Bibi being in possession of the suit land sold the same in favour of Tullai Bibi in the year 1979; thereafter Tullai having been in possession of the suit land got her name mutated in the record of rights and eventually she gifted away the suit land to her son Moklis Miah by a deed of gift dated 20.11.1986 and upon taking over possession of the suit land Moklis Miah got his name mutated in the record of rights in respect of the suit land; thereafter on 27.06.1992 Moklis Miah sold the suit land in favourt of plaintiff Fazal Ahmed and one Akbor Ali and had handed over possession; said Akbor Ali subsequently sold his part of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff Fazal Ahmed, thereafter the plaintiff got his exclusive title in the suit land in the manner aforesaid and also got possession thereof.

Thereafter, the plaintiff made an attempt to get his name mutated in respect of suit land but it was found that the names of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had already been recorded in respect of the suit land although they had no right, title, interest or possession therein and upon query the defendant No. 3 disclosed for the first time that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had purchased the suit land from Abul Hashem by a registered kabala dated 18.11.74 in the name of Chand Miah the defendant No. 1 and by another kabala dated 02.12.1974 in favour of defendant No. 2 Raja Miah; and defendant No. 3 made an attempt for sale of the suit land; thereafter the plaintiff got information about the three kabalas as disclosed above which are dated 30.03.1973, 18.11. 1974 and 02.12.1974; thus the cause of action arose and the suit was filed seeking redress.

4. The defendant Nos. 4-6 who are the appellants before us, got themselves added in the suit and upon filing written statement denied the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that it is indeed Mohendra and Mahnada Mohantha were the original owners of the suit land who in fact sold the suit land in favour Rosomoy Nath by a registered kabala dated 16.06.60; thereafter Rosomoy Chandra Nath sold the suit land in favour of Abdul Hashem on 30.03.1973, meanwhile the original owners namely, Mahendra Chandra Mohantha and Mohananda Mohantha died leaving behind their sole heir Sachin Chandra Mohantha who was childless. It was asserted in the written statement that one Taheruddin who flashed his greedy eyes over the suit land and consequently at his instance a Certificate Case being No. 188 of 1964-65 was initiated for realization of arrear rent in respect of suit land and in the said proceeding no notice was served upon Abdul Hashem as contemplated under section 7 of the Public Demand Recovery Act and eventually Taheruddin purchased the suit land on 23.10.1964 in the auction held in respect of the aforesaid certificate case. Thereafter Sachindra Mohantha, Rosomoy along with Abdul Hashem filed a joint application giving rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 1973-74 with a prayer for setting aside the aforesaid sale and in the said Miscellaneous proceeding 2 of 1973-74 the Certificate Officer having heard both sides, allowed the same by his order dated 30.02.1974 setting aside the sale in auction held on 29.10.1964 in Certificate Case No. 188 of 1964-65 as a result the kabalas in favour of Rosomoy Chandra Mahantha and subsequent kabala in favour of Abdul Hashem executed by Rosomoy remained valid and effective consequently Abdul Hashem having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land sold .15 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 18.11.74 appertaining to S.S. plot No. 2007 as also .48 acres of land appertaining to S.S. plot No. 2088 totaling .63 acres of land out of the suit land in favour of defendant No. 1 Chand Miah. Said Abul Hashern also sold .15 acres of land out of S.S. plot No. 2007 and .48 acres out of 2088 total .63 acres of land in favour of defendant No. 2 Raja Miah by a Registered kabala dated 02.12.1974.

5. In the process aforesaid the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered into possession of the entire suit land in exercise or their right and title they also got their names mutated in respect of the record of right. It is also asserted in the written statement that in view of setting aside of the sale in auction in the Certificate Case as aforesaid the registered sale deed in favour of Taheruddin in the Certificate Case was rendered invalid, therefore, subsequent purchases as claimed in the plaint from Taheruddin were also rendered invalid consequently they did not acquire any right, title, possession and interest in respect of their alleged purchased land. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are residents of London, therefore, they appointed one Manik Miah as their attorney empowering him to sell the suit land. The answering defendant Nos. 4-6 purchased the suit land from appointed attorney of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered kabala dated 22.05.98 at a consideration of Tk. 50,000/00 and after such purchase they have been in possession of the suit land in exercise of their right title and interest.

It was also asserted in the written statement that the plaintiff though admitted that Rosomoy Chandra Nath was the owner of the land yet he was not impleaded as a party in the certificate case, therefore, no notice was served upon him in the said certificate proceeding and that the plaintiff brought the suit with false allegation as such same is liable to be dismissed with costs.

6. Having taken up the suit for hearing the learned Joint District Judge framed as many as 6(six) issues including one to the effect as to whether the kabalas dated 18.11.1974 and 02.12.1974 are forged, fabricated and sham paper transaction or not.

7. In the suit the plaintiff examined 10(ten) witnesses while the defendants adduced 8(eight) witnesses in support of their case and upon conclusion of the trial the learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit in part declaring right title of the plaintiff in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession. It may 4G be mentioned that no decree was granted for setting aside the kabala as prayed for, by the learned Joint District Judge in his judgment and decree dated 28.03.2000 passed in Title Suit No. 43 of 1999.

8. Having felt aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree in part passed by the learned Joint District Judge the added defendant Nos. 4-6 as appellants preferred this appeal.

9. Mr. Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants along with Mr. Surojit Bhattacharjee submits at the out set that the learned Joint District Judge having found that the plaintiff failed to prove their case in respect of allegation of forgery or fabrication of the document, did not pass any decree in favour of the plaintiff to that effect but the suit was decreed on a ground which is expressly extraneous to the proceeding.

10. Elaborating his submissions Mr. Mondal has pointed out that nowhere in the four corners of the plaint the plaintiff pleaded acquisition of title by adverse possession in the suit land, therefore, no evidence was lead to that effect but the learned District Judge decreed the suit declaring title of the plaintiff by adverse possession. As a matter of fact the question of adverse possession was neither pleaded nor proved by the plaintiff; therefore, part decree granted by the impugned judgment is nothing but a gratuitous decree which is not permissible.

In support of his submission the learned Advocate for the appellant placed reliance in the case of Mahaprabhu Ram Vs. Gopal Ram Ram and others reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154.

11. Mr. Mondal submits further that in view of setting aside of the sale in auction, purchase of the suit land by Taheruddin in the certificate proceeding having been rendered invalid the subsequent purchase deeds on the basis thereof don't create and right title interest or possession in the suit land by virtue of their successive kabalas originating from Taheruddin, therefore, the plaintiff had acquired no right title interest or possession in the suit land consequently the decree in his favour as granted by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge is liable to be set aside.

Referring to the evidence on record Mr. Mondal submits that the plaintiff utterly failed in substantiating his claim that the kabala dated 18.11.1974 and 2.12.74 are either forged or fabricated or sham paper transaction. Therefore, question of decree in favour of the plaintiff as claimed does not arise at all. On the contrary, the evidence adduced by the defendants in support of their case employ prove that they have indeed acquired right title interest and possession in the suit land, therefore, the suit ought to have been dismissed as a whole.

12. Mr. Fazlul Hoq the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. M.C. Chowdhury, submits that the evidence adduced by the plaintiff and the documents produced before the court if considered in their proper perspective warrant a decree in the suit not in part but as a whole.

Elaborating his submission the learned Advocate has pointed out that the act of setting aside the sale in auction having been done by the Circle Officer of the concerned Upazilla in the year 1974 it was without jurisdiction. Referring to the provisions of Section 3(3) of Public Demand Recovery Act the learned Advocate for the respondents submits that at the relevant time it was the Sub-divisional Officer who were engaged as Certificate Officer and any order setting aside such sale ought to have been made by the Sub-divisional Officer alone and nor the Circle Officer as in the instant case. Referring to Section 22 and 23 of the Public Demand Recovery Act the learned Advocate for the respondents submits that at the time of initiation of the proceeding for cancellation of sale the appellant ought to have paid entire arrear rent in respect of the suit land otherwise the said application ought not to have been entertained even but in the instant case the defendant did not submit a scrap of paper to substantiate the position that in fact they had ever paid arrear of rent as contemplated under Section 23 of the Public demand Recovery Act, therefore, cancellation of sale in auction in favour of Abdul Bari was a nullity, therefore, the defendant did not acquire any right title interest in the suit land rather it is the plaintiff who had indeed acquired the same in respect of the suit land, therefore, the learned Joint District Judge ought to have decreed the suit as a whole.

The learned Advocate for the respondents referring to section 23 of the Public Demand Recovery Act submits that any proceeding for setting aside a sale ought to have been initiated within 60(sixty) days from the date of sale but in the instant case it is about 10(ten) years after the proceeding had been initiated and in consequence thereof the sale was set aside by the Circle Officer in utter dis-regard to the provision of law, therefore, the same is not sustainable. The trial Court ought to have noticed this aspect of the case in refusing the decree in part.

13. With a view to appreciate the submissions made by the learned Advocate from both sides we have to consider the evidence to evaluate the extent to which each of the parties has proved his respective case and in doing so we find plaintiff PW.1 Fazal Ahmed deposed that the suit land originally belonged to Mohendra Chandra Mahanta and Mohananda Mohantha who owned and possessed the same by inheritances and subsequently for arrear of rent Certificate Case NO. 188 of 1964-65 was initiated and after conclusion of the said case the suit land was put to auction whereupon Taheruddin purchased the same land in auction held on 29.10.64 and subsequently certificate was issued in favour of Taheruddin on 21.01.65. Accordingly, possession was handed over in his favour and thereafter by successive devolutions on transfer by registered deeds one Ershad Ali purchased the suit land by a registered kabala dated 01.06.1966 and thereafter the suit land was also transferred from time to time from one man to another and ultimately to one Moklesh Miah who transferred the same in favour of the plaintiff and one Akbor Ali in equal share by a registered kabala in the year 1992. Thereafter Akbor Ali sold his part of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by two registered kabalas in the year 1996 one in the month of May and other one in December. This PW.1 produced all relevant documents of transfer which have been marked as Ext. 1(Ka), Ext. 1 (Kha), Ext. 1(Ga), Ext. 1(Gha), Ext. 1(Uma), Ext. 2, Ext. 3, Ext. 4, Ext. 5, Ext. 6, Ext. 7, Ext. 8, Ext. 9(Ka), Ext. 9(Kha) and Ext. 5(Ka). The aforesaid Exts. also include the mutation khatian, the application for mutation, order passed in the Mutation Case, rent receipt, information slip showing that the auction was not set aside etc.

During cross-examination this witness admitted that the khatian in respect of which mutation was made by the plaintiff was in the name of Chand Miah and Raza Miah. This witness also admitted that he did not obtain any paper of the auction proceeding. This witness also denied that Sachin Chandra Mondal, Rosomoy and Abul Hashem jointly prayed for setting aside the auction sale. This witness also denied the suggestion that on 13.02.74 the auction sale was set aside. This witness also denied the suggestion that Taheruddin did not get possession by virtue of his auction purchase. This witness admitted that in the objection filed by the defendant Nos. 4-6 in the temporary injunction matter it was claimed that defendant. Nos. 4-6 purchased the suit land from Manik Miah.

14. PW.2 Akbor Ali deposed as a plaintiff in the suit. He also admits that Mohendra and Molananda were the original owners of the suit land. This witness also deposed in the same way as that of PW. 1 about the successive devolutions on transfer as well as on gift. This witness also claimed possession in the suit land by the plaintiff and he denies possession by the defendant's sides.

During cross-examination this witness admitted that he has not seen the papers relating to auction sale. This witness also denied the suggestion that the deed of transfer from Taheruddin on wards are sham paper transaction. This witness also asserted that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 got their names mutated on the basis of a forged deed.

15. PW. 3 Masuk Miah deposed that he knows Rosomoy Chandra Nath and his brother Lakhon who transferred some land to his maternal uncle and the said land was gifted in his favour by his maternal uncle by a registered deed bearing registration No. 8693 of the 1989. The said registered deed has been produced. The photo copy of the said document has been produced and marked as Ext. Cha (with objection).

During cross-examination he admitted that Rosomoy had left for India.

16. PW. 4 Sree Lakhon Debnath son of late Ramananda Nath who deposed that his younger brother Rosomoy purchased the suit land from Mohendra and Mahananda Mohantha and after 1-2 years of such purchase Rosomoy left for India. Thereafter he had been in possession of the suit and during war of liberation he also left for India and on returning back he found Ershad Ali was in possession of the suit land who claims to have purchased the same in auction and his brother Rosomoy did not return back in this country. This witness also claims that Rosomoy left the document of his purchase to this witness Lakhon Deb Nath and on request this witness handed over the original document to Abul Hashem for the purpose of setting aside the auction sale and the said document was not returned back to him thereafter. This witness also testifies possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. This witness also admits that he did not go for any salish when Abul Hashern did not return back the documents. He does not know whether Rosomoy sold the suit land to Abul Hashem and there was no known person present when the document was handed over to Hashem. This witness denied the suggestion that he testifies falsely on payment. This witness expressed his ignorance about the setting aside of the auction sale. This witness denied the suggestion that Abul Hashem, Rosomoy and Sachin Chandra jointly filed an application for setting aside the auction sale. This witness denied the suggestion that he was deposing in the court being unduly influenced by Fazal Ahmed (plaintiff).

17. PW.5 Sachin Chandra Mohantha deposed to the effect that the suit land originally belonged to his father Mohendra and his uncle Mohananda. He also testifies that Rosomoy Nath was the younger brother of Lokhon Chandra and one Taheruddin purchased the suit land in auction and that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit land who possess the same through Akbor Ali. He also admitted that he has no claim in the suit land.

During cross-examination this witness disclosed that he read upto primary level. This witness denied the suggestion that he along with Rosomoy and Abul Hashem filed a joint application for setting aside the sale. This witness also denied the suggestion that in 1974 auction sale was set aside. This witness also admitted in his cross-examination that he got himself acquainted with Fazal Ahmed (plaintiff) in course of admission of his daughter in the school. This witness also denied the suggestion that he is deposing falsely in the case upon being unduly influenced by Fazal Ahmed (plaintiff).

18. PW.6 is one Md. Osman Miah. This witness deposed that Mokles Miah being in possession, transferred the suit land in favour of Akbor Ali and Fazal Miah and the plaintiff Fazal Miah has been in possession of the suit land now he is the owner and Akbor Ali became a borgader. This witness also disclosed that he does not know whether Abdul Hashem ever purchased the suit land and he does not know defendant Nos. 4-6 have been possessing the suit land. He also denied that he is a tutored witness.

19. PW.7 is one Abdur Rahman who testifies that he knows the suit land from 25 years before and at that time Masuk Miah was the owner of the suit land. Thereafter, Masuk Miah transferred to Akbor Ali and Fazal Miah and he did never see Adbul Hashem ever possess the suit land. This witness during cross-examination admitted that he lives in a place 1/4 mile away from the suit land and he learnt from Moklesh Mia and Akbor Ali that Muklesh Miah was in possession of the suit land. This witness also admitted that Akbor Ali is his uncle but he denies the suggestion that he is a tutored witness and that Abdul Hashem is in possession of the suit land.

20. PW.8 Mozahid Ali deposed that he purchased the suit land from Ershad Ali in the name of his wife Raisa Bibi on 07.04.75 and he used to possess the suit land through Akbor Ali. Thereafter Raisa Bibi sold the suit land to Tulai Bibi mother of Muklish Miah.

During cross-examination this witness admitted that he possessed the suit land from Ershad Ali in 1975. This witness expressed his ignorance as to whether auction sale was set aside after his purchase. He also denied the suggestion that Ershad Ali was not in possession after his purchased. He also denied the suggestion that he did not ever get possession of the suit land. This witness also denied the suggestion that he is in the habit of purchasing disputed lands.

21. PW.9 Taher Ali deposed to the effect that Akbor Ali has been in possession of the suit land for 20/22 years and he possess one part and bagadar on the other part and none else except Akbor Ali in possession of the suit land.

During cross-examination this witness deposed that he lives in a place ¼th mile away from the suit land. This witness also admits in his cross-examination that Fazal Miah asked him to depose in the case. He also denied the suggestion that he is a tutored witness. He expressed his ignorance as to whether Taheruddin purchased the suit land in auction.

22. PW.10 Denesh Chandra Debnath also deposed that Akbor Ali is in possession of the suit land Fazal Miah posted piller in the suit land and non else except Akbor Ali, Fazal Miah was found by him to be in possession. This witness during cross-examination admits that he lives in a place one kilometer away from the suit land and he does not know the plot number of his own land and he knows no plot number either. In cross-examination this witness admits that he does not know which land is covered by piller posted by Fazal Mia and he does not know from whom Akbor Ali purchased the suit land. He also does not know who are the others in possession of the suit land from his boyhood. This witness also denied the suggestion that he had no land contagious to the suit land and he does not know the suit land.

23. Defendant No. 4 figured as witness No. 1 for the defendants who deposed that defendants 5-6 are his co-sharers who filed written statement jointly upon being added as defendants and he is deposing on behalf of defendants 5-6 as well. He also testifies that Mohendra and Mohananda were the original owners of the suit land who having been in possession thereof sold the same in favour of Rosomoy by registered kabala dated 11.06.1960, thereafter Rosomoy Nath sold the suit land to Abdul Hashem by registered kabala. He also deposed that Sachindra son of Mohendra became the Sole heir of two Mohanthas. This witness also testifies that after purchase by Abdul Hashem it was detected that Taheruddin once purchased the suit land in auction though no notice either upon Rosomoy or Abdul Hashem was ever served, record of right was in favour of Mohendra and Mohantha and on the basis of such record of right certificate case was proceeded and the auction took place. It was also deposed that Abdul Hashem, Rosomoy and Sachindra jointly initiated Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 for setting aside the auction sale on the basis whereof, on 13.02.74 the auction sale was set aside. This witness also produced the certified copy of the order dated 13.02.74 passed in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 and marked as Ext. Ka. This witness produced the certified copy of the application for setting aside the sale which has been marked as Ext. Kha. This witness testifies further that after setting aside the auction sale the subsequent title on purchase were rendered invalid, therefore, title of purchasers have extinguished and upon setting aside the action sale Abdul Hashem entered into possession of the suit land. Thereafter, Abdul Hashem sold the same in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered kabla in the year 1974. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 has been residing in London. Defendant No. 3 is the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who is also a resident of London. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 executed a power of attorney for transfer of the suit land in favour of Manik Miah, the plaintiff wanted to purchase the suit land but he was not agreeable to pay the market price so he failed, therefore, Manik Miah sold the said land in favour of defendant Nos. 4-6 by a registered kabala dated 22.05.1988. This said document has been produced in the court and marked as Ext. Ga (with objection). This witness also testifies that he had purchased the suit land at a consideration of Tk. 5(five) lacs. The original deed of transfer was in custody of the seller so he handed over to the defendant Nos. 4-6 which has been produced before the court and marked as Ext. Ga-1. The registered sale deed dated 30.03.1973 executed by Rosomoy in favour of Abul Hashem has also been produced before the court and marked as Ext. Ga-2. Thereafter Abul Hashem sold a part of the suit land in favour of defendant No. 1 by a registered kabala dated 18.11.1974 which has been produced and marked as Ext. Ga-3. The said Abdul Hashem also sold other part of the suit land in favour of defendant No. 2 by a registered kabala dated 01.12.74 which has been produced and marked as Ext. Ga-4 after purchase the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 Chand Miah and Raja Miah got their names mutated in respect of the suit land being suit plot Nos. 2007 and 2088. This witness also produced the rent receipt evidencing payment of rent. This witness also testifies that the document in favour of the plaintiffs are collusive paper transaction which were never acted upon.

During cross-examination this witness admitted that he reside in a place eight miles away from the suit land while defendant No. 5 Imran Ahmed is a resident of a place 15-16 miles away. The defendant No. 6 Ashis Kapali reside at 3 miles away from the suit land and he had seen the suit land for the first time one or two months before the date of their purchase, and they had no knowledge about the same earlier. This witness also disclosed that he had no knowledge, about the case prior to his purchase. This witness also admitted that Akbor Ali is a resident of a place situated near to the suit land. This witness also disclose that Abdul Hashem is no more. This witness also claims that the information slip filed by the plaintiff is a collusive paper. This witness also admitted in his cross-examination that record of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 has not been called for. This witness denied the suggestion that there was no case initiated for cancellation of the auction sale. This witness also denied the suggestion that their document of purchase is forged one. This witness expressed his ignorance as to whether any heirs of Abdul Hashem is alive. This witness testifies that the document by which the suit land was purchased from Mohendra and Mohantha, was handed over to Manik Miah who handed over the same to this witness. This witness denied the suggestion that Abdul Hashem obtained the custody of the said document by practicing fraud.

24. D.W.2 Manik Miah deposed to the effect that he knows the plaintiff and the defendants as well as the suit land. This witness testifies that he purchased the suit land on behalf of Raja Miah and Chand Miah defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are his cousins by maternal uncle. This witness also produced the power of attorney executed in his favour by Chand Miah and Raja Miah defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The said power of attorney was produced before the court as Ext. Gha. This witness also deposed that the plaintiff also wanted to purchase the suit land at a lesser price, therefore, land was sold to defendant Nos. 4- 6 at a consideration of Tk. 5 (five) lacs. This witness is the executants of the deed of transfer in favour of defendant Nos. 4-6 and also handed over possession. It is also deposed by this witness that defendant Nos. 4-6 has been in possession of the suit land after their purchase.

During cross-examination this witness admitted that he reside at a place three miles away to the east of the suit land. This witness however could not disclose the boundary of the suit land. This witness denied the suggestion that there was no transfer or handing over possession of the suit land by him as alleged and that no consideration was passed.

25. D.W.3 Khalendra Chandra Nath is a witness residing at a distance of 500 yards from the suit land who testifies possession of the suit land by Abdul Hashem. He also testifies possession by Rosomoy prior to the transfer of the suit land in favour of Abdul Hashem. This witness also testifies that Manik purchased the suit land on behalf of Chand Miah and Raja Miah.

During cross-examination this witness reiterated possession of the suit land by Rosomoy and Manik Miah. This witness deified the suggestion that he was deposing upon being unduly influenced.

26. D.W.4 Kutubuddin is a deed writer of the deed in favour of Nazir Ahmed and others by Chand Miah and others who testifies that the attorney of Chand Miah is also executants of the deed and consideration was Tk. 5(five) lacs. He also testifies that it is a genuine deed. He knows Nazir Ahmed, Azad and others. This witness also testifies during cross-examination that he witnessed passing of the consideration between the vendor and vendees and that the money was paid on half of Nazir Ahmed and others. This witness also testifies that the executants used the pen belonging to this witness D.W.4.

27. D.W.5 Md. Sultran Miah is also another deed writer of the registered deed dated 30.03.1973 executed by Rosomoy Nath in favour of Abdul Hashem. He also disclosed that Rosomoy came to his office for the purpose of writing the said deeds. Thereafter, Rosomoy put his signature in his presence upon receipt of the consideration money. This witness also put his signature as a deed writer. This witness also disclosed during cross-examination that he used to know both Rosomoy and Abdul Hashem and that the consideration of Tk. 5(five) lacs was received by the executants from the purchaser in his presence.

28. D.W.6 is Suruj Ali who is the resident of a place situated at a distance of 700 cubits from the suit land, who disposed in the same line as that of defendant No. 1 in respect of transfer from the original owners namely Mohonathas. He is a resident of the same locality where Rosomoy, Abdul Hashem, Mohnandha used to live. He also testifies possession of the suit land by Abdul Hashem as also by Rosomoy and Chand Miah through Manik Miah. He also testifies that he did not see possession of the suit land by Taheruddin, Ershad Ali, Fazal Ahmed and Akbor AIL This witness specially disclosed the boundaries of the suit land. This witness denied the suggestion that he was deposing falsely.

29. D.W.7 is one Shamim Ahmed who testifies that he is a attesting witness of Ext.Ga the registered deed dated 22.06.98 in favour of Ashis Kapali and two others executed by Manik Miah. He knows the suit land situated at a distance 1/4th miles from his house. He also testifies that the purchasers are in possession of the suit land but also disclosed in his cross-examination that the purchases were not known to him from before but it is Manik Miah who got himself acquainted with them. He also specifically mentioned the boundary men of the suit land. He denied the suggestion that he was deposing being unduly influenced.

30. D.W.8. is Taheruddin the auctioned purchaser of the suit land from whom the plaintiff claims to have purchased the suit land by way of successive devolution on transfer, deposed to the effect that he knows the plaintiff Fazal Ahmed, Nazir Ahmed, the defendants and the suit land. He also testifies that he had purchased the suit land in auction held in the auctioned Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 and his purchase took place on 29.10.64, he received possession through papers and as a matter of fact he did not get possession of the suit land physically. He also disposed that he sold the suit land in favor of Ershad Ali. Thereafter he received the notice for correction of record of rights in the year 1973 but he did not turn up on receipt of the said notice, this witness also testifies that he was informed about the setting aside of the auction sale in the year 1974. Thereafter he did not take care of the suit land.

During cross-examination this witness disclosed that he used to know Ershad Ali from before but he did not go to the suit land physically and eight years after his purchase. Ershad Ali informed this witness about the setting aside of the auction sale. This witness denied the suggestion that he was deposing being unduly influenced.

31. These are all about the deposition of the witnesses in a nutshell wherefrom it transpires that the plaintiff in this suit claims their title and possession over the suit land from Taheruddin D.W.8 the auctioned purchaser thereof held in Certified Case No. 1 88/64-65 on 20.10.1964.

32. On the other hand, the defendants are claiming their title and possession in the suit land from Rosomoy Chandra Nath who also got the auction sale set aside in Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 and thereafter by successive transfer the answering defendant Nos. 4-6 are claiming their title and possession in the suit land who are as a matter of fact the appellants in this appeal.

33. From the materials placed before us and on consideration of evidence on record including the Exts. We find that the plaintiffs made desperate attempts to show that the action sale in favour of Taheruddin in connection with Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 was never set aside, therefore, they produced three information slip which have been marked as Ext. 9, Ext.9 (Ka) and 9(Kha). On a perusal of these Exts. we find that the Assistant Commissioner of Land (A.0 Land) Sardar Sylhet in his information slip issued on 01.07.1998 disclosed that Miscellaneous Cases, in the year 1973-74 used to have been filed before the R.D.C. Sylhet, therefore, no further information could be detected by this information slip which is Ext.9. The other information slip issued by A.D.C. (Rev.) Sylhet shows that a question put to them as to whether the records of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 were available in the said office or not. The answer was given by the officer as "1". This information slip obtained by the plaintiff and marked as Ext. 9 (Ka) is dated 09.08.98. It may be mentioned that we have already noticed from Ext.9 the information slip dated 01.07.98. That the record of the said Miscellaneous Case was available with the office of the R.D.0 not with the A.D.C. (Rev). The other information slip which is marked as Ext. 9(Kha) is dated 24.10.1988 obtained from the Officer-in-charge. Collectorate, Sylhet singed by the A.C. (Land) disclosing to the effect that in his office the record of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 is not available. Banking upon these exts. the plaintiffs made an attempt to show that the very proceeding in Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 is non existent, therefore, the question of cancellation of sale in favour of Taheruddin does not arise but in appreciation of the aforesaid position disclosed by the plaintiffs we feel inclined to take notice of two Exts. marked as Ext. Ka and Kha.
