full_judgment:
Mr. A. N. M. Bashir Ullah, J:- This Rule on an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) at the instance of the defendants-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 11.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge. 2" Court, Sherpur in Title Appeal No.106 of 2004 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.09.2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Nokia in Other Class Suit No.01 of 2003 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the opposite party no. 1 Most. Nazma Begum as plaintiff instituted the above number title suit in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Nokia, Sherpur for recovery of the schedule land of the plot removing the structure thereon contending, inter-alia, that the suit land along with some other lands of mouza Kaida and Bazardi of hal Police Station Nokla former Nalitabari originally belonged to Kosor Maraud Parai, the father of the plaintiff who gifted 5.47 acres of land by a deed of Hebabill ewaz on 22.02.1972 and registered on 13.07.1972 to his 5 daughters including the plaintiff. 

3. By an amicable arrangement amongst the 5 sisters. The plaintiff got 1.10 acres of land through the said Hebabil ewaz. The plaintiff erected a house in the land of plot No.50 of settlement khatian no.I 08 and while she was living with her mother in the said house and she got married with her husband. 

4. The plaintiff engaged Abdus Samad Parai father of the defendant Nos.1-4 and predecessor of defendant Nos.5-7 the cousin for borga cultivation of .95 acres of land. In the month of Choitra, 1389 B.S the husband of the plaintiff has been serving in the Army of Bangladesh. Thus, the plaintiff himself was looking after the lands. When the plaintiff came to look after her lands, the defendant Nos.1-4 the predecessor of defendant Nos.5-8 Md. Abdus Samad Parai fraudulently created a Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 in the name of defendant Nos.1- 4 and Hafizul Haque predecessor of defendant Nos.5-8 and the defendant disclosing that the said Hebabil ewaz denied to make payment of the crops to the plaintiff. 

5. The plaintiff under the prevailing circumstances filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Nokia against defendant nos.l-8 and Abdus Samad Parai and the said suit was decreed on contest on 26.04.1986 and against the said judgment and decree the defendants filed Title Appeal no. 63 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge, Jamalpur. Later on, the appeal was transferred in the Court of District Judge, Sherpur and was renumbered as Title Appeal no. 10 of 1988. During the pendency of the appeal Hafizul Haque the predecessor of defendant nos. 5-8 died as appellant no.2. As such, the appellate Court belw passed an abatement order on 05.04.1989. The defendant nos. 1-4 and the heirs of Hafizul Haque filed Miscellaneous Case no. 9 of 1980 under Order 9 Rule 4 of the Code for setting aside the abatement order but the said proceeding was dismissed on contest on 07.05.1999 and as against the said order the defendants filed Civil Revision no. 1839 of 1990 in the High Court Division. The High Court Division making the Rule absolute in the said revision by its judgment and order dated 03.11.1997 set aside the abatement order dated 07.05.1999 with a direction to rehear the Miscellaneous Case No.16 of 1989 for setting aside the abatement order and during the pendency of the said miscellaneous case in the Joint District Judge, I" Court, Sherpur, but the said miscellaneous case was dismissed for default on 27.01.2000. Thereafter, the appellate Court sent the record of the suit to the Court of Assistant Judge, Nokia, Sherpur and on a prayer dated 13.04.2000 filed by the plaintiff of that suit, the Court by its order dated 05.07.2000 sent the order of the Court to the concerned Sub-Registry Office to record the order of cancellation of the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983. 

6. When the plaintiff was taking preparation for getting the land back, the defendant Nos.1-8 dispossessed the plaintiff erecting tin shed and wooden house in the suit land on 27.08.2000. The plaintiff having been tried to resist them failed. When the Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 and the subsequent proceedings arose out of the said suit were pending in the Courts for verdict, the defendants in order to create some cumbersome on the title of the plaintiff created as many as 8 deeds but all those deeds are collusive, fraudulent, motivated and illegal, hence the suit. 

7. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos.l-4 who filing written statement denying the materials allegation made in the plaint. The case of the defendants are, in short, is that the plaintiff is out of possession from the date of execution of Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 and from then the plaintiff is nobody for the suit land. Thus the plaintiff has filed the present suit after 19 years 2 months and 7 days. The defendants have acquired title by adverse possession from 23.10.1983. Since the plaintiff is out of possession from 1983 the suit is not maintainable at her instance. The plaintiff is a shrewd and cunning woman who at the instance of others have filed the suit for illegal gain. Abdus Samad Parai the predecessor of the defendant was a man of choice and solvate. He did not plough his own land and borga cultivate the land of others. He did not also borga cultivate the land of the plaintiff. The vexatious suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

8. Upon the above pleadings, the trial Court framed as many as 6 issues to dispose of the suit. They examined 3 witnesses while the defendant examined 3 witnesses and both the parties filed some documentary evidences which were duly marked as exhibits in the suit. The trial Court upon considering of the evidence on record dismissed the suit that the suit is barred by limitation and as against the said judgment the plaintiff preferred title appeal in the appellate Court below and the said Court after hearing both the parties allowed the appeal holding that the suit is not barred by limitation and thereupon he decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. The defendant-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said impugned judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam Mehedi with Mr. Md. Abul Bashar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners supports the Rule and he sought to impeach the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below on the following four fold arguments.

10. Firstly, he submits that the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation as the plaintiff was ousted from the suit land on 23.10.1983 when she executed the Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants. Thereupon she could not come back into the possession of the suit land and the plaintiff filed the suit on 02.01.2003 that is almost after 19 years 3 months and 7 days of her dispossession. So, the defendants have acquired good title into the suit land by their such adverse possession and since the plaintiff could not file the suit within 12 years from her dispossession in 1983 as prescribed in Article 144 of the Code, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation under section 28 of the Limitation Act. But the appellate Court below without appreciating this fact and circumstances wrongly came to a conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation. He also submits that the plaint itself discloses the fact that after the disposal of the former Other Class Suit no. 26 of 1985 the plaintiff was taking steps for getting the land back from the defendants and this fact reveals the dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land. He also submits that the date of dispossession as ventilated in the plaint on 27.08.2000 is an imaginary date which has been introduced for creating a cause of action for the present suit. Since the suit was not filed within 12 years from the date of dispossession, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree and relief in the suit. 

11. Secondly, he submits that the plaintiff has been claiming the suit land relying on the deed of gift dated 22.02.1972 reportedly executed by her father. But all the lands of the said deed of gift is situated within the Nokia Police Station but the said deed of gift was executed and registered at Mymensingh Sadar Sub-Registry Office. So, no title was passed in favour of the plaintiff through the said Hebabil ewaz as such the plaintiff did not acquired title into the suit land. 

12. Thirdly, he also submits that the correct identity of the land has not been given in the plaint though there appears some khatian nos. and plot nos. as to the description of the land but there is nothing in the record to show that which survey attract the said khatian and plot nos. So, this type of identity is vague and indefinite and upon relying such vague and indefinite identity of land there is a. little scope for giving possession to anybody else. 

13. Fourthly and lastly he submits that the plaintiff has filed the suit for recovery of khas possession for an area of .90 acres of land as described in the schedule of the plaint. In the first schedule, there is a description of .30 acre of land from plot No.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. But the deed of gift dated 22.02.1972 will go to show that the father of the plaintiff gifted only .20 acres of land to his 5 daughters from the land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10. So, the plaintiff cannot claim .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and the Court will not a pa'ss decree for the land where apparently the plaintiff has no right, title and possession. Thus, he referring the above points and arguments submits that the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit holding that the suit was barred by limitation. But the appellate Court below on some erroneous view came to a wrong finding and conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation. So, the judgment of the appellate Court below is liable to be set aside restraining that of the judgment passed by the trial Court. 

14. On the other hand, Mr. M. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party no.1 opposing the Rule submits that the suit is not barred by limitation and the defendants did not acquire title into the suit land by adverse possession. He categorically submits that the defendants were claiming their possession into the suit land from 1983 relying, on the fraudulent and collusive Hebabl ewaz dated 23.10.1983. But the said Hebabil ewaz have been declared illegal by the trial Court in Other Class Suit no. 26 of 1985 and the said judgment was upheld and confirmed in that Title Appeal being no. 63 of 1986 and the said proceeding continued till 05.07.2000 and the trial Court and the appellate Court in that suit found the possession of the plaintiff into the suit land whereupon the Hebabil ewaz reportedly executed by the plaintiff in favour of the defendants was cancelled and the same was also noted in the volume of the deed. So, for any view of the matter the defendants cannot claim their possession into the suit land from 1983 to 2000 and the very claiming of the possession of the defendants in to the suit land during this period that is 1983 to 2000 is against the law as their possession has not been found in the former suit. 

15. He also submits that the defendants ousted the plaintiff from the suit land on 27.08.2000 erecting some houses on the suit land with the notice of all concerned and this type of hostile and notorious position can only be the counted as the date of beginning of adverse possession. So, from the date of dispossession of the plaintiff on 27.08.2000, the suit has been filed within 12 years as prescribed in Article 144 of the Limitation Act. So, in computing the time it will be resulted that the suit has not been filed within 3-years from the dispossession of the plaintiff. So, the suit is not hit under Section 28 and Article 144 of the Limitation Act. 

16. He next submits that the defendants-plaintiff at this stage raised question as to the registration of the deed of gift by the father of the plaintiff in 1972 in the District Sub-Registry Office, Mymensingh. But this fact was not raised in the Court below. As such, the plaintiff could not show any evidence of this point. Since this is a purely question of fact as to whether the District Registrar, Mymensingh had the jurisdiction to entertain such a deed of a police station under that district cannot ascertain at this moment. More so, the plaintiff acquired title into the suit land through the deed of gift by her father in the year 1972 and the defendant admitting the title of the plaintiff in to the suit land created Hebabil ewaz on 23.10.1983. So, at this stage of the proceeding the defendants cannot deny the title of the plaintiff on the strength of the deed of gift in 1972. In fact, the defendants in order to take some undue advantage have been using this point only. 

17. He also submits that it is not comet to say that the identity of the survey related with the khatian and plot numbers of the suit land have not been given in the plaint. He referring the plaint submits that the khatian and plot numbers are related with the settlement khatian. In this connection he also submits that when the first record of right was started under the provision of Bengal Tenancy Act in some of the area of our country. The first record of right is known as C.S record of right, that is, Cadstale Survey and in some district the same survey is known as settlement khatian. In the area of Mymensingh the first survey is know as settlement khatian and the same has been given in the pleadings. He candidly admits that it is fact that in the schedule of the plaint there is no identity of the survey and the same should have been there and if it would have been their, their would have no scope to create any confusion and unwanted debit on this fact. 

18. He also submits that in the record of right there appears no name of the concerned survey. After C.S. record of right in many area of our country revisional survey, that is, R.S. record of right and after coming operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the S.A record of right has been prepared but in no record of right, the name of the survey has been articulated by the authority. So, it is not a ground for disbelieving the case of the plaintiff. 

19. He also submits that it is fact that the father of the plaintiff had gifted .20 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida but the plaintiff has been claiming .30 acres of land from the said plot number. In this connection he argued that the defendants are nobody but the co-sharers of the plaintiff, thus the by an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers has been possessing .30 acres of land from the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and since from the said particular land the plaintiff was ousted by the defendants, the same has been included in the schedule of the plaint.

20. In his concluding submission he submits that the appellate Court below did not commit any error of law rather considering the pros and cons of the suit decreed the suit rightly. So the decree passed by the appellate Court below should not be interfered by this Court. The appellate Court below of the right assessment of the evidence, fact and low involved there to rightly found that the suit is not barred by limitation and decreed the suit accordingly. So, the rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

21. I have considered the above submissions and arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

22. On going to the materials on record it appears that amongst the questions of limitation is the burning question in the suit. Most of the arguments of the learned Advocate for the petitioners are convergent to the fact of limitation. The plaintiff has asserted in the suit that on 27.08.2000 the defendants erecting tin shed and wooden house in the suit land dispossessed her. On the other hand, the plain case of the defendants is that from 1983 when the plaintiff executed Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants on 23.10.1983 for the suit land defendants have been possessing the suit land on the strength of the said Hebabil ewaz and from then the plaintiff is out of possession. 

23. From the materials on record it appears that this plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 in the competent civil Court for declaration that the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 allegedly executed by the plaintiff in favour of Abdus Samad Parai has not been executed by her and the said suit was decreed on contest and the said judgment was alleged in an appeal being Title Appeal no.63 of 1986, later on the same was re-numbered as Title Appeal no.10 of 1988 but the appeal was abated on 05.04.1989 and a Miscellaneous Case being No.I6 of 1989 under Order 22 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the abatement order was tiled. But the said miscellaneous case was dismissed on contest on 07.05.1990. Against that order the defendants preferred Civil Revision being no.1839 of 1990 in the High Court Division and the Rule was made absolute on 03.11.1997 restoring the Miscellaneous Case no.16 of 1989 for rehearing. But after restoration of the said miscellaneous case the same was again dismissed on 27.01.2000. Thereafter, the defendants did not take any further step and ultimately the decree passed in Other Suit no.26 of 1985 remain intact till now. 

24. The defendants have been claiming heavily that the plaintiff has been dispossessed from the suit land on 23.10.1983 when she executed the Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants. Now, the question before me whether if for the sake of argument it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiff was dispossessed on 23.10.1983 whether this sought of dispossession can be considered as adverse possession of the defendants. 
25. Now, let us have a look-what is adverse possession in the eye of law. In the case of Secretary of State for India vs Devendra Lal Khan reported in 61 I A.78=38 C W N.. 285, the Privy Council laid down what constitutes adverse possession and observed in the following ways: "As to what constitutes adverse possession, a subject which formed the topic of some discussion in the case, their Lordships adopt the language of Lord Robertson in delivering the judgment of the Board in Radhamoni Devi Vs Collector of Khulna" (27 I.A. 136), where his Lordship said that the possession required must be adequate in continuity, in publicity and in extent to show that it is possession adverse to the competitor . It is sufficient that the possession should be overt and without any attempt at concealment so that the person against whom time is running ought, if he exercises due vigilance, to be aware of what is happening." 

26. The jest of the adverse possession as observed by the Privy Council is that the possession must be continuous having knowledge to others and it must have an expose against the real owner. In my consideration, the written statement of the defendants and their claim of possession in to the suit land from 1983 through the deed of Hebabil ewaz allegedly executed by the plaintiff is sufficient to hold that the possession of the defendants from 1983 is not any adverse possession at all rater the possession that have been claimed by the defendant themselves is based on the so-called deed of gift and this sort of possession can never be adverse possession against the real owner. 

27. Adverse possession is something as described by the Privy Council that it must be publicity to the all and adverse to the competitor. The case of the defendants that they are in possession of the suit land from 1983 is founded on the basis of the so-called Hebabil ewaz which has been cancelled subsequently. So, how this sought of possession can be manifested as adverse possession. The defendants having been claiming their possession heavily into the suit land from 1983 not by way of adverse possession but relying on the deed of gift which runs as follows:“বাদীর আরজির ৩নং দফার বর্ণিত ও স্বীকৃত মতে আরজির লিখিত ইং ২৩/১০/৮৩ বাংলা ১৩৯০ সনের ৫ইং কার্তিক তারিখের ৬৫৭৬ নং দলিলের দ্বারা উক্তরুপ ইং ১৯৮৩ সন হইতে মোকদ্দমা সংকান্ত দাবীর ভূমি হইতে বাদীনী নিঃস্বত্ববান দখল সংশ্রবহীন।”
If this is the dazzling case of the defendants as to their possession which is the crux point of the suit land, can their possession be considered as adverse possession. Adverse possession must be always hostile and notorious against the real owner. But the possession as claimed by the defendants into the suit land from 1983 was not hostile on notorious, rather/the same was founded on the so-called deed of gift dated 23.10.1983. Although, in my consideration after the judgment of the former suit the defendants cannot claim any right, title and possession in to the suit land on the basis of deed of gift dated 23.10.1983. But even then they showing their disrespect to the law as well as to the judgment of the former suit have been claiming their possession in to the suit from 23.10.1983. The assertion of possession of the defendants from 1983 on the basis of the deed of gift is a boomerang as to their case of adverse possession. 

28. The possession of the defendants in to the suit land if it is conceded for a moment from 23.10.1983 that would not come under the purview of adverse possession. The possession of the defendants in to the suit land from 1983 is not adverse possession in the eye of law rather the same was based on a deed of gift. The case of the plaintiff is that the defendants was inducted in to possession of the land in 1983 as her borgader while the definite case of the defendants that they have been possessing the suit land on the basis of Hebabil ewaz. If the case of the defendants are taken in to consideration in that case also their such possession is not adverse possession against the plaintiff, the real owner of the suit and they did not raised the pica of adverse possession at any point of time before filing of the present suit in the year 2003. 

29. In the case of Abdus Samad and others Vs. Deputy Commissioner and Custodian of the Vested Property and Non Resident Property, Munshigong reported in 5 MLR (AD)73 it was held that permissive possession of a party is not a adverse possession against the real owner. In the reported case, I find that the suit land of that suit originally belonged to Gobinda Chandra Dutta and others who had left this country for India some timing 1920 making over its possession daily to one Lal Mia who possessed the some for over 65 years without any interruption from any quarter. After his death the plaintiffs having been possessing the suit land for over 12 years and thus they have acquired title thereto by way of adverse possession and the defendants have no right, title or possession therein but they had most illegally enlisted the suit property as vested property, hence that suit was filed for declaration that the enlistment of the property as vested property is illegal and that the plaintiffs have title thereto by way of adverse possession. The vested property authority appearing in the said suit stated that the suit property has been correctly enlisted as vested property as the owners thereof had left for India and the government is in possession thereof through its lessee. In the trial the suit was dismissed by the Senior Assistant Judge but in the appeal, the appellate Court reversed the decision of the trial Court and decreed the suit. Against the judgment of the appellate Court below a civil revision was preferred in the High Court Division and this Division setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court below restored the judgment of the trial Court. Thereafter, leave was sought for before the Appellate Division whether plaintiffs' possession in to the suit land can be considered as adverse possession. The Appellate Division ultimately found that Lal Mia was always permissive possessor and his such possession cannot be considered as adverse possession in order to create title. The observations of the Appellate Division runs as follows: 

"Admittedly, the possession of Lal Mia, the predecessor of the petitioners was permissive. Lal Mia's possession was that of a licensee the possession of the petitioners who are his heirs could not he better than that of licensees. Permissive possession, however long cannot bestow title upon the possessor or his successors. It is fairly settled that when possession commences in a permissive character it does not become adverse unless by some positive overt act it is indicated that such possession became adverse either in the hands of the successors or even in the hands of the original permissive possessor. None of the courts below have found that there was assertion of hostile title to the knowledge of the true owners for 12 years or more. In the circumstances we do not find fault with the ultimate decision of the High Court Division." 

30. In the reported case Lal Mia and his heirs were in possession of the suit land more than 75 years but even then they did not acquire title in to the suit land by adverse possession as that was not adverse and hostile against the real owner and as against the government also. I find similarity between the fact of the reported case and the case in my hands. In the instant case, the defendants were allegedly inducted in to possession of the suit land as borgader of the plaintiff to borga cultivate her land. But, in the written statement it has been articulated that the father of the defendants  was a luxurious man and he did not plough his own land, rather he employing labors use to cultivate his land. So, he did not take any land from the plaintiff for borga cultivation. If the case of the defendants is taken as a fact that he was not engaged as borga cultivator in that event also since the defendants were allegedly possessing the suit land on the strength of an illegal Hebabil ewaz their such possession would not be adverse possession at any point of time against the real owner. But their possession had become adverse on 27.08.20(8) when they notoriously dispossessed the plaintiff erecting tin shed and wooden house on the suit land. As such, I find that the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendants on 27.08.2000 and the suit has been filed within 12 years from such dispossession as required under Article 144 of the Limitation Act. As such, the suit cannot be considered as barred by limitation. 

31. The learned Advocate for the petitioners raised question as to the legality of the registration of the deed of gift in 1972 at Mymensingh Sub-Registry Office. As it has been found that this question of fact was not raised at the time of trial of the suit. So there is no evidence and materials on record on this fact but the fact remains that the plaintiff acquired title into the suit land through the deed of gift from 1972 and the defendants admitting the said deed took the land through Hebabil ewaz from the plaintiff on 23.10.1983. So, the defendants cannot raise any question as to the genuinely of the deed of gift of 1972. 

32. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also raised question as to the identity of the suit land as in his estimation there appears no identity of survey in the schedule Nos. l and 2 of the plaint. It is fact, that in the schedule Nos.1 and 2 of the plaint, the description of the land has been given articulating the khatian and plot numbers without mentioning the identity of the survey. 

33. From the plaint it appears that the plaintiffs has mentioned the plot and khatian numbers corresponding to the settlement khatian in the averment of the plaint but the same did find place in schedule of the plaint. However, in my consideration for this reason a suit must not be failed. 

34. The last point raised by the petitioner in this suit is that the plaintiff has claimed .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khtain no.10 of mouza Kaida although the father of the plaintiff gifted on .20 acres of land from that particular plot. In answering this point the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party no.1 submits that in an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers, the plaintiff used to possessed .30 acres of land from the particular plot. I find no logic to accept this argument, because them was no scope for having possession into .30 acres of land of that particular plot as neither the plaintiff nor her other sisters jointly got .30 acres of land from their father through the deed of gift in the year 1972 and the amicable possession of the plaintiff is a absurd story because the relationship between the plaintiff and the defendants are very much hostile in nature. So, in my consideration I find logic and justification in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the /4- plaintiff cannot get any relief whatsoever in .30 acre of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza kaida. 

But so far the other materials on record is concerned, I find that them appears no legal 
impediment in taking the suit as a whole in favour of the plaintiff save and except the land of the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. As it appeals from the materials on record that the plaintiff is a woman who got the suit land from her father in 1972 and when she was living in the house of her husband, the defendants who are nobody but the members of the same clan tried to grab the land in this or that way and as part of their said ill device they created a collusive and fraudulent Hebabil ewaz. dated 23.10.1983 and the plaintiff in order to protect her right and interest into the suit land filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 and the said suit was decreed and against the said verdict appeal was tiled by the defendants but the judgment and decree of Other Class Suit no.26 of 1985 remained enact and the proceeding arising out of the said suit was ended on 27.01.2000. Thus, it appears that the plaintiff being a woman was in litigation with the defendants from 1983 to 2000, that is, for about 17 years for the suit land. Thereafter, whenever the plaintiff got the judgment in her favour finally in the former suit the defendants enmeshed her in the present suit dispossessing her from the suit land on 27.08.2000 and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants from 2000. By this time when the former proceeding was pending the defendants have created as massy as 7/8 documents in order to create more cumbersome and complication into the peaceful enjoyment of plaintiffs title into the suit land. The defendants left no stone untouched to deprived the plaintiff from the suit land creating obstruction and hindrance one after another. They have been chasing the plaintiff from 1983 involving her with the suits one after another encyclicals and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants to foil their such ugly brazen attempt to grab the suit land.


35. On a careful scrutiny of the impugned judgment I find that the appellate Court below rightly passed the decree in the favour of the plaintiff, but the plaintiff is not entitled to get .30 acres of land from the plot no. 68 of khatian no. 10 of mouza Kaida but she is entitled to get a decree for .20 acres of land from that plot. It pertinent to point out here that the defendants also admit the title of plaintiff into .20 acres of land from plot no.68 as it reveals from the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983, as the plaintiff admitting the title of the plaintiff into .20 acres of land in that particular plot created the deed. So, in my consideration, the decree passed by the appellate Court below may be affirmed subject to modification in respect of quantity of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. 

36. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below is modified. The plaintiff will get khas possession into .10 acres of land in plot no.1452/85 of khatian no.458 and into .20 acres of land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida and also into .30 acres of land in plot no.10 of khatian 106, into .09 acres of land in plot no.45 of -khatian no.108 and into .11 acres of land in plot no.49 of khatian no.108 of mouza Bajardi, that is, the plaintiffs suit be decreed for an area of .80 acres of land in stead of .90 acres of land. She will get the recovery of khas possession of the land specified in the schedule Nos.' and 2 of the plaint within the given boundary subject to the above modification. 

37. Let a copy of this judgment and order along with the lower Courts record be sent to the Court concerned.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, Advocate ----- for the Petitioner 
Mr. Biswojit Roy, D.A.G. ----- for the respondent No.1
parties:
Khaleda Begum ----- Petitioner
Versus
Bangladesh & Others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Habibul Gani, J:- On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution this Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the failure/refusal of the respondent No.4 to start a mutation case/proceeding in the name of the petitioner in respect of 91 decimals of land -appertaining to R.S.: Khatian No.10, S.A. Khatian No.68, S.A. Plot No.62 and other 79 decimals of land appertaining to R.S. (P.R.R.) Khatian No.92, S.A. Khatian No.57, S.A. Plot Nos.65/66 (total 1.70 acres of land) of mouza Madandia under P.S. Kotwali (Faridpur Sadar), District Faridpur pursuant to a decree passed by the competent civil Court in favour of the petitioner should not he declared to be illegal and is of no legal effect and why the respondent No.4 should not he directed to start a mutation case/proceeding in the name of the petitioner in respect of the land in question and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court seems fit and proper. 
2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the parties were directed to maintain status quo in respect of the possession and position of the land in question for a period of three months which was extended subsequently till disposal of the rule. 

3. The short facts for disposal of the rule are that the father of the petitioner got ex-parte decree over the land in question in a case of specific performance of contract on 12.05.1975 in Title Suit No.50 of 1973 and subsequently, filed Execution Case No.10 of 1978 and got registered kabala through Court being No.5224 on 9.5.1978. After death of her lather she riled Title Suit No.88 of 2001 impleading her brothers and sisters as defendants for declaration that her father was mere a benamder in respect of the schedule property in question which was subsequently on compromise decreed in favour of the petitioner vide decree dated 16.08.2001. Thereafter, the petitioner on 16.09.2001 went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kotwali (Faridpur Sadar) with an application for mutating her name but the Assistant Commissioner (Land) refused to receive the application saying that the land in question is a khash land and those have been leased out to other parties. The petitioner knowing about the land in question as khash land filed Title Suit No.164 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur implcading the Government as defendants seeking declaration that the land in question is not a khash land and to declare the title over the land in question in favour of the petitioner wherein the Government and other defendants contested the suit by filing written statements. Learned Assistant Juke, Sadar, Faridpur after hearing decreed the suit on contest declaring the title of the suit band in favour of the petitioner vide judgment dated 07.07.2004. The Government preferred Title Appeal No.150 of 2004 against the said judgment dated 07.07.2004 before the learned District Judge. Faridpur which on transfer was heard by the learned Third Court of Joint District Judge, who vide its judgment dated 23.01.2007 was pleased to dismiss the appeal affirming title of the petitioner. The Government did not Pile any civil revision before the Hon’ble High Court Division challenging the decree of the Court of the appeal passed on 23.01.2007 in Title Appeal No.150 of 2007. Thereafter, the petitioner again went to the office of the respondent No.4. Assistant Commissioner Land, with an application for mutation of the schedule land in question but the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), was unwilling to receive the application rather abused her. It is further asserted that though the petitioner for a several times went to the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for tiling mutation case but refused and on 05.01.2009 the petitioner again went to the office of the respondent No.4 for filing application for mutation of the schedule land but respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) did not receive the said application rather abused her and drove her away from the office. Then the petitioner through registered post with acknowledgement due sent legal notice on 01.03.2009 requesting him to start a mutation proceeding by receiving the application for mutation through her lawyer but got no response. The petitioner finally went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner Land on 15.03.2009 with an application for mutation and requested him to start a mutation proceeding but the Assistant Commissioner Land refused to receive the application for mutation and very furiously drove her away from his office. The _ petitioner again served a legal notice upon the respondent No.4 requesting him to start a mutation proceeding on 25.3.2009 but got no reply. Hence, the petitioner being failed to accept her application to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Faridpur has been constrained to file this writ petition for a direction upon the respondent No.4 to receive the application for initiation of a mutation proceeding and to dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

4. By filing supplementary affidavit to the writ petition the petitioner further asserted 
that after filing of the writ petition the petitioner received a reply of the legal notice dated 01.03.2009 from the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) vide Memo No.13-7/07-08-239 dated 01.04.2009 to which the respondent No.4 stated that the petitioner sought mutation from S.A. record but in the meantime latest i.e. present B.R.S. record of the concern Mouja has been finally published in the gazette and the land in question in the present Khatian has been recorded in the khash Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. as such, there is no scope to mutate the land in the name of the petitioner. 

5. The respondent No.1 Secretary. Ministry of Land by filing affidavit in opposition opposes the rule and denying material allegations made in the writ petition asserted that the land m question all along has been recorded in the khash khatian and the said land now also has been recorded as khash in the name of the Government in the khatian i.e. present B.R.S. Khatian in khash Khatian No. l. 
6. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner vide solenama decree obtained title of the suit property and then went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutating her name. While office of the respondent No.4 was unwilling to receive the application for mutation from the petitioner informing tier that the property in question has been recorded in the khash khatian the petitioner filed Title Suit No.164 of 2001. against the Government for declaration of title and the learned Court passed decree in favour of the petitioner on contest vide judgment dated 07.07.2004. Learned Advocate again submits that the Government filed Title Appeal No.150 of 2004 before the learned District Judge but the same was dismissed on 23.01.2007. Learned Advocate further submits that the Government did not file any revisional application against the judgment of the Court of appeal and as such the title of the petitioner is still undisturbed. Learned Advocate again submits that the petitioner after obtaining the decree from the competent civil Court went to the office of the respondent No.4 for mutating her name but respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) did not receive the application for mutation. Learned Advocate finally submits that the petitioner issued legal notice upon the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) through her lawyer and in reply to the legal notice the respondent No.4 stated that as the mutation sought on the basis of S.A. record there is no scope to mutate her name as because the present B.R.S. record has been finally published in the gazette in the name of the Government in khash khatian No. l. In this regard Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate contended that from the reply of respondent No.4 it is proved that the petitioner went to the office of the respondent No.4 who did not receive the application for starting mutation case and as such failed to perform his duty as Government servant in accordance with law. Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that it is the hounded duty of the respondent No.4 to receive the application and to start a mutation case and dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

7. Mr. Biswojit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney General by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondent No. l. Secretary, Ministry of Land submits that the land in question has been recorded as khash land and it has been settled to the landless agriculturist families. He further submits that the schedule land is all along a khas land and the application for mutation could not be entertained as the mutation was sought from S.A. record while the schedule land has been recorded in the latest Khatian i.e. in the present B.R.S. record as khas on the basis of latest survey of the concern mouja and Government published final gazette notification of B.R.S. record showing the land in question as khash in khash Khatian No.) in the name of the Government. 

8. Mr. Roy further submits that the petitioner had alternative efficacious remedy to the higher authority i.e. to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) (shortly ADC Revenue) and the petitioner could agitate her grievance to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) but not doing that the petitioner has come directly to this Court for invoking the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court conferred under Article 102 of the Constitution which is not at all maintainable. Mr. Roy finally submits that there was no formal mutation proceeding before the respondent No.4 as such no order was passed by the respondent No.4 and in absence of any formal order the present application is totally misconceived. In support of his submission the learned DAG referred the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. M. Anwar Hossain and others reported in 16 BLC (AD) 155. 

9. We have perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit thereto and the affidavit-in-opposition and considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties.

10. It appears that the writ petitioner obtained contesting decree from competent civil Court in Title Suit No.164 of 2001 against the Government and the Government preferred Title Appeal k No.150 of 2004 against the said judgment. Admittedly, the appeal was dismissed on 23.01.2007 affirming the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge who decreed the suit in favour of the petitioner. The Deputy Attorney General on -query of the Court could not show any document that Government filed any revisional application against the judgment of dismissal of appeal by the Court of appeal. It further appears from annexure-H to the supplementary affidavit to the writ petition filed by the petitioner, the reply of the legal notice by the respondent No.4, that the respondent No.4 was reluctant to mutate the schedule land in the name of the petitioner on the ground that the mutation was sought from the S.A. record while the final survey of the land in question that is B.R.S. survey of the concern mouja has been finally published in the Government gazette in khash Khatian No.1 in the name of Government. By this reply it is clear to this Court that the petitioner truly .went to the office of ` the respondent No.4 with an application for mutation but the same was not received to initiate a mutation proceeding for disposal and as such the grievance of the petitioner sustain to the fact that the respondent No.4 did not receive the application for mutation and no formal order was passed by starting a, mutation proceeding. The contentions of the learned Deputy Attorney General that the petitioner could avail other remedy by filing application to the ADC (Revenue) and in absence of any formal order in the mutation proceeding the writ petition is not maintainable in the form of mandamus are not at all acceptable to this Court as the respondent No.4 being a Government officer while dealing with mutation of land of concern mouja was totally unwilling to receive the application for mutation and to dispose of the same by starting mutation proceeding in accordance with taw by passing an order. As the respondent No.4 did not do so and passed no formal order, the petitioner was deprived from taking next course of law meaning other efficacious remedy to the higher authority. 

11. Chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and tenancy Act, 1950 in the heading of "Maintenance and Revision of the Record of Right" and Rule 23 of the Chapter VI of State Acquisition Rules, 1955 framed under the Act in the heading of "Maintenance of Record of Rights under Section 143 of the Act" are related to mutation process. Concern Assistant Commissioner land or other revenue officers, if empowered are duty bound to start a mutation proceeding either upon prayer of any person or as per procedure laid down in the aforementioned chapters and dispose of the same by passing necessary order after scrutinizing the previous records and documents and hearing the parties concerned. In the present case we find that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), respondent No.4 was unwilling to receive the application for mutation and failed to understand the legal proposition of aforementioned laws and rules and utterly failed to start mutation case upon receipt of the application for mutation from the petitioner. The respondent No.4 without starting mutation case by the reply of the legal notice informed the petitioner that as the mutation sought under S.A. record is not entertain able due to present B.R.S. record of the concern mouja has been published in the gazette notification showing the land in question as khash land in the name of the Government and gave no opportunity of hearing the petitioner. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) on receipt of the application could start a mutation proceeding and upon hearing the parties and scrutinizing the documents could pass any order in accordance with law and then the petitioner could take next recourse of law if aggrieved. It is apparent from the records and facts of the case that the petitioner repeatedly tried to file the mutation application to the office of the respondent No.4 and being failed, filed the present writ petition. 

12. We have already discussed the legal proposition of law that the empowered revenue officer shall deal with the mutation process as per Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and under Rule 23 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 but the concern revenue officer respondent No.4 utterly failed to deal with the matter. In the case of Bangladesh Vs. M. Anwar Hossain and others reported in lb BLC(AD) 155 it was clearly observed by his Lordships Mr. justice Surendra Kumar Sinha in para No.15 of the said decision of the Appellate Division that ; 

"As the petition for mutation is If awaiting decision before the Revenue Officer, writ of mandamus may he issued upon such Revenue Officer to hear and dispose of the matter within a reasonable time after issuance of notice upon all the persons interested in the property and affording them an opportunity of being heard."

 After going through the aforesaid decision of our Appellate Division and keeping in mind the observations of the said decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case and discussion made above our considered view is that the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) ought to receive the application for mutation and dispose of the same at the earliest possible time in accordance with law. 

13. Accordingly we direct the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) to receive the application for mutation from the petitioner, if so file any and dispose of the same within the shortest possible time preferably within 45 days from the date of receipt of the application in accordance with law. 

14. With the aforesaid direction this rule is disposed of.
End.

lawyer:
Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Shankar Chandra Dash Advocates   For the petitioner. 
Mr. S. N. Goswami, Advocate   For the Opposite Party No.2
parties:
Nidhuram Mondal ----- Petitioner
Versus
Sumitra Mondal and others ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, .J: Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.07.1993 and 21.7.1993 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge, (Artha Rin Adalat), Mymenshing in Other Appeal No.14 of 1991 should not be set aside and / or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts, necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.204 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Mymensingh for declaration that the record of rights prepared in the name of the defendant relates to the suit schedule property is wrong and for a further declaration of title in the suit schedule 2 property measuring 2.14 decimals of land contending inter alia that in 30.32 decimals of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.199, Jagmohan Namadash and Harimohan Namadash had one ana share each. Said Jagamohan Namodash died leaving 2 sons Motiram and Sutiram who inherited 7.08
acres of land in the suit schedule property. Sutiram died leaving 2 sons Jogesh and Umesh, predecessor of defendant Nos.1 and 2-4 respectively. MotiraM died leaving 2 daughters plaintiff No.1 Sumitra and Niroda, mother of defendant Nos.5 and 6. The Plaintiff No.1 inherited 1.891/2 acres of land with limited right. Defendant Nos.5 and 6 inherited same portion' of land as inherited by the plaintiff No.1. Plaintiff No.2 acquired .25 decimals of land from Plot No.1234 described in suit schedule No.2 vide a deed of exchange dated 9.3.1989 and thus the plaintiffs became owners of 2.141/2 acres of land. The S.A. record is wrong and plaintiffs came to know about the wrong recording of S.A. Khatian on 3.5.1986 after obtaining certified copy of the parcha and thereafter instituted the present suit. 

3. The petitioner as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation. Further contending that Jagomohan gifted .04 minas share to his son Sutiram vide a registered deed of gift dated 16.1.1917 and accordingly Sutiram acquired 7.56 acres of land and while in possession Sutiram died leaving sons Jogesh and Umesh. Umesh transferred 1.89 acres of larid from his share to Sudangsho, Rakhal, Probat and others. Umesh died leaving defendant Nos.2-4. Who left the country giving their share to defendant No.1 and since then defendant No.1 is in possession of that share also. S.A. record correctly prepared in the name of the father of this defendant. As Motiram used to live in his father-in-law's house, Jagomohan did not give any property to Motiram. Plaintiff No.1 has been living in the village Gujiram within Thana Trishal. It has been further contended that original deed of gift was in the custody of defendant No.1. The defendant No.1 came to Mymensingh for filing written statement and stayed at Usha Boarding aild for safety kept the original deed of gift in Custody of the Manager of Usha Boarding. In the same night, the plaintiff No.2 along with his father-in-law also stayed in the same boarding. The Manager of the boarding handed over the deed of gift to the plaintiff No.2 for which this defendant filed a Complaint Case before the Magistrate but that case was ended at the stage of investigation. The Registry office of Mymensingh was burnt on 14.4.1971 and such defendant failed to obtain certified copy of the deed of gift. Defendant No.1 is in possession of the suit land and prayed to dismiss the suit with cost. 

4. After hearing the parties, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit vide his judgment and decree dated 11.11.1990 and 18.11.1990 respectively holding that from the evidence of D.Ws. it is proved that Moti Ram used to live his father-in-law's house and existence of the deed of gift dated 16.1.1917 cannot be denied and the suit land is not properly identified and demarcated. 

5. Having aggrieved the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.14 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh which was subsequently transferred in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (Artha Rin Adalat) Mymensingh for disposal. 

6. After hearing the appeal the learned Subrodinate Judge allowed the appeal vide his judgment and decree dated 14.7.1993 and 21.7.1993 respectively by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge holding that the defendant No.1 failed to prove the deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 and story regarding relating to the deed of gift is not believable and also holding that from the photocopy of the deed of gift it can be presmed that the deed was written on an old stamp paper very recently and also held that for non payment of rent, title can not be extinguished. 

7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Shankar Chandra Das, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in holding that the plea of deed of gift is nothing but a myth without considering that the trial Court arrived at a finding that the record of right was prepared pursuant to the deed of gift and Motiram used to live his father-in-law's house and never claimed the suit property during his life time. The learned Advocate also submits that the Subordinate Judge failed to consider the legal aspect of the case that as the plaintiffs did not claim the entire property of Motiram the suit is not maintainable under Order 2 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate next submits that the cause of action of the suit arose from the wrong record of S.A. Khatian which was finally published in the year 1963 and as such the suit is barred under Article 102 of the Limitation Act. 

8. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate on the other hand by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the opposite party No.2 oppose the Rule and submits that the Court of appeal below after considering and assessing the evidence on record independently, rightly and Judiciously reserved the judgment and decree of the trial Court in compliance with Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate also submits that the 
plaintiffs inherits their father's property as spends according to the provision of Dayabaga School of Hindu Law of inheritance. The learned Advocate next submits that defendant No.1 failed to prove that the deed of gift dated 16.1.1917. In elaborating his submission learned Advocate submits that defendant No.1 filed a photostate copy of certified copy of the deed of gift in the Court and the Court of appeal below after assessing the said photocopy, observed that the writing of the deed of gift is very recent on an old stamp paper and arrived at a finding that the same was manufactured for the purpose of the suit. The learned Advocate submits that in paragraph No.7 of the written statement defendant No.1 admitted that the plaintiff No.1 with her family living in the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that cause of action of the suit arose when the defendant No.1 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs on the basis of wrong record of rights and on 3.5.1986 the plaintiffs obtained the certified copy of ROR and came to know about the wrong record of rights and the instant suit filed on 19.5.1986 within 6 years from the date of knowledge and as such the suit is very much within the time. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates, perused the revisional application, counter affidavit, judgments of both the Courts below, lower Court's record and the provisions of law. 

10. Admittedly Matiram, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Sutiram, predecessor of the contesting defendant, were the sons of Jagmohan Namodas and inherited their father in equal share in the suit schedule land. The plaintiffs are claming suit schedule land as the heirs of Motiram. On the other hand the contesting defendant oppose claim of the plaintiffs on the basis of a deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 allegedly executed by Jagomohan Das in favour of Sutiram, predecessor of defendant, depriving Motiram from his legal share because Motiram used to live in his father-in-law's House. 

11. Defendant could not produce the original deed of gift or the certified copy of the deed on the plea, as stated in the written statement, that he went to Mymensingh for filing written statement of the suit and stayed night at Usha boarding and for safety he handed over the original gift of deed to the Manager of the boarding. On the same night plaintiff No.2 with his father-in-law also stayed at the same boarding and said Manager of the boarding handed over the deed to the plaintiff No.2 and his father-in-law. It is also stated in the written statement that as the registry office was burnt in 1981, he failed to obtain certified copy of the deed. 

12. It appears that the core issue is to be determined whether Jagomohan Nomodas executed any deed of gift in favour of the predecessor of defendant whether said deed of gift was proved before the Courts below. Admittedly original deed of gift or certified copy of the deed was not produced and marked as exhibits. In this regard the relevant portion of the findings of the trial Courts is quoted herein under:
“বিবাদী তাহার লিখিত বলরা তাহার মোকদ্দমায় স্বপক্ষে ১৯১৭ সনের যে দানপত্রের দলিলের কথা উল্লেখ করেন তাহা আত্নসাতের বিস্তারিত কাহিনি লিপিবদ্ধ করিয়াছেন । এতদপ্রেক্ষিতে বিগত ৩০-৩-৮৬ ইং তারিখে সংসনসিংহের সদর রেজিষ্ট্রি মহাফেজ খানায় তল্লাসীর আবেদনও করা হয় কিন্তু মহাফেজ খানা হইতে উত্তরে বলা হয় বিগত ১৪ইং এপ্রিল ১৯১৮ সনে অগ্নিকানে্ড ১৭৯৩ হইতে রক্ষিত প্রায় ৩৫০০০ টা ভলিয়ম নষ্ট হয়। ইহাতে প্রমানিত হয় বিবাদীর বর্ণিত ১৯১৭ সনের দানপত্র দলিল উতঘাটনের ব্যাপারে তাহার সদিচ্ছার অভার ছিল না। এবং ঘটনা প্রবাহ মোকদ্দমায় দায়েরী অপরাপর কাগজপত্র এবং মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য হইওত বিবাদীর স্বপক্ষে বিগত ১৬-১-১৯১৭ ইয় তারিখের দানপত্র দলিলের অস্তিত্বের সত্যতাকে অস্বীকার করা যায় না।”

The Court of appeal below reversed the findings of the trial Court which is reproduced below: 
“১নং বিবাদী তাহার বক্তব্যর সমর্থনে বিহত ১৬/১/৯৭ ইংি তারিখের দারপত্র দলিল আইনত প্রমান করিতে পারেন নােই কিংবা উহার তথাকথিত ফটোষ্টেট কপি আইনত প্রমান করার চেষ্টাও করেন নাই। উক্ত দানপতের মূল প্রত্যায়িত কপি উষা বডিং হইতে হারানো সম্পর্কে যে অবিশ্বাস্য মনগড়া উক্তি উপস্থাপন করিয়াছন তাহা নেহাযেত হাস্যকর এবং উহার অস্তিত্ব সম্পর্কে কোন যৌক্তিকতা নাই। কানণ আদালতের নথিতে রক্ষিত দানপত্র দলিলের ফটোকপিটি আমি Judicial view তে গ্রহণ করিয়া দেখিলাম যে উহার মূল কপিটি একটি পুরনো ষ্ট্যাম্পে অতি সম্প্রতি লিথিত হইয়াছে যাহার ফলে লেখাগুলি ঝাপসাইয়া গিয়াছে। বিজ্ঞ আদালত েএতদমর্মে কোন প্রকার পর্যবেক্ষনী গ্রহণ করেন নাই। উপরোক্ত আলোচনায় ইহা নিঃসন্দেহে বলা যায় যে ১নং বিবাদী জগমোগন প্রদত্ত যে দানপত্র দলিলের অবতারনা করিয়াছেন উহা সয়মনসিংহের মহাফেজ খানা পুড়িয়া যাওয়ায় সুযোগ গ্রহণ করিয়া একটি মিখ্যা ও প্রহসনমূলক উক্তি বৈ অন্য কিছু নহে । অনুরুপ জাল দলিল প্রস্তুতের জন্য ১নং বিবাদীকে ফৌজদারী কার্যবিধি আইনের ৪৭৬ ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক শাস্তি যোগ্য অপরাধ এর নিমিত্ত সোপর্দ করা ন্যায় সংগত।’

It is apparent that the findings of the trial Court is based on assumption without any plausible reason. On the other hand the e appeal Court below after assessing the evidence on record independently arrived at a finding with cogent reasons. 

13. The trial Court also came to an erroneous findings that under the Dayabhagal School of Hindu law of inheritance the married women are not entitled to get share of their father. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate for the opposite party also admits that this finding of the trial Court is not correct. The learned Advocate submits that correct position . of law is that after the expiry of Motiram, his two daughters Sumitra and Niroda will inherit their father as Sapindas. 

14. From Mulla's Hindu Law, it appears that Article 88 of the Principles of Hindu Law relating to Dayabhaga succession runs as follows : 

"88 Order of succession among Sapindas.- The Sapindas of the Bengal School are divided into two classes, namely, (i) Sapindas ex parte patema, and (ii) Sapindas ex parte maternal. Nos.l to 32, except the five females, namely, Nos.4, 5, 8, 14 and 20, are sapindas ex-parte paterna  5 females Nos.4, 5, 8, 14 and 20 succeed in the following order. 1-3 --  Son, grandson and great grand son, 4. widow 5. Daughter Priority amongst daughters-The unmarried daughter succeeds first; then the married daughter who has or is likely to have male issue". Thus it appears that a married daughter having a son will inherit their father. As such the findings of the trial Court that under the Dayabhaga School of Hindu Law of inheritance the married women are not entitled to get share of their father is absolutely wrong and erroneous. 

The appeal Court below rightly observed that: 

“১নং বিবাদী উপরোক্ত জগমোহন রায়ের প্রত্র মতিরামকে ত্যাজ্য পুত্র হিসাবে মন্তব্য করিয়াছেন কিন্তু িএতমর্মে কোন বিশ্বাসযোগ্য প্রমানাতি আসিতেছে না । শুধুমাত্র মতিরাম তাহার শ্বশুরালয়ে বাস করে এখন একটি অহেতুক অজুহাত উত্থাপন করিতেও দ্বিধাবোধ করেন নাই। বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ওউক্ত মতিরামের শ্বশুরালয়ে হইতে প্রাপ্ত পৈত্রিক সম্পত্তিচ্যুত হওয়ায় একটি কারণের অবতারনা করিয়াছেন ্ হিন্দু আেইনের কোথাও এমন কোন বিধান নাই যে কোন পুরুষ ব্যক্তি শ্বশুরালয়ে বসবাস করিলে তাহার পৈত্রিক সম্পত্তি হইতে চ্যুত হন। ইহাও বিবাদীপক্ষের ১নং বাদীনির সম্পত্তি চ্যুত করার একটি অজুহাত মাত্র । হিনাদু আইনের দায়ভাগ মোতাবেক কোন ব্যক্তির পুত্র না থাকিলে পুত্রবর্তী কন্যাগন পরিত্যক্ত হন। এই ক্ষেত্রে ও মতিরামের মৃত্যুর পর পুত্রবতী ১নং বিদীনি এবং পুত্রবতী নিরাদা মতিরামের ত্যাক্ত ৩.৭৯ শতাংশ ভূমিতে প্রত্যেকে ১.৮৯ ½ শতাংশ ভূমিতে অধিকারীনি হইতে আইনত কোন বাধা নাই। যেহেতু ১নং বিবাদী তাহার কখিত দানপত্র দলিল এবং মতিরামের তাজ্যপুত্র হ্ওয়া সম্পকির্ত বিষয়ে প্রমাণ করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন সুতরাং মতিরামের পুত্রবতী কন্যগণ ত্যক্ত সম্পত্তিতে অবশ্যই অধিকারীনি হইয়াছেন।”

15. It is apparent from the evidence on record that the alleged deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 was not marked and exhibited in the suit. Further more, the learned Subordinate Judge, as a last Court of fact recorded his suspicion relating to existence of the original deed of gift and even after assessing photocopy of the said deed of gift arrived at a finding that the photocopy is manufactured for the purpose of the suit. If the deed of gift is not proved, then question of ROR in the name of the predecessor of the defendant does not arise. On perusal of both the judgment passed by the trial Court as well as the appellate Court below it appears that the Court of appeal below after assessing the evidence on record independently reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in compliance of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code 
of Civil Procedure. 

16. In the case of Anowar Khatun Vs. Abdul Hye and other reported in 18 BLD (AD) 223, our apex Court held :-

"Ordinary in revision the High Court division should not interfere with the finding of fact arrived at by lower appellate Court upon re-appreciation of evidence.

" It is well settled Principle of law that the High Court in its revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 cannot interfere with the findings of fact recorded by the Court below and re-appreciate the evidence and interfere with the finding unless it is found that the findings recorded by the lower Court are perverse or there has been non-application of mind. 

17. Going through the impugned judgment, I do not find that the findings of fact recorded 
by the appellate Court below as a last Court of fact, are perverse or there has been any non-application of mind. 

18. In the result, the rule is discharged without any Order as to cost. 
19. However there will be no order as to costs. 

20. Send down the Lower Court's record at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order of remand dated 29-6-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar in Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The petitioners as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 22 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Baralekha, Moulvibazar praying for a decree for establishment of title, for declaration that Kabala dated 11-6-1988 purported to be executed by the defendant No. 6 in favour of defendant No. 1-3 is void, collusive and without consideration and also for permanent injunction. Subsequently, by order dated 27-7-1989 amendment was allowed to the effect of recovery of possession of .01 decimal of land to the northern part of settlement plot No. 1260.

3. During pendency of the revisional application petitioner No.1 died and his heirs was duly substituted as petitioner No. 1(a)-1(c) by order of this court dated 6-10-2010.

4. The case of the petitioner in short, is that the suit land appertaining to settlement plot No. 1259 area 11 decimals and plot No. 1260 area 19 decimals including other land while was owned and possessed by Arjad Ali and Anjab Ali father of the defendant No.7. Mujahid Ali Chowdhury purchased the suit land including some other land by registered kabala dated 20-12-1951 corresponding to 6th Poush, 1358 BS of which item No.4 of the kabala schedule land attracts the suit land Mujahid Ali Chowdhury died leaving defendant No.7 in whose name the D.P. and final settlement khatian was rightly published and while defendant No.7 was in exclusive possession to sold away by two registered kabala dated 26-6-1978 and 25-10-1978 in favour of Priya Moni Debi, who transferred the same in favour of the plaintiff by deed of gift dated 8-9-1985 and 2-6-1987 and they are in possession of the said land by growing paddy and paying rents to the government. That the defendant Nos.1-3 obtained a collusive and fictitious kabala dated 11-6-1988 from one Sonahar Ali although their vendor or his predecessor had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The plaintiff father came to know that the defendant No.7 during his father life time created a false lease deed dated 23-2-1954 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos.4-6. Asab Ali, when the defendants threatened the petitioners to dispossess them from the peaceful possession in the suit land, they were constrained to file the present suit on 21.02.1989. During pendency of the suit, the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs-petitioners from northern 01 decimal of land of suit plot No. 1260 for which they prayed for recovery of possession of the said land.

5. Defendants Nos. 1 and 2-opposite party Nos. I and 3 herein contested the said suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the defendants had no objection about the plaintiff's title in the 0.11 decimal of plot No. 1259 but regarding 0.19 decimals of land of plot No. 1260 the plaintiff case is that the total land of said plot is 0.35 decimals, same was owned by Mujahid Ali Chowdhury who for his financial crisis had leased out entire land of plot No. 1260 including other lands in favour of father of defendants Nos. 4-6 Asab Ali for a period of 10 years. It was stipulated in the leased that in case favour to return the money by the leaser within the specified period of the leased deed would automatically as complete sale and since then Asab Ali had been possessing the total land of plot No. 1260 within the knowledge of all concerned. In the last settlement operation name of Aftab Ali Chowdhury was wrongly inserted in the title column, but in the column of possession the name of Asab Ali was rightly recorded. After death of Asab Ali by amicable partition defendant No.6 Sanar Ali got the land of suit plot No. 1260 in his exclusive possession and sold it to the defendant Nos.1-3 by registered kabala dated 11-6-1988 since then they are in possession. During the war of liberation the original title deeds of the vendors of the answering defendants had been destroyed. With these averments the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit with costs.

6. The trial court framed the following issues in the suit: a. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

b. Have the plaintiffs any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land?

c. Were the plaintiffs dispossessed from the disputed 01 decimal of land?

d. Is the registered kabala dated 11.06.1988 without passing of consideration or a paper transaction?

e. Are the plaintiffs entitled to get the relief as prayed for or entitled to any other relief or reliefs?

7. Learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 28-2-1991. Against the said judgment and decree the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Moulvibazar and on transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar, who by the judgment and order dated 29-6-1997 allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial court, on the finding that the local investigation is necessary for ascertaining the identity of the separate .01 decimal of land to entitle them to get a decree for recovery of khas possession of the suit land.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 29-6-1997 the plaintiff moved this court and obtained the present rule and stay.

9. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in sending the suit on remand on his arbitrary reasoning that the local investigation of the suit land is required for effective determination of the suit. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge did not adverting to the fact that the suit land is specified by boundary in the plaint and in the absence of any objection from the defendants as to whether the specified land in plaint schedule attracts the land of the suit plot Nos. 1259 and 1260. He next submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge failed to consider the amendment of the plaint allowed the suit on 27-7-1989 before taking view that for effective decree of khas possession in 01 decimal of land local investigation was necessary. He finally submits that the learned appellate court misconstrue the exhibit-1, 3(ka) and 4 which bear sufficient identification and on proper perusal of the schedule of those kabalas attract the suit land of the plaint within the specified compact area and boundary.

10. He lastly submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge without applying his judicial mind referring to the admitted document exhibit-1 for the purpose of local investigation and for additional evidence under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

11. Mr Nirmalendu Deb, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendants-opposite parties submits whether the land describe in the schedule of the plaint is identical with the land described in the schedule 4 of the registered sale deed dated 20-12-1951(exhibit-1) but no issues was framed on this important point by the trial court whether the khatian or plot or boundaries in item No.4 land of the registered deed dated 20-12-1951 is identical with the suit schedule land. He further submits that defendant Nos. 1-3 at the earliest opportunity specifically raised preliminary objection in paragraph No. 10 of their written statement filed on 9-8-1989 that registered deed dated 20-12-1951 does not bear any khatian, plot or boundaries as that of the suit land. He next submits that although the trial court decreed the suit for '01 decimal for recovery of khas possession, but in the schedule of the plaint nothing was showing about .01 decimal land of plot No. 1260 which clearly shows that the total is 0.35 decimal out of which 0.19 decimal is the suit land. Although paragraph No. 19(kha) of the plaint was amended on 27-7-1989, but in the schedule of the plaint said .01 decimal of land has not been included, so the appellate court rightly remanded the suit for holding local investigation for ascertaining the said .01 decimal land. He also submits that since the suit land is vague, indefinite and unspecified the suit ought to have been dismissed by the trial court.

12. The appellate court after considering the materials evidence on record rightly remanded the suit for ascertainment of .01 decimal of land out of total 0.19 decimal of land of plot No. 1260. In support of his submission Mr Deb cited two decisions reported in 12 MLR (AD) 105 = 12 BLC (AD) 36 and 14 BLT (AD) 176.

13. Heard the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the revisional application and exhibited documents filed by the parties and the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates.

14. It appears that the trial judge decreed the suit upon non-consideration of preliminary point and without considering objection raised by the defendant Nos. 1-3 in their written statement at the earliest opportunity for holding local investigation into the suit land and without holding such local investigation the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any decree in the suit as prayed for since the said objection directly hit at the root of the plaintiff's title in the suit. Further, the learned trial court did not consider the factual aspect of the case that no issues was framed whether the dag/plot in item 4 of the registered kabala dated 22-12-1951 attracts the suit schedule land or not.

15. It further appears that the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint bearing dag Nos. 1259 and 1260 are unspecified, vague, indefinite and not clearly bounded and even the statements of the plaintiff are taken to be so far one block of the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff, but they failed to point out '01 decimal of land within the original boundary of the plaint from which the plaintiff alleged to have been dispossessed has not been specifically described with specific boundaries as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get decree upon unspecified suit land without holding local investigation for ascertaining the identity of the suit land.

16. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the appellate court without adverting to the fact that the suit land is specified by the boundary in the plaint and in the absence of any objection of the defendant as to whether the specified schedule attract any land of the said plot No. 1259 and 1260. But it appears that the trial court totally failed to consider that the defendant's specific objection taken in paragraph 10 of the written statement and failed to give findings in this regard, so the question of adverting to the same facts does not arise at all.

17. It further appears that the kabala dated 22-12-1951 (Exhibit- 1) bears no khatian and dag number for identification and Exhibit-2 and 3 also bear unspecified land, but only described of two plots, quantum of land and boundaries which is not sufficient to decree the suit without holding local investigation. The appellate court while examining the judgment and decree of the trial court noticed that the plaintiff is admittedly out of possession of .01 decimal of land. But in the suit plaintiffs out of total area of 0.35 decimals claimed only 0.19 decimals of land and out of which they were dispossessed from simple '01 decimal of land and that there is no specification of land claimed by the plaintiff. Thus the trial court in passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff for unspecified .01 decimal of land was in error or in other words the decree passed by the trial court was not a legal one and the appellate court after considering the evidence and provision of law rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and sent the case on remand to the trial court for holding local investigation.

<u>18. Law as in order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the plaintiff to give clear description of the land in suit so that the land in suit is identifiable. In the present case it is seen that the particulars of the land as in schedule of the plaint is vague and unspecified. In that state of the matter it is clear that the plaintiff have sought for declaration of title in respect of unspecified, vague and undivided land. If the land in suit is vague, unspecified and that relief sought is in respect of undivided portion of land of particular plot in that case suit for mere declaration of title is not maintainable.</u>

19. In the present case the learned appellate court rightly consider this aspect of the case and without dismissing the suit sent the suit on remand for ascertaining .01 decimal of land from which the plaintiff was dispossessed and sought for recovery of possession from that part of the suit land by holding local investigation.

20. It further appears that although the plaintiff amended his plaint, but failed to include the area of .01 decimal of land in the schedule of the plaint amended on 27-7-1989.

21. In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that the case should go back to the trial court for relaying of the suit for the purpose of ascertaining whether the land in suit of 1 decimal as stated in the schedule of the plaint from where the plaintiff was dispossessed by holding local investigation. In this regard reference may be made to the case of Nazrul Islam (Babul) vs Santi Rani Dhupi reported in 14 BLT (AD) 176.

22. In the background made above I find no merit in this revision.

23. Accordingly, the rule is discharged. The order passed by the Subordinate Judge now Joint District First Court, Moulvibazar is upheld.

24. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. Send down the Lower Court Records and communicate the order at once.

End.
