full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali, J: This application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure by the defendants petitioners is directed against two orders namely order No 110 dated 18. 3. 1995 and order No 112 dated 2.4. 1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, lit Court, Chittagong in other Suit No 169 of 1985 asking first the defendant petitioners to cross examine P.W.1 one Omar Faruque Chowdhury and thereafter rejecting the application of the Petitioners under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for vacating the said order respectively. Facts relevant for the disposal of the application may briefly be stated as follows: 

2 Opposite parties No 1-6 and with some others instituted a suit being other suit No 169 of 1985 in the court of the 1st Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against the present defendant petitioners and some other defendants for the following reliefs: 

a) that a decree be passed declaring that the plaintiffs are entitled to the compensation money assured for the schedule land in L. A Misc. Case No 128 of 1983 -84 (Misc. Case No 2/1984-85) 

b) that the cost of the suit be decreed against the contesting defendants

c) that any other relief to which the plaintiffs are deemed entitled to.

3. The case of the plaintiffs opposite parties herein is interalia that the original owner of the land mentioned in tic schedule below was one Ramjan Ali and that C .S Khatian No 23 was finally published in his name. The said Ramjan Ali died leaving behind two sons namely Gura Miah and Syed Ali and two daughters namely, Sabur Khatun and Sadar Nisa alias Khatuni as his legal heirs. That during the time of R. S operation the said two daughters of Ramjan Ali were at their husbands house for which their names could not be recorded in the R S Khatians. But in spite of that they were in joint possession with their brothers Syed Ali and Gura Miah and. that the said Sadar Nisa alias Khatuni, Syed Ali, Thanda Miah, Abul Khatun and Tambia Khatun sold out 2.00 acres of land to plaintiff No 1 for their legal necessity including the schedule land vide registered kabala dated 9. 5. 1966 and delivered possession thereof to him and since the date of purchase the plaintiff No 1 is in peaceful possession of the same by paying rents, revenues etc. to the Government. Then he filed a Mutation Case No 572/11 of 1967-68 before the Circle Officer Hathazari, Chittagong who ordered for mutation of his name in S A Record but subsequently it was lost. Similarly the plaintiff No 2 also purchased .80 acre of land vide Registered kabala deeds dated 23.1.1984 and the plaintiff No 3 purchased .20 acre of land vide Registered kabala deed dated 23.1.1984 from one Bazal Ahmed, Oli Ahmed, Kabir Ahmed, Thanda Meah, Abul Khatun, Saleh Ahmed and Nur Begum on payment of proper consideration money and since then they are in peaceful possession of their purchased lands including .15 acre of the schedule land on payment of rent, to the Government. That the names of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were also recorded in the S.A Khatian through Mutation and the names of all the plaintiffs subsequently were recorded in present revisional survey khatian vide Appeal Case No 28876 of 1982. Out of the purchased lands of the plaintiff .30 acre as mentioned in the schedule has been acquired by the Government vide L. A Case No 128 of 1983-84 (Misc. Case No 2 of 1984-85) for Gas line which was in the possession of the plaintiffs and the compensation money for the said acquisition has been assessed at Tk. 188442/-and that the plaintiffs are entitled to get the said compensation money and accordingly they filed a petition to the Land Acquisition Officer for getting the compensation money. It appears that the original defendant Nos. 1 to 3 who also claimed to have purchased some land of the R. S Khatian from said Syed Ali and Gura Meah lodged a claim for the compensation money, besides some other groups of peoples have also applied for getting their alleged shares in the compensation money and the Land Acquisition Officer after hearing all the parties passed his order on 12.10.1985 and awarded compensation to only defendants 1 to 3 and hence the present suit by the plaintiffs. 

4. Now it appears that there are two grounds of contesting defendants in the suit namely defendants No 1 to 3 in one group and defendants No 6-12 in the another group and both the above groups have filed separate written statements, to contest the suit denying all the material allegations in the plaint, contending interalia that the suit is not maintainable, that there is no cause of action the suit is barred by limitation and also by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, waiver, estoppel and acquiescence; that the plaintiffs have got no right, title and interest or possession in the suit land and they have no right to the compensation money etc. that the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. Besides both the groups of defendants claimed their own right, title and possession in the suit land and hence claimed their right to the compensation money of the L.A. Case. Apart from filing the written statement the defendant Nos. 6-12 instituted another suit being other suit No 171 of 1985 as plaintiffs on 23.11.1985 in the same court of the Subordinate Judge, Chittagong praying for a declaration that they are only entitled to get the compensation money assessed for the suit lands in L.A. Case No 128 of 1983-84 as described in the schedule below. The Court passed an order for hearing of both the suits together and date was accordingly fixed for evidence on 18.3.1995. The plaintiffs of suit No 169 of 1985 examined one Omar Faruque Chowdhury as P.W. 1 who proved some documents which were marked as Exhibits. Then' a question came up which of the two groups of the contesting defendants would cross examine the P.W. 1 first. The defendants 1-3 made a prayer by an application that defendant Nos. 6-12 should be asked to cross examine the said P.W.1 first as they as well as the plaintiffs of the suit are opposing the claims of the defendant petitioners. The learned Subordinate Judge then neared both the sides on the said point and thereafter asked the first group of the defendants namely defendant Nos. 1-3 to cross examine the said witness P.W.1 by his order dated 18. 3.1995. The defendants No 1-3 being aggrieved by that order filed an application under section 151 C.P.C. before the learned Subordinate Judge to reconsider the order dated 18.3.1995 and to ask the defendants 6-12 to cross examine the witness first alleging interalia that unless defendants no 6-12 are asked to cross examine first, the defendants Nos. 1-3 will be seriously prejudiced in their defence, particularly when the said defendant Nos. 6-12 have not denied the title of the plaintiffs of suit No 169 of 1985 in the other suit No 171 of 1985. The learned Subordinate Judge then heard both the sides of the said application but rejected the same by his order No 112 dated 2.4.1995. Now being aggrieved by the aforesaid two orders the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 along with the substituted heirs of defendant No 2 who died subsequently have filed this application before us. 

5. Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners contends that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed error of law in asking defendant Nos. d-3 instead of defendants 6-12 to cross examine P.W.1 first and illegally passed the impugned order dated 18.3.1995 and also the order dated 2.4.1995 as a result the defendants petitioners have been seriously prejudiced and there has been failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that when there are 2 sets of defendants to contest the suit and if one set of defendants goes to support the claim of the plaintiffs wholly or in part, then in that case that set of defendants should be asked to cross examine the witness of the plaintiff first. His further submission is that in the instant case the contesting defendants 6-12 are in fact partially supporting the case of the plaintiffs; hence they should be asked to cross examine the. P.W.1 first. But the learned Subordinate Judge instead of asking them to cross examine P.W.1 has most illegally asked the defendant Nos. 1-3 to cross examine the said witness first and as a result there has been miscarriage of justice. In support of this contention Mr. Chowdhury has relied on 2 decisions, one reported in 32 ILR Bombay series at page 599 in the case of Haji Bibi Vs. H.H Sir Sultan Mahomed Khan and others wherein it has been held: 

"The word plaintiff means every person asking relief against another person.

"The plaintiff and such of the defendants as support the plaintiffs case wholly or in partly, must address the court and call their evidence in the first place, and then following the words of section 180 of the Civil Procedure Code the other party namely the persons opposed to the plaintiffs case and that of the other defendants supporting the plaintiff, must address the court and call their evidence. 
6. The other decision relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioners is in the case of Shah Harilal Hamitalal and others Vs. M.G. Pathak and others reported in A.I.R.1964 Gujrat 26 wherein it has been held in para 3. 

On the question of right to begin and the question of leading evidence, we have provisions in order 18, rule] C .P .Code which reads as follows: 

The plaintiff has the right to begin unless the defendant admits the facts alleged by the plaintiff and contends that either in point of law or on some additional facts alleged by the plaintiff, the plaintiff is not entitled to any part of the relief which he seeks in which use the defendant has the right to begin. 

Sub-rule (2) of Rule 2 of order 18 C.P.C. reads thus: 

The other party shall then state his case and produce his evidence (if any) and may then address the court generally on the whole case. 

4) So far as the defendants go, the question which of the defendants should begin has not been dealt with in order 18 C.P.C. But on general principle, if any of the defendants supports the plaintiffs in whole or in part, then he should address the court and lead his evidence first before the other defendants who do not support wholly or in part the plaintiff's case. The order in which defendants lead evidence becomes important only when some of them support the case of the plaintiffs in whole or in part while the others do not if all the defendants completely oppose the plaintiffs case, then the question of order of leading evidence amongst the defendants is immaterial. It is only when the defendants are divided into two groups,, one group consisting of the defendants supporting the plaintiffs case in part and the other group consisting of the defendants who do not support the plaintiffs case in any part that the question of order of leading evidence becomes important. In such cases among defendants the order of leading evidence should be as follows: 

1) Those defendants who fully support the case of the plaintiff 
2) Those defendants who partly support the case of the plaintiff. 

3) Those defendants who do not support the case of the plaintiff in any part. 

7. Now, let us examine the instant case in the light of the above decisions cited before us. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has placed before us a certified copy of the plaint of other suit No 169 of1.985 and the ordinary copy of the 2 sets of written statements of defendant. Nos. 1-3 and defendant Nos. 6-12. On perusal of the written statements of the 2 sets of defendants, we find that both the sets of defendants have equally challenged the claim of the plaintiffs in the instant suit in which P.W.1 has been examined by the plaintiffs and at this stage it is difficult to say only from a reading of the written statements that the group of defendant Nos. 6-12 is at all supporting either wholly or in part the claim of the plaintiffs Now in our view so far the order in production and examination of witnesses in a case either civil or criminal it is the absolute discretion of the court concerned unless there is any specific law or rule therefor. In this regard we may look at section135 of the Evidence Act in chapter X . Section135 of the Evidence Act runs thus:- 

"135. The order in which witnesses are produces and examined shall be regulated by the law and practice for the time being relating to Civil and Criminal Procedure respectively and in the absence of any such law, by the discretion of the court. 

For the above we are of the view that a judge must necessarily be invested with a wide discretion in regard to ordering or permitting an alternation of the ordinary rules of practice and procedure at trials and the time and order in which the evidence shall be introduced. These rules are always subject to be modified in their application to particular case at the discretion of the Judge While counsel has discretion, the court has also power under this section to direct the order in which witnesses cited by a party shall be examined. 

Admittedly there is nothing in the code specifically as to which of the defendants should cross examine any prosecution witness first and hence in the above circumstances a court is to fall back on section 135 of the Evidence Act which speaks of the discretion of the court to fix the order of production and examination of witnesses, of course such discretion should be exercised judicially and not arbitrarily in the facts and circumstances of each case. In the instant case, as we have observed that from the reading of the written statements of the 2 sets of defendants it does not appear that the group of defendants 6-12 is supporting the plaintiffs claim either wholly or partially; hence the decisions relief on the learned Advocate for the petitioners cannot be of any help to his clients. Had it been a vase that the defendants 6-12 were supporting the plaintiffs claim wholly or partly in the written statement then possibly it could be said that unless defendant Nos. 6-12 were examined first then defendants 1-3 would have been prejudiced. But what we see at this stage on scrutiny of the written statements is that the case is a different one. From the impugned order we also find that the learned Subordinate Judge after hearing both the side decided in the facts and circumstances of The case to ask the defendants 1-3 cross examine the witness of the plaintiff first in Suit No 169/1985. As we have already pointed out that in the absence of any specific law, rules procedure, it is the discretion of the court concerned to order production of examination of a witness, we think that the learned Subordinate Judge has exercised his discretion judiciously and not arbitrarily. Further merely non making of the plaintiffs of the present suit as party defendants in other suit No 1.71of 1985 as alleged by the petitioners cannot be a ground for holding that the defendants 6-12 arc supporting the case Of the plaintiffs in T.S. No 169 of 1985. 

8. However for the reasons stated above, we find no substance in this revisional application and the same is summarily rejected. But before parting with this application we like to observe that if it transpires subsequently from the case and  conduct of the defendants No 6-12 that they are going to support the plaintiffs claim either wholly or partially, in that case certainly they should be steed to cross examine the witness of the plaintiffs first before the defendant petitioners. 

Let a copy of this judgment and order be transmitted to the court below at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J. The Judgment and decree passed by learned Additional District Judge, Chittagong on 29.3.2000 in Other Appeal No. 235 of 1999 reversing the Judgment and decree dated 27.9.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chittagong in Other Suit No.23 of 1998 has been called in question by invoking the revisional jurisdiction on laying an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in which a single Judge of this Court on perusal of the impugned judgment issued rule calling upon' the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment complained should not be set aside should not be set aside or any other order/ or orders as to this court deem fit and proper. 

2. The short facts for disposal of the role are that the land originally belonged to Joy Chandra Banta and R.S. Khatian in respect thereof was correctly prepared and finally published in his favour. Joy Chandra Barua transferred the suit schedule-I land in favour of Mohan Banshi Banta by a registered Kabala and accordingly delivered possession of the same. Mohan Banshi Barua by a registered kabala dated 14.10.1969 transferred the suit schedule-I land in favour of Hamangshu Barua who subsequently transferred the same in favour of Sneha Bala Barua mother of the plaintiffs by a registered kabala dated 10.3.1970 and accordingly delivered possession of suit schedule-1 land in her 'favour. After purchasing the schedule-1 land Sneha Bala Banta constructed a dwelling house on the suit schedule-1 land and had been possessing the same with her family members; that being satisfied by the nursing of the of the plaintiff No. 1 Sneha Bala Barua transferred .02 acres of land out of suit schedule-I land to the plaintiff No. I by a registered deed of gift dated 28.12.1987 and accordingly delivered possession of the same in favour of the plaintiff No.1 and the plaintiff No.1 has been possessing the some giving specific boundaries. Sneha Bala Barua died on 19.1.1993 and as such the plaintiffs became owners in possession of rest .02 acres of land by inheritance. The Plaintiff No.1 by amicable arrangement with his brothers and sisters became owner in possession of the entire suit schedule I land and have been possessing the same on payment of rent till to-day. The defendant No.1 claimed suit schedule 1(Ka)land for the first time at the last part of November 1997 which is the part of schedule I land and in collusion with defendants 2 and 3 gave out open threat to the plaintiffs that they would take possession of the suit schedule- bka) land by evicting the plaintiffs there from by force. On enquiry plaintiffs came to know that the defendant No I has created a deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 in respect of the suit land alleged to be executed by the mother of the plaintiffs in his favour. Sneha Bala Barua mother of the plaintiffs did not execute any such kabala in respect of the suit land in favour of the defendant No.1. The alleged registered deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 is false, fraudulent, collusive without consideration and void and mother of plaintiffs did not execute the said deed in favour of defendant No. l. Plaintiffs have been possessing land of schedule 1 (ka) in which they acquired right and title by inheritance from their mother and defendants have acquired no right and title in suit schedule 1(ka) land by the alleged deed of gift dated 19.6.1991. As the defendants gave out open threat to the plaintiffs on 18.1.1999 for taking forcible possession of the suit land and as the alleged deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 has created clouds in the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land plaintiffs were compelled to file the suit with the prayer for the reliefs slated above. 

3. Defendants No. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and after taking all the preliminary objection as to maintainability of the suit it is their respective case that the suit land originally belonged to Joy Chandra Barua in whose name R.S. Khatian was correctly prepared and finally published; Joy Chandra Barua transferred the suit schedule 1 land in favour of Mohan Banashi Barua by a registered Kabala and Mohan Banshi Banta while in possession of the suit schedule-I land transferred the same to Himangshu Banta and subsequently Himangshu transferred .04 acres of land to Sneha Bala by registered Kabala dated 10.03.1970 and accordingly delivered possession to her. Sneha Bala Banta gifted .02 acres of land out of P4 acres to the plaintiff No.1 by a registered deed of gift dated 28.12.1987 and the rest .02 acres of land was transferred by Sneha Bala Barua by a registered deed of gift dated 19.06.1991 in favour of defendant No.1. Plaintiff No.1 and defendant No.I Acquired .02 acres of land each by the above said two registered deeds of gift dated 28.12.1987 and 19.06.1991. Defendant No.1 has been possessing the land described in schedule I(ka) of the plaint and on the other hand plaintiff No.1 has been possessing the rest .02 sataks which is adjacent to the land of schedule I (ha) land. Plaintiff never possessed or ever claimed the land described in schedule I (ka) land of the plaint. It is a down right falsehood to say that defendants gave out open threat to plaintiffs on 18.01.1998 to dispossess them from the suit land as alleged in the plaint and as such there is no cause of action for filing the suit. Deed of gift dated 19.1K,I991 executed by Sneha Bab in of defendant No.1 is a genuine and on the basis of the same defendant No.1 has been possessing the suit schedule l(ka) land, plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit schedule I (ka) land and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

4. Four P. Ws. including plaintiff No.1 were examined on behalf of the plaintiff. On the other hand, three D.Ws. including defendant No.1 were examined to prove their respective cases. 

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, upon reading the case of the contesting parties on considering the oral and documentary evidence on record dismissed Other Suit No. 23 of 1998 by her judgment and decree dated 21.9.1999. 

6. Being aggrieved by dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, plaintiffs filed Other Appeal No. 235 of 1999 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chittagong which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge. 7th Court Chittagong, who by his judgment and decree dated 29.3.2000 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree dated 21.9.1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge. Chittagong. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.3.2000 defendants preferred this revision before this Hon'ble Court and obtained the present Rule. 

8. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that, the Court of appeal below wholly misconceived the issues involved in the suit and the relevant law applicable thereto and in consequence erred in law resulting in an error in the decision in decreeing the suit. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner further submits that having regard to the established principle that if a person alleges that a particular transaction is false, fraudulent, collusive and void the burden is on that person to prove the allegation and having regard to the pleading of the plaintiffs in the suit and evidence adduced by them in support of their case learned Additional District Judge committed a grave error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not dismissing the appeal upon a finding that the plaintiffs singularly failed to discharge the burden on them in this regard. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Additional District Judge framed five issues for deciding the appeal and committed mistakes and illegalities in deciding issue Nos. 3-5 together and so doing jumbled up the subject matter of the suit thereby could not le and decide the case of the parties from their proper angle of vision and perspective and made a mess of whole thing in deciding the issue, learned District Judge therefore committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge without noticing and reversing the findings of the learned Assistant Judge the Court of appeal below failed to read and appreciate the oral and documentary evidence of the parties on the question of the plaintiffs knowledge of alleged disputed Kabala dated 19.6.1991 and therefore, apparently committed an error in disturbing the finding of the Trial Court in this point in as much as the findings of the Trial Court is based on proper reading and appreciation of the oral evidence adduced by the parties, the judgment of reversal in this case is neither legal nor proper. The learned Advocate also submits that there is error apparent in the judgment of the Court of appeal below in that the Court of Appeal below reversed the positive finding of the Trial Court on the point as to the possession of the suit property without assigning any cogent reason therefore and even without referring to the oral evidence on record on the question and thus the Appellate Court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Counsel for the petitioner then submits that the genuineness of the registered deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 executed by Sneha Bala Banta has been questioned in the plaint by the plaintiff and therefore the onus of proving the plaint case lies upon the plaintiff opposite parties. The learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal selling aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court upon a finding that the learned Assistant Judge should have sent the disputed deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 before Hand Writing Expert for opinion by examination and comparison of the L.T.I. of Sneha Bala appearing in the deed of gift with those admitted signature and L.T.Is. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner again submits that the learned Assistant Judge found that Sneha Bala gifted .02 acres of land to the plaintiff  Deizi Banta & Ors M.K.M. Shohidul litta,J1465 no.I by a registered deed of gift dated 28.12.1987 and subsequently she again transferred the rest .02 acres of land to the defendant no. 1 by registered deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 which has been challenged by the plaintiffs in the instant suit, the above said two registered deed of gills were written by the same scribe the. L.T.I. of Sneha Bala apparent on both the deeds have been indentified by the same person namely. Prabodh Ranjan Banta and the attesting witnesses of both the documents are the same. Probodh Ranjan Banta was examined and cross examined as D.W.3 who proved execution of both the deeds by Sneha Bala. The learned Additional District Judge without considering the above aspects decreed the suit upon a finding that the Trial Court should have sent the disputed deed of gift for experts opinion and thus the learned Additional District Judge is totally misdirected in passing such erroneous finding and committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice as such as the learned Assistant Judge is quite competent under Section 73 of the Evidence Act to compare the L.T.I. of the executants Sneha Bala appearing in the aforesaid deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 with her other L.T.I.'s available in the record of the suit such as admitted registered deed of gift dated 28.12.1987. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that the appellate Court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not dismissing the suit upon a finding that the.suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner also submits that the learned Additional District Judge decreed the suit declaring the deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 is collusive and void upon an erroneous finding based on surmise and conjecture that though the defendant no.1 got the disputed land by a registered deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 executed by Sneha Bala but he neither mutated his name in the khatian by filling a Mutation case nor he paid rent of the disputed land in as much as Mutation Khatian and the rent receipts are not the documents of title. The learned Advocate for the petitioner lastly submits that the defendant petitioners became owners in possession of the suit land on the strength of a registered deed of gift dated 19.9.1991, the impugned judgment and -decree dated 29.3.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. 755 Court Chittagong in other Appeal No.235 of 1999 is erroneous. 

9. On the other hand Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for plaintiffs opposite parties supported the judgment of the last Court of fact. Learned Advocate submits that the last Court of fact rightly decreed the suit and declaring the deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 as collusive and void and such finding of the last Court of fact is based on sound reasoning as the trial Court at the time of passing the judgment and decree ought to have taken into consideration that vital aspect of the case and the last Court of fact on due and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record rightly decreed the suit and did not commit any wrong in decreeing the suit which deserves no interference under the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon’ble Court as laid down under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure as the last Court or fact rightly decreed the suit which is immune from attack. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party lastly submits that the judgment and decree of the last Court of fact is the proper judgment of reversal based on sound reasoning as such. does not deserve any interference under the provision of law as contain in section I 15(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the rule is liable to he discharged with cost. 

10. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides and consider the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides, On perusal of the impugned judgment and decree of the last Court of facts as it is not based on sound reasoning of the trial Court who measurably failed to take into notice that a person alleged with particular transaction is false. fraudulent, collusive and void the burden is on that person to prove the allegation and having regard to the pleading of the plaintiff in the suit and evidence adduced by them in support of their case. learned Judge committed a grave error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not taking into consideration of those aspect of this case. The final Court of fact at the time of disposal of the appeal would have taken into considerations that the plaintiffs singularly failed to discharge burden on them in proving the alleged transaction which the learned trial Court rightly held that the. said transaction is false fraudulent and void, lower appellate Court instead of dismissing the appeal arrived at a wrong finding in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court upon an erroneous finding which is not at all based on oral and documentary evidence as adduced by the respective parties in support of their easel The final Court of fact also committed serious illegality in deciding the issue Nos. 3-5 together and in doing so jumble up the subject matter of the suit and thereby could not see and decide the case of the parties from their proper angle of vision and perspective and thus arrived at an erroneous decision in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The learned Advocate for the petitioner rightly submits that the Court of Appeal below reversed the positive finding of the Trial Court on the point as to the possession of the suit property assigning any reason therefore and even without referring to the oral evidence on recursion the question and thus the final Court of facts committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The final Court of facts also failed to consider genuineness of the registered deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 executed by Sneha Bala Barua has been questioned in the plaint by the plaintiff and therefore onus of proving the plaint case lies upon the plaintiff. The final Court of facts at the time of disposal of the appeal has totally misdirected in arriving at a finding to the effect that the learned Assistant lodge should have sent the disputed deed of gift dated 19.6.1991 before hand writing expert for opinion by examination and comparison of the L.T.I of Sneha Bala appearing in the deed of gift with those admitted signature and L.T.I is absolutely an erroneous finding on the part of the learned Additional District Judge ought to base concur with a reasonable finding of the trial Court on this point. The learned Advocate for the petitioner rightly submits that two registered deed of gift were written by the same scribe, the L.T.l of Sneha Bala apparent on both the deed have bee it identified by the same person namely prabodh Ranjan Barua and the attesting witnesses of both the documents are the same as such there is no confusion or ambiguity in arriving at a finding that the trial Court on the basis of the registered deed of gift rightly dismissed the suit on proper appreciation of oral and documentary evidence on records and the learned Additional District Judge at the time of disposal of the appeal ought to have affirmed the finding of the learned trial Court and would not have interfered with the finding of the learned trial Court.

11. The aforesaid submission as advanced by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner we find merit and substance in the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, accordingly the rule succeed. 

12. In the result the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 29.3.2000 of the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court Chittagong passed in Other Appeal No. 235 of 1999 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 21.9.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. 5th Court Chittagong in Other Suit No. 223 of 1998 is hereby affirmed. 

13. The order of status quo granted at the time of issuance of rule is hereby recalled and vacated. 

14. The office is hereby directed to transmit a copy of this judgment along with lower Court records to the concerned Court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mashuque Hosain Ahmed, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party no. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.09.1997 passed by the learned Additional District. Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.182 of 1990 affirming the judgment and decree dated 16.04.1990 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.25 of 1990 should not be set aside or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The back ground of the case is that the plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 instituted Title Suit No. 561 of 198 in Fourth Court of Munsif, Dhaka seeking a Decree of Permanent Injunction against Defendant Nos. l, 2, 5 and 6 Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka, Executive Engineer and Deputy-Executive Engineer. Railway Division, Dhaka restraining them permanently from evicting him from suit property described in Schedule to plaint measuring i.e. 0.34 acres property without payment of Compensation Money in L.A. Case No. 63 of 1959-1960, and, also, without allotment of Rehabilitation Plot. Suit was thereafter renumbered as Title Suit No. 25 of 1990 on transfer to Fourth Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. Case of the Plaintiff Opposite Party No.1, in short, is that he became rightful owner and possessor in respect of 0.17 +0.17 = 0.34 acres property by way of Two Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 30.10.1948 and 29.10.1948 in C.S Plot No.1356 corresponding to S.A. Plot No. 401 and 4019. Plaintiff constructed houses on 0.34 acres of property and had have been residing there with family members and, also, on inducting some tenants and realising Rent from tenants and has been enjoying vacant land on producing vegetables and leaves. S.A. Record of Right had been prepared in the name of plaintiff. Plaintiff recently in the month of May, 198 came to that property of C.S. Plot No.I356 was acquired by Government for Bangladesh Railway in L.A. Case No.63 of 1959-1960. Plaintiff, also, became aware that Defendant Nos.1 and 2 has been in charge of Acquisition process and Defendant Nos.5 and 6 had been engaged for possession and maintenance of acquired property. 25. Let me now address the point of Notice upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 before Requisition and Acquisition of Suit Property by Government of Bangladesh for Defendant-Petitioner Bangladesh Railway. 

Section 3 of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 speaks of Requisitioning of Properly required for Public Purpose or in Public Interest Section 4 of The Act of 1948 provides for Service of Order of Requisition which enjoins when an order of requisition has been made under section 3, it shall be served on the owner of the Property by delivering or tendering it to him, or, where the owner cannot be found, it shall be served by leaving an authentic copy thereof with some adult male member of the family of such Owner or, if no such adult male member of the family can be found, it may he served by affixing an authentic copy thereof to some conspicuous part of the premises in which he is known to have last resided or carried on business or personally worked for gain and also by affixing another such copy to some conspicuous part of the Requisition Property. An authentic copy of such order shall also be affixed on the notice board of the local Union Council and the order shall also be proclaimed by beat of drum in the locality in which the property is situate, Section-5 of The Act of i948 Deeds with Acquisition of Property Section enshrines: 

(1) The Government may, if it thinks fit, acquire any requisitioned property on the proposal of the Deputy Commissioner in the manner hereinafter provided in the section. 

Rule 4 of The Rules runs as follows: 

"4. Notice referred to in sub-Section (1), (3) &(7) of section 5 shall be in Form B, in Form C and in Form D, respectively." 

(la) The Deputy Commissioner shall, if he considers that the acquisition of any requisitioned property is expedient for a public purpose or in public interest, cause a public notice to be given at convenient places on or near the requisitioned property stating that the property is proposed to be acquired. 

(2) Such notice shall state particulars of the Property to be acquired, and shall require all persons interested in the property to appear personally or by agent before the Deputy Commissioner at a time and place therein mentioned (such time not being earlier than fifteen days after the date of publication of the notice) and to state the nature of their respective interests in the property, their objections (if any) to the acquisition of the Property and particulars of their claims to compensation for their respective interests. 

(3) Notice shall also be served to the above effect on the owner of such property and on all such persons known or believed to be interested therein or to be entitled to act for persons so interested as reside or have agents authorized to receive service on their behalf within the revenue district in which the property is situated. 

(4) In case any person so interested resides elsewhere and has no such agent, the notice shall be sent to him by registered post in a letter addressed to him at his last known residence, address or place of business. 

Section 5 B of The Act provides Payment of Compensation in Advance which enjoins. 

Subject to the provisions of Sections 6 and 7 when a Property is requisitioned under Section 3 with a view to its permanent acquisition under Section 5, the owner of such property shall be offered, and if agreeable, paid in advance, before possession is taken over under sub-section (2) or section 4 a Compensation to the extent of 
(a) 100% for structures and buildings, 
(b) 90% for lands, 

On the basis of a provisional estimate prepared on rough and ready calculation. 

Section 7 of The Act of 1948 provides Compensation for Immovable Property which says: 

26. Whenever any immovable property is requisitioned or acquitted under this Act, there shall he paid compensation the amount of which shall be determined in the matter, and in accordance with the principles, hereinafter set out, that is to say 

(a) where the amount of compensation can be fixed by agreement, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement, 

(b) where no such agreement can be reached, the Deputy Commissioner shall, having regard to the provisions of clause (e), assess compensation for the immovable property, and shall after obtaining the approval of the Government thereto, give immediate notice of the assessment to the person or persons interested.

This takes me to the question raised from the side of Defendant Petitioner that the Suit is barred under Section 14 A of the Act of 1948. 
The Question now is answered. 

Section 14 A of the Act. 1948 reads thus: 

Except as expressly provided in this Act, no Civil Court shall entertain any Suit or application against any order passed or any action taken under this Act and all suits and appeals pending in any such Court against any order passed or any action taken under this Act shall abate with effect from the date of coming into force of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963. 

30. On a plain reading of Provision contained in Section 14A of The Act of 1948 it is manifestly clear that Civil Court shall not entertain any Suit or application against any Order passed or any action taken under the Act and all Suits and Appeals pending in any such Court against any order passed or any action taken under the Act shall abate with effect from coming into force of (Emergency) Requisition of Property (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963. Since Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 did not challenge any order passed or any action taken under The Act of 1948. Plaintiff filed the Suit for Decree of Permanent Injunction under Section 54 of The Specific Relief Act. The Plea taken from the side of Defendant-Petitioner that the Suit is hit under Section 14A of The Act of 1948 is not tenable in law, and as such, the plea stand rejected. In this context it can be conveniently said that even if Jurisdiction of Civil Court is excluded, still Civil Court got the Jurisdiction to examine into cases where the provision of The Act have not been complied with or the Statutory Tribunal has not acted in conformity with Fundamental Principles of Judicial Procedure. Support for the proposition is sought is drawn from a series of Judicial Authorities of Superior Courts of The Sub-continent. Basic Judicial Authority is -Secretary of State vs. Mask and Co. AIR 1940 PC 1055= 44 CWN 709 P.C. 

31. The Judicial decision of Privy Council had been and has been consistently followed by Superior Court of this Sub-continent. Learned Assistant Judge on consideration of Pleading evidences, Exhibits and other materials on record held: 

I. There is no bar in proceeding with the Suit as framed, that is, Suit as framed in maintainable. 
II. Plaintiff got the cause of action to file the Suit. 
III. Suit is not barred by Limitation. 
IV. Plaintiff proved his ownership and possession on Suit Property, and. as such, entitled to gel reliefs as prayed for, and, thus, granted Decree of Permanent Injunction in favour of Plaintiff. 
32. Learned Additional District Judge as Last and Final Judge of fact, also, duly considered pleadings, evidence of parties, provisions of Law embodied in The Act of 1948 and other materials on record came in full agreement with the decisions reached at by Learned Assistant Judge and maintained those Decisions. Decisions rendered by Learned Assistant Judge and Learned Additional District Judge are well founded, well grounded and well reasoned and those do not suffer from any illegality and legal infirmity and those do not warrant any interference by this Court in its Civil Revisional Jurisdiction under Section 115 (I) of The Code of Civil Procedure. 

33. In the Result, Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition under Section 115 (1) of The Code of Civil Procedure got no merit and the same is discharged however, without any order as to costs. 

34. Lower Courts Records be sent down as immediate as possible. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 22nd day of August, 2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2934 of 2000)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 22nd day of August, 2007 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2934 of 2000 discharging the Rule.

2. Facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that respondent Nos. 1-21 as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 116 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land on the averment that Saroda Proshad Roy Chowdhury was the owner of the suit land and on his death, his legal heirs were continuing to possess and enjoy the suit land who settled 1.00 acre land to the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by an amalnama who paid rents for a long time and after his death, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. The plaintiffs came to know from a reliable source that defendant No. 4 was trying to record 1.66 acres land in his name. As on 26.06.1989, defendant No. 4 with the help of some other unruly persons, tried to take possession of the suit land by applying force, the plaintiffs were compelled to institute the suit.

3. The suit was contested by defendant No. 4 (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) by filing written statement denying the material statements of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit, the suit was barred by limitation and was also barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The plaintiffs had neither any right nor any title in the suit land. The defendant had been enjoying the suit land along with other lands by taking settlement from the Zamindari State of Kashimpur. The then landlords accepted rents from him and his name was recorded in the S.A. Khatian, but due to mistake only .66 acre land out of 1.6 acres was recorded in the name of the Government. After the S.A. record the defendant filed an appeal being No. 4493/69/70 before the Settlement Office. Thereafter 1.00 acre land was recorded in the R.S. Khatian in the name of the defendant. The defendant filed Title Suit No. 266 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title in respect of .66 acre land since his name was not recorded in respect of the said area of the land which was pending. The defendant did not pay rents because the case was pending. The defendant paid the rents to the landlord and he had been possessing the suit land.

4. At the trial, both the parties produced evidence, oral and documentary.

5. The learned Subordinate Judge on conclusion of trial by his judgment and decree dated 23.11.1998 dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 132 of 1999 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka having heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 29.02.2000 allowed the same and decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellant Court, the defendant filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. A Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule. Against the impugned judgment and order, the defendant preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1626 of 2007 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the submissions made by their learned Counsel as under:

"The learned Counsel submits that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court being the last Court of fact committed an error of law in relying on the Ext.2, the amalnama of the plaintiff ignoring the fact the "প্রদর্শন-২ ঐ কাগজটিতে যে ০৫-০৯-৯৪ বাংলা তারিথ লেখা আছে তাহা ভিন্ন কালিতে এবং ঘষামাজা আছে।” as found by the trial Court. Thus both the Court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division on misreading the material evidence on record arrived at an erroneous finding that the plaintiff opposite party has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. He further submits that the appellate Court below as well as the High Court Division fell into an error of law in finding that the plaintiff opposite party is in possession of the suit land totally ignoring the S.A. and R.S. Khatians of the suit land which are documents of possession and collateral documents of title. He next submits that in decreeing the suit and affirming the appellate decree by the High Court Division, both the Courts fell into an error of law in not noticing the material fact that the plaintiff Nos. 1-16 are heirs of Gani Munshi but how the suit land is possessed by them have not been described in the plaint nor there is cogent oral evidence to show that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land rather P.W.1, the plaintiff No. 1 in his deposition stated that he used to possess the suit land through his father in law. He lastly submits that the finding of the High Court Division as well as the appellate court below that the suit is not barred by law is also based on non-consideration of material evidence on record inasmuch as P.W.1 in cross candidly admitted that "১৯৭৮ সনে খাজনা দিতে গিয়াছিলাম তহসিল অফিসে। কিন্তু তহসিল অফিস খাজনা নেয় নাই।" This P.W. 1 in his chief also stated that " নালিশী সম্পত্তির খাজনা প্রদানের জন্য তহসিল অফিসে গেলে তহসিল অফিস খাজনা গ্রহণ করে নাই। পরে জানিতে পারি যে নালিশী সম্পত্তি ৪নং বিবাদীর নামে রেকর্ড হইয়াছে এবং .৬৬ শতক জমি ভূল দেখানো হয়েছে।”" Thus it is clear that the suit is barred by limitation inasmuch as in 1978 at least the plaintiff Abdul Hai came to know that the land is not recorded in their name."

6. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellant, has, in fact, reiterated the points on which leave was granted. Therefore, we are not restating his argument.

7. Mr. Abdul Momen Chowdhury, learned Council, for respondent Nos. 1-21, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

8. From the judgment and decree of the trial Court, it appears that it dismissed the suit on the findings, inter alia, that amalnama exhibit-2 which was the basis of the plaintiffs' case was dated 05.09.1924 B.S., but the date was written as " প্রদর্শন-২ ঐ কাগজটিতে যে ৫/৯/২৪ বাংলা তারিখ লেখা আছে তাহা ভিন্ন কালিতে এবং ঘষামাজা আছে।” the two witnesses, who deposed to prove the amalnama, the evidence of PW6 was wishful and false, because the documents filed by the plaintiffs, such as, amalnama, the rent receipts appeared to have been created subsequently; no proof was filed to show that PWs 5 and 6 used to serve at Kashempur Zamidari Estate; the story that the (PWs 5 and 6) knew the hand writing of the persons who granted dhakhilas and that they used to serve with them was also wishful and false; after the abolition of the zamindari system in 1950, the plaintiffs did not pay any rent in respect of the suit land and the SA and the RS records were also not prepared in their names; the plaintiffs failed to give any reason of non recording of their names in the SA and the RS khatians; therefore, he cause of action on which the plaintiffs filed the suit was also wishful one and false; the areas of the suit land was 1.66 acres. The plaintiffs claimed to be the heirs of one Sheikh Goni Munshi, but they did not say in the plaint how did they possess the suit land as the heirs of Gani Munshi and nothing was also stated by the witnesses who tried to prove their possession in the suit land; PW 1 stated that he used to possess the suit land through his father-in-law, Ghughur Ali, but they said fact was not stated in the plaint. The PWs. Stated in their deposition that for the last 4/5 years, the plaintiffs stated possessing the suit land, but actually no such witness was examined in Court; from the deposition of the witnesses, it appeared that the plaintiffs' side used to look after the suit land, but possession and looking after were not the same thing; amongst the defendants, defendant No.4 got the suit land by way of settlement and exhibit- 'Kha' and 'Kha(1) showed that the suit land was recorded in his name in the SA and the RS records in respect of 1 acre land. So it was proved that defendant No. 4 got 1 acre land by way of settlement; DWs 2 and 3 proved that defendant No. possessed the suit land; no document was filed to prove that the suit land was the Government land; no document was also produced to show that the Government possessed the suit land through its lessees; besides defendant No.4 also filed Title Suit No. 16 of 1993 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in respect of .66 acre land out of 1.66 acres land which was pending. The trial Court concluded that from the facts and circumstances of the case, it was proved that the defendant was the owner of the suit land and that the plaintiffs had no title and possession therein. The trial Court further found that the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit inasmuch as from the plaint, it appeared that the defendant with his cohorts tried to dispossess the plaintiffs on 26.06.1989 which gave the cause of action to file the suit. Whereas, in paragraph 2 of the plaint, it was stated that the plaintiffs came to know from the reliable source that the defendant was trying to record his name in the khatian which gave cause of action to file the suit. The trial Court further held that the SA record was finally published in 1961-62 and long thereafter the suit was filed and as such, the same was barred by limitation.

9. From the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, it appears that it after noting down the submissions of the learned Advocate of the respective party found title of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the basis of amalnama, exhibit-'2'. The Appellate Court did not at all reverse the finding of the trial Court in respect of amalnama, exhibit- '2'. The Appellate Court did not also reverse the finding of the trial Court as to the competence of PWs 5 and 6 in proving the rent receipt and the amalnama. The Appellate Court did not also reverse the finding of the trial Court that the documents filed by the plaintiffs, such as, the amalnama and the rent receipts appeared to have been created subsequently. The Appellate Court in one sentence said that on sifting the evidence of the plaintiffs, it was found that the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land without discussing the oral evidence and also considering the fact that the SA and the RS records were prepared in the name of the defendant. The Appellate Court found that the suit was not barred by limitation in as much as the plaintiffs filed the suit after coming to know about the record of rights in the name of the defendant; it did not consider the fact that the Tahsilder refused to accept rent from the plaintiffs in 1978, whereas the suit was filed only on 18.07.1989, i.e. after 11 years.

10. Let us see first whether the Appellate Court was correct in holding that the suit was not barred by limitation as the same was filed by the plaintiffs after they had come to know about the wrong recording. It is by now a well settled legal proposition that mere non-recording of a suit land in the name of the plaintiff or party concerned does not extinguish his title and a cause of action to file a suit would arise when title is invaded and the fact of invasion of title of the plaintiff in the suit land has to be gathered from the facts and circumstances of a particular case. In the instant case, plaintiff No. 1 as PW1 in his examination-in-chief stated that they went to Tshsil Office in 1978 to pay rent, but the Tahsil Officer did not accept the rent. This clearly shows that the plaintiffs very much knew about the wrong recording of the suit land, in 1978, in fact, was clear invasion on their title in the suit land, but they filed the suit only on 18.07.1989, i.e. after 11 years of the refusal of rent from them by the Tashil Office. Therefore, the knowledge of wrong recording as stated by the plaintiffs was not correct and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the trial Court rightly found the suit barred by limitation.

11. Now another pertinent question arises for consideration whether the plaintiffs could maintain the suit for simple declaration of title to the suit land in view of the assertion made in paragraph 7 of the plaint that on 26.6.1989, the defendant (defendant No.4, the appellant herein) accompanied by his hired goondas numbering 40/50 came to the suit land to dispossess them there from, but on being resisted by them and hearing the hue and cry, the neighboring people came running and then the defendant left the place and declared that he would come soon and would dispossess them. Besides paragraph 7, in paragraph 6 also, the plaintiffs stated that they were innocent, peace loving and law abiding citizen of the country, the defendant who was influential, dangerous and greedy person, was applying force to dispossess them from the suit land and also threatening them with dire consequences. We consider it better to quote paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint which read as:

“৬। বাদীগণ শান্ত নিরীহ সত ও আইনের প্রতি শ্রদ্ধাশীল অপর দিকে ৪নং বিবাদী প্রভাবশালী দুর্ধষ, দুর্নাম ও লোভের বশবর্তী হইয়া জোর পূর্বক বে-আইনী ভাবে বাদীগনকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বে-দথল করিতে জোর জবর দস্তি করিতেছে এবং প্রাণ নাশের ও হুমকি দিতেছে। ৪নং বিবাদী আইনের প্রতি শ্রদ্ধাশীল নয়।

৭। যেহেতু ৪নং বিবাদী ও তাহাদের ভাড়াটিয়া গুন্ডা পান্ডা আনুমানিক ৪০/৫০ জন লোকসহ বিগত ২৬-৬-৮৯ ইং তারিখে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে জোর জবর দস্তিতে বে-দথল করিতে আসিলে বাদীগণ তাহাদের বাধা দেন এবং আত্নচিতকারে আশে পাশের লোকজন চলিয়া যাওয়ার সময় জোর চিতকারের বলিয়া যায় আকস্কিকভাবে শীঘ্রেই ৪নং বিবাদী ও তাহার লোকজন বাদীগনকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বে-দখল করিবে এবং প্রয়োজন বোধে প্রাণ নাশ করিতেও দ্বিধাবোধ করিবে না বিধায় বাদীগন অসহায় নিরুপায়া ও বাধ্য হইয়া ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে অত্র স্বত্ব সাব্যস্তের ঘোষণা ডিক্রির মোকদ্দমা হুজুরের আদালতে দায়ের করিয়াছেন এবং অত্র মোকদ্দমা নিষ্পত্তি না হওয়া পর্যন্ত যাহাতে অবৈধ ভাবে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বাদীগণকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বে-দখল করিতে না পারে।”

12. In paragraph 7, in fact, the plaintiffs attempted to make a prayer for temporary injunction so that they could not be dispossessed during the pendency of the suit.

<u>13. From the above quoted statements of the plaint, it is apparent that on the date of filing the suit or on the date of cause of action for filing the suit, the plaintiffs were under the constant threat of dispossession by the defendant. Therefore, they were legally obliged either to pray for permanent injunction or to pray for confirmation of possession as consequential relief along with the prayer for declaration of title to the suit land within the meaning of the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, but they did not make any such prayer and they only prayed for a declaration of title to the suit land. Therefore, the plaintiffs' suit was not maintainable in law within the meaning of the said proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It is true that the trial Court dismissed the suit not on the ground of its maintainability, but on other grounds as noted down hereinbefore, but this being a point of law and maintainability of the suit goes at the very root of the matter and when this has come to the notice of this Court, this Court cannot overlook the provision of law.</u>

14. The High Court Division, like the Appellate Court while affirming the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court did not at all notice and consider the factual finding arrived at by the trial Court about the amalnama, the basis of the plaintiffs title, the maintainability of the suit and therefore, erred in law in discharging the Rule.

15. For the discussions made above, we find merit in the appeal and accordingly, the same is allowed. The impugned judgment and order affirming those of the Appellate Court is set aside and those of the trial Court are restored.

16. There will be no order as to costs.

End.
