full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker J: The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Kishoreganj in Other Appeal No. 25 of 2005 disallowing the same affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.11.2004 and 10.01.2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Kishoreganj in Other Class Suit No. 225 of 2000 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 (now dead) one Abdul Jabbar as plaintiff instituted the Other Class Suit No. 225 of 2000 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kishoreganj Sadar against the present petitioner for a declaration that the deed of exchange being No.6203 dated 19.09.2000 in the office of the Sub-registrar, Kishoreganj relating to the suit property is collusive and ineffective with a further prayer for recovery of khash possession in the suit property described in the schedule of the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff namely Mali Hossain. At the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, 08(eight) sons and 03 (three) daughters became the heirs. Among the heirs of the original owner by way of an amicable partition the brother of the plaintiff Bonde Ali obtained 333/4 decimals of land out of 45 decimals of land and the other sisters jointly obtained 111/4 decimals of land and possess their portion. Subsequently, by a sub-kabala deed dated 15.05.1980 Bonde All transferred 83/4 decimals of land to the northern side of two plots and handed over possession therein in favour of the purchaser-plaintiff. The plaintiff in respect of the property of his sisters borga possess 111/4 decimals of land. Among the sisters of the plaintiff, Amena Khatun and Rahima Khatun transferred their share in favour of their sister Jobeda Khatun and Jobeda Khatun subsequently by a sub-kabala dated 01.10.2000 transferred her land measuring 10 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the plaintiff by way of sub-kabala dated 30.11.1998 purchased 25 decimals of land in the suit plot and possessed therein and in this way the plaintiff acquired 45 decimals of land in two plots. On 08.10.2000 the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendant and the defendant without the knowledge of the plaintiff at night erected a tin-shed but in the suit property, having no manner of valid right, title, interest therein which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the defendant-petitioner in short is thus that Bonde Ali is the full brother of the plaintiff who is the vendor of the defendant-petitioner. The suit land was acquired by Bonde Ali in his share amicably after the death of his father and thereafter on 19.09.2000 by way of a registered ewaj deed the defendant-petitioner acquired title and possession in the suit property. The defendant-petitioner obtained possession within the knowledge of the plaintiff and other villagers of the locality and through survey by a government-surveyor but the plaintiff out of ill-motive to grab the property suppressing the facts have instituted the suit.

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing five different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 25.11.2004.

5. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred the Other Appeal being No. 25 of 2005 in the court of learned District Judge, Kishoreganj which was transmitted to the 1st Court of learned Additional District Judge, Kishoreganj for hearing and disposal. The learned Additional District Judge hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2012.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioner have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay and status quo.;

7. During hearing of this Rule Mr. Moira Uddin, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Subrata Saha with Mr. Kamal Hossain the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the courts below during passing the judgment and decrees in favour of the plaintiff committed illegality. The learned Advocate further submits that it is the settled principle of law that the plaintiff is to prove his own case and he is not entitled to get a decree on the weakness of the defendant. But the learned trial court shifted the responsibility of proving the case on the defendant illegally and subsequently the appellate court also disallowed the appeal without proper appreciation of law and thereby both the courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff examined 04(four) witnesses including himself as P.W.1 but he could not prove his plaint case and on the contrary the defendant examined two witnesses including the defendant No.1 as D.W.1 who successfully proved the case of the defendant. But the courts below on non-consideration and non-reading of evidence illegally decreed the suit. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below in fact not at all discussed any evidence. The learned Advocate argued that, P.W.1 in his testimony did not state the time of his alleged dispossession but the learned trial court held that at night the dispossession took place. The 2nd witness of the plaintiff P.W.2 in his deposition did not state the day and date of dispossession and P.W.3 also did not state the specific day and date of dispossession. The last witness P.W.4 is the witness of a deed given by his mother dated 01.10.2000 and thus the courts below without proper assessment of evidence on records arrived an erroneous findings that the plaintiff have been successfully proved his possession and dispossession over the suit property. Furthermore; no boundary man as stated from the side of the plaintiff has deposed to prove the possession and dispossession of the plaintiff while the brother of the plaintiff-D.W.2 who was the vendor of the defendant-petitioner categorically proved the case of the defendant and disproved the case of the plaintiff. But the learned court below misdirected himself on such evidence and without any basis held that the defendant did not examine any witness to substantiate his case. The learned Advocate Mr. Moinuddin at a stage of his submissions submits that the most important witness of this case is D.W.2 who is the vendor of the defendant and this witness in his deposition specifically asserted that at the time of giving possession of the suit land to the defendant No.1 the plaintiff and his other brothers and sisters were present and there is no specific denial from the side of the plaintiff with regard to this which amounts to admission of the matter. In the plaint the plaintiff sought for three separate reliefs but the learned courts below without giving two reliefs gave only one relief which is vague and indefinite and that there was no separate issue even on the ewqjnatna deed of the defendant-petitioner and also there is no issue on possession and dispossession specifically.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality, irregularity or infirmity. The learned Advocate further submits that in disposing the appeal the learned lower appellate court in deciding the merit of the appeal committed no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned trial court during deciding the onus of proof committed no illegality, since it is the specific case of the defendant-appellant-petitioner that his predecessor-in-interest i.e. from whom he obtained the suit land acquired right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property by way of amicable partition between the co-sharers of the heirs of admitted original owner Male Hossain and it was further specific case of the present petitioner that by way of a registered that ewajnama deed dated 19.09.2000 the defendant-petitioner acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and immediate after that ewajnama; the possession was delivered in favour of him and in exchange of a property the brother of the plaintiff-opposite party, Bonde Ali executed and registered the alleged ewajnama in his favour in respect of his property which he acquired. The learned Advocate submits that among the prayers of the plaintiff in the original suit although the trial court in respect of 'recovery of khash possession' passed his verdict in the order-portion of his judgment and decree but within the body of the judgment the learned trial court decided all; after proper evaluation of the evidence on record and that the plaintiff have valid right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff at night and it is a bonafide omission of the learned trial court in the order-portion, despite; in the findings and decisions he has categorically arrived at a decision as to the matter of controversy between the parties and with regard to possession and dispossession of the suit property and although the learned court below not framed specific issue but he has categorically arrived at a decision as to the possession and dispossession in the suit property. The learned Advocate argued that the plaintiff to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient credible evidence in support of his case have successfully discharged his onus in proving his respective case and both the courts below on preponderance of evidence rightly decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal in favour of the plaintiff. Under the purview of Order V rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure the learned trial court rightly discussed and decided each and separate issue on the basis of the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and no objection or challenge was raised from the side of the defendant-petitioner as to the acquisition of title by virtue of two registered documents in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. In the pleadings of the defendant neither in his written statement nor in the appeal-memo as well as in the ground of this revisional application the title documents of the plaintiff has been challenged or objected from the side of the defendant-petitioner. In the memo of appeal the defendant-petitioner has totally waived his claim as agitated during hearing of this revisional application. The learned Advocate submits that the courts below prior to their observation and findings rightly assessed the evidence on records and in absence of any sort of illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate court the impugned judgment and decree cannot be interfered with. Two registered Kabala deeds (Exhibit 3, 4); by which the plaintiff acquired title in the suit property are not challenged from the side of the defendant and the learned courts below with regard to this rightly held that the plaintiff had title and interest in the suit property and the plaintiff also possessed the suit land but the defendant out of ill-motive dispossessed him. In fact; there is no evidence from the side of the defendant as to his alleged acquisition of title in 45 decimals of land in the suit holding by the vendor of the defendant-petitioner Bonde Ali who is the full-brother of the plaintiff-opposite party. Therefore; obviously the disputed ewajnania deed was a forged document which was not regally acted upon and the learned courts below concurrently with regard to this holding the view that the defendant-appellant-petitioner in fact did acquire any property by dint of his so called ewajnanur deed which is nothing but a paper transaction only. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below at the time of disposal of the original suit and subsequent appeal hearing the arguments advanced from the side of the respective parties decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal on the basis of evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties on proper appreciation of law and inasmuch as there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice the Rule have got no merit to succeed. The learned Advocate Mr. Subrata Saha in his concluding submissons submits that this civil revision is not maintainable inasmuch as before filing of this rev isional application the defendant-appellant-petitioner preferred a review application before the lower appellate court which was awaiting for disposal on merit being No. Review Case No.02 of 2012 under Order XLV11 Rule 1/2 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in which the plaintiff-respondent filed a written objection. Before disposal of that Review Case the defendant-appellant out of ill-motive suppressing the actual facts practicing fraud upon the court have instituted this revisional application and as such the civil revision is not maintainable.

10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides having gone through the impugned judgment and decree along with the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court and the evidence on records as adduced from the sides of the respective parties with all other documentary evidence including connected papers on records it transpires that admittedly the suit property originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff and his brothers namely Mali Hossasin. It is also an admitted position that at the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, eight sons and three daughters inherited the property left behind him. The brother of the plaintiff Bonde Ali by way of amicable partition among the heirs of Mali Hossain obtained .333/4 acres of land and the sisters obtained .111/4 acres of land in the disputed holding. It is the case of the plaintiff that Boucle Ali after getting .333/4 acres of land transferred 8% decimals of land from the suit two plots in the northern side by way of sub-kabala deed and thereby exhausted his share therein and the plaintiff use to borga possess the land of his sisters measuring an area of 111/4 decimals of land. The further case of the plaintiff to the original suit is such that his sister Jobeda Khatun by a sub-kabala deed dated 01.10.2000 transferred 10 decimals of land in his favour and the plaintiff by virtue of another sub-kabala deed dated 30.11.1998 acquired 25 decimals of land in the suit plots. It was contended from the side of the plaintiff in his pleadings that in the night following 08.10.2000 the defendant No.1 who is allegedly acquired the suit land from the defendant No. 2 Bonde Ali disposed him (plaintiff) from the suit property by erecting a tin-shed but therein.

11. The contrary case as it appears from the pleadings of the contesting defendant No.1 is such that his vendor Bonde Ali is the full-brother of the plaintiff who acquired the suit land through an amicable partition among the brothers and sisters who are the heirs of admitted original owner Mali Hossain. It was further contended from the side of the defendant-petitioner that there was a ewaj exchange between he and Bonde Ali in respect of the suit property on 19.09.2000 A.D. and possession was delivered in his favour by Bonde Ali on the very date and the defendant-appellant-petitioner after erecting his dwelling but use to possess the suit property since then.

12. To substantiate the respective cases of the, parties the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party adduced 04 (four) witnesses and submitted 05 documentary evidence which was marked as Exhibits No.1-5.

13. Vis-a-vis; from the side of the defendant-appellant-petitioner two witnesses were examined in support of his respective case but did not life any documentary evidence to substantiate his case.

14. It is a fact that, at the demise of the original owner, the plaintiff along with his 07(seven) brothers, 01(one) mother and 03(three) sisters inherited the property left behind their father Mali Hossain. Taking into consideration to that the learned trail court rightly held that the onus in proving the fact that one of the twelve heirs of Mali Hossain Bonde Ali obtained the total 45 decimals of land in the suit holding is required to be proved from the side of the defendant as it was his pleadings specific case. Inasmuch as it was the positive case of the defendant that the other brothers and sisters deprived of getting their shares the onus of proving the same lies upon the defendant under section 103 of the Evidence Act.

15. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records it is noticed that within the contents of the plaint the plaintiff to the suit contended that his brother Bonde Ali in collusion with the defendant No.1 have created a forged ewajnama deed in respect of the suit property which in fact did not acquire by Bonde Ali. It was further contention within the pleadings of the plaintiff that on 08.10.2000 corresponding to 23rd Ashwin, 1407 B.S. at night the defendant behind his back all on a sudden dispossessed him from the suit property and erected a tin-shed but therein. It further appears that in the schedule of the plaint the land in dispute has been properly specified from the side of the plaintiff and in the written statement or in the memo of appeal including the grounds of the revisional application the defendant remained silent in challenging or stating that the suit land is not specified or that it is vague and indefinite.

16. Apart from this; from the case records it is obvious to note that after disposal of the appeal being Title Appeal No.25 of 2005 by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2012 by the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Kishoreganj the defendant-appellant preferred a Review Miscellaneous Case under Order XLV11 rule 1/2 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and this case was registered as case No.02 of 2012 "Review (Chhany)". In that case the plaintiff-respondent appeared and filed written objection. That Review Miscellaneous Case was preferred on 30.05.2012 and it's written objection was filed on 06.09.2012. While this Revisional Application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure has been preferred on 14.11.2012 before disposal of the aforesaid Review Miscellaneous Case No.02 of 2012 in which the defendant-appellant-petitioner has obtained the present Rule with an interim order of stay on 19.11.2012 and an order of status quo on 27.05.2014.

<u>17. Taken into consideration of the above facts and circumstances of the case it can be easily held that there has been a willful suppression of facts from the side of the defendant-appellant-petitioner during institution of this Civil Revision before this Court which amounts to fraud upon the court as well as the parties.</u>

<u>18. Be that as it may; it can be easily decided that fraud has vitiated the entire proceedings of this civil Rule, even then; for the interest of justice especially for complete justice I like to draw my attention over the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties in support of their respective cases. During trial of the original suit being Other Suit No.225 of 2000 the witness No.1 is the plaintiff himself who is Abdul Jabbar. The plaintiff in his testimony affirmed his respective pleadings as cited in his plaint and it is within his deposition that his father Mali Hossain purchased the suit land from the original owners Hem Chandra Dutta and 04 others prior to 50/60 years. Subsequently, at the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, 08 sons and 03 daughters inherited his property. There has been an amicable partition among the brothers and sisters and the plaintiff acquired the suit land in his exclusive possession but one of his brother Bonde Ali out of ill-motive transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant No.1 namely Abdul Barik by a forged ewajnama deed by dint of which Abdul Barik on 08.10.2000 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property. With regard to the documentary evidence produced from the side of the plaintiff I find that the respective S.A. Khatian No.786 has been marked as Exhibit-1 and the subsequent deeds has been marked as Exhibits-2, 3, 4 and 5. The disputed exchange deed being No.6203 dated 19.09.2000 is exhibit-2 from the side of the plaintiff.</u>

19. In the context of specification of the suit land with regard to boundary; the plaintiff at a stage of his cross-examination categorically testified that to the western side of the suit land Abdul Hamid, to the northern side the plaintiff himself and to the western side one Mohor Uddin possess.

20. P.W.2 Abdul Khalek in his examination-in-chief corroborated the case of the plaintiff with regard to possession and dispossession of the suit land. In his cross-examination he categorically testified at a stage that the area of the suit land is 10 decimals and it's plot number is 1796 and to the western side of the suit land one Abdul Hamid and to the northern the plaintiff himself and to the southern side one Mohor Uddin possess. With regard to dispossession this witness testifies at a stage that in his own eyes he found that the defendant No.1 in the night at 11/12 P.M dispossessed, the plaintiff from the suit land and prior to that the plaintiff had possession.

21. P.W.3 Anu Miah is another possession and dispossession witness of the plaintiff who has testified that the defendant possess the suit 10 decimals of land from four years and lie dispossessed forcibly the plaintiff therefrom at night and prior to that dispossession; the plaintiff possessed. In the cross-examination P.W.3 again testified categorically about the dispossession of the plaintiff by the defendant No. l.

22. The last witness Md. Nazrul Islam is the attesting witness of a transfer deed dated 01.10.2000 in respect of 10 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff by his mother. This witness proved this document and identified his signature therein which has been marked as exhibit-5.

23. On the other hand; D.W.1, Abdul Khaleque the defendant No.1 himself in his testimony categorically stated in the examination-in-chief that in the month of 'Ashur' the ewaj was held and from the date of ewaj he possess the suit land. He expressed his inability in his cross-examination to state the plot number of the suit land but admitted to the effect that the suit land originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff namely Mali Hossain and Mali Hossain died leaving behind 08(eight) sons, 03(three) daughters and 01(one) wife and there has been amicable partition among the sons and daughters of Mali Hossain. During cross-examination the defendant-appellant-petitioner frankly admitted at a stage that Bonde Ali did not obtain possession in his (D.W 1) exchanged land which was given by him (D.W.1) in favour of Bonde Ali in exchange of the suit land. The courts below giving much emphasis on this admission rightly arrived at a conclusive decision as to the nature of the disputed deed of exchange (Ewajnama) which admittedly did not take it's effect. In his (D.W.1)cross examination lie further admitted that he cannot say the Bengali date and year of his taking possession in the suit land and he also cannot say the Bengali date of his Ewaj deed.

24. D.W. 2 Md. Bonde Ali contradicted D.W.1 as to the taking over and giving over possession in favour of defendant No.1 by him. He also like D.W.1 in his cross-examination expressed his inability to state that on what month he handed over possession in favour of the defendant No. 1.

25. Consulting the disputed deed of exchange being No.6203 it appears to me that in the month of `Aswin' this was executed which is totally contradictory with the defendant's case.

<u>26. With regard to the mistake done by the trial Judge during disposal of the original suit as to the framing of respective issue on possession and dispossession of the suit land our Apex Court in the case of Ismail Ullah being dead his heirs Baizidulluh and others —vs.- Sukumar Chandra Das, 1986 BLD(AD)251 held that the judge of the trial court can always amend the decree if there is a bonafide mistake done by him.</u>

<u>27. When an order is passed by a court on being misled or due to its own mistake and such issue not raised or decided in appeal or review, the court of law is obliged to correct the mistake when true facts are brought before it and make such order as necessary for ends of justice. The court must not allow its process to be abused by any unscrupulous person, ["Ref. Master Abdul Aziz —vs.- Aboni Mohar Mukharjee and others; 30 DLR (SC)221]</u>

<u>28. Having regard to the provisions of law 1 have every reason to inclined such a view that this Court as already have elaborately discussed the matter of possession and dispossession from the sides of the respective parties on assessment of evidence adduced from the sides of the parties rectified the defect of framing respective issue from the side of the trial court to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court and for complete justice such sort of observation is inevitable for dispensation of justice among the litigants.</u>

29. In view of the discussions and findings referred to above 1 am constrained to hold such a view that the courts below during disposal of the suit and its subsequent appeal committed no such material illegality or infirmity by dint of which it can be held that the judgment and decision is passed on misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice rather; I have already pointed out earlier that this revisional application is barred ab-initio inasmuch as suppressing the facts it has been preferred which was willful from the side of the petitioner and consequently; it amounts to fraud upon the party as well as upon the court, which has vitiated the entire proceedings.

30. Be that as it may; I have nothing but to hold such a view that this Rule is liable to be discharged forthwith with a cost of Tk. 5,000/-(Five thousand) payable by the petitioner.

31. In the result, the Rule having no merit is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1s1 Court, Kishoreganj in Other Appeal No.25 of 2005 disallowing the same affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.11.2004 and 10.01.2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Kishoreganj in Other Class Suit No.225 of 2000 is hereby affirmed.

32. The order of stay and status quo granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

33. Communicate the judgment and order at once.

34. Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: This appeal is directed at the instance of the defendant-appellant against the judgment and decree dated 24.11.2010 and 30.11.2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 245 of 2004 decreeing the suit on contest.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal in a nut shell can be stated thus the present respondent No.1 as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 245 of 2004 in the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka against the defendant-appellant and others for declaration of title with a further declaration that the R.S. khatian in the name of the defendant-appellant is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. In the original plaint the plaintiff's case in short is as follows that the disputed property appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.6231 originally belonged to one Felu Sheikh. At the demise of Felu Sheikh one Fakir Chand and others inherited the property left behind the C.S. recorded tenant Felu Sk. Subsequently, the entire land of the suit plot has been transferred in favour of the father of defendant No.1 Jogendra Kumar Guha by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 04.08.1943 A.D. In the disputed plot the entire area was 1776 "ajutangsha" and out of that portion of land 833 "ajutangsha" was acquired by the government in L. A. Case No.36/1950-51. The remaining 943 "ajutangsha" is situated beside a road. To the north-east side of the road the land measuring 412 "ajutangsha" and to the north-west side of the road there is 531 "ajutangsha" of the property lies and those lands has been recorded in the name of Jogendra Kumar Guha during S.A. operation. From S.A. khatian No.1214 the land measuring 560 "ajutangsha" was declared to dispose of by the S.A. recorded tenant Jogendra Kumar Guha. There has been a bainapatra in respect of 943 "ajutangsha" of land on 01.01.1958. Jogendra Kumar put his signature behind the baina-patra and in respect of the suit land there was an additional bainapatra dated 15.05.1960 but Jogendra Nath Guha subsequently denied to hand over possession in favour of the purchaser Abdul Mannaf. Thereafter an Other Class Suit No.82 of 1963 was filed by Abdul Mnnaf in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract. In that suit after service of summons-notice Jogendra Kumar did not contest and accordingly the suit was decreed ex-parte on 06.02.1967. That decree was modified subsequently on 19.09.1967 A.D. The decree-holder Abdul Mannaf obtained the kabala deed registered through court on 28.06.1967. The further case of the plaintiff was such that there was a sweeper-passage in the disputed property and while that passage was closed arbitrarily; there was a Civil Suit being No.51 of 1967 in the 61h Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka and that suit was ended pursuant to a solenama. In the said suit it was decided by a decree that 44 "ajutangsha" properties would be used jointly for the aforesaid purpose. In the year 1969 the kabala purchaser Abdul Mannaf transferred the suit land in favour of his brother Abdul Majid by a kabala deed dated 02.07.1969. Thereafter, Abdul Majid mutated his name in the city corporation and paid rent. Abdul Majid after payment of electricity, water and gas connection bill regularly use to possess that land through his tenant. During the continuation of such constrictive possession peacefully while the concerned `tahsil' office denied to take rent from the plaintiff he felt aggrieved of that and his title is clouded which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for declaration of title and a further declaration that the R.S. record is wrong and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. The contrary case of the defendant-appellant in short is thus that Jogendra Kumar Guha by a registered deed No.4478 purchased the suit land measuring .1776 "ajutangsha" from the heirs of Felu Sk. Out of that land in L.A. Case No.36/1950-51, 0.833 "ajutangsha" land has been acquired by the government and Jogendra Kumar obtained compensation amount of Tk.2619/- (Taka two thousand six hundred and nineteen). There is a mention within the remaining portion of land that to the right sight of that; there exist a road. Defendant's further case is such that Jogendra Kumar entered into a contract with Md. Abdul Mannaf in respect of the land and after getting baina money executed a bainanama deed. There was an agreement between the parties that the remaining consideration money will be paid within one year of the bainanama but the plaintiff’s side in spite of several requests did not execute and register a sale deed. The defendants thereafter on 16.12.1960 sent a registered notice but getting that registered notice the recipient of the bainanama did not pay any heed of it and accordingly the baina patra became cancelled. Thereafter; a Title Suit being No.82 of 1963 was instituted but there was no service of summons-notice upon the defendant and the defendant expired on 13.03.1965. Subsequently; an ex-parte decree was obtained collusively without service of summons notice. Subsequently, the present defendant came to learn that the disputed property has been sold out by Abdul Mannaf in favour of his brother Abdul Majid. The R.S. record of right in the name of defendant-appellant is correct but the plaintiff on false allegations suppressing the facts instituted the original suit.

4. The learned trial judge during trial of the original suit after examining four Witnesses from the side of the plaintiff and one witness from the side of the defendant on perusal of the exhibited papers from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.11.2010.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant have preferred this appeal to set aside the impugned judgment and decree.

6. During hearing of this Appeal Mr. Md. Aminul Islam, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the appellant while Mr. Ashim Kumar Mollik the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the respondent.

7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the learned trial court during passing the impugned judgment and decree committed illegality and infirmity. It was further submitted from the side of the learned counsel of the appellant that the impugned judgment and decree is based on surmise and conjecture. The learned Joint District Judge, misdirected himself on the point of facts and laws and in fact the original suit was hopelessly barred by the law of limitation as it was not filed within the statutory period of limitation from the date of knowledge that the R.S. record of right stands recorded in the name of defendant. The learned Advocate further submits that the bainanama which was registered on 01.01.1958 was not acted upon as the conditional clause of the bainapatra was not complied with within time which was automatically stood cancelled. But the learned trial court without grapsing the actual facts as well as the evidence on records decreed the suit on contest arbitrarily. The learned Advocate also submits that the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties were not properly evaluated during deciding the issues of the original suit and the assessment of evidence is not proper in deciding the merit of the case. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court during disposal of the original suit failed to apply his judicial mind and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

8. As against the aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent opposing the appeal memo controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the defendant-appellant and opposing the appeal submits that the learned trial court was quite justified and legal in deciding the merit of the suit and there is no infirmity or illegality in deciding the fate of the issues framed during disposal of the original suit on merit. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff to the suit while felt aggrieved due to the wrong R.S. record of right the cause of action accrued in other words when the title of the plaintiff was denied by dint of R.S. record of right the cause of action of the original suit arises and from that date, the original suit was instituted well within the period of limitation prescribed in the Limitation Act and the learned trial court rightly held that the suit is not barred by the law of Limitation. The learned Advocate also submits that the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties were properly assessed in its true perspective and the learned Joint District Judge conclusively held after proper sifting of evidence and appreciation of law that the plaintiff to the suit have every right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property and he has successfully discharged his onus in proving his case by adducing sufficient oral and documentary evidence. The witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiff successfully proved the respective case of the plaintiff and they have corroborative one-another in respect of the right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the R.S. record of right which has been prepared in the name of the defendant is wrong, collusive and never acted upon which has been reflected through the evidence adduced from the side of the defendant and thus the learned trial court committed no wrong or illegality whatsoever in decreeing the suit on contest.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and have gone through the respective cases of the parties including the documentary evidence and oral evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties and the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka.

10. On perusal of the case records it transpires that during pendency of the original suit both the parties to the suit have adduced evidence in support of their respective cases and it is an admitted position that the suit property described in the schedule of the plaint had been owning and possessing by the C.S. recorded tenant Felu Sheikh. The respective C.S. khatian no.6231 has been produced which has been marked as Exhibit-2, and there is a presumptive value of it's correctness.

11. It has been contended from the side of the plaintiff that the entire land of the suit plot is 1776 "ajutangsha" and out of that land 833 decimals was acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.36/1950-51.

12. The plaintiff's witness P.W.1 Maleh Mohammad who is the "power of attorney" of the plaintiff and as power of attorney by virtue of a deed dated 29.10.2009 (Exhibit-1) P.W. I deposed on behalf of the plaintiff. With regard to the area of the suit land there is a clear recital from the side of the P.W.1 that 552 decimals of land is being possessed by the plaintiff. For the suit land the S.A. khatian is 1214 and its plot No. is 4003. The subsequent R.S. khatian which has been challenged from the side of the plaintiff is 3111. Swearing a supplementary affidavit the plaintiff to the suit submitted some papers relating to an order passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka in connection with Mutation Case No.105/2004 vide Annexure-`A'.

13. Having gone through the papers it appears that during pendency of the original suit an appeal case being No.3-105/04 in respect of mutation of the suit land was instituted by the present appellant against the order dated 02.11.2004 passed by the Additional Commissioner (Rev.), Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No.85 of 2001. The case which was pending during pendency of the suit in the Court of Chairman, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka has been disposed of in favour of the present appellant vide judgment and order dated 11.12.2013. In the said order Chairman of Land Appeal Board held that the plaintiff-respondent No.1 Mst. Noor Begum use to possess the suit land for more than 60 years and it was further held that in respect of the suit land the present plaintiff-respondent have got her right, title and interest. The mutation in respect of R.S. khatian No. 3111 has been corrected pursuant to the order of the Chairman dated 11.12.2013.

14. Besides this; we have come across from the plaint of the original suit No.245 of 2004 that the plaintiff-respondent in the said suit in paragraph No.16 specifically contended that on 17.05.2004 while the plaintiff went to pay rent to the concerned tahshil office, the Tahshilder stating about the R.S. record of right denied to accept rent from the plaintiff and thereby the plaintiff became aggrieved and thus her title to the suit land was threatened which constituted the cause of action of the original suit. With regard to this; the learned court below in his findings and decisions rightly held relying upon the decision of this court that mere wrong record does not cast any cloud on the title of anybody until and unless the title is denied. With regard to this; the witness No.1 of the plaintiff testified specifically that on 23.05.2004 he went to the local tahsil office to mutate the name of the plaintiff for payment of rent but the concerned Tahshilder stating about the R.S. record of right denied to mutate the name of the plaintiff and thereby the plaintiff felt aggrieved. Hence; obviously this is the cause of action of the original suit and from this date; within the statutory period of limitation the original suit was instituted.

15. In this context; in the case of Government of Bangladesh —vs. - AKM Abdul Hye and others 56 DLR(AD)53, their lordships held in paragraph-7 that,

"The law is now settled that against the wrong record of rights the person whose interest is affected by such wrong recording need not file suit questioning legality of the record of rights so prepared and finally published within 6 years from said date or from the date of knowledge of such wrong record of rights, but he is required to file the suit seeking declaration of title within six years from the date the person in whose name record has been wrongly prepared and finally published raises claim denying his claim on the basis of wrong record. But if the entry in the record of rights is made the cause of action one has to file the suit within 6(six) years from the dale of final publication of the record of rights and not from the date of the certificate of the final publication."

<u>16. Apart from this; consulting the relevant evidence on records we find that to corroborate the case of the plaintiff excepting the power of attorney P.W.1 Maleh Mohammad, the witness No. 2 Md. Naharul Hoque Mollik specifically testifies that he is a tenant under the plaintiff for the last 10/12 years and he has got the rent receipts in respect of his rented house. With regard to the possession of the plaintiff P.W.2 has been corroborated by P.W.3 Shibu Chandra Sarker and P.W.4 Sheikh Abdur Rob and all these witnesses have been thorough cross examined from the side of the defendant, but none of them appears to have been discredited except some minor discrepancies. They have corroborated one-another in respect of the respective case of the plaintiff which has been properly evaluated by the learned court below.</u>

<u>17. Vis-à-vis; the solitary witness of the defendant, D.W.1 Jagannath Dey in his testimony tried to establish the case of the defendant but from the trend of his cross-examination it is evident from the face of the records that he has failed to establish the case of the defendant rather it has been established from his testimony that the defendant have got no possession and interest in the disputed property. The learned trial Judge during passing the impugned judgment and decree vividly discussed the evidence on records and arrived at a conclusive decision as to the issues framed which were four in numbers. The exhibited documents including the oral evidence have been evaluated properly in it's true perspective. Besides this; in respect of right, title, interest and possession it has been categorically held after proper sifting of evidence that the plaintiff to the suit have got her right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and the only hurdle in respect of land is the R.S. record of right which stands recorded in the name of the defendant. In fact; the R.S. record of right has got no presumptive value of it's correctness and especially when it is rebutted by tangible evidence as the instant case be; there is nothing to hold such a view that the R.S. record has been correctly prepared.</u>

18. Be that as it may; we have every reason to incline such a view that the plaintiff to the suit in order to succeed have discharged her onus of proof under the purview of section 101 and 102 of the Evidence Act. Accordingly; the learned trial court was quite justified in holding such view that the issues are decided in favour of the plaintiff and there is no legal embargo in obtaining the decree as prayed for by the plaintiff.

19. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above; we are constrained to hold such a view that the appeal have got no merit to succeed.

20. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 24.11.2010 and 30.11.2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 245 of 2004 in decreeing the suit is hereby upheld and confirmed.

21. Communicate the judgment and order at once and send back the Lower Court's Record immediately.

End.

lawyer:

parties:
Md. Shamsul Haque ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md. Jabbar and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 05.10.2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2294 of 2009).
full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. This appeal by leave is directed from a judgment of the High Court Division which has affirmed the judgment of the lower appellate court. The appellate Court reviewed the judgment of the trial court.

2. Short facts are as under:

<u>3. Plaintiff instituted other Class Suit No.44 of 1995 for partition on declaring nullity of a deed against the appellant Md. Shamsul Haque and others. Plaint case in short is that on Md. Chulai was the original owner of 2.07 acres of land by purchase from one Sattar Mia by kabala dated 18th April, 1952. Said Md. Chulai died leaving 06 sons, wife Sakhina and another wife Rabeya who died during his life time. Three sons of Md. Chulai namely Md. Rawshan, Md. Asgor and Md. Sabdar through Chulai's predeceased wife rabeya sold out their entire 7 (seven) anal share of 90 decimals to one Min Uddin and Akbar by registered kabala dated 13th December, 1972. Said Alim Uddin and Akbar subsequently sold the said 90 decimals of land to the defendant Shamsul Haque in 1988. The remaining 1.17 acres of land remained in the possession of Chuli's other three sons Md. Jabbar, Md. Sattar Mia and Md. Abbas and wife Sakhina Khatun. Subsequently Md. Abbas died unmarried and his other two full brothers Md. Jabbar and Sattar Mia and mother Sakhina Khatun inherited his share. While Md. Jabbar, Md., Sattar Mia and their mother Sakhina Khatun were in possession of their 1.17 acres of land, they came to know in the middle part of 1994 that 06 decimals land out of their 1.17 acres were acquired by the government for the purpose of construction of a bypass road and that the defendant Shamsul Haque, by creating a false deed was trying to receive the compensation money Md. Jabbar, Md. Sattar and their mother then procured the certified copy of the deed and confirmed that Shamsul, Haque created the deed by false personation.</u>

4. Thereafter Md. Jabbar, Md. Sattar,  Mia and their mother Shakhina Khatun tiled the Suit in respect of their 1.17 acres of land and also for declaration to the effect that the deed 5;08.2008 in respect of their 1.17 acres of land is forged and not binding upon them.

5. Defendant No.1 (defendant) Shamsul Haque contested that suit by filling written statement. His case is that the plaintiffs sold said 1.1.7 acres of land to him in the year 1974 at a consideration of taka 2000/-and delivered possession; that though a sale deed was executed on 25,08.1974, it could not have been registered for want of necessary permission of the government which was necessary during the relevant time for transferring 'Bihari refugess' land that after withdrawal of that restriction, the deed was registered in favour of the defendant and that the defendant has been possessing this 1.17 acres of land for more than 20 years by exercising his right little and interest therein.

<u>6. The trial Court dismissed the suit holding that the defendant acquired a good title by adverse possession act that the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land extinguished. The lower appellate court decreed the suit and the High Court Division has affirmed the judgment. Leave was granted to consider as to whether the High Court Division is justified in affirming the judgment of the appellate court negating the claim of adverse possession by the defendant in the suit land.</u>

7. Though the plaintiff's claim partition and entitlement of compensation money assessed by the Government in L.A. Case No. 69 of 1993-94 the only point requires to be considered is whether the defendant has acquired title b adverse possession in the suit land. It the defendant's plea of adverse possession is established, the plaintiffs cannot get a decree as prayed for.

8. There is no dispute that the plaintiffs entered into an agreement for sale of the suit land with the defendant on 25th May, 1974, but ultimately they did not execute a sale deed. Defendant claimed that the plaintiffs had executed a sale deed on 5th July 1980 but the courts below disbelieved the defendants claim which clear findings that the defendant had created the deed by false personation. Taking these admitted Nets into consideration let us consider whether the defendant can claim adverse possession in the suit land to the basis of the possession taken in pursuance of the execution of the agreement dated 25th May, 1974.

<u>9. There is no dispute that a person cannot claim title by adverse possession in the land in dispute on the basis of an agreement even if his possession exceeds over the statutory period. To constitute title by adverse possessions, the claimant must prove his hostile possession over statutory period to the knowledge of the real owner. The High Court Division, Therefore, has rightly observed, that to constitute adverse possession, One must be in possession for the statutory period openly, in assertion of his own title as owner and denying the title of the true owner, and such open hostile possession, under claim of ownership, must be to the knowledge of the true owner; mere possession without the necessary ingredients of adverse possessions however long continued, does not and cannot ripen into title by adverse possessions ". In talking the above views it has relied upon the case of Dalimunessa Bewa V. Md. Hashmat Ali. 61 DLR (AD) 8.</u>

10. The High Court Division held that though the defendant is in possession of the suit land for more than 20 years, he is not in possession as of right with a notorious hostile claim of exclusive title in arriving at such finding; the High Court Division has not assigned any reason on appraisal of the materials on record. The plaintiffs have admitted the defendant's possession of the suit land over 20 years, but according to them, the defendant was their borgader. The plaintiffs. However failed to prove their claim of giving borga cultivation. They led no legal evidence in support of their such claim. In the absence of legal evidence, the court may draw adverse inference against the assertion of claim under the rules of evidence.

11. The trial court on assessment of the evidence on record observed that the plaintiff’s witness (P.W.!) admitted that since 1994 the defendant had stopped giving the usufructs of the suit land. This is the solitary evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiffs did not adduce any other evidence in support of giving borga cultivation of the suit land to the defendants. Therefore, the trial court has rightly held that the plaintiffs could not substantiate their claim by producing witness of giving borga cultivation to the defendant. It held that P.W.1 had admitted about the execution of unregistered deed in favour of the defendant.; that he failed to prove his plea of borga cultivation of the suit land; that the defendant has proved possession of payment of rent and mutation of his name in respect of the suit land; that the plaintiffs have failed to give any explanation for non-payment of rent; that this fact proved that the plaintiff's sold the suit land by an unregistered deed and that the plaintiffs title in the suit land extinguished by advice possessions. These findings are in conformity with law and we find nothing wrong in the conclusions arrived by the trial court.

12. The court of Appeal below notice that the plaintiffs had failed to give any explanation for non-payment of rent and held that this non-payment' of rent proved that the plaintiffs sold the suit land by an unregistered deed; that the defendant on payment of consideration money of the suit land has been in possession but that his claim of hostile possession has not been established. In arriving at such conclusion, the court of appeal below has not assigned proper reasons despite that it has found that the defendant has been in possession on payment of the sale price of the suit land to the plaintiff. It seemed that the court of appeal below was confused on the question of accrual of title by adverse possession.

<u>13. If the possession is actual, open, uninterrupted, notorious, exclusive and continuous over a statutory period, it confers an indefeasible title upon the possessor. The extent of the title acquired by adverse possession depends on the extent of the claim or right under which possession is obtained and kept, To constitute possession in the claim of the possessor must of be effectively realised in the facts, It is sufficient if the possession is overt without any attempt of concealment. That possession to the extent to which it is capable of demonstration must be hostile, notorious and exclusive to make it adverse and will only extend to the land in actual occupation of the wrong doer. All these elements of hostile possessions are present in this case and the defendant has been able to prove it by oral and documentary evidence, The trial Court has rightly held the extinguishment of plaintiff's title by adverse possession.</u>

14. The High Court Division in the Premises has committed error of law ignoring those elements and thereby committed fundamental error in affirming the judgment of the appellate court in failing to consider that the initial onus lies upon the plaintiffs that the defendant is in possession as borgadar of the plaintiffs. If the plaintiffs claim is not substantiated by legal evidence, the court can draw adverse inference against them. The plaintiffs have miserably failed to substantiate their claim and they have not adduced any iota evidence in this regard. On the other hand the defendant is claiming hostile title against the plaintiffs by proof of oral and documentary evidence. Though he entered possession by execution of an agreement, according to him he has purchased the suit land on payment of the sale price. His positive claim is that as there was restriction for selling land of non-Bengali citizens, the deed could not have been registered. The court below concurrently found in favour of the defendant. Admittedly the defendant in assertion of his right has mutated his name and has been paying rent to the government and possessing the suit land to the knowledge of the plaintiffs since 1974 claiming as owner.

15. This possession of the defendant in assertion of his right is no doubt to be treated as hostile possession to the knowledge of the true owners. The plaintiffs are totally silent why they did not take any step for eviction of the defendant had he been a borgadar under them even after knowing that the defendant has mutated his name in the record-of-right and has been paying rent. Therefore, the court of appeal below wrongly disbelieved the claim of adverse possession by the defendant or in the alternative, it can be said that the court of appeal below has failed to comprehend the accrual of title by adverse possession in a disputed land. The High Court Division committed similar error in affirming that judgment. The defendant has been possessing the suit land as of right adversely to the knowledge of the plaintiffs for 20 years. He has mutated his name and has been paying rent throughout this period. If this act of possession in assertion of right is not matured into title, what else will create title by adverse possession? Therefore, the trial court is perfectly justified in dismissing the suit.

<u>16. The High Court Division has totally overlooked the facts-proved by the defendant in support of his claim of hostile possession and on misconception of law it has affirmed the judgment of the court of appeal below. The case considered by the High Court Division squarely supports the case of the defendant. The High Court Division misconstrued the decision in failing to consider that in that case, it has been held that if there is a complete ouster by asserting hostile title the plaintiff's title is extinguished, inasmuch as, he has lost his title by the acts of the defendant who having been in possession denying the plaintiff's title openly.</u>

17. The appeal, is therefore, allowed without any order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:

Mr. Md. Habibur Rahman, Advocate, for the opposite parties
parties:
MD. SUKUR ALI AND OTHERS
Vs.
MD. HASHAR ALI AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J: The judgment of reversal has been called in question by invoking the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court on laying an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, in which a single judge of this Hon'ble court on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 26.04.2004 and 02.05.2004 passed by learned Joint District Judge 1st Court, Chuadanga in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2000 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 19.07.2000 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Alamdanga, in Title Suit No. 507 of 1983 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts for disposal of the instant Rule is that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed title suit No. 507 of 1983 in the court of Assistant Judge, Alamdanga, stating that one Domon Mistry was the C.S. recorded tenant while he had been living on the suit land by constructing but he brought his daughter and son-in-law Kheru Shaikh to live with him. Domon Mistry on 29.09.1232 B.S gifted the suit land since then Kheru Shaikh had been living on the suit land.

3. Kheru Shaikh died leaving two sons in plaintiff No. 1 and Ramjan who is the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 2 to 8. One son of Domon Mistri was Rahim. He died leaving defendant Nos. 4 to 8 as his heirs. Defendant No. 9 purchased five decimals of land from the plaintiffs on the east of the suit land and has been residing there erecting hut.

4. During S.A. survey operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of defendants subsequently on the basis of the wrong S.A. record the plaintiffs claimed title of the suit land. Then the plaintiffs filed a title suit No. 374 of 1980 renumbered as T.S. No. 507 of 1983. While the suit was pending the plaintiffs were forcibly dispossess by the defendants from the suit land. Then the plaintiffs amended the plaint and prayed for declaration of title and khas possession.

5. The learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 24.09.1992 on contest. Thereafter the defendants preferred an appeal being title appeal No. 154 of 1992 in the appellate court the defendants Nos. 15 and 16 Jahangir and Jamal prayed for being added as parties to the suit. Then on the prayer of the defendants appellants the learned Additional District Judge-1 Chuadanga remanded the suit to the lower court for retrial.

6. The defendants contested the suit stating that the C.S. recorded tenant of the suit land was Domon Mistri. He did never gifted the suit land to his son in law Kheru Shaikh. The contesting defendants are the owners of the suit land by way of inheritance and purchase. The plaintiff appellant had no title to the evict land. The judgment of the trial court should be affirmed.

7. The learned Joint District Judge found, that all the parties admitted that the C.S. recorded owner of the suit land was Domon Mistri. The defendant Nos. 12(ka) to 2(cha) and 4 to 8 stated that Domon died leaving the only son Rahim while he was in possession and enjoyment of the land he died leaving the only son Dukhi wife Raushan nessa and three daughters in Rahaton Jahaton, Ranganessa, They sold 25 decimals of land to the defendant No. 1 Negarun by a registered kabala dated 16.12.1959 Negarun out of 25 decimals of land sold 12.. decimals to the defendant No. 2 Putiruddin. Putiruddin made a gift of 61/4 Decimals of land to Ansar Ali. He gifted 2 decimals of land to his sister Elemun Nessa. Subsequently Ansar Ali and Elemun sold the land to Shukur Ali and others by three kabalas.

8. The added defendant Nos. 10 to 14 contested the suit stating that Domon left behind three sons in Rahim Box, Karim Box and Yasin and died unmarried. Their shares were inherited by Rahim Box and their two sisters. After the death of Rahim Box his land was inherited by his wife Raushan Nessa, son Dukhi and three daughters in Ranga Nesa, Rahatan and Jahatan. Fate Nessa made a verbal gift of her share to her sister Aijan alias Maijan after the death of Aijan alias Maijan her own share and which she inherited form her sister Fate Nessa in total 121/2   decimals was inherited by her two sons being Abul Hossain and ismail and husband Kheru Shaikh. The heirs of Rahim Box sold 121/2 decimals of land at a consideration of taka 92/- through an unregistered deed dated 05.03.1995 to Negarunnessa and Kabil Mondal. Thus their interest in the land ceased to exist. Two sons of Aijan Alias Maijan and her husband Kheru Shaikh. Sold 121/2 decimals of land at a consideration of Tk. 96/-through an unregistered kabala dated 06.03.1955 to Negarun Nessa, but out of mistake in the S.A. record the name of Kheru Shaikh has been recorded.

9. Subsequently Dukhi Shaikh became an adult and claimed back his land which was sold earlier. At that time Negarun nessa on 16.12.1959 by a registered kabala numbered 8789 purchase that 121/2  decimals of land. But the scribe by mistake inserted 25 decimals instead of 121/2 decimal in the deed Negarun Nessa out of 25 decimals sold 121/2 decimals on 06.07.1961 by a registered kabala numbered 6511 to the defendant No. 2 Putiruddin. During the R.S. operation the names of Nigarun Nessa and Putiruddin Shaikh were recorded in respect of 25 decimals of land jointly with other co-sharers on the death of Nigarun Nessa for her 121/2 decimals of land was recorded in the name of her brother Elahi Box. He was in the enjoyment of that land jointly with Putiruddin Sheikh. He sold 61/2 decimals of land of the suit plot to Ansar Ali, Putiruddin gifted some land to the heirs of his deceased son Shamsher ali. Ansar All and Elejan sold 61/2 decimals to the defendant Nos. 1 to 14. The learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 19.07.2000 was pleased to dismiss the suit. Being dissatisfied with and aggrieved by the judgment and the decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Alamdanga in title suit No. 507 of 1983 the plaintiff filed an appeal being title appeal No. 109 of 2000. The appeal came up for hearing in the court of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chuadanga. The Appellate Court by his judgment and decree was pleased to allow the appeal with direction upon the defendant Nos. 10 to 14 to surrender the possession of .06 decimals of land to the plaintiff appellate within 45 days in default the plaintiff appellant will be entitled to enforce the direction through the court.

10. Mr. Hasan Shahid Kamruzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in support of the rule while Mr. Md. Habibur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties 1 to 4 and 6 to 13.

11. Mr. Hasan Shahid Kamruzzaman, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the Joint District Judge 1st Court, Chuadanga, in his judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2000 committed an error of law in not taking into consideration the two kabalas dated 05.03.1955 and 06.03.1955 respectively and thus came to an error decision in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

12. Learned Advocate further submits that the learned Joint District Judge, Chuadanga committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in holding that the plaintiffs proved the deed of gift made by Eomon Shaikh in favour of Kheru Shaikh and as such the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge Chuadanga is liable to be set aside.

13. He further submits that the appellants and respondents died during the pendency of the appeal and the fact being not brought on record the appeal suffered from the defect of parties. And the learned appellate court committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in passing the decree against dead person.

14. Learned Advocate next submits that that the unregistered kabalas dated 05.03.1955 and 06.03.1955 have been proved by D.W. 2 Shukur Ali and D.W.S Ismail Biswas who attested the thumb impression of the vendor though the scribe Monsor All could not call as a witness on account of his being dead by that time. The learned Advocate for the petitioner in course of his submissions has drawn my attention to the deposition of D.W.8 Ismail Biswas who deposed “আমার নাম মোঃ ইসমাইল বিশ্বাস ৬/৩/৫৫ তারিখের অরেজিস্টীকৃত দলিলটা মুনসুর আলী লিখেছিল ৷ আমি তার সঙ্গে কাজ করেছি ৷ তার হাতের লেখা আমি চিনি ৷ আমি ইসাদী হিসাবে এই দলিলে সই করি ৷ দাতাদের সই আমি বঃ কঃ করি ৷ ৫/৩/৫৫ তারিখের অরেজিস্টীকৃত দলিলের দাতা নাবালক দুঃখী শেখ পক্ষে মাতা বসনেছা রাহাতন জাহাতন গ্রহীতা নেগারন নেছা, এই দলিলের লেখক মনসুর। আমি দাতাদের টীপ ঊহ্য করি এবং ইসাদি হিসাবে সই করি।”

15. The learned Advocate next submits that the plaintiffs opposite parties failed to prove the gift in favour of the plaintiff no. 1 Abdul Hossain in as much as the P.W.1 deposed in cross examination “ভবন কে আমি দেখিছি ৷ ভবন যখন মারা যায় তখন আমার বয়স ৯/১০ বৎসর হবে৷ এখন আমার বয়স ৭০ বৎসরের কাছাকাছি।” He further deposed in cross examination “দানপত্রটি হয়েছিল ১৩৩৯ সালের ১২ তারিখে। তখন আমার বয়স

১২/১৩ বৎসর হবে। দানপত্রটি করে দিবার পর আমার নানা উবন মিস্তী ২/৩ বছর পর মারা যান এবং তখন আমার মামা রহিম জীবিত ছিল না।”

16. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff as P.W. 1 deposed beyond the pleading in the plaint and made out a different case. On the other hand Mr. Habibur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that the last court of fact rightly reversed the judgment and decree of the trial judge and came to his finding on due and proper consideration of both oral and documentary evidence on record. The last court of fact as a final court of fact after thorough discussion of the materials on record rightly arrived at his finding in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial judge as such the same does not call for any interference under the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court as laid down in section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

আমার নাম খোকাই শেখ। আমার বয়স ৮০/৮৫ বৎসর হবে৷ দোবনকে, খেডু এদেরকে দেখেছি এবং নিগারন, পটা অর্থাৎ পক্ষদের চিনি ও নাঃ জমি চিনি৷ নাঃ জমি থেকে ২০/২৫ হাত দূরে আমার বাড়ী এবং এটা আমার দাদার বাড়ী এবং নাঃ জমির পরিমান বলিতে পারিব না তবে নাঃ জমিটা বোধ হয় এক বিঘার উপরে হবে এবং এই জমিতে শৃকুর আলীরা এখন ঘর করে আছে এবং নাঃ জমির খানিক অংশে আবুল ও তার ভইিয়ের ছেলেপিলে আছে ও ফনি আছে৷ নাঃ জমি আগে দোবন মিস্ত্রী ছিল এবং দোবন মিস্তুী কিছু জমি বাদী পক্ষের পূৰ্বাধিকারী খেভুকে দান করেছিল এবং দোবনের বাড়ীতে তার খেভু থ1কির্ত এবং দোবন ঐ জমিতে ঘরে এবং দোবনের তিন ছেলে রহিম, করিম ও ইয়াসিন এবং রহিম তার ফুফুর কাছে ছিল ৷ এবং রহিম নৈহাটি গন্ডোগলে মারাযায় এবং ইয়াছিন ও করিম ও রহিম দোবনের আগেমারা গেছে৷ রহিমের ছেলে মেয়েরা অন্য জমিতে ছিল ৷

25. P.W.3 Shamsuddin deposed that:

আমার নাম শামসুদ্দিন ৷ পক্ষদের ও নাল জমি চিনি ৷নাঃ জমি থেকে দুই পা পরে আমার বাড়ী৷ দোবন ওখেড়ুকে দেখেছি৷ দোবনের জামাই খেভু ছিল৷ দোবন থেভৃকে জমি দান করে তাহা জানি৷ নাঃ জমিতে দানপত্রের পর থেকে খেডু ও তার ছেলেরা পর্যায় ক্রমে বসবাস করিয়া আসিতেছে৷ কাবিন, পৃটা, নিগারণ, এলেজান এদের চিনি এবং নাঃ জমিতে এবং বসবাস করেনাই বা গাছপালা লাগাই নাই বা দখলের কোন কাজকরে নাই৷ বন্দীদের দখলে কেহ বাঁধা সৃষ্টি করে নাই৷ শুককুর কিছু জমি প্রাচীর দিয়া দখল করে ব্লেখেছে এবংআবুল ও রমজানের ছেলে মেয়েরা ও ফনি বেদখল কৃতজমি বাদে বক্রী জমি দখল করিতেছে এবং মামলা চলাকালিন বেদখল করেছে ৷ বন্দীদের এবং ঘোষণা করে কোনখরিদ বিক্রি হয় নাই৷

26. P.W.4 Nanda Sheik deposed that:

আমার নাম নন্দ শেখ 1 পক্ষদের ও নাঃ জমি চিনি৷ নাঃ জমি আগে দোবন মিশ্ৰীর ছিল এবং তাকে দেখেছি এবং দোবনের বাস ছিল যেখানে এবং নাঃ জমি দোবন থেভৃকে দান করে এবং দানপত্রের বিষয় জানি এবং আমার সামনে লিখাপড়া হয়েছিল এবং লিখে কালিপদ বিশ্বাস এবং দানপত্রে দোবন টিপসহি করে তাহা দেখি নাই এবং দানপত্রে কাদের বিশ্বাস সহি করে ও বামে টিপসহি দেয় এবং দোবন লেখাপড়া জানিত না ৷ সাদা কাগজে লিখাপড়া হয়। নাঃ জমিতে খেড়ু বসবাস করেছি৷ নাঃ জমিতে দ্যেবনের ছেলে বসবাস করেনি ৷ নিগারণ, পুটা, এলজান নাঃ জমিতে কোন দিন দখল করে নাই৷ নাঃ জমিতে বাদীপক্ষরা পর্যায়ক্রমে নাঃ জমিতে বসবাস করিয়া আসিতেছে তাতে কেহ কোন দিন কোন বাধা দেয় নাই।

27. P.W.5 Shaban Sheikh deposed that

আমার নাম সাবান আলী ৷ ৭০ বৎসর বয়স আমার ৷ নাঃ জমিও পক্ষদের চিনি৷ আমাদের বুদ্ধিকাল থেকে দেখেছি খেড়ু ঐ বাড়ীতে জামাই হিসাবে বসবাস করিত এবং দোবনের সে জামাই৷ শুনেছি খেভুকে নাঃ জমি তার শ্বশুর দান করিয়াছিল ৷ খেভু ঐ জমিতে মারা যায় এবং থেড়ু মারা গেলে তার ওয়ারিশরা দখল কল্পিত এবং খানিক জমি তারা ফনির কাছে বিক্রী করেছে৷ নিগারণ, এলেজান, পুটা নাঃ জমি দখল করে নি এবং স্বত্ব দখলের বিষয়ে নাঃ জমিতে গন্ডগোল দেখি নাই এবং মামলা চলাকালে শুককুর আলি বেদখল করেছে৷

28. P.W.6 Hashor Ali deposed that

আমার নাম মোঃ হাসোর আলী৷ আমার পিতা মারাপেছে৷ সবার পক্ষে জবানবন্দী দিচ্ছি৷ আরজির বক্তব্যসত্য ৷ সত্য নয় যে, ১৩৩২ সালের ১০ই মাঘ ১২১/২ শতক জমি খেলাপি নিয়ে খাজনা ধার্যো ২৫ শতক জমি থেড়ু শেখকে ছেড়ে দেয় ৷ সত্য নয় যে, দোবন মিদ্রী মারাগেলে ৩ পুত্র ২ মেয়ে ওয়ারিশ থাকে ৷ সত্য নয় যে, রহিম, আইজান, খতেজান নালিশী জমি পেয়ে ভোগদখল করে ৷ সত্য যে, যে রইিম মারা গেলে ত্রী রশো, পুত্র দুঃখী ও ৩কন্যা … রাহাতন, জাহাতন ও অন্য এক মেয়ে থাকে। সত্য নয় যে, ফতেজান তার জমি আইজানকে দান করে দখল দেয়। সভ্য নয় যে , আইজান মারা গেলে তার জমি স্বামী ও ২ পুত্র ওয়ারিশ হিসেবে পায় ৷

29. D.W.1 Rahatunnesa deposed that

আমার নাম রাহাবুন্নেছা 1 আমি ১, ২খ, ২চ, ৪-৮ নম্বর বিবাদী পক্ষে জবানবন্দী করিতেছি ৷ সকলের পক্ষে মামলার শরীক ও কোন হিসাবে জবানবন্দী করিতেছি৷ না 8জমির সি, এস প্রজা ছিলেন দোবন মিদ্রী এবং তিনি আমার দাদা হইতেন এবং দোবন মিত্রী মারা গেলে রাহিম থাকে যেয়ে আমারা দেখি নাই৷ রহিম আমার পিতা ছিলেন এবং আমার পিতা রহিম তার বাবার জমিতে বিভিন্নভাবে দখল করিত। আমার পিতা রহিম মারা গেলে আমরা তিন বোন, এক ভাই ও মা ওয়ারীশ থাকি এবং আমরা নাল জমি বিভিন্ন ভাবে দখল কবিতায়। নাঃ জমিতে আমরা ভোগদখল করিতে থাকাকালে দৃঃখী দিং ১৬/১২/৫৯ ইং তারিখে রেজিস্টি কবলায় নিগারুন (১ন বিবাদী) কাছে নাল জমি বিক্রী করে ও দখল দেয় ৷ পরে নিগারুন নেছা নাঃ জমি খরিদের পর বসবাস করে…।

30. D.W.2 Shukkur Ali deposed that

আমার নাম শুককুর আলি ৷ আমরা সংযুক্ত বিবাদী ৷ সকল সংযুক্ত বিবাদী পক্ষে আমি জবানবন্দী করিতেছি। নাঃ জমি দোবন মিত্রীর ছিল। বোদন মিদ্রী মারা গেলে তার ছেলে রহিম ও মেয়ে আয়জান পেয়েছিল নাঃ জমি ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে ৷ রহিম মারা গেলে ছেলে দুঃখী, ত্রী রয়স্ক ও তিন কন্যা রাহাতন, যাহাতন ও রহাদা ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে পেয়েছিল ৷ দুঃথী ও তার মা রসন্দো নিগারন বরাবর ইং ৫৯ সালে ১২1/2 শতক জমি বিক্রী করে। নিগারুন ১২1/2  শতক জমি দখল করিতেন এবং নিগারুন তার স্বামীর সাহায়ে দখল কল্পিত বাড়ী করে এবং নাঃ জমিতে শাকসবজীর আবাদ করিয়া দখল করিতেন এবং এস এস রেকর্ড নিপারপ্স কাবিন ও থেড়ুর নামে হয়।

31. D.W.3 Harun-or-Rashid deposed that:

আমার নাম হারুন-আর রশীদ ৷ আমি সহকারী তহসীদার। আলমডাঙ্গা ৷ আমি আমি ইউনিয়ন ভুমি অফিসে চাকুরী করি৷ আমি ........... দাখিল করিলাম এবং ৭২নং গোবিন্দপুর মৌজার হোল্ডিং নং ৩১৯০ খতিয়ান নম্বর ২২৭8/১ দাগ নং ২৬৮৯ এ . ১২1/2 শতক জমি যাহা আবুল মন্ডল, পিতা-মৃত খেডু শেখ সাং নিজ নাম পত্তনকেস নং ৩২ lX-P2 /৮৪-৮৫ এবং ৯/১২/১৯৮৪ লিখা আছে এবং ব্লেজিস্ট্রারে তার নাম পত্তন হইলে আবুল মন্ডলের নামে ডি, সি, আর ইস্যু হয়। ডি, সি, আর, পাতা নম্বর ১৮৩৮২২৪ তাৎ ১৫/১২/১৯৮৪ এবং ৩২মিস কেস বুনিয়াদে এবং ডি, সি, আর, বহি নম্বর ৩৩/৮8…৮৫ দাখিল করি নাম এবং তার বুনিয়াদে বাংলা ১৩৮৭ সাল পর্যন্ত খাজনা আদায় করিয়াছি যার দাখিলা নম্বর এল- ৪ ২৪ ৬০ এ, সি ল্যান্ড হয় আদেশমতে খাজনা আদায় করিয়াছি৷

32. D.W.4 Idbar Ali deposed that:

আমার নাম ইদবার আলি 1 আমি দলিল লেখক I এস, আর, অফিসের দলিল নম্বর ৫৫০ এবং ১৫/০১/১৯৮৫ এবং ৫৫২ এবং ১৫/০১/১৯৮৫ এবং ৫৪৯ এবং ১৫/০১/৮৫ ইং তারিখের দলিল তিনটি এবং ৮৩৩৯ এবং১০/১ ১/১৯৮৫ তারিখের দলিল সহ উপরের চারখানা দলিলই ��মার লিখা এবং দলিল গুলিতে লেখক হিসাবে আমার নাম সহ আমার লিখা যাহা প্রদর্শনী (ক) সিরিজ।

33. D.W.5 Tufan Ali deposed that:

আমার নাম তুফন আলী। পক্ষদের ও নাঃ জমি চিনি৷ নাঃ জমির পাশ দিয়া চুয়াডাঙ্গা রাস্তা গ্রেছে৷ ঐ রাস্তা দিয়া আমরা যাতায়াত করি ফলে নাল জমি সব সময় দেখতে পাই৷ শুককুর আলি গং নাঃ দাগবন্দের রাস্তার পাশে পশ্চিম ভাগে দখল করে এবং জমিতে শুককুর আলিদের দখল করিতে দেখিতেছি এবং শুককূরদের টিনের ঘরের আগে দিন পাকা ঘরে স্থানে এবং শুককুররা নাঃ জমির তাদের অংশের একটি ভেটুন গাছ কেটে নিয়াছিল ৷

34. In order to arrive at a finding the learned trial judge examined 5 P.Ws and 8 DWs at the trial but in his impugned judgment the trial Judge did not discuss the deposition of P.ws and D.Ws at all without any discussion of oral and documentary evidence of the parties the trial judge passed the impugned judgment in a very perfunctory manner which has suffered from serious legal perversity material irregularity, non consideration of both oral and documentary evidence on record in arriving its finding and most illegally dismissed the suit.

<u>35. On appeal the last court of fact on due and proper consideration of the depositions of P.Ws and D.Ws and after thorough examination of the materials on record rightly arrived at his finding in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial judge on proper assessment of the evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment of the last court of fact does not call for any interference under the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court as laid down in section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. I find no merit in this Rule.</u>

36. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 26.04.2004 and 02.05.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge Court, Chuadanga in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2004 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 19.07.2000 and 25.07.2000 passed in Title Suit No. 507 of 1983 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge Alamdanga is hereby affirmed. Title suit No. 507 of 1983 is hereby decreed against the defendants. There will be no order as to cost.

37. The order of stay operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 26.04.2004 and 02.05.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Is' Court Chuadanga, in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2000 is hereby re-called and vacated.

38. Send down the lower court record along with a copy of the judgment to the concern court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.
