full_judgment:
ANM Bashir Ullah J: This First Appeal at the instance of the defendant-appellants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-6-2004 and 10-7-2004 respectively passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 30 of 2003 decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-10.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, in short, are that Md Meser Uddin filed Title Suit No. 1 of 1998 for declaration of his title along with confirmation of possession into the suit land. During the pendency of the suit he died, accordingly his legal heirs were substituted. Subsequently it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 82 of 2000 and lastly as 30 of 2003.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that 0.09 acres of land appertains to CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 12/87 of CS khatian Nos. 38 and 39 originally belonged to Sebesawor Das who settled the said land in favour of Sashi Kanto Dutta by a registered patta deed on 23rd Falgun, 1310 BS Sashi Kanta Dutta also settled the land in favour of Krishna Mohan Das and others by a registered patta on 11th jaista 1312 BS Krishna Mohan Das transferred the land by a registered kabala in favour of Gobinda Chandra Roy Chowdhury on 11th Vhadra, 1312 BS. The heirs of Gobinda Chandra Roy Chowdhury transferred the land by a kabala on 12th Boishakh, 1323 BS in favour of Bhabu Mohendra Chandra Dhar.

4. Babu Mohendra Chandra Dhar died leaving 5 sons. Surendra Chandra Dhar and others, the sons of Babu Mohendra Chandra Dhar transferred the land by a kabala dated 21-5-1939 in favour of Usa Rani Ghosh and Bijoy Hori Ghosh. Bijoy Hon Basu died leaving 2 sons Sudhir Ranjan Bosu and Subash Ranjan Bosu. Sudhir Ranjan Boshu as power of attorney of Usa Rani Gosh and Subash Ranjan Bosu and also on his behalf settled the land to one Abdul Karim Karwada by a registered deed dated 10-10-1952.

5. In the said instrument dated 10-10-1952 among other it was stated that the measurement of the land is 85' x 49' along with 21/2 passage in eastern side for sweeper. In the SA records of right the said land was recorded in the name of Abdul Karim Karwada. Abdul Karim Karwada gifted the said land through a heba deed to one Abdul Rouf Baburchi on 18-2-1960. Abdul Rouf sold the said land to one Kazi Serajul Islam by a kabala dated 10-4-1963. Kazi Serajul Islam sold the land to Meser Uddin, the original plaintiff (predecessor of the substituted plaintiffs) by a kabala dated 27-4-1964.

6. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Meser Uddin being the owner and possessor of the suit land paid rents to the government and constructed a 4 storied building on the suit land to live therein. The plaintiffs through amendment of the plaint claimed that from the very beginning Sebeswaor Das upto the last. kabala in favour of the plaintiffs Meser Uddin, the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12, 12/87 though were repeatedly in corporate in the instruments of transfer but in fact the suit land covered the CS and SA plot No. 12/87 corresponding to RS plot No. 75 of RS khatian No. 80 having an area of 0.05 acres of land and the same was recorded in the name of Profullah Roy Choudhury in the RS records of right. It is also averred in the plaint that when the plaintiffs approached the defendant No. 3 for taking the land development tax of 1402-1404 BS the defendant No. 3 declined to take the same from the plaintiffs for the wrong records of right. Thus the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of his title and confirmation of his possession.

7. The defendant No. 3 filing two written statements and additional written statement contested the suit. The statements of both the written statements are all most same and identical. The defendant in the written statement stated among others that the case is not maintainable in its present form and the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest into the suit land.

8. The case of the defendant, in short, is that 0.12 acres of land appertains to SA plot No. 12/88 corresponding to RS plot Nos. 75 and 76 of RS khatian Nos. 80 and 125 originally belonged to Non-bengali Abdul Halim and Harun. The suit land has been declared as abandoned property under President Order No. 16/72 and on the said land in one portion there are Sadar Thana land office, DB Police Office and in other parts different persons have been living taking lease from the government. Since the suit land is abandoned property, the present suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable.

9. It is also stated in the written statement that the plaintiffs did not purchase the land of plot No. 12/88 from its real owner. Since the plaintiffs were not in a possession of the said land in SA and RS operation their names have not been recorded. The plaintiffs have introduced a fictitious boundary in order to grab the suit land. So, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

10. The trial Court upon the above pleadings framed as many as 5 issues to dispose of the suit and at trial the plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses while the defendant examined 1 witness and the plaintiffs filed some documents which were marked as exhibits 1-8(ka) while the defendant filed certified copy of RS khatian No. 125 only marked as exhibit A and A(1).

11. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence and other materials on record decreed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree. The defendant-appellants being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the trial Court preferred this appeal in this Court.

12. At the time of hearing of this appeal Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr Dipayan Saha, the learned Assistant Attorney-General taking us through the plaint, written statements, issues, both oral and documentary evidence and the memo of appeal supporting the appeal and assailing the judgment of the trial Court submits that the trial Court erred both in law and facts in decreeing the suit, the trial Court did not at all consider that the plaintiffs could not prove their title into the CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 or 12/88, the trial Court did not at all consider that at any stage of the records of right neither the name of the plaintiffs nor his predecessor were recorded, the trial Court did not at all consider that the suit land is in the possession of the defendants.

13. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submits that since the plaintiffs could not show any document in support of the land which they allegedly purchased, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any decree for the suit land and the trial Court should have dismissed the suit. So, this Court should interfere in the judgment and decree, appealed against.

14. On the other hand, Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondents supporting the judgment of the trial Court submits that it is fact that in all the deeds related to the suit land starting from the transfer Sebeswaor Das to Sashi Kanto Dutta the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 were incorporated in the instruments but during pendency of the suit a local investigation was held into the suit land when the Advocate Commissioner found that within the boundary given by the plaintiffs the land of CS plot No. 12/87 corresponding to RS plot No. 75 attract to the suit land and accordingly the plaint was amended to that effect.

15. The learned Advocate also submits that if it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiffs had entered into the possession on the basis of some erroneous or invalid title deeds but since their possession has been proved for the long time starting from 1310 BS till filing of the suit, the plaintiffs have acquired indefeasible title into the suit land.

16. The learned Advocate also further submits that it is in the evidence of the defendant's witness that the DB Police Office and the AC (Land) office are situated in RS plot No. 76 but the plaintiff's clear case is that their suit land attract the RS plot No. 75 of RS kahtian No. 80 but the RS plot No. 75 will go to show that only 0.05 acres of land have been recorded in R5 plot No. 75. Although the plaintiffs are in possession of 0.09 acres of land but whenever there will be a conflict between the area of land mentioned in the plot number and the land found within the given boundary physically, the area of land found within the boundary will prevail and in support of his such contention the learned Advocate of the respondents referred the case of Md Alkas Ali Khan vs Monsur Ahmed Khan 1983 BLD (AD) 126.

17. The learned Advocate also submits that in the written statements among others it was averred that the suit land has been declared as abandoned property under President Order No. 16 of 1972 but the defendants at trial could not show papers that the suit land was listed in the gazette notification under Ordinance 54 of 1985. So, the oral claim as to the abandoned property of the suit land is not sufficient to hold that the suit land was declared as abandoned property at any point of time. The learned Advocate for the respondents in support of his such contention referred the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mir Md Imam Hossain 2 AIR (AD) 47.

18. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that there is no denial of the fact that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land having a 4 storied building thereon and there is no case in the hands of the defendant-appellants that anybody else other than the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. So, the trial Court considering all these facts and materials on record rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and since there appears no error or law and facts in the judgment of the trial Court, the same may kindly be upheld.

19. We have considered the above arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the plaint, written statements, evidence on record, the judgment pronounced by the trial Court and the appeal filed by the defendant-appellants.

20. In order to appreciate the arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on record. As we have noticed it earlier that the plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses at trial of them PW 1 Md Osman Gani, who is the plaintiff No. 2 stated that they have been possessing 0.09 acres of land which has been recorded in RS plot No. 75 of RS khatian No. 80, there is a road in the north of their suit land, in the south a filled up tank, in the east the building of Mr Harun where there is an office of defendant No. 2 and in the west Shamsuddin Ahmed and others.

21. He further stated that the arms of the suit land in the east-west side is 85 feet and in the north south side 49 feet having a passage of 2½' x 49' in its east side.

22. He also stated that while Gobinda Chandra Roy Choudhury was owner and possessor of the suit land transferred the same in favour of Mahendra Chandra Dhar. The 5 sons of Mahendra Chandra Dhar namely Surendra and others sold the suit land to Usa Rani in 1939, Sudhir Ranjan Basu on his behalf and also as power of attorney of Usa Rani and Suvas Ranjan Basu transferred the suit land in favour of Abdul Karim in 1952, Abdul Karim transferred the suit land to Abdur Rouf on 18-12-1960 and possession was delivered to Abdur Rouf, Abdul Rouf sold the suit land by a kabala dated 10-4-1963 in favour of Sirajul Islam and Sirajul Islam sold the land to their predecessor Md Meser Uddin on 27-11-1964, his father constructed a building on the suit land and paid land development taxes upto 1401 BS but declined to take rents for the years 1402-1404 BS.

23. He also stated that in RS plot No. 75 though 0.05 acres of land has been recorded but within their given boundary there is 0.09 acres of land which also attract the CS and SA plot Nos. 12/88 and 12/89. He also stated that they did not possess the land of RS plot No. 76. PW 1 proved the deed in favour of Abdur Rouf by Abdul Karim Karwada marked as Exhibit-1, the sale deed in favour of Kazi Sirajul Islam by Kazi Abdul Rouf dated 10-4-1963 marked as Exhibit-2 and also sale deed in favour of Meser Uddin by Kazi Sirajul Islam on 27-11-1964 marked as Exhibit-3. He also filed the certified copy of RS khatian No. 80, marked Exhibit 5 and CS khatian No. 38 marked Exhibit 5(ka).

24. In cross-examination of the defendants he denied the defendants suggestion that they are not in the possession in RS plot No. 75. He also denied the further defendants suggestion that their suit land did not cover the land of RS plot No. 75.

25. PW 2 Gopal Chandra Das stated that he is a Staff Moharar of Registration Complex, Tejgaon, Dhaka. He further stated that perpetual lease deed No. 561 dated 17-1-1953 has been registered in volum No. 253 at page Nos. 172-177. The certified copy of the lease deed in favour of Abdul Karim Karwada has been marked as Exhibit 6. There is no significant cross-examination of this PW 2. In the aid deed Usa Rani Das and others appear as the 1st party.

26. PW 3 Md Habib Ullah stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land from 1965 and before the plaintiffs All Kazi, Sirajul Islam and Abdul Rouf used to possess the suit land and before them. Abdul Karim Karwadi used to possess the suit land. In cross-examination PW 3 stated that he has no house at Narayanganj but in 1380 BS he used to live at Chashara, Karim Karwada was known to him from 1963-64.

27. PW 4 AKM Bodiruzzaman stated that the heirs of Meser Ali have been possessing the suit land and Meser Ali had purchased the land in 1964 who got the same from Karim Karwada. In cross-examination he stated that he has house at Narayanganj.

28. PW 5 Md Giasuddin, a Survey knowing Advocate Commissioner stated that he held a commission as per direction for the Court and submitted his report on 10-7-2002 in the Court. He proved the local investigation report marked Exhibit 7 and his signature in it marked exhibit 7(ka). In cross-examination he stated that he had related the CS and RS map, he took a fixed station in the west corner of plot No. 12/87 since there was a pillar. He also stated that the suit land covered the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS plot No. 12/88 and the land of RS plot No. 76 is situated just east of the land of RS plot No. 75 and in the land of RS plot No. 76 there are CID Police Office and AC (Land) office also.

29. The defendant examined 1 witness Md Abdur Rahman who in his testimony stated that he has been serving as a Land Assistant Officer. He also stated that the suit land has been recorded in SA plot No. 12/88 corresponding to RS plot Nos. 75 and 76. The RS plot No. 76 has been recorded in the name of the government as abandoned property while the land of RS plot No. 75 has been recorded in the name of Profulla and others. At the time of preparation of RS records of right, the plaintiffs were not in possession into the suit land and the plaintiffs did not raise their voice against RS records of right. In the suit land there are some government establishment like Union Vumi Office, CID office and Staffs quarters. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land. The DW 1 filed the certified copy of Rs khatian Nos. 125 and 80 marked exhibits A and A(1).

30. In cross-examination DW 1 stated that the RS plot No. 75 corresponds to SA plot No. 12/88 the land of RS plot No. 76 is the government land, the area of RS plot No. 75 is 0.05 acres. He denied the suggestion that RS plot No. 75 is covered by an area of. 0.09 acres of land.

31. These are the evidences that have been given by the plaintiffs and the defendants in the suit. It is almost admitted in the suit that though all the kabalas mentioned in the plaint were for the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 but after filing of the suit the plaintiffs amended the plaint claiming the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88 and those plot numbers were very much absent in the deeds mentioned in the plaint.

32. A local investigation was held in to the suit land by PW 5 who in his cross-examination stated that the lands found within the given boundary by the plaintiffs in the plaint covers the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88. The Advocate Commissioner's report shows the area of the land within the given boundary covers as .09 acres of land. The RS khatian No. 80 is going to show that RS plot No. 75 appears to have .05 acres of land.

33. The plaintiffs in order to prove their possession into the suit land examined PWs 1, 3 and 4. PW 1 stated that his father purchased the land from Sirajul Islam in 1964 and from then they are in possession into the suit land and his father constructed a building into the suit land to live therein. His such evidence is being strongly corroborated by the evidence of PWs 3 and 4. PWs 3 and 4 were cross-examined extensively by the defendants but there is nothing in their testimonies for which we can disbelieve their evidence as to the possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land.

34. There is also strong hint in the evidence of DW 1 regarding the possession of the plaintiffs. DW 1 in his evidence stated that the land of CS and SA plot No. 12/88 has been recorded in RS plot Nos. 75 and 76. He also stated that the land of RS plot No. 76 is the government property. There is no case either, in the written statement or in the evidence of DW 1 that the land of RS plot No. 75 was purchased and possessed by any other person other than the plaintiffs.

35. The trial Court on the right assessment of the evidence of PWs 1, 3 and 4 and DW 1 rightly found the uninterrupted possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land from 1964 till the filing of the suit in the year 1998. Though the correct RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88 were not mentioned in the purchase deed of Meser Ali dated 27-4-1964 but on the basis of the said wrong or invalid instrument Meser Ali had been into the possession of the suit land and he maintained his such possession till now. As such we are of the view that though the plaintiffs had entered into the possession of the suit land on the basis of invalid transfer deed but the plaintiffs have acquired good title for his long possession which is in all counts more than 12 years and our such views are strongly supported by the decisions of the cases of 1 MLR (AD) 71, 54 DLR (AD) 173 and also 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183.

36. It is the case of the plaintiffs that though the suit land has been recorded wrongly in RS plot No. 75 showing an area of 0.05 acres but in fact within the given boundary as appended in the deed of the plaintiffs of 1964 (Exhibit 2(ka) covers an area of 0.09 acre of land. This case of the plaintiffs has been supported by the Advocate Commissioner's report. PW 5 in his evidence testified that he held the local investigation into the suit land and filed a report on completion of the investigation. The report shows that he found 0.09 acres of land within the given boundary.

<u>37. In this case the learned Advocate for the respondents referring the case of 1983 BLD (AD) 126 submits that when there is conflict between the area of plot mentioned there and the area within the boundary of the instrument, the area within the boundary of instrument shall prevail over the area of the plot mentioned. We have gone through the reported case of Md Alkas Ali vs Mansur Ahmed Khan 1983 BLD (AD) 126. In the reported case it was held that conflict between the area of the plot mentioned in the plot Nos. and within the boundary, the area within the boundary shall prevail. As such we are of the view that though in RS plot No. 75 only 0.05 acres of land has been recorded in the name of others but the plaintiff's possession have been found in the RS plot No. 75 and in the local investigation an area of 0.09 acres of land has also been found within the given boundary of the plaint. So, we are of the view that the area of the land found within the given boundary by the Advocate Commissioner will prevail upon RS plot No. 75 of RS khatin No. 80.</u>

38. As such having regards to the above discussion and also going through all the relevant documents connected with the suit we are of the view that the trial Court did not commit any error of law and fact in coming to the conclusion to find the title of the plaintiffs into 0.09 acres of land which the plaintiffs have been possessing from 1964. So we find it difficult to discover any error of fact or law in the judgment passed by the trial Court.

39. In the result, the appeal is dismissed. However there is no order as to costs.

Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the Court concerned with the lower Court's record at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J: The instant Appeal at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the Judgment and decree dated 18-1-2016 (decree signed on 24-1-2016) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 231 of 2015 allowing the application for rejection of the plaint and thereby rejected the plaint.

2. The materials facts, relevant, for disposal of the instant First Appeal, succinctly, are that, the appellant as plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in schedule Ka land, the City Jorip Khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 AMG Belayet Hossain described in schedule Kha of the plaint is illegal, wrong, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiffs and further prayed for declaring that partnership establishment M/s "Hossain and Hossain" has already been dissolved and ineffective.

3. The plaint case in short are that the suit property is situated at Mirpur Housing Estate under the authority and control of National Housing Authority. The plaintiff Md Mosharaf Hossain applied for a commercial plot to the Housing Authority who allotted plot No. 7, Block-B, Main Road No. 1, section 1 in favour of the plaintiff who paid the value of the plot. The Housing Authority registered a lease deed being deed No. 2697 dated 30-6-1985 in favour of the plaintiff Md Mosharaf Hossain and handed over the possession of the property to him. The plaintiff by dint of registered lease agreement got mutation in his name through the office of Assistant Commissioner (land) and paid the taxes. The plaintiff while has been owning and possessing the same the defendant No. 1 AMG Belayet Hossain created a partnership deed showing the aforesaid property as the property of partnership firm "Hossain and Hossain." On 18-10-1986 the said firm was registered in the office of Registrar of Joint Stock Companies & firms, Dhaka being No. PE 28008/86 of 1986. Thereafter, the aforesaid property was mortgaged vide mortgage deed No. 3344 dated 27-10-1986 to the Rupali Bank, Motijheel Branch though suit property has been purchased and 4-storied building was constructed by the plaintiff at his own cost and money. The Rupali Bank instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 260 of 1998 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for realization of the loan money selling the suit property. The plaintiff bank got the decree in the suit. However, the plaintiff Md Mosharaf Hossain paid the decreetal amount in favour of the Rupali Bank, Motijheel Branch and got release the property and obtained a deed of redemption being No. 4654 dated 18-10-2005 in his name. In the suit property Bata Shoe Company (Bangladesh) Limited as a tenant running their business. The defendant No. 1 AMG Belayet Hossain wrote a letter on 27-11- 2014 to the Manager, Bata Shoe Company (Bangladesh) Limited, Tongi claiming 1/2 (half) share of the property. In the above facts and circumstances the plaintiff has been compelled to file the suit for declaration.

4. The defendant No. 1 appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint.

5. However, while the suit was so pending the defendant No. 1 by filing an application under Rule 11 of Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short Code) sought rejection of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that—

“ বাদীর দায়েরকৃত ১ম সহকারী জজ আদালতের দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা নং-৩৭৮/৯৩ মোকদ্দমায় ১-৬-১৯৯৭/৩১-৫-১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখে প্রদত্ত নালিশী সম্পত্তি আকৃষ্ট বাদী এবং অত্র বিবাদীর সমান অংশে মালিকানা ঘোষিত ডিক্রী কার্যাকর হইয়া আসা এবং উক্ত ডিক্রী অদ্যাবধি Unchallenged বিধায় একই ডিক্রীভূক্ত সম্পত্তি নিয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা তাৎক্ষণিক অরক্ষনীয় উহার আরজি প্রত্যাখ্যানযোগ্য হয়।”

6. It has been further contended in the application that the plaintiff has no cause of action to file the instant suit.

7. The plaintiff filed an objection against the application for rejection of the plaint denying the material allegations made in the application pointing that application is not maintainable. However, the defendant claimed that the plaint cannot be rejected because the Artha Rin Case was decreed against both of them and thereafter, the plaintiff paid the decreetal amount of the bank and got the deed of redemption in his favour. So, the suit must be determined after appreciating the evidence at the trial.

8. The learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka by his judgment and decree 18-1-2006 allowed the application for rejection of the plaint and thereby rejected the plaint of Title Suit No. 231 of 2015.

9. The plaintiff feeling aggrieved prefer-red the instant First Appeal against the judgment and decree dated 18-1-2016 (decree signed on 24-1-2016).

10. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Counsel with Mr Enayet Hussain Khan, Mr Md Ziaul Haque, and Mr Hasibur Rahman, the learned Advocates appearing for the appellants and took us through the impugned judgment and decree.

11. Mr Khan placed the impugned judgment and decree, application for rejection of the plaint, the plaint of Title Suit No. 231 of 2015 the written statement filed by the defendant No.1 and contended that on perusal of the averment made in the plaint there was no such averment that the suit is barred by any law. He took us through the prayer portion of the suit and argued that there is no nexus between the judgment and decree of the earlier suit or arbitration clause of the agreement to determine the prayer K, Kha and Ga of the plaint.

12. He has further pointed that the learned Joint District Judge arrived at a wrong decision rejecting the plaint for declaration and confirmation of possession wherein in the averments of the plaint clearly reflected the cause of action and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

13. He referring the application for rejection of the plaint has clearly pointed that the points raised by the defendant No. 1 in the application are clearly beyond the averment of the plaint therefore, all the points are extraneous defence material however, the learned Joint District Judge without considering the legal proposition in its true perspective rejected the plaint and, as such, erred in law.

14. He has further added that before filing the application for rejection of the plaint the defendant No. 1 by filing written statement has taken the clear defence in the suit which reflected from the pleadings, thereafter, he filed the application for rejection of the plaint and, as such, the application is liable to be rejected.

15. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Counsel has submitted that in passing the impugned judgment and decree the learned Joint District Judge has specifically arrived at a wrong decision and thereby committed an error in rejecting the plaint and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. Mr Ali has further submitted that the plaint can only be rejected if from the averments of the plaint it is apparent on a plain reading of the plaint and from the prayer of the suit that it is barred by any law or there is no cause of action to file the suit. He has added that the learned Joint District Judge in rejecting the plaint travel beyond the settle legal maxim as enunciated by the apex Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

16. Mr Ali took us through the impugned judgment specifically referring the provision of section 7 of the Arbitration Act as quoted by the learned Judge which as under:

"Jurisdiction on Court in respect of matters covered by arbitration agreement.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, where any of the parties to the arbitration agreement files a legal proceedings in a Court against the other party, no judicial authority shall hear any legal proceedings except in so far as provided by this Act.

“অর্থাৎ উক্ত বিষয় দেওয়ানী আদালত মোকাদ্দমা করার বাদীর কোন সুযোগ নেই। যে কারণে বাদীর আরজিটি আইনগতভাবেই বারিত।”

17. Upon bare reading the aforesaid observation and provision of arbitration of the partnership agreement Mr Ali pointed that the relief sought in the prayer of the instant suit cannot be resolved in view of the arbitration clause by the Arbitrator because the prayer of the plaint not within the purview of partnership agreement rather, all the prayers of the suit as prayed by the plaintiff beyond the jurisdiction of the Arbitration clause which have to be decided by competent Court of law for determination as to whether the plaintiff is entitled to get reliefs as per provision of Specific Relief Act not within the ambit of the provision of the clause of the arbitration of the partnership agreement.

18. He has in the same breath added that section 7 of the Arbitration Act does not exclude the jurisdiction of the Civil Court or taking away the jurisdiction to determine the legal and lawful prayer regarding civil dispute however, if there is any agreement in between the parties and in that agreement there is a clause for arbitration either of the parties can seek remedy within the ambit of the arbitration clause. The defendant No. 1 however, neither pleaded in the written statement nor in the application for rejection of plaint that he sought for arbitration in view of the arbitration clause as provided in the partnership agreement therefore, no legal proceeding is pending before any Court in view of the Arbitration clause. Hence, rejecting the plaint in view of the arbitration clause of the agreement cannot be invoked as bar to file the present suit, and, as such, the learned Joint District Judge committed an error thus, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

19. Mr Ali in support of his submissions relied upon the precedences to the case of Mahbubul Haque (Md) vs Md A Kader Munshi reported in 52 DLR (AD) 49, to the case of Shahjahan Siraj (Md) vs Md Rafique Quoraishi reported 19 BLC (AD) 143, to the case of Guiness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman reported 44 DLR (AD) 242.

20. Mr Md Waliur Reza Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1 has submitted that the plaintiff has filed the suit for declaration of 16 annas title over the suit property however, referring the paragraph 3 of the plaint he argued that at the earlier occasion the present plaintiff filed the title suit No. 378 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka admitting the sole decree though in the some portion of the averment indicated that this solenama has been created forgedly by the plaintiff however, the plaintiff did not challenge that solenama in this case rather, on an exceptional pretext filed the suit for declaration of title over the suit property although according to the averment he can filed the suit for declaration that the sole decree passed in Title Suit No. 378 of 1993 is null and void and not binding upon the, plaintiffs.

21. He has further pointed that the plaintiff filed the instant suit after expiry the period of limitation to challenge the earlier judgment and decree dated 1-6-1997 passed in title suit No. 378 of 1993. So, as per averment of paragraph 3 and paragraph 6 and prayer portion admittedly the plaintiff and defendants are owners in equal share but in a cunning way filed the instant suit for declaration that he is the only sole owner of the suit property which attract earlier judgment and decree dated 1-6-1997 passed in title suit No. 378 of 1993. So, in no way the plaintiff is now entitled to file the suit and to have the decree because earlier decree is till in force and bar as res-judicata. Therefore, the learned Joint District Judge rightly rejected plaint which does not call for interference by this Court.

22. He has further added that this defendant neither produced any external materials beyond the averment of the plaint nor superfluous matter as a defence case but very categorically referred the paragraph 3 and 6 of the plaint from which it is crystal clear that the plaintiff filed the instant suit for the same schedule property as of earlier suit in between the same party which has already decided on earlier occasion.

23. He has further pointed that it would have been otherwise or the plaintiff have to proceed with the suit if he did not mention the facts in paragraph 3 and 6 in respect of earlier Title Suit No. 378 of 1993 and it's judgment and decree. Therefore, he referring the impugned judgment and decree of the Court below very categorically pointed that since judgment and decree in between the same party is still now subsisting for the same property, therefore, the instant suit cannot be proceeded. He has argued that in the plaint the plaintiff does not disclose any cause of action in respect of prayer of the suit hence, the impugned judgment and decree is not liable to be set aside rather, the impugned judgment and decree based on legal and lawful proposition as enunciated by the apex Court that if on a mere reading of the averment of the plaint it appears that the plaint is barred by any law that can be thrown way by rejecting the plaint.

24. Mr Chowdhury has further submitted that the points raised by the defendant No.1 neither extraneous matter nor beyond the averment of the plaint hence, the impugned judgment and decree does not call for any interference.

25. He has specifically pointed that the earlier judgment in Title Suit No. 378 of 1993 passed on 1-6-1997 and the instant suit filed by the plaintiff on 31-3-2015 i.e. after expiry the period of limitation to set aside the compromise decree from which it is divulged that the present suit is nothing but a test case to set aside the earlier judgment and decree in external way after expiry the period of limitation.

26. In support of his submissions he referred a decision of Indian Supreme Court reported in Supreme Court cases 1992 Vol-3, page 31 to the case of Byram Pestonji Gariwala vs Union Bank of India and others.

27. In view of the above decision Mr Chowdhury argued that the earlier Judgment and decree obtained both the parties on compromise would be binding upon them and, as such, the instant suit is barred by res-judicata. Moreso, he pointed that the plaintiff did not prayed any relief against that compromise decree in the prayer portion but it is apparent that all the prayer portion touch the merit of the earlier compromise decree. So, the learned Joint District Judge in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no error nor the judgment and decree suffers for any legal infirmity and, as such, the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed.

28. We have anxiously considered the submissions of the learned Advocate of the respective parties. We have meticulously examined the averment of the plaint and prayer portion of the instant suit. We have gone through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Court below. Considering the application under Rule 11 of the Order 7 of the Code it appears that in the prayer portion except paragraph 10 nothing has been narrated for rejecting the plaint. We have examined the narration of paragraph 10 of the application for rejection of the plaint which runs as follows:

" বাদীর দায়েরকৃত ১ম সহকারী জজ আদালতের দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা নং ৩৭৮/৯৩ মোকদ্দমায় ১-৬-১৯৯৭/৩১-৫-১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখে প্রদত্ত নালিশী সম্পত্তি আকৃষ্ট বাদী এবং অত্র বিবাদীর সমান অংশে মালিকানা ঘোষিত ডিক্রী কার্যাকর হইয়া আসা এবং ডিক্রী অদ্যাবধ��� Un challenged বিধায় একই ডিক্রীভূক্ত সম্পত্তি নিয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা তাৎক্ষণিক অরক্ষনীয় বিধায় উহার আরজি প্রত্যাখ্যান যোগ্য হয়।”

29. On perusal of the narration of the paragraph 10 it appears that another suit being Suit No. 378 of 1993 has been filed by one Md Mosharaf Hossain against the AMG Belayet Hossain and compromised the matter while the suit for foreclosure and realization of payment of Bank money was pending however, bank was not the party of that suit. On perusal of the supplementary affidavit dated 8th, December, 2016 the plaintiff annexed some document including the judgment and decree passed in earlier suit in favour of the bank and also annexed the judgment of the compromised decree. It is apparent from the face of the record that judgment and decree passed in the Artha Rin Case on 7th, August of 1999 before that both the plaintiff and defendant of the instant suit had obtained a compromise decree on 03 June 1997 pending the Artha Rin Case. One of the party of the compromise suit referring the compromise decree raised the question of res-judicata referring a decision of the Indian Jurisdiction.

30. However, the learned Joint District Judge in the Judgment and decree dated 18-1-2016 opined that—

“অর্থাৎ বাদীর আরজির স্বীকৃত মতে নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদ পূর্বে সোলে সূত্রে রায় ডিক্রী হয় এবং উক্ত রায় ডিক্রী বর্তমানে বহাল রয়েছে। উক্ত রায় ডিক্রীর বিরুদ্ধে বাদীপক্ষ তার আরজিতে কোন প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করেন নাই। যে কারণে উক্ত রায় ডিক্রী বহাল থাকাবস্থায় এই মোকদ্দমাটি বাদীর স্বীকৃত মতেই রেসজুডিকাটা দ্বারা বারিত। যদিও রেসজুডিকাটা নীতিটি একই সাথে আইনগত এবং তথ্যগত বিষয়। কিন্তু যদি বাদী পক্ষ আরজিতেই পূর্ববর্তী মোকদ্দমার কথা স্বীকৃত করে সেক্ষেত্রে রেসজুডিকাট বিষয়টি শুধুমাত্র আইনগত বিষয় হিসাবে পরিগণিত হয়।”

31. In that view of the matter the learned Joint District Judge allowed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code. Further he opined that the cause of action in respect of the suit is illegible.

32. In the appeal crux point has to be decided whether the suit is barred by res-judicata, law of Arbitration and in the plaint no cause of action has been described for filing the suit.

33. On bare reading of the plaint it appears that in so many paragraphs of the plaint the plaintiff described the facts and specifically in paragraph 9 stating the date of cause of action from which it appears that the opinion "the suit is barred by non disclosing the cause of action" is not correct.

34. Moreso, according to apex Court decision the cause of action is bundle of facts which may be gathered from whole averments of the plaint. Therefore, view taken by the learned Joint District Judge that cause of action is illegible is not correct.

35. Next question whether the suit is barred by res-judicata or not. On perusal of the averment of the plaint it appears that the plaintiff narrated some facts including the facts of earlier compromise decree in paragraph 3 and 6 of the plaint. Wherefrom it is apparent that for the same property, between the same party there was a compromise decree while the suit property was mortgaged to the bank however, in that suit i.e. suit No. 378 of 1993 the bank was not party and bank got the decree in favour of it in the year 1999 i.e. after the compromise decree. None of them raised any question or raised the said point before the Artha Rin Adalat referring the compromise decree.

36. However, the facts remain is that both of them lost in the Artha Rin Case and property was declared as a mortgage property in favour of the bank and the suit was decreed for the purpose of selling the property to realize the loan money that decreee was not challenged either of the parties. It is, therefore, the question before us, after decree of Artha Rin Case if one of the party redeem the mortgage property in his favour paying the decretal amount whether he would be entitled to get the benefit of the transaction with the bank.

37. We are of the considered view that as the appellate Court should not resolve and discuss the matter in details, because it is to be decided after appreciating evidence. Therefore, our opinion is it would be beneficial for both the parties to determined this question before the Court below at the trial after appreciating the materials on evidence. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the learned Joint District Judge in rejecting the plaint has failed to consider the averment of the plaint, side by side the plaintiff and the defendants case in juxta position of the yardstick of fair justice.

38. It is a long line of catena of our jurisdiction specially by the pronouncement of the apex Court that the question of limitation raised must be decided after appreciating the materials/evidence. The learned counsel for the appellant referred the decision to the case of Mahbubul Haque (Md) vs Md A Kader Munshi reported in 52 DLR (AD) 49, to the case of Guiness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman reported in 44 DLR (AD) 242 and 19 BLC (AD) 143.

39. In the case of Mabbubul Haque's case was held as under:

"Question of limitation and res-judicata raised in the application for rejecting the point are mixed question of law and fact which need thorough investigation on adequate evidence for arriving at a correct decision on framing specific issues by the trial Court."

40. In the case of Guiness Peat (Trading) Limited was held as under:—

"In an application for rejection of the plaint on the ground of non disclosure of cause of action the court need not dissect the plaintiff's case part by part, if a part of the cause of action arises within its jurisdiction

A distinction is to be borne in mind between a case where the plaint does not disclose a cause of action and another where after considering the entire materials adduced in evidence the court finds that there is no cause of action. The plaint can only be rejected in the former case. A defendant's plea that there was no cause of action for the suit must be rejected when his contention fails to show that the plaint did not even disclose a part of the cause of action."

41, In the case of Shahjahan Siraj (Md) was held as under:—

"The Plea of res judicata is to be decided after framing an issue to that effect. There is no scope for application of section 11 of the code for rejection of plaint"

42. Now, the pertinent question has to address regarding the Arbitration as opined by the Court below. According to learned Joint District Judge the plaintiff has no authority to file the suit and, as such, the suit is barred.

43. In the above backdrop we can notice the provision of section 7 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 which runs as under:

“৭। সালিশ চুক্তির আওতাভূক্ত বিষয়ে আদালতের এখতিয়ার।– সালিশ চুক্তির কোন পক্ষ অপর কোন পক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে উক্ত চুক্তির অধীনে সালিশে অর্পণে সম্মত কোন বিষয়ে আইনগত কার্যধারা রুজু করিলে, বর্তমানে প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনে যাহাই থাকুক না কেন, এই আইনে বিধান ব্যতীত অন্য কোন আইনগত কার্যধারার শুনানীর এখতিয়ার আদালতের থাকিবে না।”

<u>44. On a careful reading the provision of section 7 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 we are of the considered view that the learned Joint District Judge has misconstrued the provision of section 7 of the Act, because neither of the party sought arbitration before any Court and no proceeding is pending in any Court regarding the prayer of the suit or for any dispute. So, we are of the considered opinion to invoke the Arbitration jurisdiction as bar to file the suit either of the party must file any proceeding before any Court seeking redress against another party invoking the provision of Arbitration clause before filing the suit however, in the present case no arbitration proceeding is pending regarding the suit property. We are, therefore, of the view that the prayers of the suit are not decidable by the Arbitrator as per Arbitration clause which reflected from pleadings and prayers of the suit because those are the beyond jurisdiction of Arbitrator and a competent Court of civil jurisdiction has to decide the suit in accordance with law. We have noticed the pleadings and prayers of the suit. On a careful scrutiny it is apparent that those claims and prayers are outside the clause of Arbitration of partnership deed because the Bank has already acquired the title of the suit property within the knowledge of both the parties which supersede the provision of Arbitration. We can place reliance in support of our view to the precedence of the case of Chittagong Port Authority vs M/s Crete Construction Company Ltd. reported in 31 DLR (AD) 138. Beside the defendant has already filed the written statement against the pleadings of the plaint taking clear defence. So, when the defendant surrender jurisdiction to the court instead of taking recourse of arbitration at the first instance, so later filing application for rejection of plaint is not entertainable, rather, it becomes academic. We find support of our view to the case of Seafarers Ino. through Shaw Wallace Pakistan Ltd. vs Province of East Pak reported in 20 DLR (SC) 225.</u>

45. In the result, the appeal is allowed.

46. The impugned judgment and decree dated 18-1-2016 is hereby set aside.

47. The application for rejection of the plaint is hereby rejected.

48. The learned District Judge is directed to proceed with the suit in accordance with law and dispose of the suit expeditiously within 1 (one) year positively from the date of receipt of this judgment however, without any order as to cost.

Office is directed to communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1(ka) 12 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 101 of 2001 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur against the defendant-respondent-petitioners and others for a declaration of title with a further declaration that the deed in the name of the defendants No. 29-32 is collusive, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with a prayer for recovery of khash possession contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to Mouza Ichli under Chandpur Sadar comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land out of 6.97 acres of land originally belonged to one Loknath and others. Subsequently, one Nurul Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and a Sekander Sheikh in 04 annas share obtained settlement from the original owners Loknath and others. During CS operation the suit land went under water and after its appearance from the bad of the river the Ex-Zaminder filed a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 in which the settlement holders Nurul Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham. Thereafter, while Nurul Islam and Sekandar failed to pay the rent the Ex-Zamindar started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and in .Rent Execution Case No. 02 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain. Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land by way of 'boynama' on 10-3-1951. The further case of the present petitioners i.e. the plaintiffs is such that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Mohammad Ali and others by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1956 became the owner of the suit land. The auction purchaser Zamir Hossain exhausted his share after his transfer. Thereafter, the SA khatian No. 28 was correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land measuring 3.60 acres. The father of the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the land-in-dispute and after his demise the land was inherited by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs after erecting their homestead in the suit properties use to possess the same and also paying rent to the government regularly. Out of the total land 42 decimals was recorded in the name of the plaintiff during BS operation and 461/2 decimals went into the khash khatian of the government. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit land is in the khash land of the government but taking advantage of that the defendants No. 29-32 and 33-36 collusively obtained settlement from the government by kabuliyat dated 22-5-2000. On 20-2-2001 all on a sudden the defendants No. 29-32 dispossessed the plaintiffs from the 'kW schedule land forcibly and erected huts therein. The plaintiffs to the suit thereafter learnt about the settlement of the defendants from the government and after getting certified copy of the kabuliyate on 11-6-2001 filed the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No. 2-32 and 33-36 after filing separate written statements contended that the land measuring 84.00 acres under Mouza Ichuli of SA plot No. 251 is the khash land of the government and BS khatian has been correctly prepared in the name of the government in its khash kahtian No. 1. The defendants being landless persons prayed for settlement of the land from the government and the government being satisfied by way of registered kabuliyat No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the defendants on 22-5-2000. The further case of the contesting defendants is such the plaintiff No. 4 admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 took settlement of 25 decimals of land in Settlement Case No. 178/199-2000. The plaintiff No. 4after taking settlement from the government erecting homestead use to possess the same. It is the case of the defendants that the plaintiffs were never dispossessed from the suit properties since they had no possession therein but only to grab the government property on the basis of false allegations and created forged papers filed the original suit.

4. The leaned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 6-10-2002.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred a Title Suit being No. 170 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chandpur which was transmitted to the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Chandpur for hearing and disposal. The learned appellate court hearing the appeal allowed 'the same by the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil. Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay.

7. During hearing of this Rule Mr Md Abdul Kader Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury and Mr Mithun Roy Chowdhury the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite-parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law as the learned lower appellate court violating the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure decided the merit of the appeal arbitrarily in favour of the plaintiffs without reversing the findings and decisions of the trial court adverting evidence therein. The learned Advocate also submits that there has been non-reading and misreading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the Appellate Court in a slipshod manner and not applying it's judicial mind. The learned Advocate submits that the Appellate Court not assessed the evidence on records in its true perspective and evaluated the same causing miscarriage of justice. The learned court during taking decision not at all considered all the papers on records properly and the plaintiffs to the suit during trial utterly failed to discharge their onus in proving their respective case. But the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur without taking it into consideration decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and in fact there is no paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Nur Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham as alleged comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the impugned judgment and decree is highly defective and it is not at all enforceable as it is not a speaking decree. The plaintiffs' original suit was a suit not for declaration of title, but for a declaration that the kabuliyat in favour of the defendants in respect of settlement is collusive, forged and not acted upon along with further prayer of recovery of khash possession. The learned Appellate Court misconceived the matter from the very beginning and, as such, failed to consider that the plaintiffs were totally failed to prove their possession and dispossession in the disputed property by producing tangible evidence. The learned Advocate submits that the learned Lower Appellate Court also failed to appreciate that, among the plaintiffs the plaintiffs No. 4 and 5 admitting the right, title, interest of the government in the suit property took settlement from the government and the conclusive findings with regard to this from the side of the trial court was not reversed by the appellate court adverting evidence on records. The learned Advocate relying upon the provisions laid down in section 115 of the Evidence Act argued that the plaintiffs are stopped from challenging the title of the Government inasmuch as among them some of the plaintiffs admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 obtained settlement by kabuliyate.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient evidence proved their case that the original owners of the disputed properties were Loknath and others and from them one Nurul Islam Sheikh and Sekandar Sheikh in 12 annas and 04 annas share took settlement. The learned Advocate also submits that during CS operation although the land-in-dispute went under water but subsequently it was re-appeared by alleviation and the Ex-Zamindar pursuant to a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 gave the land amicably in favour of their settlement holders Nur Islam and Sekandar Sk. and in fact the partition suit was ended in favour of the Plaintiff's-Predecessors Nur Islam and Sekandar. Subsequently, for arrear of rent a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 was started and in Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land on 10-3-1951 and from that Zamir Hossain; predecessors of the plaintiffs kabala purchased the land-in-dispute. The learned Advocate also submits that the Lower Appellate Court during deciding the merit of the appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below.

10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates I have perused the case records, pleadings of the respective parties, impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in consultation with the judgment and dismissal decree passed by the trial court, evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties and all other connected papers on records.

11. On perusal of the case records; it transpires that the positive contention as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs was such that the land-in-dispute originally belonged to ex-Zamindars namely Loknath and others. From them one Nur Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and one Sekandar Sheikh in 04 annas share took settlement. It is an admitted position that during CS operation the land in dispute went under water of the river. With regard to this; it is the contention of the plaintiffs that while the land-in-dispute reappeared from the bad of the river the ex-Zamindar started a "Touzi Bontan" (Partition Suit) Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and in that suit the settlement holder Nur Islam and Sekandar Sheikh obtained their respective saham in respect of the suit properties. The further pleadings of the plaintiffs were such that the Zaminders for arrears of rent started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and obtained a decree. In decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the land by way of "Boynama" on 10-3-1951. From that auction purchaser the predecessors of the plaintiffs obtained the suit land.

12. Vis-a-vis; it is the plain case of the contesting defendants that they are the landless cultivators and inasmuch as the property-in-dispute is the khash land of the government they prayed for settlement and the government being satisfied on 22-5-2000 by two registered kabuliyats No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the contesting defendants. It was further contended from the side of the defendants in their pleadings that the plaintiffs had no manner of title, possession and interest in the disputed properties and thereby there is no question of dispossession from the side of the defendants as alleged from the side of the Plaintiff-Opposite parties.

13. In this context; having gone through the case records I find that the plaintiffs to the suit to substantiate their claim examined 5 (five) witnesses and on the contrary the defendants examined 3 (three) witnesses.

14. PW 1 is the plaintiff No. 5 himself namely Abdul Hamid Bepari. This witness in his examination-in-chief frankly conceded at a stage that during the CS operation the land-in dispute went under water and subsequently when the land reappeared the ex-Zamindar started a Partition Suit in which the earlier settlement holders of the Zaminders namely Nur Islam and Sekander Sheikh obtained a separate saham in respect of the suit properties. The plaintiff No. 5 in his testimony testified at a stage that during BS operation the land measuring 461/2 decimals become the khash land of the government in its khash khatian No.1. In his cross-examination he testified at a stage that they did not submit any paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit No. 65 of 1930 and also did not produce the judgment and decree passed in Rent Suit No. 350 of 1950. The plaintiff also admitted that they could not furnish any paper showing the existence of decree of the Execution case. At a stage of his testimony P.W.1 testifies that they did not sought for any relief against the government with regard to SA khatian which stands recorded in the name of government. He expressed his inability to state the CS khatian of the disputed property and also expressed his inability to state about the area of land in CS plot No. 251.

15. It is to be noted here that the learned trial court in his observation and findings pointed out specifically about the discrimination and contradictions with material omissions as transpired within the depositions of the plaintiff's witnesses. The plaintiff No. 5 in his testimony testifies categorically at a stage-(quote):

“নালিশা ভূমি (২৫১ দাগের) সরকার হতে কারা বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত হয়েছে তা জানি না। তাদেরকে অত্র মামলায় পক্ষ করিনি। নালিশা ভূমিতে যে আশ্রয়ন প্রকল্প আছে তাতে প্রায় ৩০০/৪০০ জন লোক বসবাস করেন। তন্মেধ্যে আমি এ মামলায় কাউকেই পক্ষ করিনি। বাদীরা সবাই আমার ভাই বোন। ৪নং বাদী আবুল হোসেন বেপারী ১৭৮/৯৯-২০০০নং বন্দোবস্ত মামলা মূলে নালিশা ২৫১ দাগের খাস ২৫ শতক বাবদ বন্দোবস্ত পেলে তার নামে ৫৪১ নং জোত খতিয়ান খোলার বিষয় আমার জানা নাই। আমরা সবাই নালিশা ভূমিতে বসবাস করি না।

16. In another stage of his deposition he (PW 1) deposed that they did not submit the papers of Mutation Case No. 40 of 2000-2001 and also not impleaded the government as a party to their suit in the name of whom 84 acres of land has been recorded as khash khatian.

17. The witness number two of the plaintiffs PW 2 Oli Miah Bepari in his testimony testifies at a stage that the plaintiffs possessed the land for about 40/45 years and the defendants Bachchu and Mosharraf Dhali dispossessed the plaintiffs from 53 decimals of land. In the cross-examination this witness testified that the plaintiffs are his (PW 2) paternal brothers and sisters.

18. The other possession witness of the plaintiffs PW 3 Ruhul Amin Bepari who happens to be another relative of the plaintiffs testifies at a stage that he cannot say about the original owners of the suit property from whom the plaintiffs acquired the suit land.

19. PW 4 Ashraf Ali Gazi is one of the vendors of the plaintiff's predecessor who transferred 06 decimals of land by a sub-kabala dated 27-6-1980.

20. The last witness of the plaintiffs is the attesting witness of a deed dated 17-2-1987 which has been marked as Exhibit-5(ka).

21. On the other hand the witness No. 1 of the defendants Md Amir Hossain is a Tahsilder, who deposed on behalf of the government and corroborated the case of the defendants. This witness testified about the settlement khatian in favour of the defendants by way of kabuliyats being No. 2481 and 2485. He also submitted the papers relating to the right, title, and interest of the government with regard to khash khatian No. 1 and the settlement khatian in favour of the plaintiff No. 4 and all these papers has been duly exhibited.

22. The defendant No. 29 Mosharrof Hossain as DW 2 testified before the learned trial court and deposed in support of their pleadings.

23. The last witness of the defendants Md Mojibor Rahman Sheikh corroborated the case of the contesting defendants No. 29-32. It was contended by the witness No. 3 in his deposition that there exist "গুচ্ছ গ্রাম" in the said properties wherein the settlement holders of the government use to possess and do reside in their homesteads.

24. On meticulous consideration and assessment of evidence it is evident to note that the witnesses produced from the side of the plaintiffs has become shaky and contradicted one-another in respect of material aspects. Furthermore; they are not independent disinterested and credible witnesses who can be relied upon to substantiate or prove the case of the plaintiffs; but on the other hand, the witness Nos. 1, 2 and 3 of the defendants despite were thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the plaintiffs but none of them appears to have been discredited.

<u>25. it is a decided matter that under the ambit of sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act it is the incumbent duty upon the plaintiffs to the suit to discharge their onus of proof in proving their respective case but in the instant case as I have come across from the evidence on records that the plaintiffs to the suit could not discharge their onus of proof as observed by the learned trial Judge in his judgment and dismissal decree. The learned lower appellate court at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree without reversing the conclusive findings of the trial court on the title, possession and dispossession as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs reversed the judgment and decree as a whole which is a clear violation of the provision laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Under this provision of law in case of reversal of the trial court's judgment the Appellate Court is under legal obligation in reversing the findings of the trial court and give bona fide reasons for it's decision on the points for determination and shall have to give reasons therein at its own independent findings. The appellate court must contain definite findings on the question involved and must give reason when reversing the material findings of the trial court [Ref: Mohsena vs Habib, 17 BLD (AD) 47, Abu vs Sharifa, 15 BLD (AD) 91, Nur vs Nur 40 DLR (AD) 175, Abdus vs Jonab (Md) 57 DLR (AD) 112, Profulla vs Nagen, 6 BLC (AD) 1301.</u>

26. Having regard to the aforesaid legal proposition I have the reason to inclined such a view that the arguments advanced from the side of the learned counsel Mr Abdul Kader Bhuiyan having much nexus are acceptable in view of the judgment and decree passed by the Lower Appellate Court. The impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law inasmuch as the legal lacuna which is already transpired within the case of the plaintiffs has been totally overlooked as well as ignored from the side of the Lower Appellate Court and ignoring the material facts and evidence of the case the impugned judgment and decree was passed which is not sustainable in the eye of law.

27. Besides this; the chain of title since not at all proved from the side of the plaintiffs which is badly required and the possession and dispossession as alleged from their side as not proved by tangible evidence the plaintiffs are not entitled the relief as prayed for.

28. In the forgoing narrative; having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule have got much merit to succeed.

29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 is hereby set aside.

30. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Communicate the judgment and order immediately and send back the lower Court's record at once.

End.
