full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-7-2006 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj, in Title Appeal No. 14 of 2005 reversing those dated 6-10-2004 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, (in-Charge) Jamalganj, Sunamganj, in Title Suit No. 18 of 2002 should not be set aside and such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 18 of 2002 for a decree of permanent injunction against the opposite parties as defendants claiming inter aria, that the suit land covered by Plot Nos. 504 and 503 measuring 0.0481 acres and .0344 acres respectively belonged to কালীগড় ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিমিটেড presently known as Sachna Bazar Banik Samity. Accordingly, SA Khatian No. 244 prepared in the name of কালীগড় ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিমিটেড. The said Samity while in possession of the schedule land leased out 0.0413 acres of land to the father of the plaintiff-petitioner, who after getting lease in the year 1971 filled up the low land and made the same into bhiti land. Thereafter, father of the plaintiff-petitioner constructed a tin shed shop house in the schedule land and possessing the same since 1971 upon payment of rents to the Government. After death of lessee Iskander Ali, the plaintiff got the property by inheritance and has possessed the same with the knowledge of the defendants upon payment of arrear rents as demanded by the defendant-opposite party Nos. 2 and 3. While the plaintiff-petitioner possessing the suit land peacefully without any disturbances from any quarter, all on a sudden, the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-3 came to the suit land on 16-11-2002 and asked the plaintiff-petitioner to remove the shop house else they will demolish the same and evict the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit land by applying force. On query the defendant-opposite parties could not give any satisfactory reply as to why they will evict the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit land.

3. The plaintiff-petitioner made a search about title of the defendant-opposite party in the suit land but found nothing in their favour. Further case of the plaintiff-petitioner, is that,

the property in question belongs to কালীগড় ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিমিটেড known as Sachna Bazar Banik Samity from whom father of the plaintiff-petitioner obtained lease. The defendant-opposite parties have had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. They being biased and gained over, by some interested persons, illegally threatened the plaintiff-petitioner with dispossession from the suit land. In the circumstances, the plaintiff-petitioner has become compelled to file the suit against the defendant for a decree of permanent injunction.

4. The defendant-opposite parties contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter-alia, that the schedule to the plaint is indefinite and unspecified; the plaintiff-petitioner has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and also stated that there is no existence of Samity named কালীগড় ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিমিটেড and the alleged Sachna Bazar Banik Samity has/had no right to lease out the suit land to the plaintiff's father. Further case of the defendant-opposite parties, is that, the property in question belongs to nobody and there is no owner and claimant of the suit property. For that reason the property in question is liable to be made khas under section 19(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and accordingly, the Government is taking step for making the property khas to the government. The plaintiff being informed about the said process of the Government, for illegal gain and to grab the property filed the suit against the defendants with false allegation of giving threat to the plaintiff. The plaintiff has got no cause of action against the defendants to file the suit for permanent injunction and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. The plaintiff examined three witnesses including himself as PWs 1-3 and exhibited his documents as Exhibits 1-3 and the defendant No. 1 deposed as DW 1 on behalf of the defendants.

6. The trial court decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 6-10-2004. The defendant-opposite parties preferred Title Appeal No. 14 of 2005 before the District Judge, Sunamganj, who transferred the same to the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj for hearing and disposal. The appellate court after contested hearing allowed the appeal by its judgment and decree dated 18-7-2006 and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. The present-petitioner being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate court has moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay and status quo in respect of possession of the suit property.

7. None appears to press or oppose the Rule.

8. One Md Mobarak Hossain Talukder during pendency of this Rule by filing an application added as opposite party No. 4 by order dated 11-3-20104 but he was not a party in the suit or appeal.

9. From a perusal of the application for addition of party, it appears that father of the added opposite party tried to be added as defendant in the suit before the trial court but the trial court rejected the application against which he preferred Civil Revision before the District Judge, Sunamganj that was also rejected. After a long time, his son Mobarak Ali Talukder added in this revisional application as opposite party No. 4.

10. Mr Mustaque Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 4 submits that the property in question belongs to the father of the opposite party No. 4 but since the application of his father for addition of party was rejected by the trial court as well as by the revisional court he could not contest the suit by filing written statement and produce the Relevant title documents in the name of his father. He further submits that the plaintiff-petitioner or his father never possessed the suit land and the lease agreement/deed filed on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner showing Sachna Bazar Banik Samity as executants of the deed is anti dated and the said Samity has/had no right, title and interest in the property to lease out the same. It is also argued that the petitioner is not in possession and the story of making shop house on the suit property by his father is absolutely false and untrue. The plaintiff being not in possession and having no title in the suit property, suit for injunction is not at all maintainable. The plaintiff-petitioner has filed the suit to grab the property against the Government without making the real owner as defendant. He also submits that the appellate court rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court as the petitioner utterly failed to prove his title and possession in the suit property.

11. Heard the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 4, gone through the revisional application, judgment of both the courts below, evidences adduced by the parties and the exhibits submitted by the plaintiff-petitioner.

12. From a perusal of the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, it appears that the trial court while decreeing the suit observed as follows:—

“স্বীকৃত যে নালিশী ভূমিতে দোকন ঘর আছে। বাদী উক্ত দোকান ঘর তাহার পিতা উত্তোলন করিয়াছেন বলেন। জ.অ. খতিয়ানে নালিশী ভূমিতে ভিটি ও বাড়ী লিপি দেখা যায়। জেরায় ঈ.ঠ-১ নালিশী ভূমিতে অবৈধ দখলকার বাদী নহেন তৃতীয় কোন ব্যক্তি আছেন উল্লেখ ��রিলেও নাম বলিতে পারেন নাই। স্বীকৃত যে নালিশী ভূমিতে ১-৩ নং বিবাদী সরকারের বা ১-৩ নং বিবাদীপক্ষের কোন দখল নাই । উ.ঠ-১, উ.ঠ-২, ও. ঠ-৩ এর সাক্ষ্য ও জেরা পর্যালোচনায় নালিশী ভূমিতে বাদী ব্যতিত তৃতীয় কোন ব্যক্তির দখল দেখা যায় না।

তদাবস্থায় বাদীর নালিশী ভূমিতে ও দোকানঘরে সাচনা বাজার ব্যবসায়ী সমিতির অধীনে লীজ সুত্রে আপাত স্বত্ব ও একচ্ছত্র দখল আছে মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত নিয়া ২ নং বিচার্য বিষয় বাদীর অনুকূলে নিষ্পত্তি করা হইল।

বিচার্য বিষয় ১/৩

১-৩ নং বিবাদীর জবাব ও ঙ.ঠ-১ এর জবানবন্দি পর্যালোচনায় নালিশী ভূমিকে দাবীদারহীন লা-ওয়ারিশ সম্পত্তি গন্যে তাহা খাস করার জন্য সরকার পদক্ষেপ গ্রহনে উদ্যোগী হইয়াছেন।কিন্তু নালিশী সম্পত্তি সরকারী খাস খতিয়ান ভুক্ত করার কোন লিগ্যাল প্রসিডিং চলমান থাকার কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট বক্তব্য ১-৩ নং বিবাদীগণ বলে নাই।বাদী ১-৩ নং বিবাদী বা সরকারের কোন চলমান আইনী প্রক্রিয়ার বিরুদ্ধে স্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রার্থনায় অত্র মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করেন নাই।SAT Act (Act XXVIII of 1950)এর ৯২(গ)ধারায় সরকার নালিশী ভূমি বিষয়ে এখনো ব্যবস্থা নেয় নাই।যথাযথ আইনী প্রক্রিয়ার দ্বারা নালিশী সম্পত্তিকে সরকার বা নিজেদের নিয়ন্ত্রনে নেওয়ার পূর্বেই জোরে বলে বাদীকে তথা হইতে বে-দখল করার কোন অধিকার ১-৩ নং বিবাদীর এমূহূর্তে নাই। তদ্রুপক্ষেত্রে বাদীর অত্র মোকদ্দমা চলিতে পারে এবং বাদী প্রার্থিত নিষেধাজ্ঞা আদেশ পাওয়ার হকদার মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত নিয়া ১/৩ নং বিচার্য বিষয় বাদীর অনুকূলে নিষ্পত্তি হইল।

13. Apart from the observations made hereinabove, it was also observed by the trial court that:—

বাদীর পিতা ইসকান্দর আলী, সাচনা বাজার বনিক সমিতির তৎকালীন সম্পাদক ঙ.ঠ-৩ এর পিতা আঃ রহমান হইতে নালিশী ভূমি ২৫-২-১৯৭১ ইং তারিখে লীজ নেন মর্মে দাবী করেন। উক্ত লীজ দলিলটি (প্রদ-৩) ঙ.ঠ.-৩ সাক্ষী দেখা যায়।

14. PW 3 সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা নালিশী ভূমি তাহার পিতা কর্তৃক বাদীর পিতা বরাবরে লীজ দেওয়াকে সমর্থন করেন।

15. I have gone through the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court. It appears that the appellate court in its judgment observed as follows:—

“বাদীপক্ষের দাখিলীয় প্রদঃ-১ অর্থাৎ নালিশী এস,এ ২৪৪ খতিয়ানের জাবেদা নকল পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, ৫০৪ দাগে বাড়ী পরিমাণ ৪.৮১ একর এবং ৩০৫ দাগের ভিটা পরিমাণ ৩.৪৪ একর জমি ভূমি হইতেছে। কিন্তু বাদীপক্ষ আরজিতে উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন যে, নালিশী ২৪৪ খতিয়ানের ৫০৪ দাগে .০৪৮১ একর এবং ৫০৩ দাগে .০৩৪৪ একর ভুমি। এমতাবস্থায়, বাদীর আরজির সম্পত্তির বনর্নার সহিত নালিশী এস,এ ২৪৪ খতিয়ানের ভূমির বনর্নার মিল নাই।বাদীর দাখিলীয় প্রদঃ-৩ অর্থাৎ ইং ২৫-২-৭১ তারিখের ইজারানাগা দলিল দৃষ্টে প্রতিয়মান হয় যে, মোঃ আব্দুর রহমান পিতা হাজী কালা কাজী সাং কালীপুর হাং সাং সাচনা বাজার, সম্পাদক, সাচনা বাজার বণিক সমিতি।প্রদঃ-১ অর্থাৎ নালিশী এস,এ ২৪৪ খতিয়ানের জাবেদা নকল দৃষ্টে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, অত্র খতিয়ানের প্রজ্ঞা কালীগঞ্জ ব্যবসার সম্পদ লিঃ।এমতাবস্থায় দেখা যাইতেছে যে, বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী ভূমির এস,এ প্রজার নিকট হইতে নালিশী ভূমি ইজারা গ্রহণ করেন নাই।তাহা ছাড়া বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী ভূমির এস,এ খতিয়ান ভ্রমাত্মকভাবে প্রকাশের দাবী আরজিতে উল্লেখ করিলেও তাহা দুরীভূতকরনের জন্য কোন মোকদ্দমা করেন নাই বা অত্র মোকদ্দমায় ততমর্মে কোন প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করেন নাই। অপরদিকে সাচনা বাজার বণিক সমিতির সম্পাদক নালিশী সম্পত্তি ৯০ বছরের জন্য আইনসঙ্গতভাবে লীজ দেওয়ার অধিকার রাখেন না। বিবাদী/আপীলকারীপক্ষ দাবী করিয়াছেন যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি লাওয়ারিশ ও দাবীদার বিহীন, পরিত্যক্ত সম্পত্তি এবং নালিশী সম্পত্তি হাট-বাজারের সম্পত্তি মর্মে দাবী করিয়াছেন। এমতাবস্থায় দেখা যাইতেছে যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদীপক্ষের পূর্বাধিকারীর বা বাদীর স্বত্ব বিদ্যমান নাই বিধায় বাদীপক্ষ মূল মোকদ্দমায় প্রার্থীতমতে প্রতিকার পাইবার হকদার নহেন।”

16. The above quoted observations of the appellate court is contrary to the actual facts and circumstances of the case and the exhibits. The appellate court found that the suit Plot Nos. 305 and 504 covered a total quantum of land 8.25 acres but the plaintiff-petitioner mentioned in the schedule to the plaint as .0826 acres of land, which is not in conformity with the document. It is also wrongly found that the plaintiff-petitioner's father obtained the lease from Sachna Bazar Banik Samity which was not the owner in SA. record. The lease deed itself disclosed the fact that SA recorded Samity is presently known as Sachna Bazar Banik Samity. Apart from such controversies about the documentary evidences produced on the plaintiff's side the appellate court ought to have observed about the possession of the property in question but the appellate court totally remained silent about the possession of the property in question which is a paramount issue and consideration in a suit for injunction. From the papers and documents available in file and exhibited on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner this court finds a prima facie case and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land, entitling him to get a decree for injunction.

17. Apart from title, a person found in exclusive possession of certain plot of land for a period of more than 30 years without any disturbances cannot be dispossessed by any authority or person without due process of law.

<u>18. In the present case, the trial court found that the plaintiff-petitioner has failed to prove his clear and undisputed title in the suit property though some documents have been filed trying to establish his title but the trial court has found that the plaintiff is in exclusive possession of the suit land. Therefore, a person in possession is legally entitled to retain his possession and in the absence of any lawful claim of the defendants they are not in any way entitled to dispossess the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit land without due process of law. The written statement filed by the defendant clearly speaks that the government has not yet acquired any right, title in the property by any means or by any legal process. So, in the absence of any legal basis, the defendant-opposite parties cannot initiate any action against the plaintiff-petitioner.</u>

19. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds that the trial court rightly decreed the suit and the appellate court in allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The appellate court in its judgment neither controverted the observations made by the trial court regarding possession of the plaintiff-petitioner in the suit land nor appreciated the documents in its true perspective and, as such, this Court finds merit in this Rule Galling interference by this Court.

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. however, there will be no order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 18-7-2006 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Sunamganj in Title Appeal No. 14 of 2005 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge, Jamalganj, Sunamganj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2002 is restored.

21. The orders of stay and status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stand vacated.

22. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.

Md Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate with Saidul Alam Khan, Advocate ---- For the Petitioner. 
Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocate ----- For the Opposite-Party Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Mohammad Ali ----- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner 
Vs 
Ali Ahammad and others ----- Defendants-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Haque, J: This Rule, under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, was issued calling, upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2010 passed by the learned joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No. 240 of 2006 in disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant judge, Rupgonj, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 dismissing the suit of the plaintiff-petitioner should not be set aside and pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper.

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the parties were directed to maintain status-quo in respect of position and possession of the suit property.

3. The facts leading to the instant Civil Revision Petition may conveniently be presented briefly as follows: The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rupgonj Court, Narayangonj for declaration of title on the suit land, and further sought for declaration that suit land is not the property of No. 167 Keshrab, of khatian Nos. 229/230 of plot No. 399 rather it is the property of Mouza- No. 159 Keshrab of CS Khatian No. 707 containing CS Plot No. 309 and for declaration that deed No. 2203 dated 7-4-1960 is not binding upon him as well as for confirmation of possession and so on.

4. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner in short is that the suit properties along with other properties were belonged to Jalaluddin, Jorali, Taripullah and Achia Bibi. By an amicable partition the suit plot No. 309 having 56 decimals of land fell in the shaham of Jorali alias Janu, out of 56 decimals he sold 19 decimals of land by the east to the predecessor of the defendants Abdur Rahim and he used to possess the said 19 decimals till his death, Jorali alias Janu while in possession of 39 decimals of land by the west side of the suit plot died leaving only son Kazimuddin and his name was duly recorded in the SA and RS khatian. In the RS Khatian suit land measuring 39 decimals of land was recorded in RS plot No. 435 and was duly published without any objection. Kazimuddin for want of money sold the above said 39 decimals of land to his son Abdul Mojid vide deed No. 2476 on 10-3-1973 and handed over possession on the same date. Thereafter Abdul Majid sold the same to Rahman Ali on 31-12-1976 vide deed No. 7787 and handed over possession to the purchaser. Thereafter Rahman Ali died leaving Asirun Nesa as wife, Mohammad Ali, Idris Ali, Meher Ali, Misir Ali as 4 sons, Hawlatun Nesa, Rashida Begum and Rehena Akhter as 3 daughters who inherited his property. Then Asirun Nesa died leaving the above 4 sons and 3 daughters. The above 4 sons and 3 daughters made an amicable partition of the landed property left by Rahman Ali on 29-10-1998 vide deed No. 10629. In that amicable partition, the plaintiff as 4th party got the suit land in his shaham along with other lands; his brother and sisters got shaham from other land. The plaintiff peacefully possessing the suit land for more than 12 years within the Knowledge of the defendants and others and acquired adverse title by adverse possession. The plaintiff built up house in one portion of the land on 30-3-1998 and planted trees on the rest of the land. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 raised objection that there are mistakes in the deed of Abdul Majid and then the plaintiff having got the original deeds saw that there are mistakes in the deeds which have omitted by the deed writer. Me wrote in the deed Mouza No. 167 instead of 159 plot No. Sabek 399 instead of 309 but the Mai plot No. 435 has been written correctly. Kamizuddin has ownership in plot No. 309 and he had no right to sale the property of plot No. 399. This is a bonafide mistake of the deed writer as well as the parties. The plaintiff sought for declaration of title on the suit land, and further sought for declaration that suit land is not the property of No. 167 Keshrab, of khatian Nos. 229/230 of plot No. 399 rather it is the property of Mouza No. 159 Keshrab, of CS Khatian No. 707 containing CS Plot No. 309 and so on.

5. The defendants- Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement; that the said defendants contended that Jalal Uddin, Jorali, Toriqulla and Achia Bibi was the CS recorded owners of the schedule land along with other lands which comprised a total area of 407 decimals of land of 13 plots appertaining to CS Khatian No. 707; that CS record was prepared in their names in equal share; subsequently said Jalal Uddin, Jorali, Toriqulla and Achia Bibi for their convenience divided the schedule land along with their other properties by way of amicable family settlement; by such amicable settlement Achia Bibi got in her saham 38 decimals of schedule plot land along with other properties and the rest 18 decimals of schedule plot land was included in the saham of Jorali; thus the CS recorded owners after amicable settlement was possessing their respective land peacefully to the knowledge of others. Subsequently said Jorali transferred his 18 decimals land of the schedule plot to Abdur Rahim; subsequently Abdur Rahim died leaving behind his sons namely Alauddin, Serajuddin and Mohijuddin who inherited 18 decimals of the schedule plot land along with other properties left by their father; subsequently by way of an amicable settlement out of the said 18 decimals of land 9 decimals of land was included in the saham of Alauddin, 3.5 decimals of land was included in the saham of Serajuddin and 5.5 decimals of land was included in the saham of Mohijuddin. That thereafter Alauddin on 11-10-1955 and Serajuddin on 23-3-1953 sold their portion of land in the schedule plot to Subed Ali, the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. On the other hand CS tenant Achia Bibi died leaving behind her only daughter Amirun Bibi and this Amirun Bibi being the owner of 38 decimals land of plot No. 309 along with other land by way of inheritance and sold 38 decimals of land of plot No. 309 and 3 decimals of land of plot No. 358 on 7-4-1960 to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali, that subsequently during SA survey name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali was recorded in the SA Khatian correctly; in this way Subed Ali owned and possessed 31.50 decimals of land from CS plot No. 309; subsequently said Subed Ali died leaving behind defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and others as his heirs; that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is possessing the their land peacefully to the knowledge of all; for their convenience they dug some land, filed up some portion and growing trees over the other portion; that during RS survey due to the mistakes of the survey officers less share of land was recorded in the names of their predecessors and the RS record was not prepared correctly; that the defendants are possessing their land by paying rent to the government; that name of CS recorded owner Jorali was never Jorali alias junu; that Jorali did not get in his saham 37 decimals of land from the schedule plot; that Jorali had no son namely Kazimuddin alias Kamizuddin; Kazimuddin alias Kamizuddin never possessed 37 decimals of land from the western portion of the suit plot land; that SA and RS khatian was not prepared in the sole name of Kazimuddin and there was no such scope and if there is any such khatians that would be a collusive and fake one; that Kazimuddin was not the owner of 37 decimals of land and he did not sell the same to his son Abdul Majid on 10-3-1973 and any such deed if so produced that would be a collusive one and ineffective; Abdul Mazid never acquired ownership and possession in the suit land; Abdul Majid did not sell the 37 decimals of land to the father of the plaintiff and he had no right to transfer the said land; that the-plaintiffs had full knowledge about the contents of their alleged deed since 1977; that the plaintiffs has no right, title and possession and their instant suit is a malafide one; therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. Over pleadings learned trial Judge framed the following issues:

i. whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and nature?

ii. whether there is any defect of parties?

iii. whether the suit is burred by limitation?

iv. whether the plaintiffs has right, title and possession in the suit land?

v. whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get the relief as prayed for?

vi. whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get any other relief?

7. The plaintiff-petitioner in support of his case adduced 4 witnesses and produced some documents which, have been marked as Exhibit 1 to 4; in Appellate stage on recall the plaintiff exhibited some other documents which has been marked as Exhibit 5 series to 10 series.

8. On the other hand the defendants-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to support their case adduced 4 witnesses and produced some documents which have been marked as Exhibit Ka to Chha. In Appellate stage DW-1 further deposed in support of their case.

9. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Trial Judge by his Judgment and decree dated 9-6-2004 (decree drawn up and signed on 15-6-2004) dismissed the suit. Learned Trial Judge while dismissing the suit held that admittedly Jorali got 18 decimals of land from Plot No. 309; in paragraph No. 3 of the plaint, the plaintiff claimed that Kazimuddin got 37 decimals of land by inheritance from Jorali but in cross examination as PW 1 he stated that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of purchase and he had not submitted the said document and therefore, PW 1 do not support his case. The learned Trial Judge further held that the defendants claimed that Amirun Nesa became the owner of the land from her mother Achia and DW 1 in his deposition supported the said case. Amirun Nesa sold 38 decimals of land to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali (Ex-Ka) and in the SA Khatian (Ex-2) name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali has been recorded. Deed dated 7-4-1960 (Ex-Ka) is a 30 years old document. Therefore, it is proved that Achia got 38 decimals of land in Plot No. 309. Since Kazimuddin has got no right and title in the suit land therefore, the wrong recordings in the deed No. 2476 dated 10-3-1973 is not proved and that statement is not believable. Since Kazimuddin has no right and title therefore, plaintiffs have acquired no right and title in the suit land. The learned Trial judge further held that it is not believable that the predecessors of the plaintiffs did not check the schedule of deed dated 10-3-1973 and 31-12-1973. Plaintiffs did not try to prove that Kazimuddin had no property in the mouza, khatian, plot which has been written in the said deeds. That the plaintiffs failed to prove their exclusive possession in the suit land and the plaintiffs had knowledge about the deeds in question since 1976. Thus the plaintiffs failed to prove their case. Furthermore, while dismissing the suit the learned Trial judge also holds that since the defendants had not taken any steps against RS Khatian No. 231 which has been recorded in the name of Kazimuddin therefore, plaintiff's title over the land in question is not also proved.

10. The plaintiff-petitioner having been resentful to the said judgment and decree preferred an appeal before the learned District judge, Narayangonj and the same was registered as Title Appeal No. 240 of 2006; the said appeal was ultimately heard by learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj who upon hearing the parties disallowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 30-11-2010 (decree drawn up and signed on 2-1-2011). While disallowing, the appeal the learned Judge of the Lower Appellate Court held that in the plaint, the plaintiff claimed that Kazimuddin got the land by way of inheritance from Jorali but in cross examination as PW 1 he stated that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of purchase. Therefore, PW 1 does not support his case. Moreover, there is no oral and documentary evidence that Jorali got the entire 56 decimals of land. Regarding alleged wrong writings in the disputed deeds the plaintiffs failed to give any cogent and believable explanation in his cross examination. The plaintiff has got no right and title by dint of exhibit Nos. 6, 7 and 8. The learned Appellate judge further held that Amirun Nesa, daughter of Achia sold 38 decimals of land to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali (Ex-Ka) and in the SA Khatian (Ex-2) name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali has been recorded. Therefore, Subed Ali got right and title in the suit land and accordingly defendant Nos. 1 and 2 also acquired ownership in the land. He further held that since PW 2 and 3 are cousins of the plaintiff therefore, their testimony as to possession of the plaintiff is not believable rather the said witnesses admitted the possession of the defendants. PW 3 failed to state the boundary of the land in his cross examination. On the other hand DWs 2-4 gave testimony in support of defendant's possession and they denied plaintiffs possession categorically. The possession of the suit land by the defendants is also evidenced from the fact that they paid rent of the land. While disallowing the appeal the Learned Appellate Judge further reversed the findings of the Trial Court against the defendants on the ground that mere record of rights do not confer any title and extinguish the right of the others and the defendants have successfully proved the title and possession over the suit land.

11. Feeling dissatisfied with the above judgment and decree the plaintiff-petitioner approached this Court in Civil Revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

12. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate along with Mr Saidul Alam Khan, Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and decree are bad in law as well as in fact; that the learned Judge of the courts below failed to consider that RS record in respect of 37 decimals of land was prepared in the name of Kazimuddin; that since the defendants admitted that Joarli had also saham in the suit land therefore, this part admission is regarded to be admission of the entire case of the plaintiff. The learned advocate further submits that since the defendants had not preferred any appeal or cross-objection against the findings of the Trial judge which goes against the defendant therefore, the plaintiffs case should be considered. The learned advocate finally submits that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from non-consideration of materials and evidences on record and prays for making the rule absolute. In support of his submission Mr Nurul Amin, the learned advocate relied on the judgments passed in the following cases: Sheikh Salimuddin vs Ataur Rahman reported in 43 DLR 18, Parul Rani Sen Gupta vs Bangladesh reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 277.

13. On the other hand Mr. Sikder Mahmudur Razi, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 opposing the rule, submits that amicable partition amongst the heirs of CS recorded tenants was held after the CS record and the same is also evident from the plaint of the petitioner. He next submits that since the plaintiff-petitioner has not prayed for rectification of the deed in question as per section 31 of the Specific relief Act, therefore the suit itself is not maintainable at all. He next submits that the plaintiff in the original plaint claimed that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of inheritance but (during trial he claimed Kazimuddin became the owner by way purchase and thus gave contradictory statement. Moreover, the identity of Kazimuddin as claimed by the plaintiff is not correct and he is not the son of CS recorded owner Jorali. He further submits that the plaintiff in the original plaint claimed ownership by way of inheritance but by way of an amendment they claimed adverse possession and these two claims cannot run side by side.

14. Mr Razi further submits that since the purchase deed of the father of the defendant Nos. 1 & 2 was a properly executed deed which was earlier in point of time and since it is the settled principle of law that kabala deed prevails over the record of rights therefore, the learned Judge of the Appellate court correctly came to the conclusion that the defendants has right, title and possession over the suit land and thereby dismissed the appeal and upheld the decree of the trial court.

15. He finally submits that the learned Judge of the Appellate Court being the last court of fact has properly assessed the evidences and materials on record and thereby came to the conclusion that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case and on the other hand the defendants has been successfully proved their title and possession over the suit land and upon such findings dismissed the appeal of the petitioner and upheld the decree of the trial court and most of its findings made in the judgment and therefore, the said judgment does not suffer from any non-reading, misreading, non-consideration of material evidences on record, misconstruction, misapplication of law and fact and therefore, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submission Mr. Razi relied on the judgments passed in the following cases: Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindu Sarkar, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 6, Tajul Islam vs Chini Miah, reported in 13 MLR 1, Saeeda Yasmin vs Capital Services Center Ltd, reported in 57 DLR (AD) 189.

16. Heard the learned advocates of both the sides, perused the revisional application, the counter affidavit, the impugned judgment and decree as well as the materials and evidence on record.

17. It appears from the plaint that the plaintiff in the original plaint claimed ownership by way of inheritance but by way of an amendment he claimed adverse possession. But interestingly during cross examination he claimed that Kazimuddin became the owner of land by way of purchase but he did not submit that document and thus he gave contradictory statement in different stages of the suit.

18. It further appears from the cross examination of the PWs 2 and 3 that they virtually admitted the possession of the defendant in the suit land. But it appears from record that the plaintiff did not pray for recovery of possession and from this point of view the instant suit is not maintainable in this present form and nature.

19. It further appears from the plaint and testimony of PW 1 that he claimed that he requested defendant No. 3 to rectify the deed in question but being refused the filed the present suit for declaration. That being the statement of the plaintiff he ought to have instituted the present suit for rectification of the deed iii question as per section 31 of the Specific relief Act, therefore the suit itself is not maintainable at all.

20. It further appears that in the instant suit the plaintiff has not impleaded Kazimuddin or his heirs as party though it is the case of the plaintiff that Kazimuddin transferred the suit land to Abdul Majid through deed dated 10-3-1973 over which the plaintiff also sought for declaration and in this count the suit is bad for defect of parties.

21. It further appears from the materials, oral and documentary evidences on record that suit plot No. 309 contains 56 decimals of land and admittedly by way of an amicable settlement Jorali got 18 decimals land in his saham in suit plot No. 309; now, the question remains who got the rest 38 decimals land of the said plot; it is the case of the plaintiff that Jorali got the entire 56 decimals land whereas the claim of the contesting defendant is that the rest 38 decimals land was included in the saham of Achia Bibi; on her death her daughter Amirun Bibi transferred the same to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali by registered deed dated 7-4-1960 and during SA survey name of said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali were recorded in SA Khatian No. 627. Exhibit Ka which is the deed dated 7-4-1960 and Exhibit 2 which is the SA Khatian No. 627 supported the defendants' case. Since, after purchase SA khatian was prepared in the name of said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali it can be said that the said deed was acted upon and said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali who are predecessors of the defendants, got possession from the date of purchase.

22. The contention of the petitioner that since RS record was prepared in the name of Kazimuddin therefore, his case stands docs not deserve any consideration since it is the settled principle of law that kabala deed prevail over record of rights and mere preparation of Khatian in the name of any particular individual without any basis does not confer any title. In the case of Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindhu Sarkar, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 6 also supported the same principle.

23. The further contention of the petitioner that since the defendants did not prefer any appeal or cross objection against the adverse finding of the Trial judge therefore, the said findings stands good. In support of such submission the learned advocate for the petitioner cited two decisions as mentioned above. From the said judgments it appears that adverse findings were given in both the cited decisions against the plaintiffs whose duty was to prove their own case. But in the instant case the adverse findings which was given by the learned Trial judge was against the settled principle of law as mentioned above and the said adverse findings was properly, addressed and reversed by the appellate court.

24. It is the settled principle of law that the plaintiff has to prove his own case and since in the instant case the plaintiff failed to prove his own case therefore, this kind of submission at the revisional stage will not help him.

25. This revisional application has been filed against judgment and decree of affirmance. In such a case the petitioner must have to make out a case of misreading, non-reading, misconstruction, non-consideration of the materials and evidences on record which in the instant case the petitioner failed to do.

<u>26. It is a settled principle that the findings of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court; which is the final court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division, as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. In the instant case, the learned advocate for the petitioner failed to point out any such exceptional circumstances. Rather from the judgment of the appellate court it is found that in arriving at its findings the said court carefully considered all the material facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, both oral and documentary and consequently these findings of facts are immune from interference in revision.</u>

27. In view of the discussion made above I find no merit in the Rule.

28. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

29. The impugned Judgment and decree dated 30-11-2010 (decree drawn up and signed on 2-1-2011) passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No. 240 of 2006 in disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 9-6-2004 (decree drawn up and signed on 15-6-2004) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rupgonj, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 dismissing the suit is hereby upheld and confirmed.

30. The order of status-quo so granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the LCR be sent down to the Courts below at once.

End.
