full_judgment:
At the instance of the present defendant-appellant-petitioners, Shawakat Hossain Prodhan and others, this Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite-party Nos.1-42 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained of in the petition moved in Court to-day should not be set aside.

2. This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28-1-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Panchagar allowing the appeal in part in Other Class Appeal No. 53 of 2007 and thereby, affirming the judgment and decree in part and reversing the judgment and decree dated 3-5-2007 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Tatulia, Panchagar decreeing the suit in Other Class Suit No.09 of 2007.

3. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule, inter alia, are that the present opposite-parties as the plaintiffs filed the Other Class Suit No. 9 of 2007 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Tatulia, Panchagar seeking a declaration to set aside the judgment and decree passed earlier in the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 by the then learned Munsif Court, Panchagar, Dinajpur on 16-9-1982 decreeing the said suit exparte.

4. The plaint case is that one Asiruddin was the owner of the suit land appertaining to RS khatian No. 271 Mouja Fetemagos Talluk Ghagra, Panchagar (previously District Panchagar). The said Asiruddin died leaving behind 3 sons Tumijuddin and others, wife Asma Khatun and daughter Jahura Khatun as his legal heirs. Tumijuddin sold 1.66 acres of land to the plaintiff No.1 on 6-3-1982. Tumijuddin and his mother Asma Khatun sold 0.41 acres to Alauddin, Sahadut and Moshiar Rahman. The said Alauddin, Sahadut and Moshiar Rahman died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 2-28 as their legal heirs. The said Tumijuddin and his mother Jahura Khatun sold 0.17 acres of land to one Eiad Ali died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 40-42 as to the legal heirs. The aforementioned plaintiffs are possessing the land ejmali. One Rafiqueuddin as the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-6 filed the Title Suit No.48 of 82 as vendor of the abovementioned land and the said suit was decreed exparte on 16-9-1982, which was not known to plaintiffs as they were not party when the above plaintiffs went for mutation they came to know about the abovementioned exparte decree.

5. The said suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-10 by filing the written statement denying the statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that one Hedaiatullah was the originally owner of the suit land along with other land measuring 68.64 acres. One Naziruddin bought the said land on auction and the said land was given pattan on the 2ild Asar, 1348 BS by to Ojiuddin Prodhan for the land measuring 4.44 acres and the land was recorded in his name. During the period of S.A. khatian the land was wrongly recorded in the name of one Asruddin Prodhan also known as Asamuddin instead of Ojiuddin Prodhan. The said Ojiuddin Prodhan died leaving behind his son Rafiquuddin as his heirs. The said Asam Uddin tried to dispossess. The defendant came to know that SA recorded of right was published in the name of Asiruddin, therefore, the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 was filed against the heirs of Asam Uddin in the Court of the then Munsif, Panchagar wherein Tumijuddin, Jajura Khatun and Asma Khatun were made defendants. The mother and the sister of Rafiquddin were also made the defendants. After service of the notices upon the defendants they appeared in the suit by filing a written statement and also sought adjournment on 15-9-1982 but the learned Judge by rejecting the said application passed the ex parte decree on 16-9-1982.

6. After hearing the parties the learned trial Court decreed the Title Suit No. 9 of 2007 (earlier Title Suit No. 25 of 2006) by his judgment dated 3-5-2007. Being aggrieved the present-plaintiff-petitioners preferred the Title Appeal No.53 of 2007 which was disallowed by the learned Joint District Judge, Panchagar on 28-1-2009. This revisional application has been filed challenging the said judgment of the appellate Court below and the Rule was issued thereupon.

7. Mr SM Bazlur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the present petitioners submits that the learned trial Court as well as the learned Appellate Court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and therefore, the same is liable to be set aside by this Court. The learned Advocate also submits that the Title Suit No.48 of 1982, was filed by the petitioners on 20-2-1982, but the present plaintiff-opposite-parties purchased the land in question on 6-3-1982, which is subsequent to the filing of the earlier suit, as such it is presumed that the present plaintiff-opposite-parties were aware or had knowledge of the suit, but they filed the present suit in the year of 2006, which is seriously barred by limitation, as such, the suit was not maintainable, but the learned trial Court and the learned appellate Court failed to consider the above legal and factual aspects of the case, therefore, came to a wrong conclusion concurrently findings in favour of the present plaintiff-opposite-parties, therefore, the impugned judgments are liable to be set aside and the Rule should be made absolute.

8. The Rule has been opposed by the pre-sent-plaintiff-respondent-opposite-parties.

9. Mr Abul Kalam Azad, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that the learned trial Court has considered the evidence adduced and produced by the parties and came to a decision to decreed the suit filed by the opposite-parties, which was affirmed by the appellate Court below, but the present petitioner obtained the present Rule misleading the Court as to the evidence, therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate further submits that the present suit was filed on 13-3-2006 after came to know of the decree passed in earlier Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 when came to mutate their names on 9-3-2006, therefore, the suit was not barred under Article 95 of the Limitation Act.

10. The learned Advocate also submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the present opposite-parties were not made the parties in the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 and therefore, notices were not served upon them, therefore, no question arises as to service of notices as per requirement under the Code of Civil Procedure. Despite, the fact, this land was recorded in the name of the predecessors of the present opposite-parties in the SA record, as such, the judgment and decree passed in the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 is liable to be set aside, which is not binding upon the present opposite-parties as the plaintiffs.

11. Considering the above submissions made by the Advocates for the respective parties and also considering the revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the annexures therein and also considering the materials in the lower Court records, it appears to me that the present opposite-parties as the plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 25 of 2006, which was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 9 of 2007 seeking a decree for setting aside the judgment and decree passed in the earlier Title Suit No. 48 of 1982, which was decreed on 16-9-1982 exparte.

<u>12. The plaint case is that the present opposite-parties filed the present suit on 13-3-2006 after came to know about the decree in the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982. The first question is to decide whether the suit is barred by limitation or not. In this regard, I have carefully examined the evidence produced by the parties. It transpires to me, that the earlier decree was passed in the year of 1982, which certainly beyond the limitation period, but under the provisions of Article 95 of the Limitation Act, the limitation period for filing a suit to set aside a decree obtained by practicing a fraud, relief must be sought within 3 years from the date when the fraud became to know to the party. In the present case, the plaintiff opposite-parties claimed that when they went to Tohsil Office under as the local Revenue Office on 9-3-2006 at that time the plaintiffs came to know for the first time as to the judgment and decree passed exparte on 16-9-1982. In view of the above, consider that the limitation has not started from the date of judgment and decree, but from the date of knowledge of the decree under the provision of Article 95 of the Limitation Act.</u>

13. I have examined the factual aspects both of the parties and I have found that the present petitioner claimed that they are the successors of the auction purchaser of the suit land, but I found that the present defendant-petitioner failed to produce any document as to this auction purchase and the subsequent transfer of the suit land in their favour. Whereas, the plaintiff-opposite-parties adduced as many as 3 PWs and also filed the documents in support of their cases being exhibit 1 series to exhibit 5 series and from those exhibit it appears that the predecessors of the present opposite-parties had the record of right in the S.A. khatian, which is exhibited marked as 3(1). Moreover, the present plaintiff-opposite-parties produced document as to the record of right being rent receipt exhibits 4 & 4(1). The present plaintiff opposite-parties claimed their title through 3 deeds dated 19-12-1981 exhibit 1 7-1-1982 exhibit 2 and 6-3-1982 exhibit 1(kha) for their ownership upon the suit land.

14. Form the above given facts and evidence adduced by the way of documentary evidence and by way of deposition, I am satisfied that the plaintiff-opposite-parties have proved their case on the balance of probability as to their claim to set aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 48 of 1982. Moreover, the present defendant-petitioner failed to produce sufficient evidence as to their entitlement upon the suit land in particular any pattan by Nazir Uddin, who purchased the land on auction, therefore, the predecessors of the present defendant-petitioner could not have any entitlement upon the land, therefore, the present petitioner certainly do not have any right upon the land.

15. I have carefully examined that the present plaintiff-opposite-parties were not made parties in the earlier Title Suit No.48 of 1982, therefore, the suit was not filed by the present defendant-petitioners with the clean hand, even though it was decreed exparte in favour of the present petitioner, as such, the suit decreed is liable to be set aside.

16. Now, I am inclined to examine the findings of the lower courts. The learned trial Court came to a conclusion decreed the suit in favour of the present plaintiff-petitioners on the basis of the following findings:—

“কিন্তু বিবাদী পক্ষ সাবেক ৭৪৬ নং খতিয়ান দা���িল করে প্রমাণে ব্যবহার করেননি । কাজেই হেদায়েতুল্লা যে সাবেক খতিয়ানের মালিক ছিলেন তা তারা প্রমাণ করতে পারেননি। নালিশী সাবেক খতিয়ানের জমি যে, নিলাম হয় তৎমর্মে বিবাদীপক্ষ কোন নিলামের কাগজ দাখিল করেননি। তাদের মৌরস যে পত্তন মূলে নালিশী খতিয়ানের 8.8৪ একর জমি প্রাপ্ত হন সেই পত্তনের কোন কাগজপত্র বিবাদীপক্ষ আদালতে দাখিল করে প্রমাণে ব্যবহার করেননি । বিবাদীপক্ষ শুধুমাত্র ৪৮/৮২ স্বতু মামলার আরজি, আদেশ ও ডিক্রির জাবেদা নকল দাখিল করেছেন। তাহাছাড়া ৪৮/৮২ স্বত মামলার বর্তমান মামলার বাদীদের মৌরসরা যে হাজির হয়ে সে সম্পর্কে কোন বিশ্বাসযোগ্য কাগজপত্র আদালতে দাখিল করেননি । বিবাদীপক্ষ তাদের দাবীকৃত জমি বাবদ কোন খাজনার দাখিল ও আদালতে দাখিল করেননি । সুতরাং সার্বিক অবস্থা বিবেচনায় প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বিবাদীপক্ষের নালিশী জমিতে কোন স্বত্ব দখল নেই।”

17. The learned appellate Court below concurrently found that the present plaintiff-opposite-parties could prove the wrongful decree in the Title Suit No.48 of 1982, however, the learned appellate Court did not concur finding with the learned trial Court as to the trial upon the suit land, because of the insufficient stamp (Court fees) by the present plaintiff-opposite-parties.

18. In this regard, I am of the view that the present-plaintiff-opposite-parties, in fact that made no prayer claiming title, but only to set aside the judgment and decree passed in the Title Suit No.48 of 1982 on the basis of the following finding:—

“উল্লেখিতভাবে বাদীপক্ষ মোট ২.৩৯ শতক জমি ভোগদখলে প্রাপ্ত হন। ৪৮/৮২ নং স্বত্ব মোকদামায় ২৮-২-৮২ ইং তারিখে দায়ের হয়। বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালতে উক্ত মোকদ্দমা দায়েরের পূর্বে সম্পাদিত ১৯-১২-৮১ ইং তারিখের ১৫৪৭ নং দলিলের ক্রেতা এবং ৭-১-৮২ ইং তারিখের ৩০৫ নং দলিলের ক্রেতাগণকে ৪৮/৮২ নং মোকদ্দমায় পক্ষ করা হয় নাই। বিজ্ঞ বচারিক আদালত সঠিকতাবে উল্লেখিত বিষয় তাহার রায়ের গর্ভে আলোচনা করেছেন। উপরন্তু বিবাদী রেসপনডেন্ট পক্ষ নালিশী খতিয়ানের জমি নিলাম হয়েছে মর্মে যে দাবী করেছেন এবং তৎমর্মে তাদের মৌরশ পত্তন মূলে

নালিশী খতিয়ানের ৪.৪৪ একর জমি প্রাপ্ত হন। সেই সম্পর্কে কোন দালিলিক প্রমাণ নাই। যাহা বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালত

বিস্তারিত বর্ণনায় রায়ের গর্ভে আলোচনা করেছেন।

তবে বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদীলত ৯/০৭ নং অন্য মোকদ্দমায় বাদীর দাবীকৃত প্রার্থনার বাইরে স্বত্ব ঘোষনার ডিত্রী প্রদান করেছেন । নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় বাদীপক্ষ ২০০ টাকার কোর্ট ফি প্রদানে শুধুমাত্র ৪৮/৮২ নং স্বত্ব মোকদ্দমার রায় ও ডিক্রী অকার্যকর, যোগসাজশী এবং বাদীর উপর বাধ্যকর নয় মর্মে ঘোষনার প্রার্থনায় আনয়ন করেছিলেন। কাজেই অত্র আদালত মনে করেন কোর্ট ফি ব্যতীত এবং স্বত্ব ঘোষরার প্রার্থনা আর্জিতে উল্লেখ না থাকায় বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালত নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের স্বত্ব আছে মর্মে যে ঘোষণা করেছেন তাহা আইন সম্মত উপায়ে হয় নাই। কাজেই স্বত্ব ঘোষণার আদেশ হস্তক্ষেপযোগ্য হইতেছে। বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালতের স্বত্ব ঘোষণার আদেশ ব্যতীত ৪৮/৮২ নং অন্য মোকদ্দমার রায় ও ডিত্রী বিষয়ে যে আদেশ প্রদান করেছেন তাহা হস্তক্ষেপযোগ্য নহে।”

19. From the above, two concurrent judgments and decree, I am- of the opinion that the learned Courts below did not comment illegality by passing the judgment in favour of the present opposite-parties. I am therefore, not inclined to interfere into this judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Panchagar.

20. Accordingly, I do not find merit in the Rule.

21. In the result, the Rule is discharged.

The office is directed to communicate this judgment and decree to the concerned court and also directed to send down the Lower Courts Records at once.

End.

lawyer:

parties:
Jagannath Dev Bigraha Thakur ----- Petitioner 
Vs 
Government of the Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur and others----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-2, 9, 9(ka) 9(gha), 12-14, 16, 20, 21(ka) 21(kha), 22(ka) 22(niya), 25, 26, 29-33, 35, 37, 43, 50 and 53-55 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15-4-1999 and 22-4-1999 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 23 of 1988 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-9-1987 and 28-11-1987 respectively passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The material facts leading to the instant civil revision are that the petitioner as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 194 of 1979 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla which being transferred to the Court of Subordinate judge Chandpur was renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 against the defendant-opposite parties praying for declaration of title to schedule-1 land to the plaint and for recovery of khas possession of the schedule-2 land to the plaint by evicting the defendant Nos. 2-54.

3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit schedule-1 property to the plaint measuring an area of 1.62 acres of land recorded in CS. Khatian No.141 of Mouza Kaladi, PS Matlab belonged originally to Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury in Hovvla who constructed a Temple in the Suit Plot No. 408 and established the Deity Sree Sree Jagannath Deb Bigraha Thakur there. The Suit Plot No. 403 was fixed for Rath (Chariot) of the Deity adjacent to the temple. There is a tank in the Plot No. 405 which is used for bathing of the Deity and his daily archana. Plot No. 402 is used as a pathway and Plot No. 407 is a garden in the Deity. Raj Kumar Roy gifted the suit land to the plaintiff-Deity on 10th Sraban, 1326 BS by a registered deed of gift and for conducting the entire ceremonies and affairs of the Deity and appointed a committee named `Sushasan Committee' except the daily puja, are held there. Dole Ceremony, Rath Jatra Ceremony, Harinam Sankirtan and Mohautsab etc. There was never any hot on the entire plot No. 402 0.28 decimals of land of the said plot from north to east side is used as hat. On the death of Raj Kumar his sons Lalit Mohan and others became the shebayet of the Deity. At that time Lalit Mahan settled-out 0.04 decimals of land from plot No. 402 with Ramani Chakraborty and thereafter, Ramani Chakraborty gifted that. On behalf of the Deity one disciple of the Deity filed Title Suit No. 145 of 1940 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court; Chandpur against the Shebayet Lalit Kumar Roy Chowdhury and others for declaration that Deity is the "Public Idol" of the Hindu Communities of Matlab Bazar and got decree on 21-2-1941 in terms of solenama and in pursuance of the decree a "Seba Committee" with Aswini Kumar Biswas as the Secretary for the performance of religious ceremony and for administration of the property of the Deity formed and attested record of rights under East Bangal Estate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was prepared on 15-10-1953 in the name of the Deity for the entire khas land of the Deity. In the said attested khatian 39 decimals of land of plot No. 402 excluding the remaining land of the plot for the hat was correctly recorded along with other land in the name of the Deity. The Secretary, Aswini Kumar Biswas paid rent in respect of the suit land to the Government for 1365 to 1368 BS and got dakhi as. During the Pak Military atrocity in 1971 the apparels of the temple was plundered away and the Hindu people of the area left for India. Taking advantage of the absence of the committee and the Hindu people the concerned officials of the Government by order dated 4-10-1971 most illegally made the entire property of schedule-I khas land of the Government and recorded the same in Khas Khatian No. 1 and started to settle out the said property to different persons illegally. After the liberation of Bangladesh the Seba Committee of the Deity started all out reforms of the temple. But the defendant Nos. 2-54 started to forcibly enter into the suit property illegally and constructed shops therein by dispossession of the plaintiff. The defendants have no right and title to the suit land. In view of the Aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff filed the suit.

4. The defendant Nos. 8, 51, 54, 23, 55, 9(ka) 9(Gha) 2, 12-15, 17, 21, 26, 27, 30-34, 36, 38, 56, 44 and 14 contested the suit by filing separate sets of written statements.

5. The case of the defendant Nos. 8, 51, 54 is that the suit land and some other land originally belonged to Raj Kumar Roy who died leaving behind 5 sons namely Lalit Mohan Roy, SUrendra Kumar Roy, Narendra Kumar Roy, Kamini Kumar Roy and Rajendra Kumar Roy Kamini Kumar died leaving behind only son Benode Behari and Rajendra Kumar died leaving behind his daughter Usha Rani. Raj Kumar never gifted the land plot No. 402 to the deity Jagannath Dev and the alleged deed does not cover the land of plot No. 402. Lalit Mohan and others settled out 1.5 decimals of land from plot No. 402 on 5th Baishakh, 1349 BS with these defendants and since then these defendants have been possessing the same. The land of plot No. 402 has been correctly recorded in khas khatian in the name of Government and the rn SDO, Chandpur settled-out the said land with these defendants.

6. The case of the defendant No. 23 is that 01 decimals of land of the suit plot No. 407 was not covered by the alleged deed of gift for the deity. One Birahini Saha purchased 01 decimal land of plot No. 407 along with some other the land from Mon Mohini Baisnabi and others on 11-2-1942. Birahini Saha sold out the said land to Sarajubal Pal Bhowmik on 27-8-1995 who in turn sold out 0.5 decimal of land of plot No. 407 to this defendant on 30-3-1965. This defendant has been residing there with his family members by constructing building thereon. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land except suit plot No. 404.

7. The case of the defendant No. 1 is that the suit land belonged originally to Raj Kumar and others. The suit land rightly been vested in the Government and it is included in Matlab Bazar. The Government is possessing the suit land. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land.

8. The case defendant No. 55 is Maulavi Amiruddin Dewan and others took settlement of 0.02 decimals of land from plot No, 402 on 1334 B.S. from the original owner and while possessing the same he executed a Kabuliat on 6.5-1939 in favour of the sons of Rajkumar. Amiruddin constructed shops there and carried on business and carried on business and delivered possession of 2/3rd of his land amicably to Abu Yusuf and others. Thereafter the land of plot No. 402 used as hat vested in the Government. There is a `Akhro' of the Hindu community in plot NO. 404. The defendant are possessing the land of plot No. 402 by talking settlement from the Government

9. The case of the defendant No. 9(Ka) to 9(gha) is that Moulvi Amiruddin Dewan, Easin Dewan and Serajuddin. Dewan took settlement of 02 decimals of land from plot No. 402 from the original owner in 1334 B.S. and thereafter, executed a kabuliyat on 6-5-1933 in favour of the sons of Rajkumar. Serajuddin has been possessing his share by a constructing shop and carrying on business there. Thereafter, the land of plot No. 402 was included in hat and vested in the Government. As such, the said land is correctly recorded in SA khatian .No. 504 in the name .of defendant No 9.

10. The case of the defendant No. 2 is that Jobeda Khatun wife of Easin; took settlement of .02 decimals of land of suit plot Nos. 402/832 from the original owner and SA record of right has been correctly prepared in her naive: Jobeda sold out the said land at a consideration of Taka 1,500 to the defendant' No. 2 by registered kabala dated 12-2-65 and the defendant No. 2 mutated his name and has been possessing the same.

11. The case of the defendant Nos.; 12-15, 17, 21, 26, 27, 30-34, 36 and 38 is that the suit plot Nos. 402 and 400 are owned and possessed by. Motlab Masjid Committee: There is a pond in plot No. 405 and water of the said pond is used by the Musallis. The Masjid committee got the said land by purchase froth Maharam Ali by registered kabala. The defendants are tenants of the Masjid committee. The Government has been using the suit land 'except the suit plot No. 402 as land of Toha Bazar from time immemorial. There is a `Alchra' of the Hindu Community in the plot No 404 where the Hindus observe their "puja and religious ceremonies. Except the plot No. 404, no other suit land is Debatar property; as per State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land is the khas land of the Government.

12. The case of the defendant No 56 is that the suit land originally belonged to Raj Kumar and others. Raj Kumar made an oral gift of 02'/2 decimals of land—from 'plot No. 402 to this defendant. Mohar Ali got settlement of 09 decimals' of land from plot No. 402 from Raj Kutner and also took settlement of 03½ decimals of land from- Raj Kumar by kabuliyat on 19-1-1954; that Mohar Ali sold out the said entire 12½  decimals of land to Ali Akbar who purchased the same 'on behalf of the Masjid Committee. The Masjid committee thus got 12½ decimals of land by oral gift: The Masjid committee possessed the said 15 decimals of land through the defendant Nos. 8;12-44 as Bharatia SA record of right has been correctly prepared in the name' of Masjid committee.

13. The case of the defendant-NO.14, is that the said suit land is khas land of the Government and this defendant took settlement of the said land on' 20-11-1970 and has been-possessing the suit land by constructing building and other structures with surrounding wall., The Government settled out some land to the Union Parishad. Ultimately, Hats and Bazar being vested in the Government, the suit land became khas land of the Government.

14. The case of the defendant No. 22 is that this defendant took settlement of .03 decimals of land of plot No. 403 from the government by dahila. Thereafter, the Government took that and bazar in khas and this defendant took lease from the government and accordingly, SA Khatian No, 590 has been correctly prepared in their names.

15. The case of the defendant No. 44 is that the :entire land of plot No. 400 was used as dust bin and said land being situated near the house of this defendant he has been using the same by carrying hotel business there'. The land being acquired by the government his defendant took lease from the government and has been residing there by constructing houses.

16. After trial, the learned Subordinate Judge, Chandpur, dismissed the suit vide the judgment and decree dated 30-9-1987 and 28-11-1987 respectively.

17. As against the judgment and decree dated 30-9-1987 and 28-11-1987 the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 23 of 1988 in the Court, of District Judge, Chandpur which was dismissed vide the impugned judgment and decree dated 15-4-1999 and 22-4-1999.

18. It is against the impugned judgment and decree, the plaintiff is before this Court by filing the instant Civil Revision Case No. 322 of 2000.

19. Mr AB Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate representing the plaintiff petitioner submits that the Courts below by passing the respective judgments and decrees committed error of law in resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice; that as the boundary of the alleged deed of gift dated 30-7-1999 being relayed by an Advocate Commissioner and on relay as the land within the boundary of the deed of gift attracts the suit land, the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the suit land: is not properly identified is not a correct decision; that the finding of the 'appellate' Court below that the suit is not maintainable on the ground that the order of the SDO,. Chandpur dated 4-10-1971 declaring the suit land as khas land of Government stands valid still now. inasmuch as the said order is illegal and void under the President Order No.12 of 1971 is an erroneous finding that the appellate Court below committed an error of law in holding that, the deed of gift dated 30-7-1919 was not acted upon that the Courts below acted on mere surmise and conjecture in passing the-respective judgment and decrees; that the Courts below should have held that the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the entire schedule property. The learned Advocate lastly prays for making the Rule absolute and to set aside the impugned judgment and decree.

20. M. Mr Khizir Hayat, the learned Deputy Attorney-General (DAG) representing the opposite parties submits that the appellate Court below rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree; that the suit land is rightly included in the khas khatian in the Government; that by passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court below committed no error of law resulting in any error in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning any failure of justice. The learned DAG lastly submits that there being no merit in the Civil Revision Case, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

21. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties and considered the materials on record. 22. As stated earlier, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 194 of 1979 which on transfer' was renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 for declaration of title in the schedule-1 land to the plaint and for recovery of khas possession in respect of the land of schedule-2 to the plaint. Said suit was dismissed by the trial Court vide he judgment and decree dated 15-4-1999 and 22-4- 1999 respectively. As against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No.23 of 1988 which was disallowed vide the impugned judgment and decree affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

23. On perusal of ,the judgment of the trial Court it is, found that the trial Court dismissed the suit finding that the suit is barred by limitation; that the suit is bad for defect of parties and that without prayer for partition the suit cannot be maintained. On the other hand, the appellate Court below passed the impugned judgment, and decree dated. 15-4-1999 and 22-4-1999 respectively holding that the suit is not barred limitation and that the suit is not bad for default of parties reversing the finding of the trial Court, The Government or the defendants did not raise any objection against the aforesaid finding the appellate Court below and, as such, it is to be taken that the defendants have accepted the said finding of the appellate court below. So, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the ambit of the instant revision has become very narrow and in the civil revision case, the point mainly to be decided is whether the suit property is Debottor property on whether the Government has rightly made the property khas land.

24. To substantiate his case, the plaintiff filed exhibit-1 the deed of gift dated .30-71 919 executed by Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury exhibit-1/1 kabala dated 15-12-1939 executed by Ramani Mohan Chowdhury favouring Lalit Kumar Roy Chowdhury, ext. 1/2 registered deed dated 15-9-1979 executed by Sree Ramani Mohan Chowdhury favouring the plaintiff. Exhibit-3-3 (Kha) khas, i.e. CS Khatian No.141. Petty khatian No. 141 and Khas khatian No. 1, exhibit-4 series rent receipts in respett of land of the khatian No. 141 for an area of 1.58 acres of land to the Government. The exhibit-1 shows that Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury gifted the suit land to the plaintiff. Exhibit-3 the CS khatian No. 141 which recorded in the name of Raj Kumar Roy Chowdhury. Exhibit-3(a), the petty khatian No. 141 stand recorded in the name of the Deity i.e. the plaintiff. Exhibit-3(b) is the khas khatian in the name of the Government. Exhibit-4 series shows that the plaintiff paid rent of 1.58 acres of land. In this case the exhibit-1 i:e. deed of gift dated 304-1999 is not denied by the defendants. The finding of the appellate Court below is that the exhibit-1 deed of gift is not acted upon. The very recording of the suit land in the name of the plaintiff Deity in Ext.3(a) petty khatian, acceptance of rent by Government from the plaintiff by issuing rent-receipts- Exhibit-4-4(a) series manifest that the Exhibit-1- Deed of gift is acted upon and that by accepting rent of the suit land from the plaintiff-Deity, the Government recognized the plaintiff as a tenant under it. Further, after admitting the plaintiff to be a tenant by way of accepting rent from him and recognizing him as a tenant under it, the Government cannot make the suit property a khas land. Section 20(5)(i)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956 puts an embargo upon the Government to make a Debutter, Waqf property to be a Government khas land. In support of the plaintiffs case, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff cited the case of Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu vs Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (now vested property), Government of Bangladesh reported in 51 DLR 300 in which case it is held that "Once a property becomes a property of the Deity, which is immortal, it continues to be a property of the Deity for all times to come."

<u>25. From the discussion made here above, and so also on observation of the aforesaid case law, this Court is of the opinion that the suit property is a Debutter Property which the Government cannot make Government khas land.</u>

<u>26. As to the finding of the trial Court that the suit land is vague and unspecified, it is to be noted here that in. the Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 a local investigation in respect of the', suit property was held to ascertain as to whether the land as described within the boundary of the exhibit-1 tally with the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint. The Advocate Commissioner after holding local investigation submitted report to the effect that the land as described within the boundary of the exhibit-1 'deed of gift is same and identical with the suit property as described in the schedule the plaint. So, the finding 'of the trial Court that the suit land is indefinite and unspecified is not correct. As to the limitation in filing the suit, the plaintiffs’ alleged dispossession from the suit schedule land was in 1972 and the suit was filed in the year 1979. So, the suit being filed within 12 years of the alleged dispossession, the appellate Court below rightly held that the suit is not barred by limitation. It is to be mentioned here that the deed of gift Ext. 1 dated 30-7-1999 was executed after publication of CS record. So, manually the suit land would not be recorded in the name of the plaintiff in the CS khatian. It has already been found that the Petty Khatian No. 141 i.e. Ext. 3(1) was recorded in the name of the plaintiff. From the discussion made here above, this Court finds right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit schedule-1 land and also find that the suit land is not a Government Khas land; that the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit schedule-2 land by the defendants and that the alleged settlement or lease by the Government to any defendants is illegal and that the deeds leasing out the suit property to the defends are also illegal and void documents.</u>

27. In the light of discussion made here above, the irresistible finding of the Court is that the appellate Court below as well as the trial Court wrongly passed the impugned judgment and decree and that by passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree warrants interference by this Court.

28. This court finds merit in the Civil Revision Case and hence, the Rule deserves to be made absolute.

29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

30. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15-4-1999 and 22-4-1999 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 23 of 1988 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-9-1987 and 28-11-1987 is hereby set aside. 5

31. The Title Suit No. 155 of 1981 is decreed the Rayoti right of the plaintiff-Deity in the suit schedule-1 land on the basis of the registered deed of gift dated 13th Sraban, 1326 BS corresponding to 30-7-1919 is hereby declared.

32. The plaintiff Deity is held entitled to get khas possession of the schedule-2 property to the plaint evicting the defendant Nos. 2-54 therefrom by removing all obstructions. The defendant Nos. 2-54 are hereby directed to vacate the schedule-2 land within 90 days from the date of receipt of this judgment removing construction, if any, raised by them in the suit land. The plaintiff is also held entitled to get manse profit of the schedule-2 land during the period of dispossession by the defendant Nos. 2-54.

33. The order of stay passed at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Let the lower Court's records along with a copy of this judgment be transmitted down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mirza Hussain Haider, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.12.2009, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2437 of 2008, making Rule absolute, reversing the judgment and decree dated 20.06.2008, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No.63 of 2007 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.03.2007, passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.287 of 2006, dismissing the suit.

2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal in short are:

That land measuring 1.29 acres in plot No.21, appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.70 (Umo) originally belonged to Yeasin Hazi who after transferring some part of it owned and possessed 0.29 acre of land. Thereafter he died leaving behind Dubuninnessa (Saburan Nessa) as his heir. Duburunnessa owned and possessed the said quantum of land till she transferred the same in favour of Khodeza Begum by a registered deed of lease bearing No.7752 on 15.12.1955 and delivered possession thereof to her and thereafter on 24.01.1956, Duburunnessa transferred her rent receiving interest to Khodeza Begum by registered deed of sale No.1142 dated 24.01.1956. Consequently S.A. record was prepared in the name of Khodeza Begum and she used to pay rents to the Government regularly. Khodeza Begum died leaving behind two sons and a daughter and they also used to own and possess the same like their predecessor. On 31.03.1969, the said heirs of Khodeza Begum transferred their entire share in the said 0.29 acre of land by registered deed of sale No.2269 dated 31.03.1969 in favour of Zumuruddin. Thereafter Zumuruddin got his name mutated in place of his predecessor and enjoyed the same till his death. At the time of his death he left behind two sons, four daughters and one wife (plaintiffs No.1 to 7), who have been possessing the entire suit land for more than 60 years, continuously, within the knowledge of the defendants and others.

On 19.09.2002, when the plaintiff No.1 went to the Tahsil Office to pay rent, the Tahsilder informed him that the suit land was recorded in the name of Bangladesh Railway and the Ministry of Defence. But actually neither of them had/have any title to and possession in the suit land. The cause of instituting the suit arose on 18.09.2002. Hence the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.287 of 2006.

3. Defendant Nos.1-3 (Divisional Estate Officer, Deputy Commissioner (Land and Building), Bangladesh Railway and Station Master, Narayangonj Rail Station) in one set and defendant No.4 (Government of Bangladesh through Deputy Commissioner, Narayangonj) in another set entered appearance and contested the suit by filing two separate written statements contending, inter alia, that the suit, as framed, is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. The specific case of defendant Nos.1-3, in short, is that long before, in 1882, 0.66 acre of land from the suit plot which was a ditch in nature, along with other lands was acquired for establishment of Dhaka-Mymenshing Rail Line. The same being a ditch it was leased out to one Monir Hossain for fish cultivation. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land.

4. The written statement of defendant No.4 supported the case of defendant Nos.1-3.

5. The trial Court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 29.03.2007 upon hearing the parties on contest against which the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.63 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Narayangonj, who transferred the same to the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Narayangonj, for disposal. The learned Additional District Judge upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record dismissed the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, by his judgment and decree dated 29.06.2008.

6. Challenging the said judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal below, the plaintiff-respondents filed Civil Revision No.2437 of 2008 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 06.12.2009 upon setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Court below.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-appellants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1741 of 2010 before this Division and obtained leave giving rise to the instant civil appeal.

8. Mr. Shaheed Alam, learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the suit land was validly acquired for Railway in L.A. Declaration in 1882 for setting up Narayangonj-Mymenshing Rail Line and accordingly RS. Record has been prepared in the name of the Railway and as such no question of title and possession of the plaintiffs arise. He submits that the High Court Division erroneously made the Rule absolute without reversing the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He further submits that the R.S. Khatian was prepared upon holding physical survey in the field and the plaintiffs having not been found in physical possession in the suit plot and the same being situated at the heart of Narayangonj town/city and no objection having been filed under Rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1954 the plaintiffs' claim of title and possession, since in purchase in 1969, is nothing but a got up story rather a cock and bull story which both the Courts below categorically found to be without any legal basis. Hence, according to him, the High Court Division committed error of law in setting aside the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He lastly submits that the High Court Division illegally interfered with the concurrent findings of fact of the Courts below that `Duburunnessa failed to prove her title on the basis of "Mourashi Patta" from C.S. recorded owner Yasin Hazi' and as such when Duburunnessa's title is not proved all subsequent transfers from Duburunnessa is nullity and as such void. Hence he prayed for allowing the appeal.

9. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Counsel with Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Senior Counsel, appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that although the defendants filed written statement, they did not specifically deny any of the specific assertions made in the plaint regarding the plaintiffs' ownership in the suit land which they purchased from subsequent transferees of Yeasin Haji. In the absence of such specific denial the assertion made by the plaintiffs is to be deemed as admission under Order VIII Rules 3 and 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the plaintiffs produced all original deeds of 1955, 1956 and of 1969 and those being more than 30 years old documents those are very much genuine and admissible under Section 90 of the Evidence Act. Moreover these documents having not been challenged by the defendants those are admitted as genuine. He further submits that mere recording of any one's name in the R.S. record of right is not an evidence of title and as such the defendants having not proved the foundation of RS record of right, title does not vest in them and both the Courts below having concurrently found that the defendants failed to prove the foundation of the R.S. record, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and decreed the suit. It is also submitted that the plaintiffs and defendants examined 2 witnesses each and the plaintiffs produced large number of documents but the Courts below without discussing single evidence dismissed the suit in violation of the mandatory provision of law. He further submits that the defendants never challenged the title of Duburunnessa Begum. Their only grievance is that the lease deed dated 15.12.1955 is hit by Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but the Courts below upon dismissing the facts and circumstances of the case and the law concurrently found that the said provision is not attracted in the present suit and as such the dismissal of the suit by the Courts below was illegal. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the Court of appeal below misread and misconstrued the material evidence on record and without proper application of the same in its true perspective, made out a third case that the plaintiffs by making some documents have been trying to validate their title through the intervention of the Court as the Railway and the Defence Ministry had an indifferent attitude. Thus it committed serious error of law, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. But the High Court Division upon considering the law and the fact in its true perspective lightly found title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and accordingly made the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree of both the Courts below. Hence there being no illegality in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division the same does not call for any interference by this Division.

10. Considering the above facts and circumstances and the submissions made by the parties leave was granted to consider whether the suit land was validly acquired for Railway in LA Declaration of 1882; whether the R.S. record was rightly prepared in the name of Railway on actual field survey; whether the plaintiffs have title and possession on the suit land; whether the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession in the suit land since their purchase in 1969 and whether the High Court Division was wrong in interfering with the concurrent finding that Duburunnessa failed to prove her title on the basis of "Mirashi Title" from the C.S. recorded owner Yeasin Hazi.

11. Admittedly both the Courts below found that the plaintiff's failed to prove the "Mirashi Title" of Duburunnessa, who transferred the suit land firstly, to Khodeza Begum and then from Khodeza, Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, purchased the suit land.

12. Clear case of the plaintiffs is that the original owner Yeasin Hazi died leaving behind Duburunnessa as his only heir who transferred firstly, the possession of the suit land to Khodeza Begum by registered deeds No.7752 dated 15.12.1955 and then transferred her rent receiving interest vide registered deed No.1142 dated 24.01.1956 respectively and accordingly Khodeza's name was recorded in the S.A. khatian. Thereafter the heirs of Khodeza Begum transferred the same to Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, by registered deed of sale No.2269 dated 31.03.1969 (28.03.1969) and Zumuruddin got his name mutated in the government record and then the plaintiffs, the heirs of Zumuruddin, are thus possessing the same within the knowledge of everyone for more than 60 years uninterruptedly and continuously having mutated their names vide Mutation Case No.5099/92-93 dated 19.04.1993 and 1503/93-93 dated 30.09.1993.

13. On the other hand, the defendants claim that the suit land is a ditch which was acquired in LA Declaration of 1882 for Narayangong-Mymenshing Railway Line and R.S. record has been prepared in the name of the Railway. It is further claimed that the suit land being a ditch the same was leased out to one Monir Hossain for five years for fish cultivation though the same has not been extended subsequently after 2005. Both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs failed to prove that Duburunnessa, the heir of Yeasin Hazi had "Mirashi Title". Side by side the Courts below also held that the defendant also failed to prove their-title in the suit land. On the other hand, in addition to the aforesaid finding of defendants' title the High Court Division, on perusal of the materials on record also held both the Courts below rightly found that Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not attracted in the present suit. The High Court Division also found that the defendants also did not produce any document to prove that the suit land was acquired by LA Declaration of 1882. On the question of possession the Courts below held that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their absolute possession on the suit land.

14. The High Court Division, upon scrutinizing the entire materials on record including the evidence of both PWs and DWs and the judgment of both the Courts below found that the defendants-failed to prove that the government acquired any title in the suit land, the defendants did not prefer any appeal or cross appeal against such finding and as such the concurrent finding of the Courts below remained unchallenged for which even if the plaintiffs' suit fails the defendants cannot claim any title over the suit land. Whereas in respect of the finding as to plaintiffs' title it appears that they have challenged the same in higher forums. So the defendants now cannot claim title in the suit land on the face of concurrent finding on the same against them specifically when the last Court of fact held the defendants failed to prove that the government has acquired any title in the suit land.

15. On perusal of the materials on record it appears that the Exhibits filed by the plaintiffs on the basis of which, two PWs clearly proved plaintiffs' title and possession in the suit land as they stated that the plaintiffs are cultivating fish in the suit land (ditch) and they are paying rents to the government regularly upon getting their names mutated vide two mutation cases mentioned above. PW2 specifically stated that he resides beside the suit land for last 15/20 years and all along he saw the plaintiffs, being the owners are possessing the same by cultivating fish. On the other hand, it appears that DW1 admitted that the suit land is a water body and it is a fallow land (পতিত জমি). On the other hand, DW2, the Litigant Inspector of Bangladesh Railway, deposed on behalf of the defendants No.1 to 3, that 'in 1882 the suit land along with other lands was acquired for setting up Narayangong-Mymenshing Railway Track. When the Railway Track was set up upon cutting the earth the suit land remained a ditch, a water body, which has been leased out to one Monir Hossain for five years. In his cross-examination he failed to say how much land Railway claims in the RS plot. He also could not say the name of the owner from whom the land was acquired nor could he say whether the C.S. and S.A. Khatians were prepared in the name of Railway. He also failed to say in whose name those were prepared. He categorically stated that he did not file any document to show that the land was ever acquired in 1882. He also admitted that he did not file any document to show that the suit land was acquired or leased out to Monir Hossain or anyone else. He admitted that after 5 years the lease has not been extended.

16. On consideration of the above evidence the High Court Division rightly found that the Courts below without discussing the evidence on record came to a wrong finding and thereby misdirected themselves in coming to the conclusion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case of title and possession in the suit land.

<u>17. In respect of vesting of title upon Duburunnessa from her father, the CS recorded owner Yeasin Hazi, the High Court Division, upon discussing the entire facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, held that the assertion made in the plaint, in respect of devolution of title and possession on her and all subsequent transfers of title upon different transferees up to the plaintiffs' predecessor by different registered deeds and thereby recording their names in C.S. and S.A. record, the defendants having not denied either of those chronology of devolution of title and transfer in their pleadings or in their oral evidence the same, is treated as admission under Order VIII Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The law of pleadings is very clear in this respect. It is said that the defendant is found to deal specifically each allegation of fact, the truth of which is not admitted. The written statement must not only deal with specifically, the defendants must also answer the point of substance. If the denial of fact is not specific but evasive, the said fact shall be taken to be admitted. In such event, the admission itself being the proof, no other proof is necessary. This view is supported by a decision of this Division in the case of Zafela Begum Vs. Akitulla (16 BLC (AD) 46). The High Court Division, it further appears, took into consideration Exhibits 1, 1(Ka) and 1 (Ga) the Original deeds of transfer dated 17.12.1955, 21.1.01956 and 31.03.1969 which are all more than 30 years old documents, and as such are very much admissible in evidence under Section 90 of the Evidence Act and those documents have strong presumption of genuineness. But the defendants having not challenged either of those documents, their plea that the deed dated 17.12.1955 (Exhibit-1) is hit by Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not at all tenable. Thus the finding of all the Courts that 'Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not at all attracted in the present suit, is thus correct finding of fact and law.</u>

18. It further appears that the S.A. record was prepared in the name of Khodeza Begum who paid rents to the government and thereafter on transfer Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the government record and lastly, the plaintiffs got their names mutated in place of their predecessor Zumuruddin in 1993 it is not understood as to how the R.S. record could be prepared in the name of the defendants after more than one hundred years of alleged acquisition in 1882 about which the plaintiffs came to know much later in 2002. In this respect, the High Court Division while reversing the finding of the Courts below considered Section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as well as several decisions of this Division and came to the conclusion that 'the burden of proof, in civil litigations initially is upon the plaintiff, but depending on the circumstances, it also shifts upon the defendant'. In the present case since the defendants did not deny the title of the plaintiffs, specifically, in their pleadings or in their evidences and since the defendants totally failed to prove acquisition of the suit land by LA Declaration of 1882 by adducing sufficient evidence, the burden of proof is thus shifted upon the defendants to prove their foundation of recording their names in the R.S. record. Having failed to do so the High Court Division, relying on the case of Cinmoy Chowdhury and another Vs. Sree Mridul Chowdhury and others (23 BLD (AD) 83) and Jonab Ali Mondal and others Vs. Md. Anowar Hossain and others (24 BLD 243), rightly came to the conclusion that the R.S. record has been prepared wrongly in the name of the defendants. Moreover, the defendants neither in their pleading nor in their depositions specifically denied publication of C.S. and S.A. record in the name of Yasin Hazi and his subsequent transferees through his daughter Duburunnessa. Apart from the above all the subsequent transferees got their names recorded and mutated in the government record and accordingly they had been paying rents to the government in respect of the suit land. A question may arise what is the presumptive value of final publication of record of rights. In the case of Akbor Ali Vs. Zahiruddin (30 DLR (SC) 81) it has been observed 'Even final publication of record of rights showing one in occupation of the suit land would not if so factor rebut the presumption raised by entries in the earlier record of rights. According to law both the records of rights shall be presumed to be correct at the respective dates of their final publication. Whether the presumption of correctness of the entries in the particular record of right has been rebutted or not shall have to be decided with reference to the facts and circumstances in each case. Thus the question as to whether the presumption of correctness of either of the record of right rebuttable on the other will depend upon the evidence adduced by the parties in the case.

19. In the present case it is claimed by the defendants that the suit land along with other lands was acquired by LA Declaration of 1882 but no evidence to that effect has been led by the defendants. On the other hand the plaintiffs claim that the Yasin Hazi, the original owner is a C.S. recorded tenant, which is generally known to have been prepared in 1920, i.e. much after the alleged acquisition of the suit land in 1882. Thereafter all the subsequent transferees, through Yasin Haji's daughter, Duburunnessa, which is not challenged by the defendants in their pleading or in the evidence, got their names recorded in S.A. record as well as got the same mutated in the government record. In the absence of specific assertions being not denied by the defendants specifically either in their written statement or in their evidence the Court is not inclined to permit the defendants to raise such a question at a belated stage nor the Court should consider such plea. Now question is on the face of all these records how the R.S. record could be prepared in the name of the defendants after more than one hundred years of so called acquisition. The evidence on records shows that the defendants miserably failed to prove such recording on any legal basis. Thus in the present case the plaintiffs having proved their better title, if not to the hilt, than that of the defendants it is enough to decide the case in their favours.

20. From the discussions made herein above since the plaintiffs have been successful in proving their genealogy of title and possession in the suit land and since the defendants failed to challenge the documents relied upon by the plaintiffs and also failed to prove their case of title and possession, it can clearly be held that the defendants have no title and possession in the suit land. On the other hand the plaintiffs could prove the title of Yeasin Hazi, the C.S. recorded tenant and thereafter devolution of title and possession upon his daughter Duburunnessa who in her turn transferred the same Khodeza Begum by two registered documents in 1955 and 1956 which are more than 30 years old documents and relying on such registered documents Khodeza Begum's name being recorded in the S.A. record and thereafter Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs having purchased the same got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the office of the Government, and after his death his heirs, the plaintiffs having got their names mutated, the title and possession of the plaintiffs are found to be proved.

21. Thus the High Court Division, in my considerate view, did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment upon setting aside the findings of the Courts below and decreeing the suit.

22. Accordingly we do not find any merit in this appeal. Hence this civil appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
