full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman J: The instant application has been filed at the instance of the plaintiffs respondents for recording abatement of the instant first appeal. 

	2. The defendant Nos.9-10 being aggrieved by judgment and decree dated 12.09.2013 and 19.09.2013 respectively has preferred the instant first appeal. 

	3. The applicants in the application for recording abatement stated the some facts and laws with some reported cases of the apex Court. 

	4. Mr Khalilur Rahman the learned Advocate for the respondent has submitted that in the present case it is found that the property in suit recorded in C.S. plot No.565 of C.S khatian No. 107 of Mouza Tejkunipara, JL No.278 (Annexure-1) was cited in the projabili property Gazette at page-504, published under Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Annexure-2). The legal effect of acquiring ownership in such projabili property is not only admitted by the defendants-appellants by their engaged Advocate at the time of argument, but also by issuing Memorandum No.বি.আর.ঢাকা-৮১/২০০৩/৩২৪ dated 10.7.2014, disclaiming the ownership and possession in the projabili properties cited in projabili property Gazettee (Annexure-6) and the Ministry of Land as controlling higher authority by issuing Memorandum No. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪২.৬৭.০৩২.১৫ dated 27.10.2015 (Annexure-7) and Memorandum No. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪৬.৫৮.০১৯.১২-৭০  dated 02.02.2016 (Annexure-8) directed the Court of wards and Land Reform Board not to claim ownership over the previous projabili properties of the Wards as cited in the projabili property Gazette. He added that the aforesaid Admitted facts has developed after the institution of the instant appeal and universal acceptance of abolishing jamindary system and declaring the projas as owners in the projabili properties, it is crystal clear that the Court of Wards and the land Reform Board who are appellants in this appeal have no locus-standi to claim over the projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette (Annexure-2). He has pointed that the trial Court has also hold after discussing the said projabili property Gazette (Annexure-2) and also the compensation payment Gazette (Annexure-3) of the Bhawal Raj Estate, that the plaintiffs and other defendants became owners in possession of the suit properly by operation of law, i.e., the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The present appellants, the Court of Wards and the Chairman, Land Reform Board have filed the instant Is' Appeal No.12 of 2014. challenging the said findings of the trial Court connecting with the acquisition of rent receiving interest of the previous Jaminders, Bhawal Rajas in their projabili properties. In such, Circumstances the present plaintiffs respondents who became owners of the suit properties by operation of law, filed the present application for recording an order of abatement as per P.O. No.90 of 1972 after serving copy thereof upon the appellants learned Advocate. 

	5. He has further pointed that the appellant's engaged Advocate had not denied such acquisition of rent receiving interest by filing affidavit in opposition against the said petition, rather all the time they admitted that they have no objection as to acquisition of rent receiving interest in the suit land, which is cited in the projabili property Gazette at page-504 (Annexure-2) He has also categorically pointed that the learned Advocate for the appellant also admitted the facts of development regarding the suit land through issuing of Memorandum dated 10.7.2014 (Annexure-6) under the signature of Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, admitting the acquisition of rent receiving interest and Memorandum dated 27.10.2015 and 02.02.2016 (Annexure-7 and 8) issued by the Ministry of Land as higher authority prohibiting the appellants from claiming right, title and possession in the projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette after filing of the instant First Appeal. 

	6. On the other hand Mr. Nurul Amin learned Senior Advocate for the appellant raised objection in recording the order of abatement of the present appeal as per P.O.90 of 1972 on the grounds that the suit was not filed by the present appellants challenging the acquisition of rent receiving interest of the Jaminder or Jamindary of the Jaminders Bhawal Rajas. They have mere filed the appeal against the judgment of the lower court as per right given to them by the Code of Civil Procedure. So, the appeal should be disposed of on merit, even if, it will ultimately be dismissed on hearing, for the sake of maintaining procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate of the appellants has further submitted referring the provision of Order 20 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure that abatement application would not be applicable in a case wherein the issues have already been framed. 

	7. In reply on the other hand, to above submissions the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs respondents has submitted that in the P.O. 90 of 1972 it clearly directed that the appeal also be abated if acquisition of rent receiving interest is found to be challenged or questioned in the appeal immaterial whether filed by the plaintiffs or defendants. Now, question whether the Plaintiffs-respondent who became owners through the Government's enactment of law, can file the petition for abatement. Answering the said question in the affirmative, the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs-respondents argued that if the Government can raise the question of abatement of appeal as per P.O. 90 of 1972, then why the plaintiffs-respondents who became owners through Government's enactments cannot file the petition for recording abatement of the appeal filed by the defendants-respondents challenging the findings of acquisition of rent receiving interest of the Wards in the pojabili property remain under the management of the Court of Wards. Moreover, the field of P.O. 90 of 1972 has already been expanded by pronouncing different judgments of the apex Court as reported in 33 DLR(SC) 13, and 53 and 14 MLR (AD) 401 and following the aforesaid judgments, the Hon'ble High Court Division in the case of Alhaj Hamdu Miah and others-Vs-Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 19 MLR page-1 categorically came to the finding that any proceeding started by any party challenging acquisition or abolishion of Jamindary by way of acquiring rent receiving interest in their projabili properties, would be deemed to have been abated as under : 

	"If in future, any such illegal uncalled for claim is sought for by the court of wards or if any litigation is continuing or started afresh because of court of wards action by claiming title over the said projabili property, then they would be liable to be dealt with for contempt of Court, apart from such litigations be abated under P.O. 90 of 1972." 

	8. Apart from the above provision of law connecting with P.O. 90 of 1972 it is argued that according to the provision of the Rule 6 of the Order 12 of the Code of Civil Procedure at any stage of the suit the court can pass judgment on admission where one party admitted the case of the other party by filing written statement or otherwise of the Rule-1 of the Order —XV of the Code of Civil procedure, the same view was also reiterated. On the other hand, in Rule 3 of the Order—XV of the Code of Civil procedure the court has been empowered to dispose of the suit as follows: 

	"If the court is satisfied that no further argument or evidence than the parities can at once adduce is required upon such of the issues as many be sufficient for the decision of the suit, and that no injustice will result from proceeding with the suit forthwith, the court may proceed to determine such issues, and, if the finding thereon is sufficient for the decision, may pronounce judgment accordingly whether the summons has been issued for the settlement of issues only or for the final disposal of the suit" 

	9. He has further submitted that now question whether the Hon'ble High Court Division as appellate Court can also have the same power as the trial Court exercise the power. The learned Advocate of the plaintiffs-respondent has submitted that appeal being a continuation of the suit, the Appellate Court will have the same power as of the trial Court. So, this court as Appellate Court can easily dismiss or abate the appeal on admission of the appellants about acquisition of title of the suit properties by the respondents by operation of law as found in annexures -6, 7 and 8 as per Rule 6, Order 12 of the Code of Civil procedure and also by taking into consideration of the provision of Order 15 Rule 1 and 3 of the Code of Civil procedure. Since at present, there is no issue between the plaintiffs-respondents and defendants-appellants nothing remained to be decided by the Court. 

	10. Moreover, every Court has inherent power for securing the ends of justice in any proceeding. So, if the Court from the admitted materials before it found that the pending litigation would ultimately brings no result in favour of the appellants can dismiss the case before it. In that situation the Court by exercising its inherent jurisdiction can dismiss or record the abatement of the suit or appeal. The said power has been approved by the precedents to the case of Abdul Jalil and others Vs. Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and others reported in 53 DLR(AD)-12, to the case of Sanatannessa Bewa Vs. Haipatullah Sarker & ors reported in 41 DLR(AD) -105. 

	11. In the present case, neither this appeal is in a stage of writing judgment nor the Court is deciding any disputed fact of issue or issues between the parties, rather, deciding the prayer of the respondents whether dismissing or abating the appeal as per P.O. 90 of 1972 which is purely a question of law and the parties in appeal being not are in issue rather are agreement with the acquisition of title by the plaintiffs-respondents in the projabili properties as cited in the projabili property Gazette, so, the provision of Order 20, Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable in this case as argued by the learned Advocate for the defendants appellants. 

	12. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective-parties. We have gone through the application for recording abatement of the instant First Appeal. We further anxiously consider and perused the annexures appended with the application for recording abatement. We have gone through P.O. 90 of 1972, referred precedents and the judgment of trial Court with prayer of the suit. 

	13. On considering the submissions of the learned Advocates for both sides and perusing the annexures the question before us is whether the instant First Appeal has been abated as per the provision of the P.O. 90 of 1972, the precedents referred by the learned Advocate for the respondents petitioners and upon the observations and opinion of the trial Court. 

	In this connection we can place reliance to the following facts, circumstances and laws which are necessary to dispose of the application for abatement. 

	14. Before enactment of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 there was Zamindary System in the land Administration and Zamindar had two types of property, one projabili property i.e. land settled to the projas subject to payment of rent to the Zamindar and another, the khas property i.e. the property remained in possession of the Zamindar like his own house, garden, ponds etc. In the projabili property though the Zamindar had only rent receiving interest but in the name of realization of that interest/rent from the projas, the servants under the Zamindar (Paik Peyada) usually oppressed the projas/raiyats which shocked the then political leaders and social reformer for the abolishing the Zamindari System. Those political Leaders and Social reformer promised to the general public that if the country is liberated from British Rule they would abolish the Zamindari System and the projas under the Zamindar would be upgraded as Malik (owner) from the status of Projas. 

	15. Accordingly, when the India was divided in the year 1947, the erstwhile Government of the province of East Pakistan for abolishing the Zamindari System declaring the projas rights and title as owners had enacted the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950. 

	16. The provincial Government for giving effect the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in respect of the projabili property of the Zamindar/rent receiver remained under the management and custody of the court of Wards, the Government of the province of East Pakistan added Section 8(A) in the Court of Wards Act, 1879 by the Act No. X of 1951 stating as follows: 

	"If the rent-receiving interests of a ward in any estate under the charge of the Court are acquired under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, then, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, the remaining properties of such ward including khas lands under the charge of the Court shall continue to remain under its charge and shall be managed in accordance with the provisions of this Act, as if such ward were a disqualified proprietor of an estate." 

	The Government as per said modes and procedure firstly published a gazette notification under Section 3 of the said SAT Act, 1950 in the year 1952 (Annexure-A(1) describing therein the description of the projabili property in the column No.2 and the name and address of the Zamindar/rent Receiver in the column No. 1. 
	
	Before publication of the said projabili property gazette the Government had issued a notice under Section 3(A) and 4 of the said SAT Act, 1950 asking the Zamindar/rent Receiver to submit a list of projabili property remained under possession of their projas and khas property under their ownership and possession with a penal clause in case of failure to submit the list as asked for. 

	The Government after receiving of the said list from the concerned Zamindar both of projabili and khas properties had published a projabili property gazette in the year 1952 under Section 3 of the said SAT Act, 1950. So, the projas under the then Zamindar whether had /have no document connecting with the settlement as projas is very immaterial at least in deciding dispute in between the Zamindar and the projas. 

	17. After publication of the projabili property gazette under Section 3 by complying 3(A) and 4 of the said SAT Act, 1950, the Government had done the following acts: 

	"(a) Assessed the compensation against acquiring the Zamindari/rent receiving interest of the Zamindar under Section 33 of the SAT Act, 1950, which was commonly known as Compensation Assessment Roll (CA Roll). 

	(b) Thereafter paid the said assessed compensation as per CA Roll to the Zamindar. 

	(C) After payment of compensation to the Zamindar the then Government published a compensation payment gazette under Section 46E of the SAT Act, 1950 in the year 1956 declaring that the compensation assessed against acquisition of rent receiving interest of the Zamindar in the projabili property cited in the projabili property gazette published under Section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950 had been paid. 

	(d) After completing the aforesaid process for acquiring Zarnindari/rent receiving interest, the property cited in the projabili property gazette were recorded in the names of concerned projas upgrading them as owners in the khatian known as State Acquisition (S.A.) khatian after determining the land revenue under Section 24(1) of the SAT Act, 1950. As such, almost in all the S.A. khatian Section 24(1) of the SAT Act, 1950 was cited as the basis of determining land development tax payable by the new owners by operation of law to the new rent receiver, the Government." 

	18. After the independence of Bangladesh Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as president of the country when found that the previous Zamindar were yet taking the advantage of loophole of the SAT Act, 1950 and thereby they were trying to make the said Act ineffective and meaningless by filing Civil Suits and other proceedings, he for protecting the projas who became owners by operation of law promulgated the President Order No. 90 of 1972 prohibiting the previous Zamindars/rent receivers from disturbing their previous projas whose properties had been cited in the projabili property gazette as follows: 

	"Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (E.B. Act No. XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Order No. III of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders, passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain, and no person shall bring, any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

	19. In spite of the aforesaid amended Section 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act, 1879 and P.O. 90 of 1972, when the previous Zamindars were found in oppression to the previous projas, some of the previous projas who became owners by operation of law, went to the Supreme Court for redress wherein apex Court of the Country gave observations and directions to the previous Zamindars/rent receivers not to claiming any right, title and interest in their previous projabili properties. 
	20. In spite of the aforementioned laws we can profitably place reliance further in the precedents to the case of Anwara Begum Chowdhury Vs Nur Jahan Begum and others reported in 27 DLR (SC) 109, Peoples Republic of Bangladesh Vs Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraha and others reported in 33 DLR (AD) 13, and Promode Ranj an Saha and others Vs Govt. of Bangladesh and another reported in the said 33 DLR (AD) 53, Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate, represented by its Manager, Dhaka —Vs-Rasheda Begum and others reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401. 

	21. We are of the further view that the parties in the instant appeal confronted with unnecessary and uncalled for litigations which has already been settled connecting with "projabili property" by the apex Court in its decision to the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Deputy Commissioner and others vs. Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraha and others reported in 33 DLR (SC) 13 wherein it has held that: 

	"It is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs. The province of East Pakistan decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiky vs. The province of East Pakistan that on the publication of the notification under section 3, of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all rent-receiving interests including that of debuttor and waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khan land also stood vested in the Government." 

	Further it has held that: P.O. 90 of 1972 puts a complete bar against any acquisition of any property by the Government — All suits. etc. questioning acquisition shall stand abated. 

	In 1963 notifications u/s 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquiring of all interests other than those already acquired under section 3 of the Act, completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act. All the notifications have been published in the official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact is that the Bangladesh (Legal proceedings) (Third) Order, 1972 (P.O. 90, of 1972) was promulgated on 3rd August, 1972. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment-roll. President's Order No. 90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in. force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications, etc. pending in any court against the Government of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B Ordinance No. III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property make there under is challenged in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction, etc. passed in such suits, appeals, etc. shall cease to have any effect and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question. 

	On the coming into operation of P.O. 90 of 1972 notwithstanding any other earlier view of law on the subject, a pending proceeding which is sought to be instituted challenging or calling in question the acquisition of any property under any of the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall abate and no proceedings shall be instituted in any Court. 

	In the Case of Promode Ranjan Saha and others vs. Govt. of Bangladesh and another reported in 33 DLR(AD)53 it has further held that: 

	After the promulgation of P.O. 90 of 1972 — all orders including orders of injunction etc. passed in appeals applications, etc. shall cease to have any effect and no court shall entertain any fresh suit, appeal, application, etc. in which the legality of any such law of acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

	"There can be no denying the fact that the plaintiffs sought to challenge the acquisition of their Hats and Bazars made under the general notification dated 2.4.56 issued under section 3(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and so it is directly hit by President's 
Order No. 90 of 1972, which gives a clear mandate of law that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this Order, all suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Ordinance No. III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect,- and no Court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal — application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question" 

	22. We are of the view that it would be further noteworthy to refer the precedent to the case of Abdul Jalil and others VERSUS Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and others reported in 53 DLR (AD)12 wherein it has held that: 

	"As the ultimate result of the suit is as clear as day light such a suit should be buried at its inception so that no further time is consumed in a fruitless litigation" 

	Following the aforesaid law and decisions of the apex Court, the Hon'ble High Court Division in a case of Sagufta M.N. Housing and others -Vs- Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 19 MLR Page-1, gave observations and directions as follows: 

	"With the publication of notifications under section 3 all rent-receiving interests including wakf and debuttor property stood acquired by and vested in the Government  after the notification issued under section 3 of the Act the status of the under raiyat became upgraded to that of raiyat. The rent receiving interests can be acquired even before the preparation of record of rights and publication of compensation assessment rolls'  with the acquisition of the rent-receiving interests by the government all intermediary interests disappeared and a person holding the land under the government becomes a "tenant", becomes a "raiyat" or a "malik" of the land recognized by the government. Consequently, the under-raiyat who actually holds the land becomes a tenant under the government. Superior land lord (i.e. the raiyat) of an under-raiyat by virtue of elimination of his rent-receiving interests disappears and the under-raiyat is upgraded to the status of a "raiyat".... record of rights prepared and finally published under section 144 cannot be varied by any authority and remedy of wrong entry if any lies with the appropriate court'  the property enlisted/ shown in the "projabili property" Gazette are the properties of "projas" who have been accepted as "owners" and the "rent receiving" interest whatsoever it had therein, of the jamindars all vested to the Government by operation of SAT Act, 1950." 

	23. Therefore, from the above provisions of law and authorities we are of the considered 
view that the Court of Wards and land Reform Board, cannot, under any circumstances, claim ownership over the projabili property of the previous jamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhnury and, as such, cannot proceed with appeal in other words the appeal in question has no legs to stand. However, even the appellant by filing the appeal try to interfere with the right, title and interest of the respondents which are nothing but harassment who has become owners of their respective properties by operation of law. 

	24. It may mention here that in spite of the observations and directions given in the aforesaid judgments by our apex Court when the Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate again started to disturb its previous projas whose property has been cited in the projabili property gazette of 1952 by giving temporary lease to third parties, some of the owners by operation of law started several contempt proceedings before the Hon'ble High Court Division including the contempt proceedings Nos. 226 of 2013 and 346 of 2013. In those two contempt proceedings the Manager of Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate and the then Chairman, land Reform Board appeared before the Hon'ble High Court Division and apologized unconditionally with undertaking that they would not further claim any sorts of right, title and interest over the projabili property as cited in the projabili property gazette dated 24.3.1952. A Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division consisting of their lordships .Mr. Justice Mirza Hussain Haider and Mr. Justice Muhammad Khurshid Alam Sarker accepted their unconditional apology and disposed of the said contempt Rule with observations.

	25. It further appears that after the aforesaid Judgments of the apex Court, the Government officer employed in the Government organization, the Court of Wards realized that the property of private incapable persons given for management and administration to the Court of Wards are not the property of the Court of Wards or Government and the Court of wards is a mere custodian or statutory attorney holder of the Wards, whose property was taken over for management and administration under the Court of Wards Act, 1879 and as such, the income whatever comes from those properties are the income of Wards and nothing of it is deposited in the Government exchequer. They also realized that they as a custodian of the Wards have no authority to retain in their khas possession firstly 375 Bighas thereafter 100 Bighas and now 60 Bighas. They further realized that they had so long done wrong acts, deeds and things in claiming over the projabili properties of the Court of Wards which vested to the projas as owners by operation of law. 

	After realizing their mistake, they firstly issued a Circular No.বি.আর.ঢাকা-৮১/২০০৩/৩২৪ dated 10.7.2014 under the signature of Mr. Raisuddin, the then Manager of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate cum Deputy Secretary of the Government of Bangladesh, stating that the Court of Wards as custodian of the Wards has no claim over the projabili properties as cited in the projabili property gazette published under Section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950 as per section 8(A) of the Court of Wards, 1879 and P.O. 90 of 1972 and also the judgments passed by the apex Court. Thereafter, the concerned Ministry of land had also issued a letter bearing Memo No.৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪২.৬৭.০৩২.১৫ dated 27.10.2015 and another letter bearing Memo NO. ৩১.০০.০০০০.০৪৬.৫৮.০১৯.১২-৭০ dated 02.02.2016 directing the Government servants engaged in the Court of Wards not to claim any sorts of right, title and interest in the projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette in 1952. 

	26. Since admittedly the property of the plaintiffs respondents were projabili properties and accordingly cited the said property in the projabili property gazette dated 24.03.1952 at page No.504 and since the Court of Wards was ordered to be refrained from claiming projabili property cited in the projabili property gazette by amended Section 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act, 1879 and P.O. 90 of 1972 and since following the aforesaid law, the Hon'ble High Court as well as Appellate Division earlier had given direction not to claim any right, title and interest over the projabili property and if claimed by initiating any legal proceeding, then those to be abated. So, the present appeal according to the aforesaid facts, circumstances and laws and the decisions of the apex Court have been cited hereinabove cannot be proceeded. 

	27. According to the pleading of the plaint, the plaintiffs prayed for relief against the present appellants are that to declare that suit R.S. khatian No.500 in the name of the appellants are wrong. As a matter of facts both the learned Advocates admitted that the suit R.S. plot arises out of C.S. khatian No.107 was recorded rightly in the name of Mr. Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury and others by Courts of Wards. It also admitted facts that at the time of the abolishing the Zamindari system the erstwhile East Pakistan Government had enacted the law namely: "The East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1950." 

	In pursuance of that law there was a clear direction upon the Zamindar to submit a report stating the description of the property which they would like to stay as their khas properties and what property would be the land of tenant i.e. projabili. 

	As per the Dacca Gazette dated 24th March 1952 the suit C.S. khatian 107 was in the part of projabili property of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury. 

	So, it is also revealed and admitted that the suit property was not khass property of the Jamindar, rather, admittedly it was projabili property. So, claiming the R.S. record of right in the name of the defendants-appellants who are none but the Court of Wards is clearly against the provision of law of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in as much as under the provision of P.O. 90 of 1972 as the suit R.S. khatian No.500 arises out of C.S. Khatian No.107. 

	28. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate though argued that the appellant did not file the suit nor challenged the order of the acquisition rather filed the appeal against the judgment and decree of the trial Court according to the Code of Civil Procedure. It is true the appellants did not file suit but it cannot be argued on behalf of the appellants that they got the R.S. record of right in its name through purchase deed or on the basis of any other instrument claiming the same from the bonafide owner. Rather, if we have gone through the case law as well as the provision of law of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and P.O. 90 of 1972 as cited herein above then it would be crystal clear that the appellants challenged the judgment and decree by preferring the appeal, resultantly challenged the acquisition of the property as a Court of Ward in violation of the provisions of sections (3) A, 4 of the SAT Act-1950 read with the section 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act 1879 (Act No. X of 1951) and P.O. 90 of 1972. 

	29. Although we are not deciding the appeal on merit but we cannot over looked the above legal and lawful consequence for which at the end of the hearing of the appeal will not give any fruit for the appellants, rather it is crystal clear as per legal provisions of law as cited above the instant appeal is nothing but a fruitless litigation. 

	We are, therefore, of the considered view that according to aforementioned facts, circumstances, laws, and the precedents of the apex Court as have been cited hereinabove and the discussions made hereinabove there is no doubt rather it is crystal clear that appeal is clearly abated in accordance with law as appellants have no locus-standi to proceed with the appeal. 

	30. In that view of the matter we find merit in the application for abatement. 

	31. Resultantly, the application for abatement is allowed. 

	32. The instant appeal is stand abated and the same be also recorded in order book of the appeal. 

	33. The office is directed to communicate this judgment to the Court below at once.

	End.

Mr. A.Y. Mashiuzzaman, with Dr. M. G. Mahmud (Shaheen), Advocates ------ For the Petitioner

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ataur Rahman Khan J.:- Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the the impugned order contained in Memo No. Prasia/5P/ 16 Bidda-Chotto/2009/913/2 dated 15.7.2013 passed by respondent No.3 on behalf of respondent No.2 (Annexure-L) shall bot be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

	2. Short facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, is that, the petitioner's Grand Father Abdur Rahman Munsi was very kind hearted man and in order to enhance education in his local area the petitioner's grand father by Registered deed gifted a piece of land of .24 decimals to the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935. The gift deed was properly executed through registration with the Sub-Registry Office of Ramgati, Noakhali. The certified copy of the said registered deed of Gift dated 12.08.1935 is annexed marked as Annexure-A. 

	3. There is a proggapon issued by respondent No.2 vide Memo No.38.008.035.00.007.2012.688 dated 15.11.2012 where it has been stated that the Managing Committee of any primary school must be consisting of a member of Land-giver (if any) of the school as a Donor Member and the successors of the land giver will decide who will be the Donor Member of the School Managing Committee or the Upazila Parisad will decide any one of the successors as the member of the Managing Committee. The copy of the Proggapan dated 15.11.12 marked as Annexure-B. 

	4. The Chairman of Upazila Parisad respondent No.6 by letter No.00.512.80.00.05.0200- 41 dated 08.04.2013 nominated the petitioner as the Donor member of the Managing Committee as the petitioner is the successor of the land giver. 

	The heirs of the late Abdur Rahman Munsi have no objection to the nomination of the petitioner to be the Managing Committee of the Alexander Model Government Primary School. 

	5. The Chairman of Upazila Parisad respondent No.6 subsequently again by letter No.00.522.00.00.05.02.2013-47 dated 23.04.2013 confirmed that the petitoner's grand father Abdur Rahman Munsi by properly executed registered deed of gift, gifted the said piece of land to the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935 and as the petitioner is the grand son of the land giver, he is the appropriate person to be nominated as the Donor Member of the Managing Committee of the Alexander Model Government Primary School. 

	6. The Upazila Education Officer, Ramgati, Lakshmipur, the respondent No.5 by letter No.12/04 dated 28.04.2013 directed the Headmaster of the Alexander Model Government Primary School to form a Managing Committee as soon as possible. 

	7. The Headmaster of the Alexander Model Government Primary. School respondent No.10 by letter dated 18.04.2013 requested the Assistant Commissioner (Land), the respondent No.9, to identify the original status of the land which was gifted by petitioner's grand father. 

	8. The Surveyor of the Upazilla Land Office, Ramgati, Lakshmipur, submitted a report dated 25.04.2013 regarding the land where the land is found as Khas land. In the report it has been stated that the gifted land of the petitioner's grand father was never a private property according to the record. 

	9. The Assistant Commissioner (Land), Ramgati, Lakshmipur, the respondent No.9, agreed with the report submitted by the surveyor and sent the report to the Alexander Model Government Primary School authority by letter vide Memo No.00.522.009.00.00.001.2013-83 dated 28.04.2013. 

	10. The Headmaster of the Alexander Model Government Primary School issued a letter dated 29.04.2013 where it requested guideline from the Upazilla Sikha Officer regarding the Donor Member as the land is khas land.

	Subsequently, the Upazilla Education Officer, respondent No.5 sent a letter to District Primary Education Officer, the respondent No.4 dated 15.05.2013 for the guideline regarding formation of Managing Committee of Alexander Model Government Primary School. 

	11. Thereafter, the District Primary Education Officer, the respondent No.4 sent a letter vide Memo No.DPU/Lokhi/S.M.C./ 2013/1036 dated 23.06.2013 to the Director General of the Primary Education Odhidaptar, respondent No.2 and requested guideline regarding formation of Committee. 

	12. Suddenly, the respondent No.3 on behalf of the respondent No.2 issued a letter vide Memo No. Prasia/5P/16Bidda-Chotto/2009/913 dated 15.7.2013 and stated that there is no scope to include any member of land-giver in the Managing Committee of Alexander Model Government Primary School as the land is khas land and therefore the gift by the petitioner's grand father was not a valid one. 

	13. Previously there was dispute between Alexander Model Government Primary School and Alexander Pilot High School. A civil case was filed by the Alexander Pilot School bearing No.59/2000. On that occasion the Headmaster of Alexander Model Government Primary School by the written statement admitted that the land was given by the petitioner's grand-father. 

	14. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) is not the authority to ascertain title of the said land which was gifted by the grand father of the petitioner to the Alexander Model Government Primary School. 

	15. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 15.7.2013, the petitioner preferred this Writ Petition before this Court and obtained Rule and operation of the decision of the impugned order contained in Memo No.Prasid5P/16/Bidda-/Chotto/2009/913/2 dated 15.7.2013 passed by respondent No.3 on behalf of the respondent No.2 (Annexure-L) was stayed. 

	16. Mr. A.Y. Mashiuzzaman along with Mr. M.G. Mahmud (Shaheen), the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the impugned order have been issued without considering the real circumstances of the School and real facts. The impugned order passed by the respondents have been issued in violation of the Principles of Natural Justice as such the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. They have further submitted that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) is not the authority to ascertain the title of the land which was gifted by the grand father of the petitioner to the Alexander Model Government Primary School. They have further submitted that grand father of the petitioner late Abdur Rahman Munshi gifted .24 decimals of land in favour of the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935, which was also admitted by the School authority in the written statement filed in Title Suit No.59 of 2000, in view of such admitted fact, the impugned order is absolutely malafide, arbitrary and without jurisdiction. They have further submitted that Chairman of Upazilla Parisad respondent No.6 by letter No.00.512.80.00.05.0200.41 dated 08.01.2013 nominated the petitioner as the Donor Member of the Managing Committee as the petitioner as the successor of the land giver. They, have further 
submitted that the Chairman of Upazila Parisad respondent No.6 subsequently again by letter No.00.522.00.00.05.02.2013-47 dated 23.04.2013 confirmed that the petitioner's grand father Abdur Rahman Munsi by properly executed registered deed of gift, gifted the said piece of land to the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935 and the petitioner is grand son of the land giver, he is the appropriate person to be nominated as the Donor Member of the Managing Committee of the Alexander Model Government Primary School. They have lastly submitted that the respondent No.2 in connivance with the Head master and others issued this impugned order which is not just and sustainable in law. Accordingly, they prayed that the present Rule may be made absolute for ends of justice. 

	17. Mr. Amit Talukder, learned Deputy Attorney General along with Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam, Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that .24 decimals of land in plot No.7619/8297 in JL No.18 of Char Alexander Mouza Ramgai Upazilla under District Lakshmipur has been recorded in khas khatian No.1 of the Government and it was finally published in P.S. record of 1935 and in remarks column of the khatian it was written as school. In S.A survey of 1960 also the said .24 decimals of land of plot No.7619/8297 was also recorded in khas khatian No.1 of the Government. They have further submitted that in this regard the grand father of the petitioner was not the owner of the said land. As per land record the school is situated as khas land and Government is the owner of the land. They have also submitted that the respondent No.3 legally and lawfully issued the impugned letter as per Nitimala dated 15.11.2012 and, as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

	18. Heard the learned Advocate of both sides, perused the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner and affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No.4 and other necessary papers as available on record. It appears from the records that the petitioner's grand father Abdur Rahman Munsi for flourishing education in his locality gifted a piece of land of .24 decimals to the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935 by a registered deed. It also appears that the gift deed was properly executed and registration was done by the Sub-Registry Office of Ramgati, Noakhali. It also appears that the Chairman of Upazilla Parisad respondent No.6 by letter No.00.512 .80.00.05.0200-41 dated 08.04.2013 nominated the petitioner as Donor Member of the Managing Committee as the petitioner is the successor of the land giver. The Chairman of Upazilla Parisad respondent No.6 again by letter No.00.522.00.00.05.02.2013-47 dated 23.04.2013 confirmed that the petitioner's grand father Abdur Rahman Munsi by properly executed registered deed of gift in favour of the Alexander Model Government Primary School on 12.08.1935 and as the petitioner is the grand son of the land giver. The petitioner is legally entitled to be a Member of the School Managing Committee as a representative of land giver. 

	19. It also appears that the Surveyor of the Upazilla Land Officer, Ramgati, Lakshmipur in pursuance of Memo No.10 dated 18.04.2013 submitted a report dated 25.04.2013 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Ramgati, Laxmipur, wherein it is clearly stated that one Abdur Rahman Munsi son of late Rahim Uddin Patwary, Village-Char-Alexander, Mouza No.1 of Char-Alexander, in Khatian No.1 and dag No.8297 by a registered deed No.1459 dated 12.08.1935 gifted 0.24 acres of land in favour of the President of District School Board, Noakhali which was recorded as Char Alexander High School on 21.07.1996. It also appears that the gifted land was wrongly recorded in the Government khas Khatian and the petitioner's grand father Abdur Rahman Munsi filed N.H. Misc Case No.01/1933-34 and on the basis of N.H. Misc. Case No.01/1933-34 the said .24 acres of land was recorded in his name and gifted said .24 decimals of land to Char Alexander Primary School. 

	20. Considering the above facts and circumstances, we find that the respondent No.2 in connivance with the Head master of the Alexander Model Government Primary School have illegally issued the Memo No. Prasia/5P/16Bidda-Chotto/2009/913/2 dated 15.7.2013 corresponding to 1420 B.S. thereby it requires interference. In such circumstances, the petitioner is the appropriate person to be nominated as the Donor Member of the Managing Committee of the Alexander Model Government Primary School as mentioned above. 

	21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. 

	22. The respondents are directed to appoint the petitioner as Donor Member of the Alexander Model Government Primary School.

	23. Communicate the order at once. 

	End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J. :- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties No.1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 passed by the learned District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.102 of 2011 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 15.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st court, Barisal in Title Suit No.31 of 2009 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties No.1-10 as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No.31 of 2009 in the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Barisal for declaration of title in the land described in schedule 'kas of the plaint contending inter cilia, that the suit property appertaining to Mouza-Bogra Alekanda under J.L. No.50 of Police. Station and District-Barisal, corresponding to R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. khatian No.1987, in plotNo.5216 consists of an area .11 acres and .02 acres in plot No.5239 in all .13 acres of land originally belonged to one Nibaran Chandra Bar. Nibaran Chandra Bar during his life time had been owning and possessing the suit property and subsequently transferred the suit land in favour of his two sons Dipok Bar and Dilip Bar and grandsons Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar by an unregistered deed of gift dated 20.04.1979 and handed over possession to them. Subsequently; Nibaran Chandra died on 20.09.1980. Among the aforesaid gift holders, on 10.08.1981 Dilip Bar, Mikel P.K. Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their portion of land in favour of Dipak Bar by a deed of gift. Thereafter; Dipak Bar by virtue of a Mutation Case being No.593/1981-82 mutated his name in the Government 'Serest-a' and paying rents regularly for the suit property. Subsequently; Dipak Bar mortgaged .51/2 acres of land in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and in lieu of that; obtained loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. After taking loan keeping mortgage of some of the properties, Dipak Bar erected a semi-pakka dwelling house consists-of 03 bed rooms, kitchen and latrine therein and started to reside therein with his family members. Thereafter; Dipak Bar died leaving behind three sons namely the plaintiff No.1 Rupak Bar and the predecessor of the plaintiffs No.2-5 Mikel P.K. Bar and the predecessor of the plaintiff No.6 & 7 Pulak Bar with two daughters the plaintiff No.8 & 9 and one wife, the plaintiff No.10 and in this way the heirs of Dipak Bar use to reside in the suit homestead property after payment of the loan amount in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. It is the case of the plaintiffs that the 'defendants having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property, on the basis of false allegation claimed the suit property on 22.04.2008 and tried to mutate their names at which the title of the plaintiffs have been clouded and to dispel that cloud, they have instituted the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No.1, 2 and 4 in short is thus that the property-in-dispute originally belonged to Nibaran Chandra Bar and he died leaving behind his heirs two sons Dipak Bar and Dilip Bar with one daughter Era Bar and in this way the sons and daughter of the original owner became the owner of the suit property. After the death of Dilip Bar his one wife Saraj Bar and brother Dipak Bar and sister Era Bar became the owner and possessors of the suit property. The further case of the defendants is such that the wife of Dilip Bar died leaving behind three sons namely Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar with two daughters; the plaintiffs No.8 and 9. Subsequently, Pulak Bar died leaving behind his one daughter the plaintiff No.6 and one wife Jesika Bar and in this way the heirs and successive heirs of Dipak Bar used to possess the suit property. The plaintiffs No.1-5 with an ill-motive to deprive the defendants created two deed of gifts and in fact Nibaran Chandra Bar or Dilip Bar never executed any deed of gift as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs and as such the plaintiff's suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing 05 (five) different issues decided the issues on maintainability, limitation and defect of party in favour of the plaintiffs and decided the issue on right, title, interest and possession, against the plaintiffs and thereby dismissed the suit on 15.06.2011.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being No.102 of 2011 in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal which was heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge himself and by the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 the learned appellate court allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and decreed the suit on contest.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-respondent-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained this Rule with an interim order of status quo.

7. During hearing of this Rule, Mr. Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Md. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal misdirected himself in his total approach of the matter and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned District Judge, Barisal at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree failed to appreciate the exact proposition of law and also failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective. The learned Advocate also submits that admittedly the property-in-dispute originally belonged to Nibaran Chandra Bar and it is the positive contention of the plaintiffs that, by two deeds of gift, they have acquired the suit property and possessing the same, but the plaintiffs to the suit have failed to prove that the executants of the deeds in fact executed the deeds in favour of the donees and there is no direct evidence of possession in favour of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate argued that none of the plaintiff's witnesses have been able to prove the case of the plaintiffs and the P.Ws. are not competent, disinterested and trustworthy while the defendant's witnesses have successfully proved the case of the defendants and disproved the case of the plaintiffs, which is totally ignored by the learned appellate court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the trial court during disposal of the original suit rightly under the ambit of Order V, rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure after proper evaluation of the evidence on records dismissed the suit on contest. But the learned appellate court without reversing the findings of the trial court reversed the judgment and decree of the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law and facts.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit by adducing sufficient tangible, credible evidence both oral and documentary have successfully proved that they have acquired their valid right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by virtue of their deeds of gift and as successors of the original admitted owner Nibaran Chandra Bar and that the plaintiffs to the suit after acquiring the suit property possessing the same after mutating their names in the government `seresta' and by regular payment of rents to the government. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court during disposal of the original suit decided in his judgment and decree that the suit in its present form is maintainable and there is no legal bar of institution of the original suit and the learned Joint District Judge, 1' Court, Barisal also decided conclusively that the suit is not barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties. The only point for dismissal the suit was such by the learned trial court that the title and interest of the suit property is not proved from the side of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate argued that against the observation and decisions of the trial court on point of limitation, defect of party and maintainability, the defendants did not file any appeal or cross-objection and thereby it is the proposition of law that they have admitted that findings and decisions of the trial court which is apparently against them. The leaned Advocate submits that the deeds of gift as contended from the side of the plaintiffs in their pleading, has been duly proved and those were exhibited under the provisions of Evidence Act without any objection. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in the year 1979 there was no provision that the unregistered deed of gift is not valid in the eye of law and the learned trial court is totally misconceived in holding the view that the title documents of the plaintiffs are not proved. The learned Advocate in his submissions categorically pointed out the evidence on records and submits that the learned appellate court at the time of deciding the merit of the appeal rightly after proper sifting of evidence and assessment of the same in its true perspective on proper appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and rebutted the findings of the trial court, adverting evidence on records and thereafter; reversed the findings and judgment passed by the trial court and in the impugned judgment and decree there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with.

10. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned counsels, having gone through the respective cases of the parties and the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court as well as the appellate court in consultation with the evidence on records and the pleadings of the parties it transpires that the suit property appertaining to Mouza Bogra Alekanda under Barisal Sadar Upazila corresponding to R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. Khatian No.1987 in plot No.5216 of the S.A. khatian No.1987 consists of an area 0.11 acres and .02 acres of S.A. plot No.5239 in all .13 acres of land originally belonged to one Nibaran Chandra Bar. Nibaran Chandra Bar during his life time had been owning and possessing the suit property and thereafter transferred the suit land in favour of his two sons Dipok Bar and Dilip Bar and grandsons Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar by an unregistered deed of gift dated 20.04.1979, which was written on 19.04.1979. It was further contention of the plaintiffs that the admitted owner of the property after execution of the deed of gift handed over possession of the suit property in favour of the aforesaid 05 donees. Subsequently; by another deed of gift dated 10.08.1981 Mikel P.K. Bar, Pulok Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their share in favour of Dipak Bar. The aforesaid two deeds of gift have been marked as Exhibit-7 and 7(ka) after its formal proof. by the attesting witness of the deeds P.W.2 Pal Sarnendu Sarker, who in fact proved the deeds dated 20.04.1979 and 10.08.1981. It further transpires from the papers on records that the plaintiffs in order to prove their case have produced the R.S. khatian No.1417 and S.A. Khatian No.1987 which has been marked as Exhibit No.2 and 3 respectively. Besides this; the Mutation Khatian No.16008 and the paper relating to Mutation Case No.593KT/81-82 has also been produced from the side of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land and these papers have been marked as Exhibit-4 and 5 respectively by which the plaintiff Dipak Bar have mutated his name in the government `seresia. The subsequent payment of rents in respect of the suit property followed by rent receipts were also produced from the side of the plaintiffs to substantiate their case. With regard to taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation by Dipak Bar, the mortgage papers in respect of .5Y2 acres of land has been marked as Exhibit-2 by the trial court and it is the positive case of the plaintiffs in their pleadings that after taking loan, their predecessor have erected a semi-pacca dwelling house in the suit property and started to reside therein. The plaintiff's predecessor Dipak Bar opened a separate khatian in the government `seresta' and after payment of rent obtained rent receipt which is Exhibit-1.

11. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records I find that the specific assertion of the plaintiffs that the son of Nibaron Chandra namely Dilip Bar was unmarried and on the contrary it is the case of the contesting defendants that the witness No.2 of the defendants namely Soraj Bar is the married wife of Dilip Bar.

12. To substantiate the respective cases of the parties, 04 witnesses were produced from the side of the plaintiffs and 03 witnesses from the side of the defendants.

13. P.W.1 is the plaintiff No.9 who is the daughter of Dipak Bar namely Orpa Bar. This witness deposed on behalf of all the plaintiffs. In her testimony, she has categorically testified that her grandfather Nibaron Chandra Bar was the original owner of the suit property and his grandfather gifted the property in favour of his sons Dipak Bar, Dilip Bar and three grand sons. In the said deed of gift of 20.04.1979 the witnesses were the Secretary of Baptist Church namely Smith Biswas and the President/Proctor of YMCA. P.W.1 further testified in her deposition that Dilip Bar subsequently by another deed of gift dated 10.08.1981 transferred his share in favour of his brother Dipok Bar. On the same date the 03 donees of the earlier gift deed, Mike! P.K. Bar, Pulak Bar and Rupak Bar transferred their share in favour of Dipak Bar and Dipak Bar in a mutation proceedings mutated his name and opened a separate khatian. He also paid rent for the suit property. The plaintiff No.9 to substantiate the pleadings of the plaintiffs also testified that her father Dipak Bar after taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation erected a dwelling house consists of 03 rooms and used to reside therein with his family members.

During cross-examination from the side of the defendants the witness No.1 of the plaintiffs in a reply to a question testified that, it is the fact that the suit property was acquired by two sons of Nibaran Chandra and one daughter Era Bar. This witness in her deposition in a reply to another question from the side of the contesting defendants testified that they have filed the mortgage deed of 16.08.1982 which is in respect of taking loan from Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. This paper has been marked as Exhibit-6, and the plaintiffs have also submitted the Poura Tax receipt vide Exhibit-7.

14. P.W.2 is the attesting witness of the deeds of gift, Pal Sarnindu Sarker. This witness in his testimony testified in support of the deeds of gift dated 20.04.1979 and 10.08.1981. He has identified his signatures in serial NO.6 of the deed of 1979 and serial No.1 of the deed of 1981.

During cross-examination this witness specifically testified about his presence at the time of delivery of possession and presence of other two witnesses who were 7/8 in numbers.

15. P.W.3 is one Kamol Sarker, who is another attesting witness of the deed of gift dated 10.08.1981. This witness identified his signature as attesting witness of the deed in serial No.2. From his cross-examination it appears that at the relevant time he was a teacher of Baptist Mission School and Secretary of the Church.

16. The last witness of the plaintiffs is P.W.4 A.T.M. Shahidullah, who is a Ward Councilor of Barisal City Corporation No.10. This witness in his testimony testifies that he knows the suit land, in where the plaintiffs are residing as of their homestead and in the said property the defendants have no possession. P.W.4 in his deposition categorically testified that in his area the defendants are not the voters, but the plaintiffs are voters. As to the identity of the suit property the witness No.4 deposed that the suit land is north-south long and in the northern side of the suit property some dwelling huts lies. P.W.4 also testified in his testimony that the defendants are not the residents of the suit Ward No.10 and they are the residents of Ward No.11 and both the two wards are adjacent.

17. Vis-à-vis; the witness No.1 of the defendants is the defendant No.4 Hiya Moni Sarker. This witness in her deposition testified that her mother's father is Nibaran Chandra Bar, who had three sons and one daughter, Rupak, Dilip, Dipak and her (D.W.1) mother Era Bar, who obtained 1/3 share in the suit property. D. W.1 further testified that Dilip Bar was married and his wife is Soraj Bar. After the death of her (D. W.1) mother the defendants No.1-5 became her heirs.

During cross-examination from the side of the plaintiffs D.W.1 frankly admitted that her residence is in Ward No.11 and the plaintiff's residence is situated in Ward No.10. This witness expressed her inability to state as to whether Nibaran Chandra Bar had signature in the deed of gift dated 19.04.1979. This witness also admitted in her testimony that the persons namely S. Biswas, Samir Adhikari, Sudhir Kumar Sarker and Probir Guha of the concerned locality are good and the defendants did not lodge any objection against the record. This witness in her testimony did not deny the building of Rupak Bar, but testifies that she does not know the area of the building and lastly this witness Hiya Moni Sarker frankly admits in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiffs that they did not file any case against the deeds of gift of the plaintiffs.

18. D.W.2 Soraj Bar testified in her testimony that Nibaran Bar was her father-in-law and in the year 1982 she married Dilip Bar at Dhaka Eskaton Church. This witness admits that the plaintiffs are the sons of her husband's brother.

During cross-examination, D.W.2 admitted at a stage that she worked as nurse at Barisal Baptist Mission Girl's School and in the school, she gave her address, which is different with her present address.

19. The last witness of the defendants D.W.3 Florence Mitra Karmakar is the Head Mistress of Barishal Baptist Mission Girl's High School. This witness in her deposition deposed that in her school, a lady namely Soraj Bar served, and her husband's name is Dilip Kumar Bar. This witness gave a certificate to that effect which has been marked as Exhibit-`ka'.

During cross-examination from the side of the plaintiffs, D.W.3 testified at a stage that she ever did not find the husband of Soraj Bar and also did not find the certificate of their marriage, but she knows that in that certificate the address of Dilip Bar was mentioned at New Eskaton. This witness in her cross-examination frankly admits that, in the certificate the address which was given by D.W.2 Soroj Bar is not same with the address of New Eskaton.

<u>20. On anxious consideration and assessment of mine on the evidence as adduced from the sides of the respective parties, I find that the learned appellate court in his observation and findings categorically adverting evidence on records reversed the findings of the trial court as to the right, title, interest and possession of the parties and after proper evaluation of the evidences, both oral and documentary, arrived at a conclusive decision that the plaintiffs to the suit have successfully discharged their onus in proving their respective case and there is no cogent and trustworthy evidence, which can be relied on from the side of the defendants to falsify the case of the plaintiffs. Under the ambit of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned appellate court elaborately discussed the evidence on records in its true perspective and thereafter decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellants therein. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from any sort of illegality or infirmity. Relying upon two decisions reported in 29 DLR 239 and 2 ADC 211, the learned District Judge, Barisal rightly decided the points in hands and the matter of adverse possession and hence, I find no ambiguity or misquoting of the provision of law as alleged from the side of the present petitioners, in the impugned judgment and decree. As to the acquisition of the right, title, interest and possession in the suit property the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs led me to draw such inference that in the suit property the plaintiffs have acquired a valid right, title, interest and they are possessing the same.</u>

<u>21. It is to be remembered that, under section 49 of the Registration Act [XVI of 1908], a document which is required to be registered under this Act, but not registered, yet be admitted for collateral purposes, as to prove the nature of possession and such an ancient document can be used to prove acquisition of title by adverse possession in appropriate cases.</u>

22. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule has got no merit to succeed.

23. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12.04.2012 passed by the learned District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.102 of 2011 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 15.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1 st court, Barisal in Title Suit No.31 of 2009 dismissing the suit is hereby affirmed.

24. The order of status quo granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

25. However, there will be no order as to costs.

26. Send back the Lower Court's Records and communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.

জনাব বিচারপতি গৌবিন্দ চন্দ্র ঠাকুরঃ গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশের সংবিধানের ১০২ অনুচ্ছেদের অধীন দায়েরকৃত অত্র রীট মোকদ্মায় গত ১৩/০৪/২০১৬ইং তারিখে এই মর্মে কারণ দর্শানোর জন্যে রুলনিশি জারী করা হয় যে, স্মারক নং-টিভি-লাইসেন্স/প্রশা-১৯৬/এফ.৩/১৩৮৪ তারিখ
১৮/০২/২০১৬ইং সংযুক্তি ই' এর মাধ্যমে ৫, ৬, ৭ ও ৯ নং প্রতিপক্ষগণ যে কার্ষধারা শুরু করেছেন তা কেন আইনগত কর্তৃত্ব ব্যতিরেকে গৃহীত হয়েছে ও তার কোন আইনগত কার্যকরতা নেই বলে ঘোষণা করা হবে না এবং অথবা অত্র আদালতের দৃষ্টিতে সমীচীন অন্য কোন আদেশ কেন প্রদান করা হবেনা।

	২। ১৮/০২/২০১৬ইং তারিখের তর্কিত স্মারক নং-টিভি-লাইসেন্স/প্রশা-১৯৬/এফ.৩/১৩৮৪ এর কার্যকারিতা রুল নিশিটি নিস্পত্তি না হওয়া পর্যস্ত প্রাথমিকভাবে ৩(তিন)
মাসের জন্যে স্থগিত করা হয়। 

	৩। উক্ত স্থগিতাদেশ সময়ে সময়ে এবং সর্বশেষ ১৩/১১/২০১৭ইং তারিখের আদেশে ০৬(ছয়) মাসের জন্যে বর্ধিত করা হয়; ফলে, উক্ত স্থগিতাদেশ এখনও বহাল আছে।

	৪ । অত্র রীট মোকদ্দমা নিস্পত্তির জন্যে প্রয়োজনীয় প্রাসঙ্গিক ঘটনাবলী সংক্ষিপ্ত আকারে নিম্নরূপঃ  
	রীট আবেদনে বলা হয় যে, আবেদনকারী ফিড অপারেটর লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্ত হয়ে চট্টগ্রাম জেলাধীন হাটহাজারী উপজেলার ১২নং চিকনদন্তী ইউনিয়নে কেবল টেলিভিশন নেটওয়ার্ক কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করে আসছেন। এ সময় প্রতিপক্ষগণ একই ইউনিয়নে অনুরূপ কার্যক্রম পরিচালনার জন্যে
এ.টি.এম. কমিউনিকেশনকেও ফিড অপারেটর লাইসে���্স প্রদান করেন। বর্তমানে উভয়ে উক্ত ইউনিয়নে তাঁদের কার্যক্রম পারচালনা করছেন৷ পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক আবেদনকারীর শান্তিপূরণ ব্যবসায় বিঘ্ন সৃষ্টি করায় তিনি ৪নং প্রতিপক্ষ তথা জেলা ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট, চট্টগ্রামের নিকট একটি 

দরখাস্ত দাখিল করেন। জেলা ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট দরখাস্তটি নিস্পত্তি না করায় তিনি রীট পিটিশন নং-৪৩৫৪/২০১৪ দায়ের করেন। হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের একটি দ্বৈত বেঞ্চ উক্ত দরখাস্ত নিস্পত্তি করার নির্দেশ প্রদান করে রীটটি নিস্পত্তি করেন। উক্ত আদেশের আলোকে অতিরিক্ত জেলা ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখে আবেদনকারীর দরখাস্ত নিস্পত্তির লক্ষ্যে এক বৈঠক আহ্বান করেন। উক্ত বৈঠকে পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক এর মালিক মোঃ নাজিম এবং বর্তমান ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ মোঃ শামছুল আলম আইনজীবিসহ উপস্থিত ছিলেন। উভয়পক্ষকে শুনে বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনার ক্ষেত্রে স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় রাখার আদেশ দেন। উভয়পক্ষ এ আদেশ মেনে নেন। উক্ত সিদ্ধান্ত বলবৎ থাকা অবস্থায় ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ একই ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ এলাকায় এস.এন.এল ডিজিটাল কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক নামে আরো একটি ফিড অপারেটর লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির জন্য কর্তৃপক্ষ বরাবরে আবেদন করেন। উক্ত আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে প্রতিপক্ষগণ বর্তমান তর্কিত কার্যক্রম শুরু করেন যা সংযুক্তি-“ই' তে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে। অন্য কোন সমফলপ্রদ প্রতিকার না থাকায় আবেদনকারী অত্র রীট আবেদন দাখিল করতে বাধ্য হয়েছেন । অত্র রীট আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে তিনি উল্লেখিত রুল নিশি এবং তর্কিত কার্যক্রমের কার্যকারিতা স্থগিতকরনের আদেশ প্রাপ্ত হয়েছেন।
	
	৫। ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ একটি আপত্তিমূলক হলফনামা দাখিল করে রীট আবেদনে প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করছেন। উক্ত হলফনামায় রীট আবেদনে আনীত অভিযোগসমূহ খন্ডনপূর্বক এই মর্মে বর্ণনা করা হয় যে, পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক এর সাথে এস.এন.এল ডিজিটাল কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক এর কোন সম্পর্ক নেই।তবে উক্ত সভায় তিনি পাহাঁড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্কের মালিকের সাথে উপস্থিত ছিলেন। একচেটিয়া ব্যবসা নিরুৎসাহিত করার বিধান সংশ্লিষ্ট আইনে রয়েছে। অত্র প্রতিপক্ষ লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির জন্যে প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্র সংগ্রহ পূর্বক উক্ত আবেদন করেছেন। আবেদনটি নিস্পত্তি করে রয়েছে। এমতাবস্থায়, রুলনিশিটি খারিজযোগ্য|

	৬। রীট আবেদনকারীপক্ষে বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি জনাব আব্দুস সালাম মামুন এই মর্মে নিবেদন করেন যে, তর্কিত কার্যক্রম ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখে প্রদত্ত স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় রাখার আদেশে বিঘ্ন ঘটিয়েছে বা উক্ত আদেশকে অকার্যকর করেছে বিধায় তর্কিত কার্যক্রম আইনগত কর্তৃত্ব, ফল ও বলবিহীন মর্মে ঘোষনাযোগ্য ।

	৭। বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি বলেন যে, ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ নিজে ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখে সভায় উপস্থিত থেকে স্থিতিবস্থা বজায় রাখার আদেশ সম্পর্কে অবহিত হয়েছেন; ফলে ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষের কার্যক্রম কেবল অবৈধ নয় তা অসৎ উদ্দেশ্য প্রণোদিত এবং আইনগত কর্তৃত্ব, ফল ও বলবিহীনও বটে।

	৮। অপরপক্ষে বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি জনাব এ.কে.এম বদরুদ্দোজা এবং জনাব মোহাম্মদ আরিফুজ্জামান খান বলেন, ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষের আবেদনটি আইনগতভাবে গ্রহণযোগ্য কিনা তা নির্ধারনের জন্যেই তর্কিত কার্যক্রম শুরু করা হয়েছে; ফলে উক্ত কার্যক্রম দ্বারা আবেদনকারীর সংক্ষুব্ধ হওয়ার কোন কারণ নেই বিধায় রুলনিশিটি খারিজযোগ্য।
	
	৯। প্রতিপক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি আরো বলেন, একচেটিয়া ব্যবসা নিরুৎসাহিত করার জন্যে আইনে যে বিধান রয়েছে সে আলোকেই অত্র প্রতিপক্ষের আবেদন যথাযথভাবে নিস্পত্তি করতে কর্তৃপক্ষ আইনগতভাবে বাধ্য; সুতরাং, অত্র রীট আবেদন দাখিল করে আবেদনকারী কর্তৃপক্ষকে দায়িত্ব পালন থেকে অবৈধভাবে বিরত রাখার অভিপ্রায় ব্যক্ত করেছেন বিধায় রীট আবেদনটি অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যপ্রণোদিত হওয়ায় তা খারিজযোগ্য।

	১০। রীট আবেদন, আপত্তিমূলক হলফনামা, উভয়পক্ষ থেকে দাখিলকৃত অতিরিক্ত হলফনামাসহ যাবতীয় কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনা এবং একই সাথে উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবির বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করলাম।

	১১। রীট আবেদনকারী ব্লাড ড্রপ কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক এটিএম কমিউনিকেশন নামে অপর একটি ফিড অপারেটরের সাথে চট্টগ্রাম জেলাধীন হাটহাজারী উপজেলার ১২নং চিকনদন্তী ইউনিয়নে কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করে আসছেন। এমতাবস্থায়, পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক নামে অপর এক ব্যক্তি ফিড অপারেটর কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করার উদ্যোগ নেয়। উক্ত উদ্যোগ আবেদনকারীর কার্যক্রমে বিঘ্ন ঘটায় মর্মে অভিযোগসহ আবেদনকারী ২২/০৩/২০১৪ইং তারিখে জেলা প্রশাসক বরাবর একটি আবেদন দাখিল করেন। কিন্তু উক্ত আবেদন নিস্পত্তি না করায় আবেদনকারী রীট পিটিশন নং-৪৩৫৪/২০১৪ দায়ের পিটিশনটি নিস্পত্তি করা হয়। উক্ত দরখাস্ত নিষ্পত্তি করার জন্যে অতিরিক্ত জেলা ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখে একটি সভার আবেদন করেন। কাগজপত্র থেকে প্রতীয়মান হয়; উক্ত সভায় অত্র ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ মোঃ শামসুল আলম পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক এর মালিক মোঃ নাজিম এর সাথে উপস্থিত ছিলেন। আলোচনার পর উভয়পক্ষকে কেবল
নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনার ক্ষেত্রে স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় রাখার আদেশ দেয়া হয়। উক্ত স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় থাকা অবস্থায় বর্তমান ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ এস.এন.এল. ডিজিটাল কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক নামে আরেকটি নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনার জন্য আবেদন দাখিল করেন। উক্ত আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশন কর্তৃপক্ষ নিম্নোক্ত বিষয়সমূহ বিবেচনা করে সরজমিনে তদন্ত পূর্বক প্রার্থীত লাইসেন্স ইস্যু করার বিষয়ে তর্কিত আদেশ প্রদান করেন।

গ. এ কার্যালয়ের রেকর্ড মতে, চট্টগ্রাম জেলার হাটহাজারী উপজেলাধীন চিকনদন্ডী ইউনিয়ন এলাকায় বিটিভির লাইসেন্সধারী একাধিক কেবল অপারেটর/ফিড অপারেটর প্রতিষ্ঠান রয়েছে। কাজেই, চট্টগ্রাম জেলার হাটহাজারী উপজেলাধীন চিকনদন্ডী ইউনিয়ন এলাকায় “এস.এন.এল ডিজিটাল কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক, ঠিকানা-নূর বিপনী বিতান (২য় তলা), বড়দিঘীরপাড়, হাটহাজারী, উট্টগ্রাম'-নামীয় প্রতিষ্ঠানের অনুকূলে নতুন ফিড অপারেটর লাইসেন্স ইস্যু করার উপযুক্ততা যাচাই করা এবং
ঘ. এই প্রতিষ্ঠানকে ফিড অপারেটর লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা হলে উক্ত এলাকায় আইন শৃঙ্খলা পরিস্থিতির অবনতি হবে কিনা-তা খতিয়ে দেখা।”

১২। তর্কিত আদেশ থেকে প্রতীয়মান হয়, উক্ত আদেশ দ্বারা বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশন কর্তৃপক্ষ ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষকে কোন লাইসেন্স প্রদানের নির্দেশ প্রদান করেননি; বরং তাকে লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা সমীচীন হবে কিনা তা নিরূপন করার জন্যেই উক্ত আদেশটি দেয়া হয়েছে। আবেদনকারীর মূল বক্তব্য হল, ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখের স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় থাকায় এরূপ তদস্ত করা সমীচীন হবে না বা এরূপ তদন্ত হবে। ইতোমধ্যে, উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে যে, তর্কিত আদেশ দ্বারা ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষকে কোন লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা হয়নি; তবে উক্ত তদন্ত চলমান অবস্থায় ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ ফিড অপারেটর হিসাবে কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করারও অধিকারী নন। আবেদনকারীর পক্ষ থেকে অভিযোগ করা হয়েছে তর্কিত আদেশ জারীর পর থেকেই ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ অবৈধভাবে নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনা করে চলেছেন। এ অভিযোগ ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ অস্বীকার করেননি। বিষয়টি আদালতের দৃষ্টিতে আনায়ন করা হলে ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ গত ২৭/০২/২০��৮ইং তারিখে অত্র মামলা নিস্পত্তি না হওয়া পর্যন্ত তা কার্যক্রম বন্ধ রাখার প্রতিশ্রাতি দেন এবং একই সাথে কিছুক্ষণ পর আদালতকে অবহিত করেন যে, ইতোমধ্যেই তারা তাদের কার্যক্রম বন্ধ করেছেন। 

১৩। কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনা আইন, ২০০৬ সালের ৮ ধারা বিধান অনুযায়ী লাইসেঙ্গীং কর্তৃপক্ষ, কোন ব্যক্তির আবেদনের ভিত্তিতে, উপযুক্ততা বিবেচনায় উহার এখতিয়ারধীন এলাকায় কেবল টেলিভিশন নেটওয়ার্ক পরিচালনার জন্য একচেটিয়া ব্যবসা নিরুৎসাহিত করণের লক্ষ্যে একাধিক ব্যক্তিকে লাইসেন্স প্রদান করতে পারে। স্বীকৃত মতেই ১২নং চিকনদস্ভী ইউনিয়নে বর্তমানে লাইসেন্সসহ কেবল রীট আবেদনকারী ব্লাড ড্রপ কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক নামে এবং অপর এক ব্যক্তি এটিএম কমিউনিকেশন নামে ফিড অপারেটর কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করছেন। ইতেমধ্যে পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক নিয়ে যে বিতর্কের সৃষ্টি হয়েছিল সে সম্পর্কে উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবি জানান, বর্তমানে পাহাড়িকা কেবল নেটওয়ার্ক তার কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করছেনা। ফলে, কেবল রীট আবেদনকারী এবং উক্ত এটিএম কমিউনিকেশন কেবল টিভি নেটওয়ার্ক তাদের ফিড অপারেটরের কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করছেন। ঈনং প্রতিপক্ষ লাইসেন্স পাইবার জন্য আবেদন করেছেন। তাঁকে একই এলাকায় লাইসেন্স প্রদান সমীচীন হবে কিনা তা নিরপন করার জন্যেই তর্কিত আদেশ দেওয়া হয়েছে। সরজমিনে তদন্ত সাপেক্ষে যদি প্রতীয়মান হয় ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ লাইসেন্স পেতে পারেন তাহলে উক্ত আইনের ৮ ধারা অনুযায়ী কর্তৃপক্ষ ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষকেও লাইসেন্স প্রদান করতে পারেন।

	তবে, উক্ত তদন্ত শেষ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত ৯নং প্রতিপক্ষ বা লাইসেন্স ছাড়া কোন ব্যক্তি উক্ত এলাকায় ফিড অপারেটর কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করতে আইনগত ভাবে অধিকারী নন| 

	এমতাবস্থায়, উক্ত তদন্ত শেষ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত কর্তৃপক্ষ তাদের প্রদত্ত ২৩/১২/২০১৫ইং তারিখের স্থিতাবস্থা বজায় রাখার আদেশ প্রতিপালন করিতে আইনগত বাধ্য। 

	১৪। সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষকে অত্র রায়ের অনুলিপি পাওয়া থেকে ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে তদন্ত সম্পন্ন করার জন্যে নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল।

	১৫। উপরোক্ত নির্দেশ ও পর্যবেক্ষণসহ রুলনিশিটি বিনা খরচায় নিস্পত্তি করা হল।

	১৬। অন্তবর্তী স্থগিতাদেশ প্রত্যাহার করা হল। 

	সমাপ্ত।
